theirs: Nay, my lord, hear me: the field give I thee, and the cave that [is] therein, I give it thee; in the presence of the sons of my people give I it thee: bury thy dead.

ours: And he spake unto Ephron in the audience of the people of the land, saying, But if thou wilt give it, I pray thee, hear me: I will give thee money for the field; take it of me, and I will bury my dead there.
theirs: And he spake unto Ephron in the audience of the people of the land, saying, But if thou [wilt give it], I pray thee, hear me: I will give thee money for the field; take [it] of me, and I will bury my dead there.

ours: My lord, hearken unto me: the land is worth four hundred shekels of silver; what is that betwixt me and thee? bury therefore thy dead.
theirs: My lord, hearken unto me: the land [is worth] four hundred shekels of silver; what [is] that betwixt me and thee? bury therefore thy dead.

ours: And Abraham hearkened unto Ephron; and Abraham weighed to Ephron the silver, which he had named in the audience of the sons of Heth, four hundred shekels of silver, current money with the merchant.
theirs: And Abraham hearkened unto Ephron; and Abraham weighed to Ephron the silver, which he had named in the audience of the sons of Heth, four hundred shekels of silver, current [money] with the merchant.

ours: And the field of Ephron, which was in Machpelah, which was before Mamre, the field, and the cave which was therein, and all the trees that were in the field, that were in all the borders round about, were made sure
theirs: And the field of Ephron, which [was] in Machpelah, which [was] before Mamre, the field, and the cave which [was] therein, and all the trees that [were] in the field, that [were] in all the borders round about, were made sure

ours: And after this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre: the same is Hebron in the land of Canaan.
theirs: And after this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre: the same [is] Hebron in the land of Canaan.

ours: And the field, and the cave that is therein, were made sure unto Abraham for a possession of a buryingplace by the sons of Heth.
theirs: And the field, and the cave that [is] therein, were made sure unto Abraham for a possession of a buryingplace by the sons of Heth.

ours: AND Abraham was old, and well stricken in age: and the LORD had blessed Abraham in all things.
theirs: And Abraham was old, [and] well stricken in age: and the LORD had blessed Abraham in all things.

ours: The LORD God of heaven, which took me from my fathers house, and from the land of my kindred, and which spake unto me, and that sware unto me, saying, Unto thy seed will I give this land; he shall send his angel before thee, and thou shalt take a wife unto my son from thence.
theirs: The LORD God of heaven, which took me from my father's house, and from the land of my kindred, and which spake unto me, and that sware unto me, saying, Unto thy seed will I give this land; he shall send his angel before thee, and thou shalt take a wife unto my son from thence.

ours: And the servant took ten camels of the camels of his master, and departed; for all the goods of his master were in his hand: and he arose, and went to Mesopotamia, unto the city of Nahor.
theirs: And the servant took ten camels of the camels of his master, and departed; for all the goods of his master [were] in his hand: and he arose, and went to Mesopotamia, unto the city of Nahor.

ours: And he made his camels to kneel down without the city by a well of water at the time of the evening, even the time that women go out to draw water.
theirs: And he made his camels to kneel down without the city by a well of water at the time of the evening, [even] the time that women go out to draw [water].

ours: Behold, I stand here by the well of water; and the daughters of the men of the city come out to draw water:
theirs: Behold, I stand [here] by the well of water; and the daughters of the men of the city come out to draw water:

ours: And let it come to pass, that the damsel to whom I shall say, Let down thy pitcher, I pray thee, that I may drink; and she shall say, Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also: let the same be she that thou hast appointed for thy servant Isaac; and thereby shall I know that thou hast shewed kindness unto my master.
theirs: And let it come to pass, that the damsel to whom I shall say, Let down thy pitcher, I pray thee, that I may drink; and she shall say, Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also: [let the same be] she [that] thou hast appointed for thy servant Isaac; and thereby shall I know that thou hast shewed kindness unto my master.

ours: And it came to pass, before he had done speaking, that, behold, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abrahams brother, with her pitcher upon her shoulder.
theirs: And it came to pass, before he had done speaking, that, behold, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother, with her pitcher upon her shoulder.

ours: And the damsel was very fair to look upon, a virgin, neither had any man known her: and she went down to the well, and filled her pitcher, and came up.
theirs: And the damsel [was] very fair to look upon, a virgin, neither had any man known her: and she went down to the well, and filled her pitcher, and came up.

ours: And when she had done giving him drink, she said, I will draw water for thy camels also, until they have done drinking.
theirs: And when she had done giving him drink, she said, I will draw [water] for thy camels also, until they have done drinking.

ours: And she hasted, and emptied her pitcher into the trough, and ran again unto the well to draw water, and drew for all his camels.
theirs: And she hasted, and emptied her pitcher into the trough, and ran again unto the well to draw [water], and drew for all his camels.

ours: And it came to pass, as the camels had done drinking, that the man took a golden earring of half a shekel weight, and two bracelets for her hands of ten shekels weight of gold;
theirs: And it came to pass, as the camels had done drinking, that the man took a golden earring of half a shekel weight, and two bracelets for her hands of ten [shekels] weight of gold;

ours: And said, Whose daughter art thou? tell me, I pray thee: is there room in thy fathers house for us to lodge in?
theirs: And said, Whose daughter [art] thou? tell me, I pray thee: is there room [in] thy father's house for us to lodge in?

ours: And she said unto him, I am the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, which she bare unto Nahor.
theirs: And she said unto him, I [am] the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, which she bare unto Nahor.

ours: And he said, Blessed be the LORD God of my master Abraham, who hath not left destitute my master of his mercy and his truth: I being in the way, the LORD led me to the house of my masters brethren.
theirs: And he said, Blessed [be] the LORD God of my master Abraham, who hath not left destitute my master of his mercy and his truth: I [being] in the way, the LORD led me to the house of my master's brethren.

ours: And the damsel ran, and told them of her mothers house these things.
theirs: And the damsel ran, and told [them of] her mother's house these things.

ours: And Rebekah had a brother, and his name was Laban: and Laban ran out unto the man, unto the well.
theirs: And Rebekah had a brother, and his name [was] Laban: and Laban ran out unto the man, unto the well.

ours: And it came to pass, when he saw the earring and bracelets upon his sisters hands, and when he heard the words of Rebekah his sister, saying, Thus spake the man unto me; that he came unto the man; and, behold, he stood by the camels at the well.
theirs: And it came to pass, when he saw the earring and bracelets upon his sister's hands, and when he heard the words of Rebekah his sister, saying, Thus spake the man unto me; that he came unto the man; and, behold, he stood by the camels at the well.

ours: And the man came into the house: and he ungirded his camels, and gave straw and provender for the camels, and water to wash his feet, and the mens feet that were with him.
theirs: And the man came into the house: and he ungirded his camels, and gave straw and provender for the camels, and water to wash his feet, and the men's feet that [were] with him.

ours: And there was set meat before him to eat: but he said, I will not eat, until I have told mine errand. And he said, Speak on.
theirs: And there was set [meat] before him to eat: but he said, I will not eat, until I have told mine errand. And he said, Speak on.

ours: And he said, I am Abrahams servant.
theirs: And he said, I [am] Abraham's servant.

ours: And Sarah my masters wife bare a son to my master when she was old: and unto him hath he given all that he hath.
theirs: And Sarah my master's wife bare a son to my master when she was old: and unto him hath he given all that he hath.

ours: But thou shalt go unto my fathers house, and to my kindred, and take a wife unto my son.
theirs: But thou shalt go unto my father's house, and to my kindred, and take a wife unto my son.

ours: And he said unto me, The LORD, before whom I walk, will send his angel with thee, and prosper thy way; and thou shalt take a wife for my son of my kindred, and of my fathers house:
theirs: And he said unto me, The LORD, before whom I walk, will send his angel with thee, and prosper thy way; and thou shalt take a wife for my son of my kindred, and of my father's house:

ours: Then shalt thou be clear from this my oath, when thou comest to my kindred; and if they give not thee one, thou shalt be clear from my oath.
theirs: Then shalt thou be clear from [this] my oath, when thou comest to my kindred; and if they give not thee [one], thou shalt be clear from my oath.

ours: Behold, I stand by the well of water; and it shall come to pass, that when the virgin cometh forth to draw water, and I say to her, Give me, I pray thee, a little water of thy pitcher to drink;
theirs: Behold, I stand by the well of water; and it shall come to pass, that when the virgin cometh forth to draw [water], and I say to her, Give me, I pray thee, a little water of thy pitcher to drink;

ours: And she say to me, Both drink thou, and I will also draw for thy camels: let the same be the woman whom the LORD hath appointed out for my masters son.
theirs: And she say to me, Both drink thou, and I will also draw for thy camels: [let] the same [be] the woman whom the LORD hath appointed out for my master's son.

ours: And before I had done speaking in mine heart, behold, Rebekah came forth with her pitcher on her shoulder; and she went down unto the well, and drew water: and I said unto her, Let me drink, I pray thee.
theirs: And before I had done speaking in mine heart, behold, Rebekah came forth with her pitcher on her shoulder; and she went down unto the well, and drew [water]: and I said unto her, Let me drink, I pray thee.

ours: And she made haste, and let down her pitcher from her shoulder, and said, Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also: so I drank, and she made the camels drink also.
theirs: And she made haste, and let down her pitcher from her [shoulder], and said, Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also: so I drank, and she made the camels drink also.

ours: And I asked her, and said, Whose daughter art thou? And she said, The daughter of Bethuel, Nahors son, whom Milcah bare unto him: and I put the earring upon her face, and the bracelets upon her hands.
theirs: And I asked her, and said, Whose daughter [art] thou? And she said, The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor's son, whom Milcah bare unto him: and I put the earring upon her face, and the bracelets upon her hands.

ours: And I bowed down my head, and worshipped the LORD, and blessed the LORD God of my master Abraham, which had led me in the right way to take my masters brothers daughter unto his son.
theirs: And I bowed down my head, and worshipped the LORD, and blessed the LORD God of my master Abraham, which had led me in the right way to take my master's brother's daughter unto his son.

ours: Behold, Rebekah is before thee, take her, and go, and let her be thy masters sons wife, as the LORD hath spoken.
theirs: Behold, Rebekah [is] before thee, take [her], and go, and let her be thy master's son's wife, as the LORD hath spoken.

ours: And it came to pass, that, when Abrahams servant heard their words, he worshipped the LORD, bowing himself to the earth.
theirs: And it came to pass, that, when Abraham's servant heard their words, he worshipped the LORD, [bowing himself] to the earth.

ours: And the servant brought forth jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment, and gave them to Rebekah: he gave also to her brother and to her mother precious things.
theirs: And the servant brought forth jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment, and gave [them] to Rebekah: he gave also to her brother and to her mother precious things.

ours: And they did eat and drink, he and the men that were with him, and tarried all night; and they rose up in the morning, and he said, Send me away unto my master.
theirs: And they did eat and drink, he and the men that [were] with him, and tarried all night; and they rose up in the morning, and he said, Send me away unto my master.

ours: And her brother and her mother said, Let the damsel abide with us a few days, at the least ten; after that she shall go.
theirs: And her brother and her mother said, Let the damsel abide with us [a few] days, at the least ten; after that she shall go.

ours: And they sent away Rebekah their sister, and her nurse, and Abrahams servant, and his men.
theirs: And they sent away Rebekah their sister, and her nurse, and Abraham's servant, and his men.

ours: And they blessed Rebekah, and said unto her, Thou art our sister, be thou the mother of thousands of millions, and let thy seed possess the gate of those which hate them.
theirs: And they blessed Rebekah, and said unto her, Thou [art] our sister, be thou [the mother] of thousands of millions, and let thy seed possess the gate of those which hate them.

ours: And Isaac came from the way of the well Lahai-roi; for he dwelt in the south country.
theirs: And Isaac came from the way of the well Lahairoi; for he dwelt in the south country.

ours: And Isaac went out to meditate in the field at the eventide: and he lifted up his eyes, and saw, and, behold, the camels were coming.
theirs: And Isaac went out to meditate in the field at the eventide: and he lifted up his eyes, and saw, and, behold, the camels [were] coming.

ours: For she had said unto the servant, What man is this that walketh in the field to meet us? And the servant had said, It is my master: therefore she took a vail, and covered herself.
theirs: For she [had] said unto the servant, What man [is] this that walketh in the field to meet us? And the servant [had] said, It [is] my master: therefore she took a vail, and covered herself.

ours: And Isaac brought her into his mother Sarahs tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife; and he loved her: and Isaac was comforted after his mothers death.
theirs: And Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah's tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife; and he loved her: and Isaac was comforted after his mother's [death].

ours: THEN again Abraham took a wife, and her name was Keturah.
theirs: Then again Abraham took a wife, and her name [was] Keturah.

ours: And the sons of Midian; Ephah, and Epher, and Hanoch, and Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the children of Keturah.
theirs: And the sons of Midian; Ephah, and Epher, and Hanoch, and Abida, and Eldaah. All these [were] the children of Keturah.

ours: And these are the days of the years of Abrahams life which he lived, an hundred threescore and fifteen years.
theirs: And these [are] the days of the years of Abraham's life which he lived, an hundred threescore and fifteen years.

ours: Then Abraham gave up the ghost, and died in a good old age, an old man, and full of years; and was gathered to his people.
theirs: Then Abraham gave up the ghost, and died in a good old age, an old man, and full [of years]; and was gathered to his people.

ours: And his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, which is before Mamre;
theirs: And his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, which [is] before Mamre;

ours: And it came to pass after the death of Abraham, that God blessed his son Isaac; and Isaac dwelt by the well Lahai-roi.
theirs: And it came to pass after the death of Abraham, that God blessed his son Isaac; and Isaac dwelt by the well Lahairoi.

ours: Now these are the generations of Ishmael, Abrahams son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarahs handmaid, bare unto Abraham:
theirs: Now these [are] the generations of Ishmael, Abraham's son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's handmaid, bare unto Abraham:

ours: And these are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, according to their generations: the firstborn of Ishmael, Nebajoth; and Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam,
theirs: And these [are] the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, according to their generations: the firstborn of Ishmael, Nebajoth; and Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam,

ours: These are the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names, by their towns, and by their castles; twelve princes according to their nations.
theirs: These [are] the sons of Ishmael, and these [are] their names, by their towns, and by their castles; twelve princes according to their nations.

ours: And these are the years of the life of Ishmael, an hundred and thirty and seven years: and he gave up the ghost and died; and was gathered unto his people.
theirs: And these [are] the years of the life of Ishmael, an hundred and thirty and seven years: and he gave up the ghost and died; and was gathered unto his people.

ours: And they dwelt from Havilah unto Shur, that is before Egypt, as thou goest toward Assyria: and he died in the presence of all his brethren.
theirs: And they dwelt from Havilah unto Shur, that [is] before Egypt, as thou goest toward Assyria: [and] he died in the presence of all his brethren.

ours: And these are the generations of Isaac, Abrahams son: Abraham begat Isaac:
theirs: And these [are] the generations of Isaac, Abraham's son: Abraham begat Isaac:

ours: And Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah to wife, the daughter of Bethuel the Syrian of Padan-aram, the sister to Laban the Syrian.
theirs: And Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah to wife, the daughter of Bethuel the Syrian of Padanaram, the sister to Laban the Syrian.

ours: And Isaac intreated the LORD for his wife, because she was barren: and the LORD was intreated of him, and Rebekah his wife conceived.
theirs: And Isaac intreated the LORD for his wife, because she [was] barren: and the LORD was intreated of him, and Rebekah his wife conceived.

ours: And the children struggled together within her; and she said, If it be so, why am I thus? And she went to inquire of the LORD.
theirs: And the children struggled together within her; and she said, If [it be] so, why [am] I thus? And she went to inquire of the LORD.

ours: And the LORD said unto her, Two nations are in thy womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels; and the one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger.
theirs: And the LORD said unto her, Two nations [are] in thy womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels; and [the one] people shall be stronger than [the other] people; and the elder shall serve the younger.

ours: And when her days to be delivered were fulfilled, behold, there were twins in her womb.
theirs: And when her days to be delivered were fulfilled, behold, [there were] twins in her womb.

ours: And after that came his brother out, and his hand took hold on Esaus heel; and his name was called Jacob: and Isaac was threescore years old when she bare them.
theirs: And after that came his brother out, and his hand took hold on Esau's heel; and his name was called Jacob: and Isaac [was] threescore years old when she bare them.

ours: And the boys grew: and Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; and Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents.
theirs: And the boys grew: and Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; and Jacob [was] a plain man, dwelling in tents.

ours: And Isaac loved Esau, because he did eat of his venison: but Rebekah loved Jacob.
theirs: And Isaac loved Esau, because he did eat of [his] venison: but Rebekah loved Jacob.

ours: And Jacob sod pottage: and Esau came from the field, and he was faint:
theirs: And Jacob sod pottage: and Esau came from the field, and he [was] faint:

ours: And Esau said to Jacob, Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage; for I am faint: therefore was his name called Edom.
theirs: And Esau said to Jacob, Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red [pottage]; for I [am] faint: therefore was his name called Edom.

ours: And Esau said, Behold, I am at the point to die: and what profit shall this birthright do to me?
theirs: And Esau said, Behold, I [am] at the point to die: and what profit shall this birthright do to me?

ours: Then Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentiles; and he did eat and drink, and rose up, and went his way: thus Esau despised his birthright.
theirs: Then Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentiles; and he did eat and drink, and rose up, and went his way: thus Esau despised [his] birthright.

ours: And the men of the place asked him of his wife; and he said, She is my sister: for he feared to say, She is my wife; lest, said he, the men of the place should kill me for Rebekah; because she was fair to look upon.
theirs: And the men of the place asked [him] of his wife; and he said, She [is] my sister: for he feared to say, [She is] my wife; lest, [said he], the men of the place should kill me for Rebekah; because she [was] fair to look upon.

ours: And it came to pass, when he had been there a long time, that Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out at a window, and saw, and, behold, Isaac was sporting with Rebekah his wife.
theirs: And it came to pass, when he had been there a long time, that Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out at a window, and saw, and, behold, Isaac [was] sporting with Rebekah his wife.

ours: And Abimelech called Isaac, and said, Behold, of a surety she is thy wife: and how saidst thou, She is my sister? And Isaac said unto him, Because I said, Lest I die for her.
theirs: And Abimelech called Isaac, and said, Behold, of a surety she [is] thy wife: and how saidst thou, She [is] my sister? And Isaac said unto him, Because I said, Lest I die for her.

ours: And Abimelech said, What is this thou hast done unto us? one of the people might lightly have lien with thy wife, and thou shouldest have brought guiltiness upon us.
theirs: And Abimelech said, What [is] this thou hast done unto us? one of the people might lightly have lien with thy wife, and thou shouldest have brought guiltiness upon us.

ours: And Abimelech charged all his people, saying, He that toucheth this man or his wife shall surely be put to death.
theirs: And Abimelech charged all [his] people, saying, He that toucheth this man or his wife shall surely be put to death.

ours: For all the wells which his fathers servants had digged in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines had stopped them, and filled them with earth.
theirs: For all the wells which his father's servants had digged in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines had stopped them, and filled them with earth.

ours: And Isaacs servants digged in the valley, and found there a well of springing water.
theirs: And Isaac's servants digged in the valley, and found there a well of springing water.

ours: And the herdmen of Gerar did strive with Isaacs herdmen, saying, The water is ours: and he called the name of the well Esek; because they strove with him.
theirs: And the herdmen of Gerar did strive with Isaac's herdmen, saying, The water [is] ours: and he called the name of the well Esek; because they strove with him.

ours: And he went up from thence to Beer-sheba.
theirs: And he went up from thence to Beersheba.

ours: And the LORD appeared unto him the same night, and said, I am the God of Abraham thy father: fear not, for I am with thee, and will bless thee, and multiply thy seed for my servant Abrahams sake.
theirs: And the LORD appeared unto him the same night, and said, I [am] the God of Abraham thy father: fear not, for I [am] with thee, and will bless thee, and multiply thy seed for my servant Abraham's sake.

ours: And he builded an altar there, and called upon the name of the LORD, and pitched his tent there: and there Isaacs servants digged a well.
theirs: And he builded an altar there, and called upon the name of the LORD, and pitched his tent there: and there Isaac's servants digged a well.

ours: And they said, We saw certainly that the LORD was with thee: and we said, Let there be now an oath betwixt us, even betwixt us and thee, and let us make a covenant with thee;
theirs: And they said, We saw certainly that the LORD was with thee: and we said, Let there be now an oath betwixt us, [even] betwixt us and thee, and let us make a covenant with thee;

ours: That thou wilt do us no hurt, as we have not touched thee, and as we have done unto thee nothing but good, and have sent thee away in peace: thou art now the blessed of the LORD.
theirs: That thou wilt do us no hurt, as we have not touched thee, and as we have done unto thee nothing but good, and have sent thee away in peace: thou [art] now the blessed of the LORD.

ours: And it came to pass the same day, that Isaacs servants came, and told him concerning the well which they had digged, and said unto him, We have found water.
theirs: And it came to pass the same day, that Isaac's servants came, and told him concerning the well which they had digged, and said unto him, We have found water.

ours: And he called it Shebah: therefore the name of the city is Beer-sheba unto this day.
theirs: And he called it Shebah: therefore the name of the city [is] Beersheba unto this day.

ours: AND it came to pass, that when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim, so that he could not see, he called Esau his eldest son, and said unto him, My son: and he said unto him, Behold, here am I.
theirs: And it came to pass, that when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim, so that he could not see, he called Esau his eldest son, and said unto him, My son: and he said unto him, Behold, [here am] I.

ours: Now therefore take, I pray thee, thy weapons, thy quiver and thy bow, and go out to the field, and take me some venison;
theirs: Now therefore take, I pray thee, thy weapons, thy quiver and thy bow, and go out to the field, and take me [some] venison;

ours: And make me savoury meat, such as I love, and bring it to me, that I may eat; that my soul may bless thee before I die.
theirs: And make me savoury meat, such as I love, and bring [it] to me, that I may eat; that my soul may bless thee before I die.

ours: And Rebekah heard when Isaac spake to Esau his son. And Esau went to the field to hunt for venison, and to bring it.
theirs: And Rebekah heard when Isaac spake to Esau his son. And Esau went to the field to hunt [for] venison, [and] to bring [it].

ours: And thou shalt bring it to thy father, that he may eat, and that he may bless thee before his death.
theirs: And thou shalt bring [it] to thy father, that he may eat, and that he may bless thee before his death.

ours: And Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, Behold, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man:
theirs: And Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, Behold, Esau my brother [is] a hairy man, and I [am] a smooth man:

ours: And his mother said unto him, Upon me be thy curse, my son: only obey my voice, and go fetch me them.
theirs: And his mother said unto him, Upon me [be] thy curse, my son: only obey my voice, and go fetch me [them].

ours: And he went, and fetched, and brought them to his mother: and his mother made savoury meat, such as his father loved.
theirs: And he went, and fetched, and brought [them] to his mother: and his mother made savoury meat, such as his father loved.

ours: And Rebekah took goodly raiment of her eldest son Esau, which were with her in the house, and put them upon Jacob her younger son:
theirs: And Rebekah took goodly raiment of her eldest son Esau, which [were] with her in the house, and put them upon Jacob her younger son:

ours: And he came unto his father, and said, My father: and he said, Here am I; who art thou, my son?
theirs: And he came unto his father, and said, My father: and he said, Here [am] I; who [art] thou, my son?

ours: And Jacob said unto his father, I am Esau thy firstborn; I have done according as thou badest me: arise, I pray thee, sit and eat of my venison, that thy soul may bless me.
theirs: And Jacob said unto his father, I [am] Esau thy firstborn; I have done according as thou badest me: arise, I pray thee, sit and eat of my venison, that thy soul may bless me.

ours: And Isaac said unto his son, How is it that thou hast found it so quickly, my son? And he said, Because the LORD thy God brought it to me.
theirs: And Isaac said unto his son, How [is it] that thou hast found [it] so quickly, my son? And he said, Because the LORD thy God brought [it] to me.

ours: And Isaac said unto Jacob, Come near, I pray thee, that I may feel thee, my son, whether thou be my very son Esau or not.
theirs: And Isaac said unto Jacob, Come near, I pray thee, that I may feel thee, my son, whether thou [be] my very son Esau or not.

ours: And Jacob went near unto Isaac his father; and he felt him, and said, The voice is Jacobs voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.
theirs: And Jacob went near unto Isaac his father; and he felt him, and said, The voice [is] Jacob's voice, but the hands [are] the hands of Esau.

ours: And he discerned him not, because his hands were hairy, as his brother Esaus hands: so he blessed him.
theirs: And he discerned him not, because his hands were hairy, as his brother Esau's hands: so he blessed him.

ours: And he said, Art thou my very son Esau? And he said, I am.
theirs: And he said, [Art] thou my very son Esau? And he said, I [am].

ours: And he said, Bring it near to me, and I will eat of my sons venison, that my soul may bless thee. And he brought it near to him, and he did eat: and he brought him wine, and he drank.
theirs: And he said, Bring [it] near to me, and I will eat of my son's venison, that my soul may bless thee. And he brought [it] near to him, and he did eat: and he brought him wine, and he drank.

ours: And he came near, and kissed him: and he smelled the smell of his raiment, and blessed him, and said, See, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which the LORD hath blessed:
theirs: And he came near, and kissed him: and he smelled the smell of his raiment, and blessed him, and said, See, the smell of my son [is] as the smell of a field which the LORD hath blessed:

ours: Let people serve thee, and nations bow down to thee: be lord over thy brethren, and let thy mothers sons bow down to thee: cursed be every one that curseth thee, and blessed be he that blesseth thee.
theirs: Let people serve thee, and nations bow down to thee: be lord over thy brethren, and let thy mother's sons bow down to thee: cursed [be] every one that curseth thee, and blessed [be] he that blesseth thee.

ours: And he also had made savoury meat, and brought it unto his father, and said unto his father, Let my father arise, and eat of his sons venison, that thy soul may bless me.
theirs: And he also had made savoury meat, and brought it unto his father, and said unto his father, Let my father arise, and eat of his son's venison, that thy soul may bless me.

ours: And Isaac his father said unto him, Who art thou? And he said, I am thy son, thy firstborn Esau.
theirs: And Isaac his father said unto him, Who [art] thou? And he said, I [am] thy son, thy firstborn Esau.

ours: And Isaac trembled very exceedingly, and said, Who? where is he that hath taken venison, and brought it me, and I have eaten of all before thou camest, and have blessed him? yea, and he shall be blessed.
theirs: And Isaac trembled very exceedingly, and said, Who? where [is] he that hath taken venison, and brought [it] me, and I have eaten of all before thou camest, and have blessed him? yea, [and] he shall be blessed.

ours: And when Esau heard the words of his father, he cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry, and said unto his father, Bless me, even me also, O my father.
theirs: And when Esau heard the words of his father, he cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry, and said unto his father, Bless me, [even] me also, O my father.

ours: And Esau said unto his father, Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, even me also, O my father. And Esau lifted up his voice, and wept.
theirs: And Esau said unto his father, Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, [even] me also, O my father. And Esau lifted up his voice, and wept.

ours: And these words of Esau her elder son were told to Rebekah: and she sent and called Jacob her younger son, and said unto him, Behold, thy brother Esau, as touching thee, doth comfort himself, purposing to kill thee.
theirs: And these words of Esau her elder son were told to Rebekah: and she sent and called Jacob her younger son, and said unto him, Behold, thy brother Esau, as touching thee, doth comfort himself, [purposing] to kill thee.

ours: And tarry with him a few days, until thy brothers fury turn away;
theirs: And tarry with him a few days, until thy brother's fury turn away;

ours: Until thy brothers anger turn away from thee, and he forget that which thou hast done to him: then I will send, and fetch thee from thence: why should I be deprived also of you both in one day?
theirs: Until thy brother's anger turn away from thee, and he forget [that] which thou hast done to him: then I will send, and fetch thee from thence: why should I be deprived also of you both in one day?

ours: And Rebekah said to Isaac, I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth: if Jacob take a wife of the daughters of Heth, such as these which are of the daughters of the land, what good shall my life do me?
theirs: And Rebekah said to Isaac, I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth: if Jacob take a wife of the daughters of Heth, such as these [which are] of the daughters of the land, what good shall my life do me?

ours: Arise, go to Padan-aram, to the house of Bethuel thy mothers father; and take thee a wife from thence of the daughters of Laban thy mothers brother.
theirs: Arise, go to Padanaram, to the house of Bethuel thy mother's father; and take thee a wife from thence of the daughters of Laban thy mother's brother.

ours: And Isaac sent away Jacob: and he went to Padan-aram unto Laban, son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah, Jacobs and Esaus mother.
theirs: And Isaac sent away Jacob: and he went to Padanaram unto Laban, son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah, Jacob's and Esau's mother.

ours: When Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob, and sent him away to Padan-aram, to take him a wife from thence; and that as he blessed him he gave him a charge, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan;
theirs: When Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob, and sent him away to Padanaram, to take him a wife from thence; and that as he blessed him he gave him a charge, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan;

ours: And that Jacob obeyed his father and his mother, and was gone to Padan-aram;
theirs: And that Jacob obeyed his father and his mother, and was gone to Padanaram;

ours: Then went Esau unto Ishmael, and took unto the wives which he had Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abrahams son, the sister of Nebajoth, to be his wife.
theirs: Then went Esau unto Ishmael, and took unto the wives which he had Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abraham's son, the sister of Nebajoth, to be his wife.

ours: And Jacob went out from Beer-sheba, and went toward Haran.
theirs: And Jacob went out from Beersheba, and went toward Haran.

ours: And he lighted upon a certain place, and tarried there all night, because the sun was set; and he took of the stones of that place, and put them for his pillows, and lay down in that place to sleep.
theirs: And he lighted upon a certain place, and tarried there all night, because the sun was set; and he took of the stones of that place, and put [them for] his pillows, and lay down in that place to sleep.

ours: And, behold, the LORD stood above it, and said, I am the LORD God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac: the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed;
theirs: And, behold, the LORD stood above it, and said, I [am] the LORD God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac: the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed;

ours: And, behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest, and will bring thee again into this land; for I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of.
theirs: And, behold, I [am] with thee, and will keep thee in all [places] whither thou goest, and will bring thee again into this land; for I will not leave thee, until I have done [that] which I have spoken to thee of.

ours: And Jacob awaked out of his sleep, and he said, Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not.
theirs: And Jacob awaked out of his sleep, and he said, Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew [it] not.

ours: And he was afraid, and said, How dreadful is this place! this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.
theirs: And he was afraid, and said, How dreadful [is] this place! this [is] none other but the house of God, and this [is] the gate of heaven.

ours: And Jacob rose up early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put for his pillows, and set it up for a pillar, and poured oil upon the top of it.
theirs: And Jacob rose up early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put [for] his pillows, and set it up [for] a pillar, and poured oil upon the top of it.

ours: And he called the name of that place Beth-el: but the name of that city was called Luz at the first.
theirs: And he called the name of that place Bethel: but the name of that city [was called] Luz at the first.

ours: So that I come again to my fathers house in peace; then shall the LORD be my God:
theirs: So that I come again to my father's house in peace; then shall the LORD be my God:

ours: And this stone, which I have set for a pillar, shall be Gods house: and of all that thou shalt give me I will surely give the tenth unto thee.
theirs: And this stone, which I have set [for] a pillar, shall be God's house: and of all that thou shalt give me I will surely give the tenth unto thee.

ours: And he looked, and behold a well in the field, and, lo, there were three flocks of sheep lying by it; for out of that well they watered the flocks: and a great stone was upon the wells mouth.
theirs: And he looked, and behold a well in the field, and, lo, there [were] three flocks of sheep lying by it; for out of that well they watered the flocks: and a great stone [was] upon the well's mouth.

ours: And thither were all the flocks gathered: and they rolled the stone from the wells mouth, and watered the sheep, and put the stone again upon the wells mouth in his place.
theirs: And thither were all the flocks gathered: and they rolled the stone from the well's mouth, and watered the sheep, and put the stone again upon the well's mouth in his place.

ours: And Jacob said unto them, My brethren, whence be ye? And they said, Of Haran are we.
theirs: And Jacob said unto them, My brethren, whence [be] ye? And they said, Of Haran [are] we.

ours: And he said unto them, Know ye Laban the son of Nahor? And they said, We know him.
theirs: And he said unto them, Know ye Laban the son of Nahor? And they said, We know [him].

ours: And he said unto them, Is he well? And they said, He is well: and, behold, Rachel his daughter cometh with the sheep.
theirs: And he said unto them, [Is] he well? And they said, [He is] well: and, behold, Rachel his daughter cometh with the sheep.

ours: And he said, Lo, it is yet high day, neither is it time that the cattle should be gathered together: water ye the sheep, and go and feed them.
theirs: And he said, Lo, [it is] yet high day, neither [is it] time that the cattle should be gathered together: water ye the sheep, and go [and] feed [them].

ours: And they said, We cannot, until all the flocks be gathered together, and till they roll the stone from the wells mouth; then we water the sheep.
theirs: And they said, We cannot, until all the flocks be gathered together, and [till] they roll the stone from the well's mouth; then we water the sheep.

ours: And while he yet spake with them, Rachel came with her fathers sheep: for she kept them.
theirs: And while he yet spake with them, Rachel came with her father's sheep: for she kept them.

ours: And it came to pass, when Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban his mothers brother, and the sheep of Laban his mothers brother, that Jacob went near, and rolled the stone from the wells mouth, and watered the flock of Laban his mothers brother.
theirs: And it came to pass, when Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban his mother's brother, and the sheep of Laban his mother's brother, that Jacob went near, and rolled the stone from the well's mouth, and watered the flock of Laban his mother's brother.

ours: And Jacob told Rachel that he was her fathers brother, and that he was Rebekahs son: and she ran and told her father.
theirs: And Jacob told Rachel that he [was] her father's brother, and that he [was] Rebekah's son: and she ran and told her father.

ours: And it came to pass, when Laban heard the tidings of Jacob his sisters son, that he ran to meet him, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him to his house. And he told Laban all these things.
theirs: And it came to pass, when Laban heard the tidings of Jacob his sister's son, that he ran to meet him, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him to his house. And he told Laban all these things.

ours: And Laban said to him, Surely thou art my bone and my flesh. And he abode with him the space of a month.
theirs: And Laban said to him, Surely thou [art] my bone and my flesh. And he abode with him the space of a month.

ours: And Laban said unto Jacob, Because thou art my brother, shouldest thou therefore serve me for nought? tell me, what shall thy wages be?
theirs: And Laban said unto Jacob, Because thou [art] my brother, shouldest thou therefore serve me for nought? tell me, what [shall] thy wages [be]?

ours: And Laban had two daughters: the name of the elder was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.
theirs: And Laban had two daughters: the name of the elder [was] Leah, and the name of the younger [was] Rachel.

ours: Leah was tender eyed; but Rachel was beautiful and well favoured.
theirs: Leah [was] tender eyed; but Rachel was beautiful and well favoured.

ours: And Laban said, It is better that I give her to thee, than that I should give her to another man: abide with me.
theirs: And Laban said, [It is] better that I give her to thee, than that I should give her to another man: abide with me.

ours: And Jacob served seven years for Rachel; and they seemed unto him but a few days, for the love he had to her.
theirs: And Jacob served seven years for Rachel; and they seemed unto him [but] a few days, for the love he had to her.

ours: And Jacob said unto Laban, Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in unto her.
theirs: And Jacob said unto Laban, Give [me] my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in unto her.

ours: And Laban gave unto his daughter Leah Zilpah his maid for an handmaid.
theirs: And Laban gave unto his daughter Leah Zilpah his maid [for] an handmaid.

ours: And it came to pass, that in the morning, behold, it was Leah: and he said to Laban, What is this thou hast done unto me? did not I serve with thee for Rachel? wherefore then hast thou beguiled me?
theirs: And it came to pass, that in the morning, behold, it [was] Leah: and he said to Laban, What [is] this thou hast done unto me? did not I serve with thee for Rachel? wherefore then hast thou beguiled me?

ours: And when the LORD saw that Leah was hated, he opened her womb: but Rachel was barren.
theirs: And when the LORD saw that Leah [was] hated, he opened her womb: but Rachel [was] barren.

ours: And she conceived again, and bare a son; and said, Because the LORD hath heard that I was hated, he hath therefore given me this son also: and she called his name Simeon.
theirs: And she conceived again, and bare a son; and said, Because the LORD hath heard that I [was] hated, he hath therefore given me this [son] also: and she called his name Simeon.

ours: And Jacobs anger was kindled against Rachel: and he said, Am I in Gods stead, who hath withheld from thee the fruit of the womb?
theirs: And Jacob's anger was kindled against Rachel: and he said, [Am] I in God's stead, who hath withheld from thee the fruit of the womb?

ours: And Bilhah Rachels maid conceived again, and bare Jacob a second son.
theirs: And Bilhah Rachel's maid conceived again, and bare Jacob a second son.

ours: And Zilpah Leahs maid bare Jacob a son.
theirs: And Zilpah Leah's maid bare Jacob a son.

ours: And Zilpah Leahs maid bare Jacob a second son.
theirs: And Zilpah Leah's maid bare Jacob a second son.

ours: And Reuben went in the days of wheat harvest, and found mandrakes in the field, and brought them unto his mother Leah. Then Rachel said to Leah, Give me, I pray thee, of thy sons mandrakes.
theirs: And Reuben went in the days of wheat harvest, and found mandrakes in the field, and brought them unto his mother Leah. Then Rachel said to Leah, Give me, I pray thee, of thy son's mandrakes.

ours: And she said unto her, Is it a small matter that thou hast taken my husband? and wouldest thou take away my sons mandrakes also? And Rachel said, Therefore he shall lie with thee to night for thy sons mandrakes.
theirs: And she said unto her, [Is it] a small matter that thou hast taken my husband? and wouldest thou take away my son's mandrakes also? And Rachel said, Therefore he shall lie with thee to night for thy son's mandrakes.

ours: And Jacob came out of the field in the evening, and Leah went out to meet him, and said, Thou must come in unto me; for surely I have hired thee with my sons mandrakes. And he lay with her that night.
theirs: And Jacob came out of the field in the evening, and Leah went out to meet him, and said, Thou must come in unto me; for surely I have hired thee with my son's mandrakes. And he lay with her that night.

ours: And Leah said, God hath endued me with a good dowry; now will my husband dwell with me, because I have born him six sons: and she called his name Zebulun.
theirs: And Leah said, God hath endued me [with] a good dowry; now will my husband dwell with me, because I have born him six sons: and she called his name Zebulun.

ours: Give me my wives and my children, for whom I have served thee, and let me go: for thou knowest my service which I have done thee.
theirs: Give [me] my wives and my children, for whom I have served thee, and let me go: for thou knowest my service which I have done thee.

ours: And Laban said unto him, I pray thee, if I have found favour in thine eyes, tarry: for I have learned by experience that the LORD hath blessed me for thy sake.
theirs: And Laban said unto him, I pray thee, if I have found favour in thine eyes, [tarry: for] I have learned by experience that the LORD hath blessed me for thy sake.

ours: And he said, Appoint me thy wages, and I will give it.
theirs: And he said, Appoint me thy wages, and I will give [it].

ours: For it was little which thou hadst before I came, and it is now increased unto a multitude; and the LORD hath blessed thee since my coming: and now when shall I provide for mine own house also?
theirs: For [it was] little which thou hadst before I [came], and it is [now] increased unto a multitude; and the LORD hath blessed thee since my coming: and now when shall I provide for mine own house also?

ours: And he said, What shall I give thee? And Jacob said, Thou shalt not give me any thing: if thou wilt do this thing for me, I will again feed and keep thy flock:
theirs: And he said, What shall I give thee? And Jacob said, Thou shalt not give me any thing: if thou wilt do this thing for me, I will again feed [and] keep thy flock:

ours: I will pass through all thy flock to day, removing from thence all the speckled and spotted cattle, and all the brown cattle among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats: and of such shall be my hire.
theirs: I will pass through all thy flock to day, removing from thence all the speckled and spotted cattle, and all the brown cattle among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats: and [of such] shall be my hire.

ours: So shall my righteousness answer for me in time to come, when it shall come for my hire before thy face: every one that is not speckled and spotted among the goats, and brown among the sheep, that shall be counted stolen with me.
theirs: So shall my righteousness answer for me in time to come, when it shall come for my hire before thy face: every one that [is] not speckled and spotted among the goats, and brown among the sheep, that shall be counted stolen with me.

ours: And he removed that day the he goats that were ringstraked and spotted, and all the she goats that were speckled and spotted, and every one that had some white in it, and all the brown among the sheep, and gave them into the hand of his sons.
theirs: And he removed that day the he goats that were ringstraked and spotted, and all the she goats that were speckled and spotted, [and] every one that had [some] white in it, and all the brown among the sheep, and gave [them] into the hand of his sons.

ours: And he set three days journey betwixt himself and Jacob: and Jacob fed the rest of Labans flocks.
theirs: And he set three days' journey betwixt himself and Jacob: and Jacob fed the rest of Laban's flocks.

ours: And Jacob took him rods of green poplar, and of the hazel and chesnut tree; and pilled white strakes in them, and made the white appear which was in the rods.
theirs: And Jacob took him rods of green poplar, and of the hazel and chesnut tree; and pilled white strakes in them, and made the white appear which [was] in the rods.

ours: And Jacob did separate the lambs, and set the faces of the flocks toward the ringstraked, and all the brown in the flock of Laban; and he put his own flocks by themselves, and put them not unto Labans cattle.
theirs: And Jacob did separate the lambs, and set the faces of the flocks toward the ringstraked, and all the brown in the flock of Laban; and he put his own flocks by themselves, and put them not unto Laban's cattle.

ours: But when the cattle were feeble, he put them not in: so the feebler were Labans, and the stronger Jacobs.
theirs: But when the cattle were feeble, he put [them] not in: so the feebler were Laban's, and the stronger Jacob's.

ours: AND he heard the words of Labans sons, saying, Jacob hath taken away all that was our fathers; and of that which was our fathers hath he gotten all this glory.
theirs: And he heard the words of Laban's sons, saying, Jacob hath taken away all that [was] our father's; and of [that] which [was] our father's hath he gotten all this glory.

ours: And Jacob beheld the countenance of Laban, and, behold, it was not toward him as before.
theirs: And Jacob beheld the countenance of Laban, and, behold, it [was] not toward him as before.

ours: And said unto them, I see your fathers countenance, that it is not toward me as before; but the God of my father hath been with me.
theirs: And said unto them, I see your father's countenance, that it [is] not toward me as before; but the God of my father hath been with me.

ours: Thus God hath taken away the cattle of your father, and given them to me.
theirs: Thus God hath taken away the cattle of your father, and given [them] to me.

ours: And it came to pass at the time that the cattle conceived, that I lifted up mine eyes, and saw in a dream, and, behold, the rams which leaped upon the cattle were ringstraked, speckled, and grisled.
theirs: And it came to pass at the time that the cattle conceived, that I lifted up mine eyes, and saw in a dream, and, behold, the rams which leaped upon the cattle [were] ringstraked, speckled, and grisled.

ours: And the angel of God spake unto me in a dream, saying, Jacob: And I said, Here am I.
theirs: And the angel of God spake unto me in a dream, [saying], Jacob: And I said, Here [am] I.

ours: And he said, Lift up now thine eyes, and see, all the rams which leap upon the cattle are ringstraked, speckled, and grisled: for I have seen all that Laban doeth unto thee.
theirs: And he said, Lift up now thine eyes, and see, all the rams which leap upon the cattle [are] ringstraked, speckled, and grisled: for I have seen all that Laban doeth unto thee.

ours: I am the God of Beth-el, where thou anointedst the pillar, and where thou vowedst a vow unto me: now arise, get thee out from this land, and return unto the land of thy kindred.
theirs: I [am] the God of Bethel, where thou anointedst the pillar, [and] where thou vowedst a vow unto me: now arise, get thee out from this land, and return unto the land of thy kindred.

ours: And Rachel and Leah answered and said unto him, Is there yet any portion or inheritance for us in our fathers house?
theirs: And Rachel and Leah answered and said unto him, [Is there] yet any portion or inheritance for us in our father's house?

ours: For all the riches which God hath taken from our father, that is ours, and our childrens: now then, whatsoever God hath said unto thee, do.
theirs: For all the riches which God hath taken from our father, that [is] ours, and our children's: now then, whatsoever God hath said unto thee, do.

ours: And he carried away all his cattle, and all his goods which he had gotten, the cattle of his getting, which he had gotten in Padan-aram, for to go to Isaac his father in the land of Canaan.
theirs: And he carried away all his cattle, and all his goods which he had gotten, the cattle of his getting, which he had gotten in Padanaram, for to go to Isaac his father in the land of Canaan.

ours: And Laban went to shear his sheep: and Rachel had stolen the images that were her fathers.
theirs: And Laban went to shear his sheep: and Rachel had stolen the images that [were] her father's.

ours: So he fled with all that he had; and he rose up, and passed over the river, and set his face toward the mount Gilead.
theirs: So he fled with all that he had; and he rose up, and passed over the river, and set his face [toward] the mount Gilead.

ours: And he took his brethren with him, and pursued after him seven days journey; and they overtook him in the mount Gilead.
theirs: And he took his brethren with him, and pursued after him seven days' journey; and they overtook him in the mount Gilead.

ours: And Laban said to Jacob, What hast thou done, that thou hast stolen away unawares to me, and carried away my daughters, as captives taken with the sword?
theirs: And Laban said to Jacob, What hast thou done, that thou hast stolen away unawares to me, and carried away my daughters, as captives [taken] with the sword?

ours: And hast not suffered me to kiss my sons and my daughters? thou hast now done foolishly in so doing.
theirs: And hast not suffered me to kiss my sons and my daughters? thou hast now done foolishly in [so] doing.

ours: And now, though thou wouldest needs be gone, because thou sore longedst after thy fathers house, yet wherefore hast thou stolen my gods?
theirs: And now, [though] thou wouldest needs be gone, because thou sore longedst after thy father's house, [yet] wherefore hast thou stolen my gods?

ours: With whomsoever thou findest thy gods, let him not live: before our brethren discern thou what is thine with me, and take it to thee. For Jacob knew not that Rachel had stolen them.
theirs: With whomsoever thou findest thy gods, let him not live: before our brethren discern thou what [is] thine with me, and take [it] to thee. For Jacob knew not that Rachel had stolen them.

ours: And Laban went into Jacobs tent, and into Leahs tent, and into the two maidservants tents; but he found them not. Then went he out of Leahs tent, and entered into Rachels tent.
theirs: And Laban went into Jacob's tent, and into Leah's tent, and into the two maidservants' tents; but he found [them] not. Then went he out of Leah's tent, and entered into Rachel's tent.

ours: Now Rachel had taken the images, and put them in the camels furniture, and sat upon them. And Laban searched all the tent, but found them not.
theirs: Now Rachel had taken the images, and put them in the camel's furniture, and sat upon them. And Laban searched all the tent, but found [them] not.

ours: And she said to her father, Let it not displease my lord that I cannot rise up before thee; for the custom of women is upon me. And he searched, but found not the images.
theirs: And she said to her father, Let it not displease my lord that I cannot rise up before thee; for the custom of women [is] upon me. And he searched, but found not the images.

ours: And Jacob was wroth, and chode with Laban: and Jacob answered and said to Laban, What is my trespass? what is my sin, that thou hast so hotly pursued after me?
theirs: And Jacob was wroth, and chode with Laban: and Jacob answered and said to Laban, What [is] my trespass? what [is] my sin, that thou hast so hotly pursued after me?

ours: Whereas thou hast searched all my stuff, what hast thou found of all thy household stuff? set it here before my brethren and thy brethren, that they may judge betwixt us both.
theirs: Whereas thou hast searched all my stuff, what hast thou found of all thy household stuff? set [it] here before my brethren and thy brethren, that they may judge betwixt us both.

ours: This twenty years have I been with thee; thy ewes and thy she goats have not cast their young, and the rams of thy flock have I not eaten.
theirs: This twenty years [have] I [been] with thee; thy ewes and thy she goats have not cast their young, and the rams of thy flock have I not eaten.

ours: That which was torn of beasts I brought not unto thee; I bare the loss of it; of my hand didst thou require it, whether stolen by day, or stolen by night.
theirs: That which was torn [of beasts] I brought not unto thee; I bare the loss of it; of my hand didst thou require it, [whether] stolen by day, or stolen by night.

ours: Thus I was; in the day the drought consumed me, and the frost by night; and my sleep departed from mine eyes.
theirs: [Thus] I was; in the day the drought consumed me, and the frost by night; and my sleep departed from mine eyes.

ours: Except the God of my father, the God of Abraham, and the fear of Isaac, had been with me, surely thou hadst sent me away now empty. God hath seen mine affliction and the labour of my hands, and rebuked thee yesternight.
theirs: Except the God of my father, the God of Abraham, and the fear of Isaac, had been with me, surely thou hadst sent me away now empty. God hath seen mine affliction and the labour of my hands, and rebuked [thee] yesternight.

ours: And Laban answered and said unto Jacob, These daughters are my daughters, and these children are my children, and these cattle are my cattle, and all that thou seest is mine: and what can I do this day unto these my daughters, or unto their children which they have born?
theirs: And Laban answered and said unto Jacob, [These] daughters [are] my daughters, and [these] children [are] my children, and [these] cattle [are] my cattle, and all that thou seest [is] mine: and what can I do this day unto these my daughters, or unto their children which they have born?

ours: And Jacob took a stone, and set it up for a pillar.
theirs: And Jacob took a stone, and set it up [for] a pillar.

ours: And Laban called it Jegar-sahadutha: but Jacob called it Galeed.
theirs: And Laban called it Jegarsahadutha: but Jacob called it Galeed.

ours: And Laban said, This heap is a witness between me and thee this day. Therefore was the name of it called Galeed;
theirs: And Laban said, This heap [is] a witness between me and thee this day. Therefore was the name of it called Galeed;

ours: If thou shalt afflict my daughters, or if thou shalt take other wives beside my daughters, no man is with us; see, God is witness betwixt me and thee.
theirs: If thou shalt afflict my daughters, or if thou shalt take [other] wives beside my daughters, no man [is] with us; see, God [is] witness betwixt me and thee.

ours: And Laban said to Jacob, Behold this heap, and behold this pillar, which I have cast betwixt me and thee;
theirs: And Laban said to Jacob, Behold this heap, and behold [this] pillar, which I have cast betwixt me and thee;

ours: This heap be witness, and this pillar be witness, that I will not pass over this heap to thee, and that thou shalt not pass over this heap and this pillar unto me, for harm.
theirs: This heap [be] witness, and [this] pillar [be] witness, that I will not pass over this heap to thee, and that thou shalt not pass over this heap and this pillar unto me, for harm.

ours: And when Jacob saw them, he said, This is Gods host: and he called the name of that place Mahanaim.
theirs: And when Jacob saw them, he said, This [is] God's host: and he called the name of that place Mahanaim.

ours: Then Jacob was greatly afraid and distressed: and he divided the people that was with him, and the flocks, and herds, and the camels, into two bands;
theirs: Then Jacob was greatly afraid and distressed: and he divided the people that [was] with him, and the flocks, and herds, and the camels, into two bands;

ours: Deliver me, I pray thee, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau: for I fear him, lest he will come and smite me, and the mother with the children.
theirs: Deliver me, I pray thee, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau: for I fear him, lest he will come and smite me, [and] the mother with the children.

ours: And he delivered them into the hand of his servants, every drove by themselves; and said unto his servants, Pass over before me, and put a space betwixt drove and drove.
theirs: And he delivered [them] into the hand of his servants, every drove by themselves; and said unto his servants, Pass over before me, and put a space betwixt drove and drove.

ours: And he commanded the foremost, saying, When Esau my brother meeteth thee, and asketh thee, saying, Whose art thou? and whither goest thou? and whose are these before thee?
theirs: And he commanded the foremost, saying, When Esau my brother meeteth thee, and asketh thee, saying, Whose [art] thou? and whither goest thou? and whose [are] these before thee?

ours: Then thou shalt say, They be thy servant Jacobs; it is a present sent unto my lord Esau: and, behold, also he is behind us.
theirs: Then thou shalt say, [They be] thy servant Jacob's; it [is] a present sent unto my lord Esau: and, behold, also he [is] behind us.

ours: And say ye moreover, Behold, thy servant Jacob is behind us. For he said, I will appease him with the present that goeth before me, and afterward I will see his face; peradventure he will accept of me.
theirs: And say ye moreover, Behold, thy servant Jacob [is] behind us. For he said, I will appease him with the present that goeth before me, and afterward I will see his face; peradventure he will accept of me.

ours: And when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh; and the hollow of Jacobs thigh was out of joint, as he wrestled with him.
theirs: And when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh; and the hollow of Jacob's thigh was out of joint, as he wrestled with him.

ours: And he said unto him, What is thy name? And he said, Jacob.
theirs: And he said unto him, What [is] thy name? And he said, Jacob.

ours: And Jacob asked him, and said, Tell me, I pray thee, thy name. And he said, Wherefore is it that thou dost ask after my name? And he blessed him there.
theirs: And Jacob asked [him], and said, Tell [me], I pray thee, thy name. And he said, Wherefore [is] it [that] thou dost ask after my name? And he blessed him there.

ours: Therefore the children of Israel eat not of the sinew which shrank, which is upon the hollow of the thigh, unto this day: because he touched the hollow of Jacobs thigh in the sinew that shrank.
theirs: Therefore the children of Israel eat not [of] the sinew which shrank, which [is] upon the hollow of the thigh, unto this day: because he touched the hollow of Jacob's thigh in the sinew that shrank.

ours: And he lifted up his eyes, and saw the women and the children; and said, Who are those with thee? And he said, The children which God hath graciously given thy servant.
theirs: And he lifted up his eyes, and saw the women and the children; and said, Who [are] those with thee? And he said, The children which God hath graciously given thy servant.

ours: And he said, What meanest thou by all this drove which I met? And he said, These are to find grace in the sight of my lord.
theirs: And he said, What [meanest] thou by all this drove which I met? And he said, [These are] to find grace in the sight of my lord.

ours: Take, I pray thee, my blessing that is brought to thee; because God hath dealt graciously with me, and because I have enough. And he urged him, and he took it.
theirs: Take, I pray thee, my blessing that is brought to thee; because God hath dealt graciously with me, and because I have enough. And he urged him, and he took [it].

ours: And he said unto him, My lord knoweth that the children are tender, and the flocks and herds with young are with me: and if men should overdrive them one day, all the flock will die.
theirs: And he said unto him, My lord knoweth that the children [are] tender, and the flocks and herds with young [are] with me: and if men should overdrive them one day, all the flock will die.

ours: And Esau said, Let me now leave with thee some of the folk that are with me. And he said, What needeth it? let me find grace in the sight of my lord.
theirs: And Esau said, Let me now leave with thee [some] of the folk that [are] with me. And he said, What needeth it? let me find grace in the sight of my lord.

ours: And Jacob came to Shalem, a city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Padan-aram; and pitched his tent before the city.
theirs: And Jacob came to Shalem, a city of Shechem, which [is] in the land of Canaan, when he came from Padanaram; and pitched his tent before the city.

ours: And he bought a parcel of a field, where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechems father, for an hundred pieces of money.
theirs: And he bought a parcel of a field, where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem's father, for an hundred pieces of money.

ours: And he erected there an altar, and called it El-elohe-Israel.
theirs: And he erected there an altar, and called it EleloheIsrael.

ours: And the sons of Jacob came out of the field when they heard it: and the men were grieved, and they were very wroth, because he had wrought folly in Israel in lying with Jacobs daughter; which thing ought not to be done.
theirs: And the sons of Jacob came out of the field when they heard [it]: and the men were grieved, and they were very wroth, because he had wrought folly in Israel in lying with Jacob's daughter; which thing ought not to be done.

ours: And make ye marriages with us, and give your daughters unto us, and take our daughters unto you.
theirs: And make ye marriages with us, [and] give your daughters unto us, and take our daughters unto you.

ours: And they said unto them, We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to one that is uncircumcised; for that were a reproach unto us:
theirs: And they said unto them, We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to one that is uncircumcised; for that [were] a reproach unto us:

ours: But in this will we consent unto you: If ye will be as we be, that every male of you be circumcised;
theirs: But in this will we consent unto you: If ye will be as we [be], that every male of you be circumcised;

ours: And their words pleased Hamor, and Shechem Hamors son.
theirs: And their words pleased Hamor, and Shechem Hamor's son.

ours: And the young man deferred not to do the thing, because he had delight in Jacobs daughter: and he was more honourable than all the house of his father.
theirs: And the young man deferred not to do the thing, because he had delight in Jacob's daughter: and he [was] more honourable than all the house of his father.

ours: These men are peaceable with us; therefore let them dwell in the land, and trade therein; for the land, behold, it is large enough for them; let us take their daughters to us for wives, and let us give them our daughters.
theirs: These men [are] peaceable with us; therefore let them dwell in the land, and trade therein; for the land, behold, [it is] large enough for them; let us take their daughters to us for wives, and let us give them our daughters.

ours: Only herein will the men consent unto us for to dwell with us, to be one people, if every male among us be circumcised, as they are circumcised.
theirs: Only herein will the men consent unto us for to dwell with us, to be one people, if every male among us be circumcised, as they [are] circumcised.

ours: Shall not their cattle and their substance and every beast of theirs be ours? only let us consent unto them, and they will dwell with us.
theirs: [Shall] not their cattle and their substance and every beast of theirs [be] ours? only let us consent unto them, and they will dwell with us.

ours: And it came to pass on the third day, when they were sore, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinahs brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males.
theirs: And it came to pass on the third day, when they were sore, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males.

ours: And they slew Hamor and Shechem his son with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah out of Shechems house, and went out.
theirs: And they slew Hamor and Shechem his son with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah out of Shechem's house, and went out.

ours: They took their sheep, and their oxen, and their asses, and that which was in the city, and that which was in the field,
theirs: They took their sheep, and their oxen, and their asses, and that which [was] in the city, and that which [was] in the field,

ours: And all their wealth, and all their little ones, and their wives took they captive, and spoiled even all that was in the house.
theirs: And all their wealth, and all their little ones, and their wives took they captive, and spoiled even all that [was] in the house.

ours: And Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, Ye have troubled me to make me to stink among the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites: and I being few in number, they shall gather themselves together against me, and slay me; and I shall be destroyed, I and my house.
theirs: And Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, Ye have troubled me to make me to stink among the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites: and I [being] few in number, they shall gather themselves together against me, and slay me; and I shall be destroyed, I and my house.

ours: AND God said unto Jacob, Arise, go up to Beth-el, and dwell there: and make there an altar unto God, that appeared unto thee when thou fleddest from the face of Esau thy brother.
theirs: And God said unto Jacob, Arise, go up to Bethel, and dwell there: and make there an altar unto God, that appeared unto thee when thou fleddest from the face of Esau thy brother.

ours: Then Jacob said unto his household, and to all that were with him, Put away the strange gods that are among you, and be clean, and change your garments:
theirs: Then Jacob said unto his household, and to all that [were] with him, Put away the strange gods that [are] among you, and be clean, and change your garments:

ours: And let us arise, and go up to Beth-el; and I will make there an altar unto God, who answered me in the day of my distress, and was with me in the way which I went.
theirs: And let us arise, and go up to Bethel; and I will make there an altar unto God, who answered me in the day of my distress, and was with me in the way which I went.

ours: And they gave unto Jacob all the strange gods which were in their hand, and all their earrings which were in their ears; and Jacob hid them under the oak which was by Shechem.
theirs: And they gave unto Jacob all the strange gods which [were] in their hand, and [all their] earrings which [were] in their ears; and Jacob hid them under the oak which [was] by Shechem.

ours: And they journeyed: and the terror of God was upon the cities that were round about them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.
theirs: And they journeyed: and the terror of God was upon the cities that [were] round about them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.

ours: So Jacob came to Luz, which is in the land of Canaan, that is, Beth-el, he and all the people that were with him.
theirs: So Jacob came to Luz, which [is] in the land of Canaan, that [is], Bethel, he and all the people that [were] with him.

ours: And he built there an altar, and called the place El-beth-el: because there God appeared unto him, when he fled from the face of his brother.
theirs: And he built there an altar, and called the place Elbethel: because there God appeared unto him, when he fled from the face of his brother.

ours: But Deborah Rebekahs nurse died, and she was buried beneath Beth-el under an oak: and the name of it was called Allon-bachuth.
theirs: But Deborah Rebekah's nurse died, and she was buried beneath Bethel under an oak: and the name of it was called Allonbachuth.

ours: And God appeared unto Jacob again, when he came out of Padan-aram, and blessed him.
theirs: And God appeared unto Jacob again, when he came out of Padanaram, and blessed him.

ours: And God said unto him, Thy name is Jacob: thy name shall not be called any more Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name: and he called his name Israel.
theirs: And God said unto him, Thy name [is] Jacob: thy name shall not be called any more Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name: and he called his name Israel.

ours: And God said unto him, I am God Almighty: be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations shall be of thee, and kings shall come out of thy loins;
theirs: And God said unto him, I [am] God Almighty: be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations shall be of thee, and kings shall come out of thy loins;

ours: And Jacob set up a pillar in the place where he talked with him, even a pillar of stone: and he poured a drink offering thereon, and he poured oil thereon.
theirs: And Jacob set up a pillar in the place where he talked with him, [even] a pillar of stone: and he poured a drink offering thereon, and he poured oil thereon.

ours: And Jacob called the name of the place where God spake with him, Beth-el.
theirs: And Jacob called the name of the place where God spake with him, Bethel.

ours: And they journeyed from Beth-el; and there was but a little way to come to Ephrath: and Rachel travailed, and she had hard labour.
theirs: And they journeyed from Bethel; and there was but a little way to come to Ephrath: and Rachel travailed, and she had hard labour.

ours: And it came to pass, as her soul was in departing, (for she died) that she called his name Ben-oni: but his father called him Benjamin.
theirs: And it came to pass, as her soul was in departing, (for she died) that she called his name Benoni: but his father called him Benjamin.

ours: And Rachel died, and was buried in the way to Ephrath, which is Beth-lehem.
theirs: And Rachel died, and was buried in the way to Ephrath, which [is] Bethlehem.

ours: And Jacob set a pillar upon her grave: that is the pillar of Rachels grave unto this day.
theirs: And Jacob set a pillar upon her grave: that [is] the pillar of Rachel's grave unto this day.

ours: And it came to pass, when Israel dwelt in that land, that Reuben went and lay with Bilhah his fathers concubine: and Israel heard it. Now the sons of Jacob were twelve:
theirs: And it came to pass, when Israel dwelt in that land, that Reuben went and lay with Bilhah his father's concubine: and Israel heard [it]. Now the sons of Jacob were twelve:

ours: The sons of Leah; Reuben, Jacobs firstborn, and Simeon, and Levi, and Judah, and Issachar, and Zebulun:
theirs: The sons of Leah; Reuben, Jacob's firstborn, and Simeon, and Levi, and Judah, and Issachar, and Zebulun:

ours: And the sons of Bilhah, Rachels handmaid; Dan, and Naphtali:
theirs: And the sons of Bilhah, Rachel's handmaid; Dan, and Naphtali:

ours: And the sons of Zilpah, Leahs handmaid; Gad, and Asher: these are the sons of Jacob, which were born to him in Padan-aram.
theirs: And the sons of Zilpah, Leah's handmaid; Gad, and Asher: these [are] the sons of Jacob, which were born to him in Padanaram.

ours: And Jacob came unto Isaac his father unto Mamre, unto the city of Arbah, which is Hebron, where Abraham and Isaac sojourned.
theirs: And Jacob came unto Isaac his father unto Mamre, unto the city of Arbah, which [is] Hebron, where Abraham and Isaac sojourned.

ours: And Isaac gave up the ghost, and died, and was gathered unto his people, being old and full of days: and his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.
theirs: And Isaac gave up the ghost, and died, and was gathered unto his people, [being] old and full of days: and his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.

ours: NOW these are the generations of Esau, who is Edom.
theirs: Now these [are] the generations of Esau, who [is] Edom.

ours: And Bashemath Ishmaels daughter, sister of Nebajoth.
theirs: And Bashemath Ishmael's daughter, sister of Nebajoth.

ours: And Aholibamah bare Jeush, and Jaalam, and Korah: these are the sons of Esau, which were born unto him in the land of Canaan.
theirs: And Aholibamah bare Jeush, and Jaalam, and Korah: these [are] the sons of Esau, which were born unto him in the land of Canaan.

ours: Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.
theirs: Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau [is] Edom.

ours: And these are the generations of Esau the father of the Edomites in mount Seir:
theirs: And these [are] the generations of Esau the father of the Edomites in mount Seir:

ours: These are the names of Esaus sons; Eliphaz the son of Adah the wife of Esau, Reuel the son of Bashemath the wife of Esau.
