theirs: So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then was the king's wrath pacified.

ours: ON that day did the king Ahasuerus give the house of Haman the Jews enemy unto Esther the queen. And Mordecai came before the king; for Esther had told what he was unto her.
theirs: On that day did the king Ahasuerus give the house of Haman the Jews' enemy unto Esther the queen. And Mordecai came before the king; for Esther had told what he [was] unto her.

ours: And said, If it please the king, and if I have found favour in his sight, and the thing seem right before the king, and I be pleasing in his eyes, let it be written to reverse the letters devised by Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to destroy the Jews which are in all the kings provinces:
theirs: And said, If it please the king, and if I have found favour in his sight, and the thing [seem] right before the king, and I [be] pleasing in his eyes, let it be written to reverse the letters devised by Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to destroy the Jews which [are] in all the king's provinces:

ours: Write ye also for the Jews, as it liketh you, in the kings name, and seal it with the kings ring: for the writing which is written in the kings name, and sealed with the kings ring, may no man reverse.
theirs: Write ye also for the Jews, as it liketh you, in the king's name, and seal [it] with the king's ring: for the writing which is written in the king's name, and sealed with the king's ring, may no man reverse.

ours: Then were the kings scribes called at that time in the third month, that is, the month Sivan, on the three and twentieth day thereof; and it was written according to all that Mordecai commanded unto the Jews, and to the lieutenants, and the deputies and rulers of the provinces which are from India unto Ethiopia, an hundred twenty and seven provinces, unto every province according to the writing thereof, and unto every people after their language, and to the Jews according to their writing, and according to their language.
theirs: Then were the king's scribes called at that time in the third month, that [is], the month Sivan, on the three and twentieth [day] thereof; and it was written according to all that Mordecai commanded unto the Jews, and to the lieutenants, and the deputies and rulers of the provinces which [are] from India unto Ethiopia, an hundred twenty and seven provinces, unto every province according to the writing thereof, and unto every people after their language, and to the Jews according to their writing, and according to their language.

ours: And he wrote in the king Ahasuerus name, and sealed it with the kings ring, and sent letters by posts on horseback, and riders on mules, camels, and young dromedaries:
theirs: And he wrote in the king Ahasuerus' name, and sealed [it] with the king's ring, and sent letters by posts on horseback, [and] riders on mules, camels, [and] young dromedaries:

ours: Wherein the king granted the Jews which were in every city to gather themselves together, and to stand for their life, to destroy, to slay, and to cause to perish, all the power of the people and province that would assault them, both little ones and women, and to take the spoil of them for a prey,
theirs: Wherein the king granted the Jews which [were] in every city to gather themselves together, and to stand for their life, to destroy, to slay, and to cause to perish, all the power of the people and province that would assault them, [both] little ones and women, and [to take] the spoil of them for a prey,

ours: Upon one day in all the provinces of king Ahasuerus, namely, upon the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar.
theirs: Upon one day in all the provinces of king Ahasuerus, [namely], upon the thirteenth [day] of the twelfth month, which [is] the month Adar.

ours: The copy of the writing for a commandment to be given in every province was published unto all people, and that the Jews should be ready against that day to avenge themselves on their enemies.
theirs: The copy of the writing for a commandment to be given in every province [was] published unto all people, and that the Jews should be ready against that day to avenge themselves on their enemies.

ours: So the posts that rode upon mules and camels went out, being hastened and pressed on by the kings commandment. And the decree was given at Shushan the palace.
theirs: [So] the posts that rode upon mules [and] camels went out, being hastened and pressed on by the king's commandment. And the decree was given at Shushan the palace.

ours: And in every province, and in every city, whithersoever the kings commandment and his decree came, the Jews had joy and gladness, a feast and a good day. And many of the people of the land became Jews; for the fear of the Jews fell upon them.
theirs: And in every province, and in every city, whithersoever the king's commandment and his decree came, the Jews had joy and gladness, a feast and a good day. And many of the people of the land became Jews; for the fear of the Jews fell upon them.

ours: NOW in the twelfth month, that is, the month Adar, on the thirteenth day of the same, when the kings commandment and his decree drew near to be put in execution, in the day that the enemies of the Jews hoped to have power over them, (though it was turned to the contrary, that the Jews had rule over them that hated them;)
theirs: Now in the twelfth month, that [is], the month Adar, on the thirteenth day of the same, when the king's commandment and his decree drew near to be put in execution, in the day that the enemies of the Jews hoped to have power over them, (though it was turned to the contrary, that the Jews had rule over them that hated them;)

ours: For Mordecai was great in the kings house, and his fame went out throughout all the provinces: for this man Mordecai waxed greater and greater.
theirs: For Mordecai [was] great in the king's house, and his fame went out throughout all the provinces: for this man Mordecai waxed greater and greater.

ours: And the king said unto Esther the queen, The Jews have slain and destroyed five hundred men in Shushan the palace, and the ten sons of Haman; what have they done in the rest of the kings provinces? now what is thy petition? and it shall be granted thee: or what is thy request further? and it shall be done.
theirs: And the king said unto Esther the queen, The Jews have slain and destroyed five hundred men in Shushan the palace, and the ten sons of Haman; what have they done in the rest of the king's provinces? now what [is] thy petition? and it shall be granted thee: or what [is] thy request further? and it shall be done.

ours: Then said Esther, If it please the king, let it be granted to the Jews which are in Shushan to do to morrow also according unto this days decree, and let Hamans ten sons be hanged upon the gallows.
theirs: Then said Esther, If it please the king, let it be granted to the Jews which [are] in Shushan to do to morrow also according unto this day's decree, and let Haman's ten sons be hanged upon the gallows.

ours: And the king commanded it so to be done: and the decree was given at Shushan; and they hanged Hamans ten sons.
theirs: And the king commanded it so to be done: and the decree was given at Shushan; and they hanged Haman's ten sons.

ours: For the Jews that were in Shushan gathered themselves together on the fourteenth day also of the month Adar, and slew three hundred men at Shushan; but on the prey they laid not their hand.
theirs: For the Jews that [were] in Shushan gathered themselves together on the fourteenth day also of the month Adar, and slew three hundred men at Shushan; but on the prey they laid not their hand.

ours: But the other Jews that were in the kings provinces gathered themselves together, and stood for their lives, and had rest from their enemies, and slew of their foes seventy and five thousand, but they laid not their hands on the prey,
theirs: But the other Jews that [were] in the king's provinces gathered themselves together, and stood for their lives, and had rest from their enemies, and slew of their foes seventy and five thousand, but they laid not their hands on the prey,

ours: But the Jews that were at Shushan assembled together on the thirteenth day thereof, and on the fourteenth thereof; and on the fifteenth day of the same they rested, and made it a day of feasting and gladness.
theirs: But the Jews that [were] at Shushan assembled together on the thirteenth [day] thereof, and on the fourteenth thereof; and on the fifteenth [day] of the same they rested, and made it a day of feasting and gladness.

ours: Therefore the Jews of the villages, that dwelt in the unwalled towns, made the fourteenth day of the month Adar a day of gladness and feasting, and a good day, and of sending portions one to another.
theirs: Therefore the Jews of the villages, that dwelt in the unwalled towns, made the fourteenth day of the month Adar [a day of] gladness and feasting, and a good day, and of sending portions one to another.

ours: And Mordecai wrote these things, and sent letters unto all the Jews that were in all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus, both nigh and far,
theirs: And Mordecai wrote these things, and sent letters unto all the Jews that [were] in all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus, [both] nigh and far,

ours: To stablish this among them, that they should keep the fourteenth day of the month Adar, and the fifteenth day of the same, yearly,
theirs: To stablish [this] among them, that they should keep the fourteenth day of the month Adar, and the fifteenth day of the same, yearly,

ours: Because Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had devised against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast Pur, that is, the lot, to consume them, and to destroy them;
theirs: Because Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had devised against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast Pur, that [is], the lot, to consume them, and to destroy them;

ours: But when Esther came before the king, he commanded by letters that his wicked device, which he devised against the Jews, should return upon his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.
theirs: But when [Esther] came before the king, he commanded by letters that his wicked device, which he devised against the Jews, should return upon his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.

ours: Wherefore they called these days Purim after the name of Pur. Therefore for all the words of this letter, and of that which they had seen concerning this matter, and which had come unto them,
theirs: Wherefore they called these days Purim after the name of Pur. Therefore for all the words of this letter, and [of that] which they had seen concerning this matter, and which had come unto them,

ours: The Jews ordained, and took upon them, and upon their seed, and upon all such as joined themselves unto them, so as it should not fail, that they would keep these two days according to their writing, and according to their appointed time every year;
theirs: The Jews ordained, and took upon them, and upon their seed, and upon all such as joined themselves unto them, so as it should not fail, that they would keep these two days according to their writing, and according to their [appointed] time every year;

ours: And that these days should be remembered and kept throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city; and that these days of Purim should not fail from among the Jews, nor the memorial of them perish from their seed.
theirs: And [that] these days [should be] remembered and kept throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city; and [that] these days of Purim should not fail from among the Jews, nor the memorial of them perish from their seed.

ours: And he sent the letters unto all the Jews, to the hundred twenty and seven provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, with words of peace and truth,
theirs: And he sent the letters unto all the Jews, to the hundred twenty and seven provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, [with] words of peace and truth,

ours: To confirm these days of Purim in their times appointed, according as Mordecai the Jew and Esther the queen had enjoined them, and as they had decreed for themselves and for their seed, the matters of the fastings and their cry.
theirs: To confirm these days of Purim in their times [appointed], according as Mordecai the Jew and Esther the queen had enjoined them, and as they had decreed for themselves and for their seed, the matters of the fastings and their cry.

ours: AND the king Ahasuerus laid a tribute upon the land, and upon the isles of the sea.
theirs: And the king Ahasuerus laid a tribute upon the land, and [upon] the isles of the sea.

ours: And all the acts of his power and of his might, and the declaration of the greatness of Mordecai, whereunto the king advanced him, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?
theirs: And all the acts of his power and of his might, and the declaration of the greatness of Mordecai, whereunto the king advanced him, [are] they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?

ours: For Mordecai the Jew was next unto king Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the wealth of his people, and speaking peace to all his seed.
theirs: For Mordecai the Jew [was] next unto king Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the wealth of his people, and speaking peace to all his seed.

ours: THERE was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job; and that man was perfect and upright, and one that feared God, and eschewed evil.
theirs: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name [was] Job; and that man was perfect and upright, and one that feared God, and eschewed evil.

ours: And his sons went and feasted in their houses, every one his day; and sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.
theirs: And his sons went and feasted [in their] houses, every one his day; and sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.

ours: And it was so, when the days of their feasting were gone about, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all: for Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually.
theirs: And it was so, when the days of [their] feasting were gone about, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings [according] to the number of them all: for Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually.

ours: And the LORD said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil?
theirs: And the LORD said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that [there is] none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil?

ours: And the LORD said unto Satan, Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand. So Satan went forth from the presence of the LORD.
theirs: And the LORD said unto Satan, Behold, all that he hath [is] in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand. So Satan went forth from the presence of the LORD.

ours: And there was a day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brothers house:
theirs: And there was a day when his sons and his daughters [were] eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house:

ours: And the Sabeans fell upon them, and took them away; yea, they have slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.
theirs: And the Sabeans fell [upon them], and took them away; yea, they have slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.

ours: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The fire of God is fallen from heaven, and hath burned up the sheep, and the servants, and consumed them; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.
theirs: While he [was] yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The fire of God is fallen from heaven, and hath burned up the sheep, and the servants, and consumed them; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.

ours: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The Chaldeans made out three bands, and fell upon the camels, and have carried them away, yea, and slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.
theirs: While he [was] yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The Chaldeans made out three bands, and fell upon the camels, and have carried them away, yea, and slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.

ours: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, Thy sons and thy daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brothers house:
theirs: While he [was] yet speaking, there came also another, and said, Thy sons and thy daughters [were] eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house:

ours: And said, Naked came I out of my mothers womb, and naked shall I return thither: the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD.
theirs: And said, Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither: the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD.

ours: And the LORD said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil? and still he holdeth fast his integrity, although thou movedst me against him, to destroy him without cause.
theirs: And the LORD said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that [there is] none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil? and still he holdeth fast his integrity, although thou movedst me against him, to destroy him without cause.

ours: And the LORD said unto Satan, Behold, he is in thine hand; but save his life.
theirs: And the LORD said unto Satan, Behold, he [is] in thine hand; but save his life.

ours: Now when Jobs three friends heard of all this evil that was come upon him, they came every one from his own place; Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite: for they had made an appointment together to come to mourn with him and to comfort him.
theirs: Now when Job's three friends heard of all this evil that was come upon him, they came every one from his own place; Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite: for they had made an appointment together to come to mourn with him and to comfort him.

ours: So they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great.
theirs: So they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that [his] grief was very great.

ours: Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said, There is a man child conceived.
theirs: Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night [in which] it was said, There is a man child conceived.

ours: As for that night, let darkness seize upon it; let it not be joined unto the days of the year, let it not come into the number of the months.
theirs: [As for] that night, let darkness seize upon it; let it not be joined unto the days of the year, let it not come into the number of the months.

ours: Let the stars of the twilight thereof be dark; let it look for light, but have none; neither let it see the dawning of the day:
theirs: Let the stars of the twilight thereof be dark; let it look for light, but [have] none; neither let it see the dawning of the day:

ours: Because it shut not up the doors of my mothers womb, nor hid sorrow from mine eyes.
theirs: Because it shut not up the doors of my [mother's] womb, nor hid sorrow from mine eyes.

ours: Why died I not from the womb? why did I not give up the ghost when I came out of the belly?
theirs: Why died I not from the womb? [why] did I [not] give up the ghost when I came out of the belly?

ours: Or as an hidden untimely birth I had not been; as infants which never saw light.
theirs: Or as an hidden untimely birth I had not been; as infants [which] never saw light.

ours: There the wicked cease from troubling; and there the weary be at rest.
theirs: There the wicked cease [from] troubling; and there the weary be at rest.

ours: There the prisoners rest together; they hear not the voice of the oppressor.
theirs: [There] the prisoners rest together; they hear not the voice of the oppressor.

ours: The small and great are there; and the servant is free from his master.
theirs: The small and great are there; and the servant [is] free from his master.

ours: Wherefore is light given to him that is in misery, and life unto the bitter in soul;
theirs: Wherefore is light given to him that is in misery, and life unto the bitter [in] soul;

ours: Which long for death, but it cometh not; and dig for it more than for hid treasures;
theirs: Which long for death, but it [cometh] not; and dig for it more than for hid treasures;

ours: Which rejoice exceedingly, and are glad, when they can find the grave?
theirs: Which rejoice exceedingly, [and] are glad, when they can find the grave?

ours: Why is light given to a man whose way is hid, and whom God hath hedged in?
theirs: [Why is light given] to a man whose way is hid, and whom God hath hedged in?

ours: If we assay to commune with thee, wilt thou be grieved? but who can withhold himself from speaking?
theirs: [If] we assay to commune with thee, wilt thou be grieved? but who can withhold himself from speaking?

ours: Is not this thy fear, thy confidence, thy hope, and the uprightness of thy ways?
theirs: [Is] not [this] thy fear, thy confidence, thy hope, and the uprightness of thy ways?

ours: Remember, I pray thee, who ever perished, being innocent? or where were the righteous cut off?
theirs: Remember, I pray thee, who [ever] perished, being innocent? or where were the righteous cut off?

ours: The old lion perisheth for lack of prey, and the stout lions whelps are scattered abroad.
theirs: The old lion perisheth for lack of prey, and the stout lion's whelps are scattered abroad.

ours: It stood still, but I could not discern the form thereof: an image was before mine eyes, there was silence, and I heard a voice, saying,
theirs: It stood still, but I could not discern the form thereof: an image [was] before mine eyes, [there was] silence, and I heard a voice, [saying],

ours: How much less in them that dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, which are crushed before the moth?
theirs: How much less [in] them that dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation [is] in the dust, [which] are crushed before the moth?

ours: They are destroyed from morning to evening: they perish for ever without any regarding it.
theirs: They are destroyed from morning to evening: they perish for ever without any regarding [it].

ours: Doth not their excellency which is in them go away? they die, even without wisdom.
theirs: Doth not their excellency [which is] in them go away? they die, even without wisdom.

ours: His children are far from safety, and they are crushed in the gate, neither is there any to deliver them.
theirs: His children are far from safety, and they are crushed in the gate, neither [is there] any to deliver [them].

ours: He disappointeth the devices of the crafty, so that their hands cannot perform their enterprise.
theirs: He disappointeth the devices of the crafty, so that their hands cannot perform [their] enterprise.

ours: Behold, happy is the man whom God correcteth: therefore despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty:
theirs: Behold, happy [is] the man whom God correcteth: therefore despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty:

ours: And thou shalt know that thy tabernacle shall be in peace; and thou shalt visit thy habitation, and shalt not sin.
theirs: And thou shalt know that thy tabernacle [shall be] in peace; and thou shalt visit thy habitation, and shalt not sin.

ours: Thou shalt know also that thy seed shall be great, and thine offspring as the grass of the earth.
theirs: Thou shalt know also that thy seed [shall be] great, and thine offspring as the grass of the earth.

ours: Thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age, like as a shock of corn cometh in in his season.
theirs: Thou shalt come to [thy] grave in a full age, like as a shock of corn cometh in in his season.

ours: Lo this, we have searched it, so it is; hear it, and know thou it for thy good.
theirs: Lo this, we have searched it, so it [is]; hear it, and know thou [it] for thy good.

ours: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me, the poison whereof drinketh up my spirit: the terrors of God do set themselves in array against me.
theirs: For the arrows of the Almighty [are] within me, the poison whereof drinketh up my spirit: the terrors of God do set themselves in array against me.

ours: Can that which is unsavoury be eaten without salt? or is there any taste in the white of an egg?
theirs: Can that which is unsavoury be eaten without salt? or is there [any] taste in the white of an egg?

ours: The things that my soul refused to touch are as my sorrowful meat.
theirs: The things [that] my soul refused to touch [are] as my sorrowful meat.

ours: Oh that I might have my request; and that God would grant me the thing that I long for!
theirs: Oh that I might have my request; and that God would grant [me] the thing that I long for!

ours: What is my strength, that I should hope? and what is mine end, that I should prolong my life?
theirs: What [is] my strength, that I should hope? and what [is] mine end, that I should prolong my life?

ours: Is my strength the strength of stones? or is my flesh of brass?
theirs: [Is] my strength the strength of stones? or [is] my flesh of brass?

ours: Is not my help in me? and is wisdom driven quite from me?
theirs: [Is] not my help in me? and is wisdom driven quite from me?

ours: To him that is afflicted pity should be shewed from his friend; but he forsaketh the fear of the Almighty.
theirs: To him that is afflicted pity [should be shewed] from his friend; but he forsaketh the fear of the Almighty.

ours: My brethren have dealt deceitfully as a brook, and as the stream of brooks they pass away;
theirs: My brethren have dealt deceitfully as a brook, [and] as the stream of brooks they pass away;

ours: Which are blackish by reason of the ice, and wherein the snow is hid:
theirs: Which are blackish by reason of the ice, [and] wherein the snow is hid:

ours: For now ye are nothing; ye see my casting down, and are afraid.
theirs: For now ye are nothing; ye see [my] casting down, and are afraid.

ours: Or, Deliver me from the enemys hand? or, Redeem me from the hand of the mighty?
theirs: Or, Deliver me from the enemy's hand? or, Redeem me from the hand of the mighty?

ours: Do ye imagine to reprove words, and the speeches of one that is desperate, which are as wind?
theirs: Do ye imagine to reprove words, and the speeches of one that is desperate, [which are] as wind?

ours: Yea, ye overwhelm the fatherless, and ye dig a pit for your friend.
theirs: Yea, ye overwhelm the fatherless, and ye dig [a pit] for your friend.

ours: Now therefore be content, look upon me; for it is evident unto you if I lie.
theirs: Now therefore be content, look upon me; for [it is] evident unto you if I lie.

ours: Return, I pray you, let it not be iniquity; yea, return again, my righteousness is in it.
theirs: Return, I pray you, let it not be iniquity; yea, return again, my righteousness [is] in it.

ours: IS there not an appointed time to man upon earth? are not his days also like the days of an hireling?
theirs: [Is there] not an appointed time to man upon earth? [are not] his days also like the days of an hireling?

ours: As a servant earnestly desireth the shadow, and as an hireling looketh for the reward of his work:
theirs: As a servant earnestly desireth the shadow, and as an hireling looketh for [the reward of] his work:

ours: My days are swifter than a weavers shuttle, and are spent without hope.
theirs: My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, and are spent without hope.

ours: O remember that my life is wind: mine eye shall no more see good.
theirs: O remember that my life [is] wind: mine eye shall no more see good.

ours: The eye of him that hath seen me shall see me no more: thine eyes are upon me, and I am not.
theirs: The eye of him that hath seen me shall see me no [more]: thine eyes [are] upon me, and I [am] not.

ours: As the cloud is consumed and vanisheth away: so he that goeth down to the grave shall come up no more.
theirs: [As] the cloud is consumed and vanisheth away: so he that goeth down to the grave shall come up no [more].

ours: Am I a sea, or a whale, that thou settest a watch over me?
theirs: [Am] I a sea, or a whale, that thou settest a watch over me?

ours: So that my soul chooseth strangling, and death rather than my life.
theirs: So that my soul chooseth strangling, [and] death rather than my life.

ours: I loathe it; I would not live alway: let me alone; for my days are vanity.
theirs: I loathe [it]; I would not live alway: let me alone; for my days [are] vanity.

ours: What is man, that thou shouldest magnify him? and that thou shouldest set thine heart upon him?
theirs: What [is] man, that thou shouldest magnify him? and that thou shouldest set thine heart upon him?

ours: And that thou shouldest visit him every morning, and try him every moment?
theirs: And [that] thou shouldest visit him every morning, [and] try him every moment?

ours: And why dost thou not pardon my transgression, and take away mine iniquity? for now shall I sleep in the dust; and thou shalt seek me in the morning, but I shall not be.
theirs: And why dost thou not pardon my transgression, and take away mine iniquity? for now shall I sleep in the dust; and thou shalt seek me in the morning, but I [shall] not [be].

ours: How long wilt thou speak these things? and how long shall the words of thy mouth be like a strong wind?
theirs: How long wilt thou speak these [things]? and [how long shall] the words of thy mouth [be like] a strong wind?

ours: If thou wert pure and upright; surely now he would awake for thee, and make the habitation of thy righteousness prosperous.
theirs: If thou [wert] pure and upright; surely now he would awake for thee, and make the habitation of thy righteousness prosperous.

ours: (For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days upon earth are a shadow:)
theirs: (For we [are but of] yesterday, and know nothing, because our days upon earth [are] a shadow:)

ours: Shall not they teach thee, and tell thee, and utter words out of their heart?
theirs: Shall not they teach thee, [and] tell thee, and utter words out of their heart?

ours: Whilst it is yet in his greenness, and not cut down, it withereth before any other herb.
theirs: Whilst it [is] yet in his greenness, [and] not cut down, it withereth before any [other] herb.

ours: So are the paths of all that forget God; and the hypocrites hope shall perish:
theirs: So [are] the paths of all that forget God; and the hypocrite's hope shall perish:

ours: Whose hope shall be cut off, and whose trust shall be a spiders web.
theirs: Whose hope shall be cut off, and whose trust [shall be] a spider's web.

ours: He is green before the sun, and his branch shooteth forth in his garden.
theirs: He [is] green before the sun, and his branch shooteth forth in his garden.

ours: His roots are wrapped about the heap, and seeth the place of stones.
theirs: His roots are wrapped about the heap, [and] seeth the place of stones.

ours: If he destroy him from his place, then it shall deny him, saying, I have not seen thee.
theirs: If he destroy him from his place, then [it] shall deny him, [saying], I have not seen thee.

ours: Behold, this is the joy of his way, and out of the earth shall others grow.
theirs: Behold, this [is] the joy of his way, and out of the earth shall others grow.

ours: Behold, God will not cast away a perfect man, neither will he help the evil doers:
theirs: Behold, God will not cast away a perfect [man], neither will he help the evil doers:

ours: I know it is so of a truth: but how should man be just with God?
theirs: I know [it is] so of a truth: but how should man be just with God?

ours: He is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who hath hardened himself against him, and hath prospered?
theirs: [He is] wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who hath hardened [himself] against him, and hath prospered?

ours: Lo, he goeth by me, and I see him not: he passeth on also, but I perceive him not.
theirs: Lo, he goeth by me, and I see [him] not: he passeth on also, but I perceive him not.

ours: If God will not withdraw his anger, the proud helpers do stoop under him.
theirs: [If] God will not withdraw his anger, the proud helpers do stoop under him.

ours: How much less shall I answer him, and choose out my words to reason with him?
theirs: How much less shall I answer him, [and] choose out my words [to reason] with him?

ours: Whom, though I were righteous, yet would I not answer, but I would make supplication to my judge.
theirs: Whom, though I were righteous, [yet] would I not answer, [but] I would make supplication to my judge.

ours: If I had called, and he had answered me; yet would I not believe that he had hearkened unto my voice.
theirs: If I had called, and he had answered me; [yet] would I not believe that he had hearkened unto my voice.

ours: If I speak of strength, lo, he is strong: and if of judgment, who shall set me a time to plead?
theirs: If [I speak] of strength, lo, [he is] strong: and if of judgment, who shall set me a time [to plead]?

ours: If I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me: if I say, I am perfect, it shall also prove me perverse.
theirs: If I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me: [if I say], I [am] perfect, it shall also prove me perverse.

ours: Though I were perfect, yet would I not know my soul: I would despise my life.
theirs: [Though] I [were] perfect, [yet] would I not know my soul: I would despise my life.

ours: This is one thing, therefore I said it, He destroyeth the perfect and the wicked.
theirs: This [is] one [thing], therefore I said [it], He destroyeth the perfect and the wicked.

ours: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof; if not, where, and who is he?
theirs: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof; if not, where, [and] who [is] he?

ours: They are passed away as the swift ships: as the eagle that hasteth to the prey.
theirs: They are passed away as the swift ships: as the eagle [that] hasteth to the prey.

ours: If I say, I will forget my complaint, I will leave off my heaviness, and comfort myself:
theirs: If I say, I will forget my complaint, I will leave off my heaviness, and comfort [myself]:

ours: If I be wicked, why then labour I in vain?
theirs: [If] I be wicked, why then labour I in vain?

ours: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, and we should come together in judgment.
theirs: For [he is] not a man, as I [am, that] I should answer him, [and] we should come together in judgment.

ours: Neither is there any daysman betwixt us, that might lay his hand upon us both.
theirs: Neither is there any daysman betwixt us, [that] might lay his hand upon us both.

ours: Then would I speak, and not fear him; but it is not so with me.
theirs: [Then] would I speak, and not fear him; but [it is] not so with me.

ours: Is it good unto thee that thou shouldest oppress, that thou shouldest despise the work of thine hands, and shine upon the counsel of the wicked?
theirs: [Is it] good unto thee that thou shouldest oppress, that thou shouldest despise the work of thine hands, and shine upon the counsel of the wicked?

ours: Are thy days as the days of man? are thy years as mans days,
theirs: [Are] thy days as the days of man? [are] thy years as man's days,

ours: Thou knowest that I am not wicked; and there is none that can deliver out of thine hand.
theirs: Thou knowest that I am not wicked; and [there is] none that can deliver out of thine hand.

ours: And these things hast thou hid in thine heart: I know that this is with thee.
theirs: And these [things] hast thou hid in thine heart: I know that this [is] with thee.

ours: If I be wicked, woe unto me; and if I be righteous, yet will I not lift up my head. I am full of confusion; therefore see thou mine affliction;
theirs: If I be wicked, woe unto me; and [if] I be righteous, [yet] will I not lift up my head. [I am] full of confusion; therefore see thou mine affliction;

ours: Thou renewest thy witnesses against me, and increasest thine indignation upon me; changes and war are against me.
theirs: Thou renewest thy witnesses against me, and increasest thine indignation upon me; changes and war [are] against me.

ours: Are not my days few? cease then, and let me alone, that I may take comfort a little,
theirs: [Are] not my days few? cease [then, and] let me alone, that I may take comfort a little,

ours: Before I go whence I shall not return, even to the land of darkness and the shadow of death;
theirs: Before I go [whence] I shall not return, [even] to the land of darkness and the shadow of death;

ours: A land of darkness, as darkness itself; and of the shadow of death, without any order, and where the light is as darkness.
theirs: A land of darkness, as darkness [itself; and] of the shadow of death, without any order, and [where] the light [is] as darkness.

ours: For thou hast said, My doctrine is pure, and I am clean in thine eyes.
theirs: For thou hast said, My doctrine [is] pure, and I am clean in thine eyes.

ours: And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is! Know therefore that God exacteth of thee less than thine iniquity deserveth.
theirs: And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that [they are] double to that which is! Know therefore that God exacteth of thee [less] than thine iniquity [deserveth].

ours: It is as high as heaven; what canst thou do? deeper than hell; what canst thou know?
theirs: [It is] as high as heaven; what canst thou do? deeper than hell; what canst thou know?

ours: The measure thereof is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.
theirs: The measure thereof [is] longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.

ours: For he knoweth vain men: he seeth wickedness also; will he not then consider it?
theirs: For he knoweth vain men: he seeth wickedness also; will he not then consider [it]?

ours: For vain man would be wise, though man be born like a wild asss colt.
theirs: For vain man would be wise, though man be born [like] a wild ass's colt.

ours: If iniquity be in thine hand, put it far away, and let not wickedness dwell in thy tabernacles.
theirs: If iniquity [be] in thine hand, put it far away, and let not wickedness dwell in thy tabernacles.

ours: Because thou shalt forget thy misery, and remember it as waters that pass away:
theirs: Because thou shalt forget [thy] misery, [and] remember [it] as waters [that] pass away:

ours: And thine age shall be clearer than the noonday; thou shalt shine forth, thou shalt be as the morning.
theirs: And [thine] age shall be clearer than the noonday; thou shalt shine forth, thou shalt be as the morning.

ours: And thou shalt be secure, because there is hope; yea, thou shalt dig about thee, and thou shalt take thy rest in safety.
theirs: And thou shalt be secure, because there is hope; yea, thou shalt dig [about thee, and] thou shalt take thy rest in safety.

ours: Also thou shalt lie down, and none shall make thee afraid; yea, many shall make suit unto thee.
theirs: Also thou shalt lie down, and none shall make [thee] afraid; yea, many shall make suit unto thee.

ours: But the eyes of the wicked shall fail, and they shall not escape, and their hope shall be as the giving up of the ghost.
theirs: But the eyes of the wicked shall fail, and they shall not escape, and their hope [shall be as] the giving up of the ghost.

ours: No doubt but ye are the people, and wisdom shall die with you.
theirs: No doubt but ye [are] the people, and wisdom shall die with you.

ours: But I have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you: yea, who knoweth not such things as these?
theirs: But I have understanding as well as you; I [am] not inferior to you: yea, who knoweth not such things as these?

ours: I am as one mocked of his neighbour, who calleth upon God, and he answereth him: the just upright man is laughed to scorn.
theirs: I am [as] one mocked of his neighbour, who calleth upon God, and he answereth him: the just upright [man is] laughed to scorn.

ours: He that is ready to slip with his feet is as a lamp despised in the thought of him that is at ease.
theirs: He that is ready to slip with [his] feet [is as] a lamp despised in the thought of him that is at ease.

ours: The tabernacles of robbers prosper, and they that provoke God are secure; into whose hand God bringeth abundantly.
theirs: The tabernacles of robbers prosper, and they that provoke God are secure; into whose hand God bringeth [abundantly].

ours: In whose hand is the soul of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind.
theirs: In whose hand [is] the soul of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind.

ours: With the ancient is wisdom; and in length of days understanding.
theirs: With the ancient [is] wisdom; and in length of days understanding.

ours: With him is wisdom and strength, he hath counsel and understanding.
theirs: With him [is] wisdom and strength, he hath counsel and understanding.

ours: With him is strength and wisdom: the deceived and the deceiver are his.
theirs: With him [is] strength and wisdom: the deceived and the deceiver [are] his.

ours: He increaseth the nations, and destroyeth them: he enlargeth the nations, and straiteneth them again.
theirs: He increaseth the nations, and destroyeth them: he enlargeth the nations, and straiteneth them [again].

ours: He taketh away the heart of the chief of the people of the earth, and causeth them to wander in a wilderness where there is no way.
theirs: He taketh away the heart of the chief of the people of the earth, and causeth them to wander in a wilderness [where there is] no way.

ours: They grope in the dark without light, and he maketh them to stagger like a drunken man.
theirs: They grope in the dark without light, and he maketh them to stagger like [a] drunken [man].

ours: LO, mine eye hath seen all this, mine ear hath heard and understood it.
theirs: Lo, mine eye hath seen all [this], mine ear hath heard and understood it.

ours: What ye know, the same do I know also: I am not inferior unto you.
theirs: What ye know, [the same] do I know also: I [am] not inferior unto you.

ours: But ye are forgers of lies, ye are all physicians of no value.
theirs: But ye [are] forgers of lies, ye [are] all physicians of no value.

ours: Is it good that he should search you out? or as one man mocketh another, do ye so mock him?
theirs: Is it good that he should search you out? or as one man mocketh another, do ye [so] mock him?

ours: Your remembrances are like unto ashes, your bodies to bodies of clay.
theirs: Your remembrances [are] like unto ashes, your bodies to bodies of clay.

ours: Hold your peace, let me alone, that I may speak, and let come on me what will.
theirs: Hold your peace, let me alone, that I may speak, and let come on me what [will].

ours: He also shall be my salvation: for an hypocrite shall not come before him.
theirs: He also [shall be] my salvation: for an hypocrite shall not come before him.

ours: Behold now, I have ordered my cause; I know that I shall be justified.
theirs: Behold now, I have ordered [my] cause; I know that I shall be justified.

ours: Who is he that will plead with me? for now, if I hold my tongue, I shall give up the ghost.
theirs: Who [is] he [that] will plead with me? for now, if I hold my tongue, I shall give up the ghost.

ours: Only do not two things unto me: then will I not hide myself from thee.
theirs: Only do not two [things] unto me: then will I not hide myself from thee.

ours: How many are mine iniquities and sins? make me to know my transgression and my sin.
theirs: How many [are] mine iniquities and sins? make me to know my transgression and my sin.

ours: MAN that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble.
theirs: Man [that is] born of a woman [is] of few days, and full of trouble.

ours: Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? not one.
theirs: Who can bring a clean [thing] out of an unclean? not one.

ours: Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months are with thee, thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass;
theirs: Seeing his days [are] determined, the number of his months [are] with thee, thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass;

ours: Yet through the scent of water it will bud, and bring forth boughs like a plant.
theirs: [Yet] through the scent of water it will bud, and bring forth boughs like a plant.

ours: But man dieth, and wasteth away: yea, man giveth up the ghost, and where is he?
theirs: But man dieth, and wasteth away: yea, man giveth up the ghost, and where [is] he?

ours: As the waters fail from the sea, and the flood decayeth and drieth up:
theirs: [As] the waters fail from the sea, and the flood decayeth and drieth up:

ours: So man lieth down, and riseth not: till the heavens be no more, they shall not awake, nor be raised out of their sleep.
theirs: So man lieth down, and riseth not: till the heavens [be] no more, they shall not awake, nor be raised out of their sleep.

ours: If a man die, shall he live again? all the days of my appointed time will I wait, till my change come.
theirs: If a man die, shall he live [again]? all the days of my appointed time will I wait, till my change come.

ours: My transgression is sealed up in a bag, and thou sewest up mine iniquity.
theirs: My transgression [is] sealed up in a bag, and thou sewest up mine iniquity.

ours: The waters wear the stones: thou washest away the things which grow out of the dust of the earth; and thou destroyest the hope of man.
theirs: The waters wear the stones: thou washest away the things which grow [out] of the dust of the earth; and thou destroyest the hope of man.

ours: His sons come to honour, and he knoweth it not; and they are brought low, but he perceiveth it not of them.
theirs: His sons come to honour, and he knoweth [it] not; and they are brought low, but he perceiveth [it] not of them.

ours: Art thou the first man that was born? or wast thou made before the hills?
theirs: [Art] thou the first man [that] was born? or wast thou made before the hills?

ours: What knowest thou, that we know not? what understandest thou, which is not in us?
theirs: What knowest thou, that we know not? [what] understandest thou, which [is] not in us?

ours: With us are both the grayheaded and very aged men, much elder than thy father.
theirs: With us [are] both the grayheaded and very aged men, much elder than thy father.

ours: Are the consolations of God small with thee? is there any secret thing with thee?
theirs: [Are] the consolations of God small with thee? is there any secret thing with thee?

ours: That thou turnest thy spirit against God, and lettest such words go out of thy mouth?
theirs: That thou turnest thy spirit against God, and lettest [such] words go out of thy mouth?

ours: What is man, that he should be clean? and he which is born of a woman, that he should be righteous?
theirs: What [is] man, that he should be clean? and [he which is] born of a woman, that he should be righteous?

ours: How much more abominable and filthy is man, which drinketh iniquity like water?
theirs: How much more abominable and filthy [is] man, which drinketh iniquity like water?

ours: I will shew thee, hear me; and that which I have seen I will declare;
theirs: I will shew thee, hear me; and that [which] I have seen I will declare;

ours: Which wise men have told from their fathers, and have not hid it:
theirs: Which wise men have told from their fathers, and have not hid [it]:

ours: The wicked man travaileth with pain all his days, and the number of years is hidden to the oppressor.
theirs: The wicked man travaileth with pain all [his] days, and the number of years is hidden to the oppressor.

ours: A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him.
theirs: A dreadful sound [is] in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him.

ours: He wandereth abroad for bread, saying, Where is it? he knoweth that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.
theirs: He wandereth abroad for bread, [saying], Where [is it]? he knoweth that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.

ours: He runneth upon him, even on his neck, upon the thick bosses of his bucklers:
theirs: He runneth upon him, [even] on [his] neck, upon the thick bosses of his bucklers:

ours: Because he covereth his face with his fatness, and maketh collops of fat on his flanks.
theirs: Because he covereth his face with his fatness, and maketh collops of fat on [his] flanks.

ours: And he dwelleth in desolate cities, and in houses which no man inhabiteth, which are ready to become heaps.
theirs: And he dwelleth in desolate cities, [and] in houses which no man inhabiteth, which are ready to become heaps.

ours: For the congregation of hypocrites shall be desolate, and fire shall consume the tabernacles of bribery.
theirs: For the congregation of hypocrites [shall be] desolate, and fire shall consume the tabernacles of bribery.

ours: I have heard many such things: miserable comforters are ye all.
theirs: I have heard many such things: miserable comforters [are] ye all.

ours: I also could speak as ye do: if your soul were in my souls stead, I could heap up words against you, and shake mine head at you.
theirs: I also could speak as ye [do]: if your soul were in my soul's stead, I could heap up words against you, and shake mine head at you.

ours: But I would strengthen you with my mouth, and the moving of my lips should asswage your grief.
theirs: [But] I would strengthen you with my mouth, and the moving of my lips should asswage [your grief].

ours: Though I speak, my grief is not asswaged: and though I forbear, what am I eased?
theirs: Though I speak, my grief is not asswaged: and [though] I forbear, what am I eased?

ours: And thou hast filled me with wrinkles, which is a witness against me: and my leanness rising up in me beareth witness to my face.
theirs: And thou hast filled me with wrinkles, [which] is a witness [against me]: and my leanness rising up in me beareth witness to my face.

ours: He teareth me in his wrath, who hateth me: he gnasheth upon me with his teeth; mine enemy sharpeneth his eyes upon me.
theirs: He teareth [me] in his wrath, who hateth me: he gnasheth upon me with his teeth; mine enemy sharpeneth his eyes upon me.

ours: I was at ease, but he hath broken me asunder: he hath also taken me by my neck, and shaken me to pieces, and set me up for his mark.
theirs: I was at ease, but he hath broken me asunder: he hath also taken [me] by my neck, and shaken me to pieces, and set me up for his mark.

ours: My face is foul with weeping, and on my eyelids is the shadow of death;
theirs: My face is foul with weeping, and on my eyelids [is] the shadow of death;

ours: Not for any injustice in mine hands: also my prayer is pure.
theirs: Not for [any] injustice in mine hands: also my prayer [is] pure.

ours: Also now, behold, my witness is in heaven, and my record is on high.
theirs: Also now, behold, my witness [is] in heaven, and my record [is] on high.

ours: My friends scorn me: but mine eye poureth out tears unto God.
theirs: My friends scorn me: [but] mine eye poureth out [tears] unto God.

ours: O that one might plead for a man with God, as a man pleadeth for his neighbour!
theirs: O that one might plead for a man with God, as a man [pleadeth] for his neighbour!

ours: When a few years are come, then I shall go the way whence I shall not return.
theirs: When a few years are come, then I shall go the way [whence] I shall not return.

ours: MY breath is corrupt, my days are extinct, the graves are ready for me.
theirs: My breath is corrupt, my days are extinct, the graves [are ready] for me.

ours: Are there not mockers with me? and doth not mine eye continue in their provocation?
theirs: [Are there] not mockers with me? and doth not mine eye continue in their provocation?

ours: Lay down now, put me in a surety with thee; who is he that will strike hands with me?
theirs: Lay down now, put me in a surety with thee; who [is] he [that] will strike hands with me?

ours: For thou hast hid their heart from understanding: therefore shalt thou not exalt them.
theirs: For thou hast hid their heart from understanding: therefore shalt thou not exalt [them].

ours: He that speaketh flattery to his friends, even the eyes of his children shall fail.
theirs: He that speaketh flattery to [his] friends, even the eyes of his children shall fail.

ours: Mine eye also is dim by reason of sorrow, and all my members are as a shadow.
theirs: Mine eye also is dim by reason of sorrow, and all my members [are] as a shadow.

ours: Upright men shall be astonied at this, and the innocent shall stir up himself against the hypocrite.
theirs: Upright [men] shall be astonied at this, and the innocent shall stir up himself against the hypocrite.

ours: But as for you all, do ye return, and come now: for I cannot find one wise man among you.
theirs: But as for you all, do ye return, and come now: for I cannot find [one] wise [man] among you.

ours: My days are past, my purposes are broken off, even the thoughts of my heart.
theirs: My days are past, my purposes are broken off, [even] the thoughts of my heart.

ours: They change the night into day: the light is short because of darkness.
theirs: They change the night into day: the light [is] short because of darkness.

ours: If I wait, the grave is mine house: I have made my bed in the darkness.
theirs: If I wait, the grave [is] mine house: I have made my bed in the darkness.

ours: I have said to corruption, Thou art my father: to the worm, Thou art my mother, and my sister.
theirs: I have said to corruption, Thou [art] my father: to the worm, [Thou art] my mother, and my sister.

ours: And where is now my hope? as for my hope, who shall see it?
theirs: And where [is] now my hope? as for my hope, who shall see it?

ours: They shall go down to the bars of the pit, when our rest together is in the dust.
theirs: They shall go down to the bars of the pit, when [our] rest together [is] in the dust.

ours: How long will it be ere ye make an end of words? mark, and afterwards we will speak.
theirs: How long [will it be ere] ye make an end of words? mark, and afterwards we will speak.

ours: Wherefore are we counted as beasts, and reputed vile in your sight?
theirs: Wherefore are we counted as beasts, [and] reputed vile in your sight?

ours: The gin shall take him by the heel, and the robber shall prevail against him.
theirs: The gin shall take [him] by the heel, [and] the robber shall prevail against him.

ours: The snare is laid for him in the ground, and a trap for him in the way.
theirs: The snare [is] laid for him in the ground, and a trap for him in the way.

ours: His strength shall be hungerbitten, and destruction shall be ready at his side.
theirs: His strength shall be hungerbitten, and destruction [shall be] ready at his side.

ours: It shall devour the strength of his skin: even the firstborn of death shall devour his strength.
theirs: It shall devour the strength of his skin: [even] the firstborn of death shall devour his strength.

ours: It shall dwell in his tabernacle, because it is none of his: brimstone shall be scattered upon his habitation.
theirs: It shall dwell in his tabernacle, because [it is] none of his: brimstone shall be scattered upon his habitation.

ours: They that come after him shall be astonied at his day, as they that went before were affrighted.
theirs: They that come after [him] shall be astonied at his day, as they that went before were affrighted.

ours: Surely such are the dwellings of the wicked, and this is the place of him that knoweth not God.
theirs: Surely such [are] the dwellings of the wicked, and this [is] the place [of him that] knoweth not God.

ours: These ten times have ye reproached me: ye are not ashamed that ye make yourselves strange to me.
theirs: These ten times have ye reproached me: ye are not ashamed [that] ye make yourselves strange to me.

ours: And be it indeed that I have erred, mine error remaineth with myself.
theirs: And be it indeed [that] I have erred, mine error remaineth with myself.

ours: If indeed ye will magnify yourselves against me, and plead against me my reproach:
theirs: If indeed ye will magnify [yourselves] against me, and plead against me my reproach:

ours: Behold, I cry out of wrong, but I am not heard: I cry aloud, but there is no judgment.
theirs: Behold, I cry out of wrong, but I am not heard: I cry aloud, but [there is] no judgment.

ours: He hath stripped me of my glory, and taken the crown from my head.
theirs: He hath stripped me of my glory, and taken the crown [from] my head.

ours: He hath also kindled his wrath against me, and he counteth me unto him as one of his enemies.
theirs: He hath also kindled his wrath against me, and he counteth me unto him as [one of] his enemies.

ours: I called my servant, and he gave me no answer; I intreated him with my mouth.
theirs: I called my servant, and he gave [me] no answer; I intreated him with my mouth.

ours: My breath is strange to my wife, though I intreated for the childrens sake of mine own body.
theirs: My breath is strange to my wife, though I intreated for the children's [sake] of mine own body.

ours: For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth:
theirs: For I know [that] my redeemer liveth, and [that] he shall stand at the latter [day] upon the earth:

ours: And though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God:
theirs: And [though] after my skin [worms] destroy this [body], yet in my flesh shall I see God:

ours: Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another; though my reins be consumed within me.
theirs: Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another; [though] my reins be consumed within me.

ours: Be ye afraid of the sword: for wrath bringeth the punishments of the sword, that ye may know there is a judgment.
theirs: Be ye afraid of the sword: for wrath [bringeth] the punishments of the sword, that ye may know [there is] a judgment.

ours: Therefore do my thoughts cause me to answer, and for this I make haste.
theirs: Therefore do my thoughts cause me to answer, and for [this] I make haste.

ours: Knowest thou not this of old, since man was placed upon earth,
theirs: Knowest thou [not] this of old, since man was placed upon earth,

ours: That the triumphing of the wicked is short, and the joy of the hypocrite but for a moment?
theirs: That the triumphing of the wicked [is] short, and the joy of the hypocrite [but] for a moment?

ours: Yet he shall perish for ever like his own dung: they which have seen him shall say, Where is he?
theirs: [Yet] he shall perish for ever like his own dung: they which have seen him shall say, Where [is] he?

ours: The eye also which saw him shall see him no more; neither shall his place any more behold him.
theirs: The eye also [which] saw him shall [see him] no more; neither shall his place any more behold him.

ours: His bones are full of the sin of his youth, which shall lie down with him in the dust.
theirs: His bones are full [of the sin] of his youth, which shall lie down with him in the dust.

ours: Though wickedness be sweet in his mouth, though he hide it under his tongue;
theirs: Though wickedness be sweet in his mouth, [though] he hide it under his tongue;

ours: Though he spare it, and forsake it not; but keep it still within his mouth:
theirs: [Though] he spare it, and forsake it not; but keep it still within his mouth:

ours: Yet his meat in his bowels is turned, it is the gall of asps within him.
theirs: [Yet] his meat in his bowels is turned, [it is] the gall of asps within him.

ours: He shall suck the poison of asps: the vipers tongue shall slay him.
theirs: He shall suck the poison of asps: the viper's tongue shall slay him.

ours: That which he laboured for shall he restore, and shall not swallow it down: according to his substance shall the restitution be, and he shall not rejoice therein.
theirs: That which he laboured for shall he restore, and shall not swallow [it] down: according to [his] substance [shall] the restitution [be], and he shall not rejoice [therein].

ours: Because he hath oppressed and hath forsaken the poor; because he hath violently taken away an house which he builded not;
theirs: Because he hath oppressed [and] hath forsaken the poor; [because] he hath violently taken away an house which he builded not;

ours: When he is about to fill his belly, God shall cast the fury of his wrath upon him, and shall rain it upon him while he is eating.
theirs: [When] he is about to fill his belly, [God] shall cast the fury of his wrath upon him, and shall rain [it] upon him while he is eating.

ours: He shall flee from the iron weapon, and the bow of steel shall strike him through.
theirs: He shall flee from the iron weapon, [and] the bow of steel shall strike him through.

ours: It is drawn, and cometh out of the body; yea, the glittering sword cometh out of his gall: terrors are upon him.
theirs: It is drawn, and cometh out of the body; yea, the glittering sword cometh out of his gall: terrors [are] upon him.

ours: All darkness shall be hid in his secret places: a fire not blown shall consume him; it shall go ill with him that is left in his tabernacle.
theirs: All darkness [shall be] hid in his secret places: a fire not blown shall consume him; it shall go ill with him that is left in his tabernacle.

ours: The increase of his house shall depart, and his goods shall flow away in the day of his wrath.
theirs: The increase of his house shall depart, [and his goods] shall flow away in the day of his wrath.

ours: This is the portion of a wicked man from God, and the heritage appointed unto him by God.
theirs: This [is] the portion of a wicked man from God, and the heritage appointed unto him by God.

ours: As for me, is my complaint to man? and if it were so, why should not my spirit be troubled?
theirs: As for me, [is] my complaint to man? and if [it were so], why should not my spirit be troubled?

ours: Mark me, and be astonished, and lay your hand upon your mouth.
theirs: Mark me, and be astonished, and lay [your] hand upon [your] mouth.

ours: Their houses are safe from fear, neither is the rod of God upon them.
theirs: Their houses [are] safe from fear, neither [is] the rod of God upon them.

ours: What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? and what profit should we have, if we pray unto him?
theirs: What [is] the Almighty, that we should serve him? and what profit should we have, if we pray unto him?

ours: Lo, their good is not in their hand: the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
theirs: Lo, their good [is] not in their hand: the counsel of the wicked is far from me.

ours: How oft is the candle of the wicked put out! and how oft cometh their destruction upon them! God distributeth sorrows in his anger.
theirs: How oft is the candle of the wicked put out! and [how oft] cometh their destruction upon them! [God] distributeth sorrows in his anger.

ours: God layeth up his iniquity for his children: he rewardeth him, and he shall know it.
theirs: God layeth up his iniquity for his children: he rewardeth him, and he shall know [it].

ours: For what pleasure hath he in his house after him, when the number of his months is cut off in the midst?
theirs: For what pleasure [hath] he in his house after him, when the number of his months is cut off in the midst?

ours: Shall any teach God knowledge? seeing he judgeth those that are high.
theirs: Shall [any] teach God knowledge? seeing he judgeth those that are high.

ours: Behold, I know your thoughts, and the devices which ye wrongfully imagine against me.
theirs: Behold, I know your thoughts, and the devices [which] ye wrongfully imagine against me.

ours: For ye say, Where is the house of the prince? and where are the dwelling places of the wicked?
theirs: For ye say, Where [is] the house of the prince? and where [are] the dwelling places of the wicked?

ours: Who shall declare his way to his face? and who shall repay him what he hath done?
theirs: Who shall declare his way to his face? and who shall repay him [what] he hath done?

ours: The clods of the valley shall be sweet unto him, and every man shall draw after him, as there are innumerable before him.
theirs: The clods of the valley shall be sweet unto him, and every man shall draw after him, as [there are] innumerable before him.

ours: Is it any pleasure to the Almighty, that thou art righteous? or is it gain to him, that thou makest thy ways perfect?
theirs: [Is it] any pleasure to the Almighty, that thou art righteous? or [is it] gain [to him], that thou makest thy ways perfect?

ours: Is not thy wickedness great? and thine iniquities infinite?
theirs: [Is] not thy wickedness great? and thine iniquities infinite?

ours: But as for the mighty man, he had the earth; and the honourable man dwelt in it.
theirs: But [as for] the mighty man, he had the earth; and the honourable man dwelt in it.

ours: Therefore snares are round about thee, and sudden fear troubleth thee;
theirs: Therefore snares [are] round about thee, and sudden fear troubleth thee;

ours: Or darkness, that thou canst not see; and abundance of waters cover thee.
theirs: Or darkness, [that] thou canst not see; and abundance of waters cover thee.

ours: Is not God in the height of heaven? and behold the height of the stars, how high they are!
theirs: [Is] not God in the height of heaven? and behold the height of the stars, how high they are!

ours: Thick clouds are a covering to him, that he seeth not; and he walketh in the circuit of heaven.
theirs: Thick clouds [are] a covering to him, that he seeth not; and he walketh in the circuit of heaven.

ours: Yet he filled their houses with good things: but the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
theirs: Yet he filled their houses with good [things]: but the counsel of the wicked is far from me.

ours: The righteous see it, and are glad: and the innocent laugh them to scorn.
theirs: The righteous see [it], and are glad: and the innocent laugh them to scorn.

ours: Then shalt thou lay up gold as dust, and the gold of Ophir as the stones of the brooks.
theirs: Then shalt thou lay up gold as dust, and the [gold] of Ophir as the stones of the brooks.

ours: When men are cast down, then thou shalt say, There is lifting up; and he shall save the humble person.
theirs: When [men] are cast down, then thou shalt say, [There is] lifting up; and he shall save the humble person.

ours: Even to day is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning.
theirs: Even to day [is] my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning.

ours: Oh that I knew where I might find him! that I might come even to his seat!
theirs: Oh that I knew where I might find him! [that] I might come [even] to his seat!

ours: I would order my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments.
theirs: I would order [my] cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments.

ours: I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me.
theirs: I would know the words [which] he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me.

ours: Will he plead against me with his great power? No; but he would put strength in me.
theirs: Will he plead against me with [his] great power? No; but he would put [strength] in me.

ours: Behold, I go forward, but he is not there; and backward, but I cannot perceive him:
theirs: Behold, I go forward, but he [is] not [there]; and backward, but I cannot perceive him:

ours: On the left hand, where he doth work, but I cannot behold him: he hideth himself on the right hand, that I cannot see him:
theirs: On the left hand, where he doth work, but I cannot behold [him]: he hideth himself on the right hand, that I cannot see [him]:

ours: But he knoweth the way that I take: when he hath tried me, I shall come forth as gold.
theirs: But he knoweth the way that I take: [when] he hath tried me, I shall come forth as gold.

ours: Neither have I gone back from the commandment of his lips; I have esteemed the words of his mouth more than my necessary food.
theirs: Neither have I gone back from the commandment of his lips; I have esteemed the words of his mouth more than my necessary [food].

ours: But he is in one mind, and who can turn him? and what his soul desireth, even that he doeth.
theirs: But he [is] in one [mind], and who can turn him? and [what] his soul desireth, even [that] he doeth.

ours: For he performeth the thing that is appointed for me: and many such things are with him.
theirs: For he performeth [the thing that is] appointed for me: and many such [things are] with him.

ours: Because I was not cut off before the darkness, neither hath he covered the darkness from my face.
theirs: Because I was not cut off before the darkness, [neither] hath he covered the darkness from my face.

ours: Some remove the landmarks; they violently take away flocks, and feed thereof.
theirs: [Some] remove the landmarks; they violently take away flocks, and feed [thereof].

ours: They drive away the ass of the fatherless, they take the widows ox for a pledge.
theirs: They drive away the ass of the fatherless, they take the widow's ox for a pledge.

ours: Behold, as wild asses in the desert, go they forth to their work; rising betimes for a prey: the wilderness yieldeth food for them and for their children.
theirs: Behold, [as] wild asses in the desert, go they forth to their work; rising betimes for a prey: the wilderness [yieldeth] food for them [and] for [their] children.

ours: They reap every one his corn in the field: and they gather the vintage of the wicked.
theirs: They reap [every one] his corn in the field: and they gather the vintage of the wicked.

ours: They cause the naked to lodge without clothing, that they have no covering in the cold.
theirs: They cause the naked to lodge without clothing, that [they have] no covering in the cold.

ours: They cause him to go naked without clothing, and they take away the sheaf from the hungry;
theirs: They cause [him] to go naked without clothing, and they take away the sheaf [from] the hungry;

ours: Which make oil within their walls, and tread their winepresses, and suffer thirst.
theirs: [Which] make oil within their walls, [and] tread [their] winepresses, and suffer thirst.

ours: Men groan from out of the city, and the soul of the wounded crieth out: yet God layeth not folly to them.
theirs: Men groan from out of the city, and the soul of the wounded crieth out: yet God layeth not folly [to them].

ours: The eye also of the adulterer waiteth for the twilight, saying, No eye shall see me: and disguiseth his face.
theirs: The eye also of the adulterer waiteth for the twilight, saying, No eye shall see me: and disguiseth [his] face.

ours: In the dark they dig through houses, which they had marked for themselves in the daytime: they know not the light.
theirs: In the dark they dig through houses, [which] they had marked for themselves in the daytime: they know not the light.

ours: For the morning is to them even as the shadow of death: if one know them, they are in the terrors of the shadow of death.
theirs: For the morning [is] to them even as the shadow of death: if [one] know [them, they are in] the terrors of the shadow of death.

ours: He is swift as the waters; their portion is cursed in the earth: he beholdeth not the way of the vineyards.
theirs: He [is] swift as the waters; their portion is cursed in the earth: he beholdeth not the way of the vineyards.

ours: Drought and heat consume the snow waters: so doth the grave those which have sinned.
theirs: Drought and heat consume the snow waters: [so doth] the grave [those which] have sinned.

ours: He evil entreateth the barren that beareth not: and doeth not good to the widow.
theirs: He evil entreateth the barren [that] beareth not: and doeth not good to the widow.

ours: He draweth also the mighty with his power: he riseth up, and no man is sure of life.
theirs: He draweth also the mighty with his power: he riseth up, and no [man] is sure of life.

ours: Though it be given him to be in safety, whereon he resteth; yet his eyes are upon their ways.
theirs: [Though] it be given him [to be] in safety, whereon he resteth; yet his eyes [are] upon their ways.

ours: They are exalted for a little while, but are gone and brought low; they are taken out of the way as all other, and cut off as the tops of the ears of corn.
theirs: They are exalted for a little while, but are gone and brought low; they are taken out of the way as all [other], and cut off as the tops of the ears of corn.

ours: And if it be not so now, who will make me a liar, and make my speech nothing worth?
theirs: And if [it be] not [so] now, who will make me a liar, and make my speech nothing worth?

ours: Dominion and fear are with him, he maketh peace in his high places.
theirs: Dominion and fear [are] with him, he maketh peace in his high places.

ours: How then can man be justified with God? or how can he be clean that is born of a woman?
theirs: How then can man be justified with God? or how can he be clean [that is] born of a woman?

ours: How much less man, that is a worm? and the son of man, which is a worm?
theirs: How much less man, [that is] a worm? and the son of man, [which is] a worm?

ours: How hast thou helped him that is without power? how savest thou the arm that hath no strength?
theirs: How hast thou helped [him that is] without power? [how] savest thou the arm [that hath] no strength?

ours: How hast thou counselled him that hath no wisdom? and how hast thou plentifully declared the thing as it is?
theirs: How hast thou counselled [him that hath] no wisdom? and [how] hast thou plentifully declared the thing as it is?

ours: Dead things are formed from under the waters, and the inhabitants thereof.
theirs: Dead [things] are formed from under the waters, and the inhabitants thereof.

ours: Hell is naked before him, and destruction hath no covering.
theirs: Hell [is] naked before him, and destruction hath no covering.

ours: He stretcheth out the north over the empty place, and hangeth the earth upon nothing.
theirs: He stretcheth out the north over the empty place, [and] hangeth the earth upon nothing.

ours: He holdeth back the face of his throne, and spreadeth his cloud upon it.
theirs: He holdeth back the face of his throne, [and] spreadeth his cloud upon it.

ours: Lo, these are parts of his ways: but how little a portion is heard of him? but the thunder of his power who can understand?
theirs: Lo, these [are] parts of his ways: but how little a portion is heard of him? but the thunder of his power who can understand?

ours: As God liveth, who hath taken away my judgment; and the Almighty, who hath vexed my soul;
theirs: [As] God liveth, [who] hath taken away my judgment; and the Almighty, [who] hath vexed my soul;

ours: All the while my breath is in me, and the spirit of God is in my nostrils;
theirs: All the while my breath [is] in me, and the spirit of God [is] in my nostrils;

ours: My righteousness I hold fast, and will not let it go: my heart shall not reproach me so long as I live.
theirs: My righteousness I hold fast, and will not let it go: my heart shall not reproach [me] so long as I live.

ours: For what is the hope of the hypocrite, though he hath gained, when God taketh away his soul?
theirs: For what [is] the hope of the hypocrite, though he hath gained, when God taketh away his soul?

ours: I will teach you by the hand of God: that which is with the Almighty will I not conceal.
theirs: I will teach you by the hand of God: [that] which [is] with the Almighty will I not conceal.

ours: Behold, all ye yourselves have seen it; why then are ye thus altogether vain?
theirs: Behold, all ye yourselves have seen [it]; why then are ye thus altogether vain?

ours: This is the portion of a wicked man with God, and the heritage of oppressors, which they shall receive of the Almighty.
theirs: This [is] the portion of a wicked man with God, and the heritage of oppressors, [which] they shall receive of the Almighty.

ours: If his children be multiplied, it is for the sword: and his offspring shall not be satisfied with bread.
theirs: If his children be multiplied, [it is] for the sword: and his offspring shall not be satisfied with bread.

ours: He may prepare it, but the just shall put it on, and the innocent shall divide the silver.
theirs: He may prepare [it], but the just shall put [it] on, and the innocent shall divide the silver.

ours: He buildeth his house as a moth, and as a booth that the keeper maketh.
theirs: He buildeth his house as a moth, and as a booth [that] the keeper maketh.

ours: The rich man shall lie down, but he shall not be gathered: he openeth his eyes, and he is not.
theirs: The rich man shall lie down, but he shall not be gathered: he openeth his eyes, and he [is] not.

ours: For God shall cast upon him, and not spare: he would fain flee out of his hand.
theirs: For [God] shall cast upon him, and not spare: he would fain flee out of his hand.

ours: Men shall clap their hands at him, and shall hiss him out of his place.
theirs: [Men] shall clap their hands at him, and shall hiss him out of his place.

ours: SURELY there is a vein for the silver, and a place for gold where they fine it.
theirs: Surely there is a vein for the silver, and a place for gold [where] they fine [it].

ours: Iron is taken out of the earth, and brass is molten out of the stone.
theirs: Iron is taken out of the earth, and brass [is] molten [out of] the stone.

ours: The flood breaketh out from the inhabitant; even the waters forgotten of the foot: they are dried up, they are gone away from men.
theirs: The flood breaketh out from the inhabitant; [even the waters] forgotten of the foot: they are dried up, they are gone away from men.

ours: As for the earth, out of it cometh bread: and under it is turned up as it were fire.
theirs: [As for] the earth, out of it cometh bread: and under it is turned up as it were fire.
