ours: The stones of it are the place of sapphires: and it hath dust of gold.
theirs: The stones of it [are] the place of sapphires: and it hath dust of gold.

ours: There is a path which no fowl knoweth, and which the vultures eye hath not seen:
theirs: [There is] a path which no fowl knoweth, and which the vulture's eye hath not seen:

ours: The lions whelps have not trodden it, nor the fierce lion passed by it.
theirs: The lion's whelps have not trodden it, nor the fierce lion passed by it.

ours: He bindeth the floods from overflowing; and the thing that is hid bringeth he forth to light.
theirs: He bindeth the floods from overflowing; and [the thing that is] hid bringeth he forth to light.

ours: But where shall wisdom be found? and where is the place of understanding?
theirs: But where shall wisdom be found? and where [is] the place of understanding?

ours: The depth saith, It is not in me: and the sea saith, It is not with me.
theirs: The depth saith, It [is] not in me: and the sea saith, [It is] not with me.

ours: It cannot be gotten for gold, neither shall silver be weighed for the price thereof.
theirs: It cannot be gotten for gold, neither shall silver be weighed [for] the price thereof.

ours: The gold and the crystal cannot equal it: and the exchange of it shall not be for jewels of fine gold.
theirs: The gold and the crystal cannot equal it: and the exchange of it [shall not be for] jewels of fine gold.

ours: No mention shall be made of coral, or of pearls: for the price of wisdom is above rubies.
theirs: No mention shall be made of coral, or of pearls: for the price of wisdom [is] above rubies.

ours: Whence then cometh wisdom? and where is the place of understanding?
theirs: Whence then cometh wisdom? and where [is] the place of understanding?

ours: For he looketh to the ends of the earth, and seeth under the whole heaven;
theirs: For he looketh to the ends of the earth, [and] seeth under the whole heaven;

ours: And unto man he said, Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom; and to depart from evil is understanding.
theirs: And unto man he said, Behold, the fear of the Lord, that [is] wisdom; and to depart from evil [is] understanding.

ours: Oh that I were as in months past, as in the days when God preserved me;
theirs: Oh that I were as [in] months past, as [in] the days [when] God preserved me;

ours: When his candle shined upon my head, and when by his light I walked through darkness;
theirs: When his candle shined upon my head, [and when] by his light I walked [through] darkness;

ours: As I was in the days of my youth, when the secret of God was upon my tabernacle;
theirs: As I was in the days of my youth, when the secret of God [was] upon my tabernacle;

ours: When the Almighty was yet with me, when my children were about me;
theirs: When the Almighty [was] yet with me, [when] my children [were] about me;

ours: When I went out to the gate through the city, when I prepared my seat in the street!
theirs: When I went out to the gate through the city, [when] I prepared my seat in the street!

ours: The young men saw me, and hid themselves: and the aged arose, and stood up.
theirs: The young men saw me, and hid themselves: and the aged arose, [and] stood up.

ours: The princes refrained talking, and laid their hand on their mouth.
theirs: The princes refrained talking, and laid [their] hand on their mouth.

ours: When the ear heard me, then it blessed me; and when the eye saw me, it gave witness to me:
theirs: When the ear heard [me], then it blessed me; and when the eye saw [me], it gave witness to me:

ours: Because I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and him that had none to help him.
theirs: Because I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and [him that had] none to help him.

ours: The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me: and I caused the widows heart to sing for joy.
theirs: The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me: and I caused the widow's heart to sing for joy.

ours: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me: my judgment was as a robe and a diadem.
theirs: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me: my judgment [was] as a robe and a diadem.

ours: I was eyes to the blind, and feet was I to the lame.
theirs: I was eyes to the blind, and feet [was] I to the lame.

ours: I was a father to the poor: and the cause which I knew not I searched out.
theirs: I [was] a father to the poor: and the cause [which] I knew not I searched out.

ours: Then I said, I shall die in my nest, and I shall multiply my days as the sand.
theirs: Then I said, I shall die in my nest, and I shall multiply [my] days as the sand.

ours: My root was spread out by the waters, and the dew lay all night upon my branch.
theirs: My root [was] spread out by the waters, and the dew lay all night upon my branch.

ours: My glory was fresh in me, and my bow was renewed in my hand.
theirs: My glory [was] fresh in me, and my bow was renewed in my hand.

ours: Unto me men gave ear, and waited, and kept silence at my counsel.
theirs: Unto me [men] gave ear, and waited, and kept silence at my counsel.

ours: And they waited for me as for the rain; and they opened their mouth wide as for the latter rain.
theirs: And they waited for me as for the rain; and they opened their mouth wide [as] for the latter rain.

ours: If I laughed on them, they believed it not; and the light of my countenance they cast not down.
theirs: [If] I laughed on them, they believed [it] not; and the light of my countenance they cast not down.

ours: I chose out their way, and sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one that comforteth the mourners.
theirs: I chose out their way, and sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one [that] comforteth the mourners.

ours: BUT now they that are younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I would have disdained to have set with the dogs of my flock.
theirs: But now [they that are] younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I would have disdained to have set with the dogs of my flock.

ours: Yea, whereto might the strength of their hands profit me, in whom old age was perished?
theirs: Yea, whereto [might] the strength of their hands [profit] me, in whom old age was perished?

ours: For want and famine they were solitary; fleeing into the wilderness in former time desolate and waste.
theirs: For want and famine [they were] solitary; fleeing into the wilderness in former time desolate and waste.

ours: Who cut up mallows by the bushes, and juniper roots for their meat.
theirs: Who cut up mallows by the bushes, and juniper roots [for] their meat.

ours: They were driven forth from among men, (they cried after them as after a thief;)
theirs: They were driven forth from among [men], (they cried after them as [after] a thief;)

ours: To dwell in the clifts of the valleys, in caves of the earth, and in the rocks.
theirs: To dwell in the clifts of the valleys, [in] caves of the earth, and [in] the rocks.

ours: They were children of fools, yea, children of base men: they were viler than the earth.
theirs: [They were] children of fools, yea, children of base men: they were viler than the earth.

ours: Upon my right hand rise the youth; they push away my feet, and they raise up against me the ways of their destruction.
theirs: Upon [my] right [hand] rise the youth; they push away my feet, and they raise up against me the ways of their destruction.

ours: They came upon me as a wide breaking in of waters: in the desolation they rolled themselves upon me.
theirs: They came [upon me] as a wide breaking in [of waters]: in the desolation they rolled themselves [upon me].

ours: By the great force of my disease is my garment changed: it bindeth me about as the collar of my coat.
theirs: By the great force [of my disease] is my garment changed: it bindeth me about as the collar of my coat.

ours: I cry unto thee, and thou dost not hear me: I stand up, and thou regardest me not.
theirs: I cry unto thee, and thou dost not hear me: I stand up, and thou regardest me [not].

ours: Thou liftest me up to the wind; thou causest me to ride upon it, and dissolvest my substance.
theirs: Thou liftest me up to the wind; thou causest me to ride [upon it], and dissolvest my substance.

ours: For I know that thou wilt bring me to death, and to the house appointed for all living.
theirs: For I know [that] thou wilt bring me [to] death, and [to] the house appointed for all living.

ours: Howbeit he will not stretch out his hand to the grave, though they cry in his destruction.
theirs: Howbeit he will not stretch out [his] hand to the grave, though they cry in his destruction.

ours: Did not I weep for him that was in trouble? was not my soul grieved for the poor?
theirs: Did not I weep for him that was in trouble? was [not] my soul grieved for the poor?

ours: When I looked for good, then evil came unto me: and when I waited for light, there came darkness.
theirs: When I looked for good, then evil came [unto me]: and when I waited for light, there came darkness.

ours: I went mourning without the sun: I stood up, and I cried in the congregation.
theirs: I went mourning without the sun: I stood up, [and] I cried in the congregation.

ours: My harp also is turned to mourning, and my organ into the voice of them that weep.
theirs: My harp also is [turned] to mourning, and my organ into the voice of them that weep.

ours: For what portion of God is there from above? and what inheritance of the Almighty from on high?
theirs: For what portion of God [is there] from above? and [what] inheritance of the Almighty from on high?

ours: Is not destruction to the wicked? and a strange punishment to the workers of iniquity?
theirs: [Is] not destruction to the wicked? and a strange [punishment] to the workers of iniquity?

ours: Then let me sow, and let another eat; yea, let my offspring be rooted out.
theirs: [Then] let me sow, and let another eat; yea, let my offspring be rooted out.

ours: If mine heart have been deceived by a woman, or if I have laid wait at my neighbours door;
theirs: If mine heart have been deceived by a woman, or [if] I have laid wait at my neighbour's door;

ours: Then let my wife grind unto another, and let others bow down upon her.
theirs: [Then] let my wife grind unto another, and let others bow down upon her.

ours: For this is an heinous crime; yea, it is an iniquity to be punished by the judges.
theirs: For this [is] an heinous crime; yea, it [is] an iniquity [to be punished by] the judges.

ours: For it is a fire that consumeth to destruction, and would root out all mine increase.
theirs: For it [is] a fire [that] consumeth to destruction, and would root out all mine increase.

ours: If I have withheld the poor from their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail;
theirs: If I have withheld the poor from [their] desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail;

ours: (For from my youth he was brought up with me, as with a father, and I have guided her from my mothers womb;)
theirs: (For from my youth he was brought up with me, as [with] a father, and I have guided her from my mother's womb;)

ours: If his loins have not blessed me, and if he were not warmed with the fleece of my sheep;
theirs: If his loins have not blessed me, and [if] he were [not] warmed with the fleece of my sheep;

ours: Then let mine arm fall from my shoulder blade, and mine arm be broken from the bone.
theirs: [Then] let mine arm fall from my shoulder blade, and mine arm be broken from the bone.

ours: For destruction from God was a terror to me, and by reason of his highness I could not endure.
theirs: For destruction [from] God [was] a terror to me, and by reason of his highness I could not endure.

ours: If I have made gold my hope, or have said to the fine gold, Thou art my confidence;
theirs: If I have made gold my hope, or have said to the fine gold, [Thou art] my confidence;

ours: If I rejoiced because my wealth was great, and because mine hand had gotten much;
theirs: If I rejoiced because my wealth [was] great, and because mine hand had gotten much;

ours: If I beheld the sun when it shined, or the moon walking in brightness;
theirs: If I beheld the sun when it shined, or the moon walking [in] brightness;

ours: This also were an iniquity to be punished by the judge: for I should have denied the God that is above.
theirs: This also [were] an iniquity [to be punished by] the judge: for I should have denied the God [that is] above.

ours: The stranger did not lodge in the street: but I opened my doors to the traveller.
theirs: The stranger did not lodge in the street: [but] I opened my doors to the traveller.

ours: Did I fear a great multitude, or did the contempt of families terrify me, that I kept silence, and went not out of the door?
theirs: Did I fear a great multitude, or did the contempt of families terrify me, that I kept silence, [and] went not out of the door?

ours: Oh that one would hear me! behold, my desire is, that the Almighty would answer me, and that mine adversary had written a book.
theirs: Oh that one would hear me! behold, my desire [is, that] the Almighty would answer me, and [that] mine adversary had written a book.

ours: Surely I would take it upon my shoulder, and bind it as a crown to me.
theirs: Surely I would take it upon my shoulder, [and] bind it [as] a crown to me.

ours: SO these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
theirs: So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he [was] righteous in his own eyes.

ours: Also against his three friends was his wrath kindled, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.
theirs: Also against his three friends was his wrath kindled, because they had found no answer, and [yet] had condemned Job.

ours: Now Elihu had waited till Job had spoken, because they were elder than he.
theirs: Now Elihu had waited till Job had spoken, because they [were] elder than he.

ours: When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, then his wrath was kindled.
theirs: When Elihu saw that [there was] no answer in the mouth of [these] three men, then his wrath was kindled.

ours: And Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, I am young, and ye are very old; wherefore I was afraid, and durst not shew you mine opinion.
theirs: And Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, I [am] young, and ye [are] very old; wherefore I was afraid, and durst not shew you mine opinion.

ours: But there is a spirit in man: and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding.
theirs: But [there is] a spirit in man: and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding.

ours: Great men are not always wise: neither do the aged understand judgment.
theirs: Great men are not [always] wise: neither do the aged understand judgment.

ours: Yea, I attended unto you, and, behold, there was none of you that convinced Job, or that answered his words:
theirs: Yea, I attended unto you, and, behold, [there was] none of you that convinced Job, [or] that answered his words:

ours: Now he hath not directed his words against me: neither will I answer him with your speeches.
theirs: Now he hath not directed [his] words against me: neither will I answer him with your speeches.

ours: When I had waited, (for they spake not, but stood still, and answered no more;)
theirs: When I had waited, (for they spake not, but stood still, [and] answered no more;)

ours: I said, I will answer also my part, I also will shew mine opinion.
theirs: [I said], I will answer also my part, I also will shew mine opinion.

ours: Behold, my belly is as wine which hath no vent; it is ready to burst like new bottles.
theirs: Behold, my belly [is] as wine [which] hath no vent; it is ready to burst like new bottles.

ours: Let me not, I pray you, accept any mans person, neither let me give flattering titles unto man.
theirs: Let me not, I pray you, accept any man's person, neither let me give flattering titles unto man.

ours: For I know not to give flattering titles; in so doing my maker would soon take me away.
theirs: For I know not to give flattering titles; [in so doing] my maker would soon take me away.

ours: My words shall be of the uprightness of my heart: and my lips shall utter knowledge clearly.
theirs: My words [shall be of] the uprightness of my heart: and my lips shall utter knowledge clearly.

ours: If thou canst answer me, set thy words in order before me, stand up.
theirs: If thou canst answer me, set [thy words] in order before me, stand up.

ours: Behold, I am according to thy wish in Gods stead: I also am formed out of the clay.
theirs: Behold, I [am] according to thy wish in God's stead: I also am formed out of the clay.

ours: Surely thou hast spoken in mine hearing, and I have heard the voice of thy words, saying,
theirs: Surely thou hast spoken in mine hearing, and I have heard the voice of [thy] words, [saying],

ours: I am clean without transgression, I am innocent; neither is there iniquity in me.
theirs: I am clean without transgression, I [am] innocent; neither [is there] iniquity in me.

ours: Behold, in this thou art not just: I will answer thee, that God is greater than man.
theirs: Behold, [in] this thou art not just: I will answer thee, that God is greater than man.

ours: For God speaketh once, yea twice, yet man perceiveth it not.
theirs: For God speaketh once, yea twice, [yet man] perceiveth it not.

ours: That he may withdraw man from his purpose, and hide pride from man.
theirs: That he may withdraw man [from his] purpose, and hide pride from man.

ours: He is chastened also with pain upon his bed, and the multitude of his bones with strong pain:
theirs: He is chastened also with pain upon his bed, and the multitude of his bones with strong [pain]:

ours: His flesh is consumed away, that it cannot be seen; and his bones that were not seen stick out.
theirs: His flesh is consumed away, that it cannot be seen; and his bones [that] were not seen stick out.

ours: His flesh shall be fresher than a childs: he shall return to the days of his youth:
theirs: His flesh shall be fresher than a child's: he shall return to the days of his youth:

ours: He looketh upon men, and if any say, I have sinned, and perverted that which was right, and it profited me not;
theirs: He looketh upon men, and [if any] say, I have sinned, and perverted [that which was] right, and it profited me not;

ours: Lo, all these things worketh God oftentimes with man,
theirs: Lo, all these [things] worketh God oftentimes with man,

ours: Hear my words, O ye wise men; and give ear unto me, ye that have knowledge.
theirs: Hear my words, O ye wise [men]; and give ear unto me, ye that have knowledge.

ours: Let us choose to us judgment: let us know among ourselves what is good.
theirs: Let us choose to us judgment: let us know among ourselves what [is] good.

ours: Should I lie against my right? my wound is incurable without transgression.
theirs: Should I lie against my right? my wound [is] incurable without transgression.

ours: What man is like Job, who drinketh up scorning like water?
theirs: What man [is] like Job, [who] drinketh up scorning like water?

ours: Therefore hearken unto me, ye men of understanding: far be it from God, that he should do wickedness; and from the Almighty, that he should commit iniquity.
theirs: Therefore hearken unto me, ye men of understanding: far be it from God, [that he should do] wickedness; and [from] the Almighty, [that he should commit] iniquity.

ours: For the work of a man shall he render unto him, and cause every man to find according to his ways.
theirs: For the work of a man shall he render unto him, and cause every man to find according to [his] ways.

ours: If he set his heart upon man, if he gather unto himself his spirit and his breath;
theirs: If he set his heart upon man, [if] he gather unto himself his spirit and his breath;

ours: If now thou hast understanding, hear this: hearken to the voice of my words.
theirs: If now [thou hast] understanding, hear this: hearken to the voice of my words.

ours: Is it fit to say to a king, Thou art wicked? and to princes, Ye are ungodly?
theirs: [Is it fit] to say to a king, [Thou art] wicked? [and] to princes, [Ye are] ungodly?

ours: How much less to him that accepteth not the persons of princes, nor regardeth the rich more than the poor? for they all are the work of his hands.
theirs: [How much less to him] that accepteth not the persons of princes, nor regardeth the rich more than the poor? for they all [are] the work of his hands.

ours: For his eyes are upon the ways of man, and he seeth all his goings.
theirs: For his eyes [are] upon the ways of man, and he seeth all his goings.

ours: There is no darkness, nor shadow of death, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.
theirs: [There is] no darkness, nor shadow of death, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.

ours: For he will not lay upon man more than right; that he should enter into judgment with God.
theirs: For he will not lay upon man more [than right]; that he should enter into judgment with God.

ours: Therefore he knoweth their works, and he overturneth them in the night, so that they are destroyed.
theirs: Therefore he knoweth their works, and he overturneth [them] in the night, so that they are destroyed.

ours: When he giveth quietness, who then can make trouble? and when he hideth his face, who then can behold him? whether it be done against a nation, or against a man only:
theirs: When he giveth quietness, who then can make trouble? and when he hideth [his] face, who then can behold him? whether [it be done] against a nation, or against a man only:

ours: Surely it is meet to be said unto God, I have borne chastisement, I will not offend any more:
theirs: Surely it is meet to be said unto God, I have borne [chastisement], I will not offend [any more]:

ours: That which I see not teach thou me: if I have done iniquity, I will do no more.
theirs: [That which] I see not teach thou me: if I have done iniquity, I will do no more.

ours: Should it be according to thy mind? he will recompense it, whether thou refuse, or whether thou choose; and not I: therefore speak what thou knowest.
theirs: [Should it be] according to thy mind? he will recompense it, whether thou refuse, or whether thou choose; and not I: therefore speak what thou knowest.

ours: Job hath spoken without knowledge, and his words were without wisdom.
theirs: Job hath spoken without knowledge, and his words [were] without wisdom.

ours: My desire is that Job may be tried unto the end because of his answers for wicked men.
theirs: My desire [is that] Job may be tried unto the end because of [his] answers for wicked men.

ours: For he addeth rebellion unto his sin, he clappeth his hands among us, and multiplieth his words against God.
theirs: For he addeth rebellion unto his sin, he clappeth [his hands] among us, and multiplieth his words against God.

ours: Thinkest thou this to be right, that thou saidst, My righteousness is more than Gods?
theirs: Thinkest thou this to be right, [that] thou saidst, My righteousness [is] more than God's?

ours: For thou saidst, What advantage will it be unto thee? and, What profit shall I have, if I be cleansed from my sin?
theirs: For thou saidst, What advantage will it be unto thee? [and], What profit shall I have, [if I be cleansed] from my sin?

ours: Look unto the heavens, and see; and behold the clouds which are higher than thou.
theirs: Look unto the heavens, and see; and behold the clouds [which] are higher than thou.

ours: If thou sinnest, what doest thou against him? or if thy transgressions be multiplied, what doest thou unto him?
theirs: If thou sinnest, what doest thou against him? or [if] thy transgressions be multiplied, what doest thou unto him?

ours: Thy wickedness may hurt a man as thou art; and thy righteousness may profit the son of man.
theirs: Thy wickedness [may hurt] a man as thou [art]; and thy righteousness [may profit] the son of man.

ours: By reason of the multitude of oppressions they make the oppressed to cry: they cry out by reason of the arm of the mighty.
theirs: By reason of the multitude of oppressions they make [the oppressed] to cry: they cry out by reason of the arm of the mighty.

ours: But none saith, Where is God my maker, who giveth songs in the night;
theirs: But none saith, Where [is] God my maker, who giveth songs in the night;

ours: Although thou sayest thou shalt not see him, yet judgment is before him; therefore trust thou in him.
theirs: Although thou sayest thou shalt not see him, [yet] judgment [is] before him; therefore trust thou in him.

ours: But now, because it is not so, he hath visited in his anger; yet he knoweth it not in great extremity:
theirs: But now, because [it is] not [so], he hath visited in his anger; yet he knoweth [it] not in great extremity:

ours: Suffer me a little, and I will shew thee that I have yet to speak on Gods behalf.
theirs: Suffer me a little, and I will shew thee that [I have] yet to speak on God's behalf.

ours: For truly my words shall not be false: he that is perfect in knowledge is with thee.
theirs: For truly my words [shall] not [be] false: he that is perfect in knowledge [is] with thee.

ours: Behold, God is mighty, and despiseth not any: he is mighty in strength and wisdom.
theirs: Behold, God [is] mighty, and despiseth not [any: he is] mighty in strength [and] wisdom.

ours: He withdraweth not his eyes from the righteous: but with kings are they on the throne; yea, he doth establish them for ever, and they are exalted.
theirs: He withdraweth not his eyes from the righteous: but with kings [are they] on the throne; yea, he doth establish them for ever, and they are exalted.

ours: And if they be bound in fetters, and be holden in cords of affliction;
theirs: And if [they be] bound in fetters, [and] be holden in cords of affliction;

ours: If they obey and serve him, they shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.
theirs: If they obey and serve [him], they shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.

ours: They die in youth, and their life is among the unclean.
theirs: They die in youth, and their life [is] among the unclean.

ours: Even so would he have removed thee out of the strait into a broad place, where there is no straitness; and that which should be set on thy table should be full of fatness.
theirs: Even so would he have removed thee out of the strait [into] a broad place, where [there is] no straitness; and that which should be set on thy table [should be] full of fatness.

ours: But thou hast fulfilled the judgment of the wicked: judgment and justice take hold on thee.
theirs: But thou hast fulfilled the judgment of the wicked: judgment and justice take hold [on thee].

ours: Because there is wrath, beware lest he take thee away with his stroke: then a great ransom cannot deliver thee.
theirs: Because [there is] wrath, [beware] lest he take thee away with [his] stroke: then a great ransom cannot deliver thee.

ours: Will he esteem thy riches? no, not gold, nor all the forces of strength.
theirs: Will he esteem thy riches? [no], not gold, nor all the forces of strength.

ours: Every man may see it; man may behold it afar off.
theirs: Every man may see it; man may behold [it] afar off.

ours: Behold, God is great, and we know him not, neither can the number of his years be searched out.
theirs: Behold, God [is] great, and we know [him] not, neither can the number of his years be searched out.

ours: Which the clouds do drop and distil upon man abundantly.
theirs: Which the clouds do drop [and] distil upon man abundantly.

ours: Also can any understand the spreadings of the clouds, or the noise of his tabernacle?
theirs: Also can [any] understand the spreadings of the clouds, [or] the noise of his tabernacle?

ours: With clouds he covereth the light; and commandeth it not to shine by the cloud that cometh betwixt.
theirs: With clouds he covereth the light; and commandeth it [not to shine] by [the cloud] that cometh betwixt.

ours: Hear attentively the noise of his voice, and the sound that goeth out of his mouth.
theirs: Hear attentively the noise of his voice, and the sound [that] goeth out of his mouth.

ours: For he saith to the snow, Be thou on the earth; likewise to the small rain, and to the great rain of his strength.
theirs: For he saith to the snow, Be thou [on] the earth; likewise to the small rain, and to the great rain of his strength.

ours: How thy garments are warm, when he quieteth the earth by the south wind?
theirs: How thy garments [are] warm, when he quieteth the earth by the south [wind]?

ours: Hast thou with him spread out the sky, which is strong, and as a molten looking glass?
theirs: Hast thou with him spread out the sky, [which is] strong, [and] as a molten looking glass?

ours: Teach us what we shall say unto him; for we cannot order our speech by reason of darkness.
theirs: Teach us what we shall say unto him; [for] we cannot order [our speech] by reason of darkness.

ours: And now men see not the bright light which is in the clouds: but the wind passeth, and cleanseth them.
theirs: And now [men] see not the bright light which [is] in the clouds: but the wind passeth, and cleanseth them.

ours: Fair weather cometh out of the north: with God is terrible majesty.
theirs: Fair weather cometh out of the north: with God [is] terrible majesty.

ours: Touching the Almighty, we cannot find him out: he is excellent in power, and in judgment, and in plenty of justice: he will not afflict.
theirs: [Touching] the Almighty, we cannot find him out: [he is] excellent in power, and in judgment, and in plenty of justice: he will not afflict.

ours: Men do therefore fear him: he respecteth not any that are wise of heart.
theirs: Men do therefore fear him: he respecteth not any [that are] wise of heart.

ours: Who is this that darkeneth counsel by words without knowledge?
theirs: Who [is] this that darkeneth counsel by words without knowledge?

ours: Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it brake forth, as if it had issued out of the womb?
theirs: Or [who] shut up the sea with doors, when it brake forth, [as if] it had issued out of the womb?

ours: And brake up for it my decreed place, and set bars and doors,
theirs: And brake up for it my decreed [place], and set bars and doors,

ours: Hast thou commanded the morning since thy days; and caused the dayspring to know his place;
theirs: Hast thou commanded the morning since thy days; [and] caused the dayspring to know his place;

ours: It is turned as clay to the seal; and they stand as a garment.
theirs: It is turned as clay [to] the seal; and they stand as a garment.

ours: Where is the way where light dwelleth? and as for darkness, where is the place thereof,
theirs: Where [is] the way [where] light dwelleth? and [as for] darkness, where [is] the place thereof,

ours: That thou shouldest take it to the bound thereof, and that thou shouldest know the paths to the house thereof?
theirs: That thou shouldest take it to the bound thereof, and that thou shouldest know the paths [to] the house thereof?

ours: Knowest thou it, because thou wast then born? or because the number of thy days is great?
theirs: Knowest thou [it], because thou wast then born? or [because] the number of thy days [is] great?

ours: By what way is the light parted, which scattereth the east wind upon the earth?
theirs: By what way is the light parted, [which] scattereth the east wind upon the earth?

ours: To cause it to rain on the earth, where no man is; on the wilderness, wherein there is no man;
theirs: To cause it to rain on the earth, [where] no man [is; on] the wilderness, wherein [there is] no man;

ours: To satisfy the desolate and waste ground; and to cause the bud of the tender herb to spring forth?
theirs: To satisfy the desolate and waste [ground]; and to cause the bud of the tender herb to spring forth?

ours: The waters are hid as with a stone, and the face of the deep is frozen.
theirs: The waters are hid as [with] a stone, and the face of the deep is frozen.

ours: Canst thou send lightnings, that they may go, and say unto thee, Here we are?
theirs: Canst thou send lightnings, that they may go, and say unto thee, Here we [are]?

ours: When they couch in their dens, and abide in the covert to lie in wait?
theirs: When they couch in [their] dens, [and] abide in the covert to lie in wait?

ours: KNOWEST thou the time when the wild goats of the rock bring forth? or canst thou mark when the hinds do calve?
theirs: Knowest thou the time when the wild goats of the rock bring forth? [or] canst thou mark when the hinds do calve?

ours: Canst thou number the months that they fulfil? or knowest thou the time when they bring forth?
theirs: Canst thou number the months [that] they fulfil? or knowest thou the time when they bring forth?

ours: The range of the mountains is his pasture, and he searcheth after every green thing.
theirs: The range of the mountains [is] his pasture, and he searcheth after every green thing.

ours: Wilt thou trust him, because his strength is great? or wilt thou leave thy labour to him?
theirs: Wilt thou trust him, because his strength [is] great? or wilt thou leave thy labour to him?

ours: Wilt thou believe him, that he will bring home thy seed, and gather it into thy barn?
theirs: Wilt thou believe him, that he will bring home thy seed, and gather [it into] thy barn?

ours: Gavest thou the goodly wings unto the peacocks? or wings and feathers unto the ostrich?
theirs: [Gavest thou] the goodly wings unto the peacocks? or wings and feathers unto the ostrich?

ours: She is hardened against her young ones, as though they were not hers: her labour is in vain without fear;
theirs: She is hardened against her young ones, as though [they were] not hers: her labour is in vain without fear;

ours: Canst thou make him afraid as a grasshopper? the glory of his nostrils is terrible.
theirs: Canst thou make him afraid as a grasshopper? the glory of his nostrils [is] terrible.

ours: He paweth in the valley, and rejoiceth in his strength: he goeth on to meet the armed men.
theirs: He paweth in the valley, and rejoiceth in [his] strength: he goeth on to meet the armed men.

ours: He swalloweth the ground with fierceness and rage: neither believeth he that it is the sound of the trumpet.
theirs: He swalloweth the ground with fierceness and rage: neither believeth he that [it is] the sound of the trumpet.

ours: Doth the hawk fly by thy wisdom, and stretch her wings toward the south?
theirs: Doth the hawk fly by thy wisdom, [and] stretch her wings toward the south?

ours: From thence she seeketh the prey, and her eyes behold afar off.
theirs: From thence she seeketh the prey, [and] her eyes behold afar off.

ours: Her young ones also suck up blood: and where the slain are, there is she.
theirs: Her young ones also suck up blood: and where the slain [are], there [is] she.

ours: Shall he that contendeth with the Almighty instruct him? he that reproveth God, let him answer it.
theirs: Shall he that contendeth with the Almighty instruct [him]? he that reproveth God, let him answer it.

ours: Deck thyself now with majesty and excellency; and array thyself with glory and beauty.
theirs: Deck thyself now [with] majesty and excellency; and array thyself with glory and beauty.

ours: Cast abroad the rage of thy wrath: and behold every one that is proud, and abase him.
theirs: Cast abroad the rage of thy wrath: and behold every one [that is] proud, and abase him.

ours: Look on every one that is proud, and bring him low; and tread down the wicked in their place.
theirs: Look on every one [that is] proud, [and] bring him low; and tread down the wicked in their place.

ours: Hide them in the dust together; and bind their faces in secret.
theirs: Hide them in the dust together; [and] bind their faces in secret.

ours: Lo now, his strength is in his loins, and his force is in the navel of his belly.
theirs: Lo now, his strength [is] in his loins, and his force [is] in the navel of his belly.

ours: His bones are as strong pieces of brass; his bones are like bars of iron.
theirs: His bones [are as] strong pieces of brass; his bones [are] like bars of iron.

ours: He is the chief of the ways of God: he that made him can make his sword to approach unto him.
theirs: He [is] the chief of the ways of God: he that made him can make his sword to approach [unto him].

ours: The shady trees cover him with their shadow; the willows of the brook compass him about.
theirs: The shady trees cover him [with] their shadow; the willows of the brook compass him about.

ours: Behold, he drinketh up a river, and hasteth not: he trusteth that he can draw up Jordan into his mouth.
theirs: Behold, he drinketh up a river, [and] hasteth not: he trusteth that he can draw up Jordan into his mouth.

ours: He taketh it with his eyes: his nose pierceth through snares.
theirs: He taketh it with his eyes: [his] nose pierceth through snares.

ours: CANST thou draw out leviathan with an hook? or his tongue with a cord which thou lettest down?
theirs: Canst thou draw out leviathan with an hook? or his tongue with a cord [which] thou lettest down?

ours: Will he make many supplications unto thee? will he speak soft words unto thee?
theirs: Will he make many supplications unto thee? will he speak soft [words] unto thee?

ours: Wilt thou play with him as with a bird? or wilt thou bind him for thy maidens?
theirs: Wilt thou play with him as [with] a bird? or wilt thou bind him for thy maidens?

ours: Behold, the hope of him is in vain: shall not one be cast down even at the sight of him?
theirs: Behold, the hope of him is in vain: shall not [one] be cast down even at the sight of him?

ours: None is so fierce that dare stir him up: who then is able to stand before me?
theirs: None [is so] fierce that dare stir him up: who then is able to stand before me?

ours: Who hath prevented me, that I should repay him? whatsoever is under the whole heaven is mine.
theirs: Who hath prevented me, that I should repay [him? whatsoever is] under the whole heaven is mine.

ours: Who can discover the face of his garment? or who can come to him with his double bridle?
theirs: Who can discover the face of his garment? [or] who can come [to him] with his double bridle?

ours: Who can open the doors of his face? his teeth are terrible round about.
theirs: Who can open the doors of his face? his teeth [are] terrible round about.

ours: His scales are his pride, shut up together as with a close seal.
theirs: [His] scales [are his] pride, shut up together [as with] a close seal.

ours: By his neesings a light doth shine, and his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.
theirs: By his neesings a light doth shine, and his eyes [are] like the eyelids of the morning.

ours: Out of his mouth go burning lamps, and sparks of fire leap out.
theirs: Out of his mouth go burning lamps, [and] sparks of fire leap out.

ours: Out of his nostrils goeth smoke, as out of a seething pot or caldron.
theirs: Out of his nostrils goeth smoke, as [out] of a seething pot or caldron.

ours: His heart is as firm as a stone; yea, as hard as a piece of the nether millstone.
theirs: His heart is as firm as a stone; yea, as hard as a piece of the nether [millstone].

ours: He esteemeth iron as straw, and brass as rotten wood.
theirs: He esteemeth iron as straw, [and] brass as rotten wood.

ours: Sharp stones are under him: he spreadeth sharp pointed things upon the mire.
theirs: Sharp stones [are] under him: he spreadeth sharp pointed things upon the mire.

ours: He maketh a path to shine after him; one would think the deep to be hoary.
theirs: He maketh a path to shine after him; [one] would think the deep [to be] hoary.

ours: He beholdeth all high things: he is a king over all the children of pride.
theirs: He beholdeth all high [things]: he [is] a king over all the children of pride.

ours: I know that thou canst do every thing, and that no thought can be withholden from thee.
theirs: I know that thou canst do every [thing], and [that] no thought can be withholden from thee.

ours: Who is he that hideth counsel without knowledge? therefore have I uttered that I understood not; things too wonderful for me, which I knew not.
theirs: Who [is] he that hideth counsel without knowledge? therefore have I uttered that I understood not; things too wonderful for me, which I knew not.

ours: Wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.
theirs: Wherefore I abhor [myself], and repent in dust and ashes.

ours: And it was so, that after the LORD had spoken these words unto Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends: for ye have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job hath.
theirs: And it was [so], that after the LORD had spoken these words unto Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends: for ye have not spoken of me [the thing that is] right, as my servant Job [hath].

ours: Therefore take unto you now seven bullocks and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you: for him will I accept: lest I deal with you after your folly, in that ye have not spoken of me the thing which is right, like my servant Job.
theirs: Therefore take unto you now seven bullocks and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you: for him will I accept: lest I deal with you [after your] folly, in that ye have not spoken of me [the thing which is] right, like my servant Job.

ours: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went, and did according as the LORD commanded them: the LORD also accepted Job.
theirs: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite [and] Zophar the Naamathite went, and did according as the LORD commanded them: the LORD also accepted Job.

ours: And he called the name of the first, Jemima; and the name of the second, Kezia; and the name of the third, Keren-happuch.
theirs: And he called the name of the first, Jemima; and the name of the second, Kezia; and the name of the third, Kerenhappuch.

ours: And in all the land were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job: and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren.
theirs: And in all the land were no women found [so] fair as the daughters of Job: and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren.

ours: After this lived Job an hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons sons, even four generations.
theirs: After this lived Job an hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons' sons, [even] four generations.

ours: So Job died, being old and full of days.
theirs: So Job died, [being] old and full of days.

ours: BLESSED is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.
theirs: Blessed [is] the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.

ours: But his delight is in the law of the LORD; and in his law doth he meditate day and night.
theirs: But his delight [is] in the law of the LORD; and in his law doth he meditate day and night.

ours: The ungodly are not so: but are like the chaff which the wind driveth away.
theirs: The ungodly [are] not so: but [are] like the chaff which the wind driveth away.

ours: The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against the LORD, and against his anointed, saying,
theirs: The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against the LORD, and against his anointed, [saying],

ours: I will declare the decree: the LORD hath said unto me, Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee.
theirs: I will declare the decree: the LORD hath said unto me, Thou [art] my Son; this day have I begotten thee.

ours: Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession.
theirs: Ask of me, and I shall give [thee] the heathen [for] thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth [for] thy possession.

ours: Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potters vessel.
theirs: Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel.

ours: Kiss the Son, lest he be angry, and ye perish from the way, when his wrath is kindled but a little. Blessed are all they that put their trust in him.
theirs: Kiss the Son, lest he be angry, and ye perish [from] the way, when his wrath is kindled but a little. Blessed [are] all they that put their trust in him.

ours: LORD, how are they increased that trouble me! many are they that rise up against me.
theirs: <<A Psalm of David, when he fled from Absalom his son.>> LORD, how are they increased that trouble me! many [are] they that rise up against me.

ours: Many there be which say of my soul, There is no help for him in God. Selah.
theirs: Many [there be] which say of my soul, [There is] no help for him in God. Selah.

ours: But thou, O LORD, art a shield for me; my glory, and the lifter up of mine head.
theirs: But thou, O LORD, [art] a shield for me; my glory, and the lifter up of mine head.

ours: I will not be afraid of ten thousands of people, that have set themselves against me round about.
theirs: I will not be afraid of ten thousands of people, that have set [themselves] against me round about.

ours: Arise, O LORD; save me, O my God: for thou hast smitten all mine enemies upon the cheek bone; thou hast broken the teeth of the ungodly.
theirs: Arise, O LORD; save me, O my God: for thou hast smitten all mine enemies [upon] the cheek bone; thou hast broken the teeth of the ungodly.

ours: Salvation belongeth unto the LORD: thy blessing is upon thy people. Selah.
theirs: Salvation [belongeth] unto the LORD: thy blessing [is] upon thy people. Selah.

ours: HEAR me when I call, O God of my righteousness: thou hast enlarged me when I was in distress; have mercy upon me, and hear my prayer.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician on Neginoth, A Psalm of David.>> Hear me when I call, O God of my righteousness: thou hast enlarged me [when I was] in distress; have mercy upon me, and hear my prayer.

ours: O ye sons of men, how long will ye turn my glory into shame? how long will ye love vanity, and seek after leasing? Selah.
theirs: O ye sons of men, how long [will ye turn] my glory into shame? [how long] will ye love vanity, [and] seek after leasing? Selah.

ours: There be many that say, Who will shew us any good? LORD, lift thou up the light of thy countenance upon us.
theirs: [There be] many that say, Who will shew us [any] good? LORD, lift thou up the light of thy countenance upon us.

ours: Thou hast put gladness in my heart, more than in the time that their corn and their wine increased.
theirs: Thou hast put gladness in my heart, more than in the time [that] their corn and their wine increased.

ours: GIVE ear to my words, O LORD, consider my meditation.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Nehiloth, A Psalm of David.>> Give ear to my words, O LORD, consider my meditation.

ours: My voice shalt thou hear in the morning, O LORD; in the morning will I direct my prayer unto thee, and will look up.
theirs: My voice shalt thou hear in the morning, O LORD; in the morning will I direct [my prayer] unto thee, and will look up.

ours: For thou art not a God that hath pleasure in wickedness: neither shall evil dwell with thee.
theirs: For thou [art] not a God that hath pleasure in wickedness: neither shall evil dwell with thee.

ours: But as for me, I will come into thy house in the multitude of thy mercy: and in thy fear will I worship toward thy holy temple.
theirs: But as for me, I will come [into] thy house in the multitude of thy mercy: [and] in thy fear will I worship toward thy holy temple.

ours: For there is no faithfulness in their mouth; their inward part is very wickedness; their throat is an open sepulchre; they flatter with their tongue.
theirs: For [there is] no faithfulness in their mouth; their inward part [is] very wickedness; their throat [is] an open sepulchre; they flatter with their tongue.

ours: For thou, LORD, wilt bless the righteous; with favour wilt thou compass him as with a shield.
theirs: For thou, LORD, wilt bless the righteous; with favour wilt thou compass him as [with] a shield.

ours: O LORD, rebuke me not in thine anger, neither chasten me in thy hot displeasure.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician on Neginoth upon Sheminith, A Psalm of David.>> O LORD, rebuke me not in thine anger, neither chasten me in thy hot displeasure.

ours: Have mercy upon me, O LORD; for I am weak: O LORD, heal me; for my bones are vexed.
theirs: Have mercy upon me, O LORD; for I [am] weak: O LORD, heal me; for my bones are vexed.

ours: Return, O LORD, deliver my soul: oh save me for thy mercies sake.
theirs: Return, O LORD, deliver my soul: oh save me for thy mercies' sake.

ours: For in death there is no remembrance of thee: in the grave who shall give thee thanks?
theirs: For in death [there is] no remembrance of thee: in the grave who shall give thee thanks?

ours: Let all mine enemies be ashamed and sore vexed: let them return and be ashamed suddenly.
theirs: Let all mine enemies be ashamed and sore vexed: let them return [and] be ashamed suddenly.

ours: O LORD my God, in thee do I put my trust: save me from all them that persecute me, and deliver me:
theirs: <<Shiggaion of David, which he sang unto the LORD, concerning the words of Cush the Benjamite.>> O LORD my God, in thee do I put my trust: save me from all them that persecute me, and deliver me:

ours: Lest he tear my soul like a lion, rending it in pieces, while there is none to deliver.
theirs: Lest he tear my soul like a lion, rending [it] in pieces, while [there is] none to deliver.

ours: Let the enemy persecute my soul, and take it; yea, let him tread down my life upon the earth, and lay mine honour in the dust. Selah.
theirs: Let the enemy persecute my soul, and take [it]; yea, let him tread down my life upon the earth, and lay mine honour in the dust. Selah.

ours: Arise, O LORD, in thine anger, lift up thyself because of the rage of mine enemies: and awake for me to the judgment that thou hast commanded.
theirs: Arise, O LORD, in thine anger, lift up thyself because of the rage of mine enemies: and awake for me [to] the judgment [that] thou hast commanded.

ours: The LORD shall judge the people: judge me, O LORD, according to my righteousness, and according to mine integrity that is in me.
theirs: The LORD shall judge the people: judge me, O LORD, according to my righteousness, and according to mine integrity [that is] in me.

ours: My defence is of God, which saveth the upright in heart.
theirs: My defence [is] of God, which saveth the upright in heart.

ours: God judgeth the righteous, and God is angry with the wicked every day.
theirs: God judgeth the righteous, and God is angry [with the wicked] every day.

ours: He made a pit, and digged it, and is fallen into the ditch which he made.
theirs: He made a pit, and digged it, and is fallen into the ditch [which] he made.

ours: O LORD our Lord, how excellent is thy name in all the earth! who hast set thy glory above the heavens.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Gittith, A Psalm of David.>> O LORD our Lord, how excellent [is] thy name in all the earth! who hast set thy glory above the heavens.

ours: Thou madest him to have dominion over the works of thy hands; thou hast put all things under his feet:
theirs: Thou madest him to have dominion over the works of thy hands; thou hast put all [things] under his feet:

ours: The fowl of the air, and the fish of the sea, and whatsoever passeth through the paths of the seas.
theirs: The fowl of the air, and the fish of the sea, [and whatsoever] passeth through the paths of the seas.

ours: O LORD our Lord, how excellent is thy name in all the earth!
theirs: O LORD our Lord, how excellent [is] thy name in all the earth!

ours: I WILL praise thee, O LORD, with my whole heart; I will shew forth all thy marvellous works.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Muthlabben, A Psalm of David.>> I will praise [thee], O LORD, with my whole heart; I will shew forth all thy marvellous works.

ours: Have mercy upon me, O LORD; consider my trouble which I suffer of them that hate me, thou that liftest me up from the gates of death:
theirs: Have mercy upon me, O LORD; consider my trouble [which I suffer] of them that hate me, thou that liftest me up from the gates of death:

ours: The heathen are sunk down in the pit that they made: in the net which they hid is their own foot taken.
theirs: The heathen are sunk down in the pit [that] they made: in the net which they hid is their own foot taken.

ours: The LORD is known by the judgment which he executeth: the wicked is snared in the work of his own hands. Higgaion. Selah.
theirs: The LORD is known [by] the judgment [which] he executeth: the wicked is snared in the work of his own hands. Higgaion. Selah.

ours: The wicked shall be turned into hell, and all the nations that forget God.
theirs: The wicked shall be turned into hell, [and] all the nations that forget God.

ours: For the needy shall not alway be forgotten: the expectation of the poor shall not perish for ever.
theirs: For the needy shall not alway be forgotten: the expectation of the poor shall [not] perish for ever.

ours: Put them in fear, O LORD: that the nations may know themselves to be but men. Selah.
theirs: Put them in fear, O LORD: [that] the nations may know themselves [to be but] men. Selah.

ours: WHY standest thou afar off, O LORD? why hidest thou thyself in times of trouble?
theirs: Why standest thou afar off, O LORD? [why] hidest thou [thyself] in times of trouble?

ours: The wicked in his pride doth persecute the poor: let them be taken in the devices that they have imagined.
theirs: The wicked in [his] pride doth persecute the poor: let them be taken in the devices that they have imagined.

ours: For the wicked boasteth of his hearts desire, and blesseth the covetous, whom the LORD abhorreth.
theirs: For the wicked boasteth of his heart's desire, and blesseth the covetous, [whom] the LORD abhorreth.

ours: The wicked, through the pride of his countenance, will not seek after God: God is not in all his thoughts.
theirs: The wicked, through the pride of his countenance, will not seek [after God]: God [is] not in all his thoughts.

ours: His ways are always grievous; thy judgments are far above out of his sight: as for all his enemies, he puffeth at them.
theirs: His ways are always grievous; thy judgments [are] far above out of his sight: [as for] all his enemies, he puffeth at them.

ours: He hath said in his heart, I shall not be moved: for I shall never be in adversity.
theirs: He hath said in his heart, I shall not be moved: for [I shall] never [be] in adversity.

ours: His mouth is full of cursing and deceit and fraud: under his tongue is mischief and vanity.
theirs: His mouth is full of cursing and deceit and fraud: under his tongue [is] mischief and vanity.

ours: He croucheth, and humbleth himself, that the poor may fall by his strong ones.
theirs: He croucheth, [and] humbleth himself, that the poor may fall by his strong ones.

ours: He hath said in his heart, God hath forgotten: he hideth his face; he will never see it.
theirs: He hath said in his heart, God hath forgotten: he hideth his face; he will never see [it].

ours: Wherefore doth the wicked contemn God? he hath said in his heart, Thou wilt not require it.
theirs: Wherefore doth the wicked contemn God? he hath said in his heart, Thou wilt not require [it].

ours: Thou hast seen it; for thou beholdest mischief and spite, to requite it with thy hand: the poor committeth himself unto thee; thou art the helper of the fatherless.
theirs: Thou hast seen [it]; for thou beholdest mischief and spite, to requite [it] with thy hand: the poor committeth himself unto thee; thou art the helper of the fatherless.

ours: Break thou the arm of the wicked and the evil man: seek out his wickedness till thou find none.
theirs: Break thou the arm of the wicked and the evil [man]: seek out his wickedness [till] thou find none.

ours: The LORD is King for ever and ever: the heathen are perished out of his land.
theirs: The LORD [is] King for ever and ever: the heathen are perished out of his land.

ours: IN the LORD put I my trust: how say ye to my soul, Flee as a bird to your mountain?
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, [A Psalm] of David.>> In the LORD put I my trust: how say ye to my soul, Flee [as] a bird to your mountain?

ours: For, lo, the wicked bend their bow, they make ready their arrow upon the string, that they may privily shoot at the upright in heart.
theirs: For, lo, the wicked bend [their] bow, they make ready their arrow upon the string, that they may privily shoot at the upright in heart.

ours: The LORD is in his holy temple, the LORDs throne is in heaven: his eyes behold, his eyelids try, the children of men.
theirs: The LORD [is] in his holy temple, the LORD's throne [is] in heaven: his eyes behold, his eyelids try, the children of men.

ours: Upon the wicked he shall rain snares, fire and brimstone, and an horrible tempest: this shall be the portion of their cup.
theirs: Upon the wicked he shall rain snares, fire and brimstone, and an horrible tempest: [this shall be] the portion of their cup.

ours: HELP, LORD; for the godly man ceaseth; for the faithful fail from among the children of men.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Sheminith, A Psalm of David.>> Help, LORD; for the godly man ceaseth; for the faithful fail from among the children of men.

ours: They speak vanity every one with his neighbour: with flattering lips and with a double heart do they speak.
theirs: They speak vanity every one with his neighbour: [with] flattering lips [and] with a double heart do they speak.

ours: The LORD shall cut off all flattering lips, and the tongue that speaketh proud things:
theirs: The LORD shall cut off all flattering lips, [and] the tongue that speaketh proud things:

ours: Who have said, With our tongue will we prevail; our lips are our own: who is lord over us?
theirs: Who have said, With our tongue will we prevail; our lips [are] our own: who [is] lord over us?

ours: For the oppression of the poor, for the sighing of the needy, now will I arise, saith the LORD; I will set him in safety from him that puffeth at him.
theirs: For the oppression of the poor, for the sighing of the needy, now will I arise, saith the LORD; I will set [him] in safety [from him that] puffeth at him.

ours: The words of the LORD are pure words: as silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times.
theirs: The words of the LORD [are] pure words: [as] silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times.

ours: HOW long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me?
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me?

ours: How long shall I take counsel in my soul, having sorrow in my heart daily? how long shall mine enemy be exalted over me?
theirs: How long shall I take counsel in my soul, [having] sorrow in my heart daily? how long shall mine enemy be exalted over me?

ours: Consider and hear me, O LORD my God: lighten mine eyes, lest I sleep the sleep of death;
theirs: Consider [and] hear me, O LORD my God: lighten mine eyes, lest I sleep the [sleep of] death;

ours: Lest mine enemy say, I have prevailed against him; and those that trouble me rejoice when I am moved.
theirs: Lest mine enemy say, I have prevailed against him; [and] those that trouble me rejoice when I am moved.

ours: THE fool hath said in his heart, There is no God. They are corrupt, they have done abominable works, there is none that doeth good.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, [A Psalm] of David.>> The fool hath said in his heart, [There is] no God. They are corrupt, they have done abominable works, [there is] none that doeth good.

ours: The LORD looked down from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there were any that did understand, and seek God.
theirs: The LORD looked down from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there were any that did understand, [and] seek God.

ours: They are all gone aside, they are all together become filthy: there is none that doeth good, no, not one.
theirs: They are all gone aside, they are [all] together become filthy: [there is] none that doeth good, no, not one.

ours: Have all the workers of iniquity no knowledge? who eat up my people as they eat bread, and call not upon the LORD.
theirs: Have all the workers of iniquity no knowledge? who eat up my people [as] they eat bread, and call not upon the LORD.

ours: There were they in great fear: for God is in the generation of the righteous.
theirs: There were they in great fear: for God [is] in the generation of the righteous.

ours: Ye have shamed the counsel of the poor, because the LORD is his refuge.
theirs: Ye have shamed the counsel of the poor, because the LORD [is] his refuge.

ours: Oh that the salvation of Israel were come out of Zion! when the LORD bringeth back the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.
theirs: Oh that the salvation of Israel [were come] out of Zion! when the LORD bringeth back the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice, [and] Israel shall be glad.

ours: LORD, who shall abide in thy tabernacle? who shall dwell in thy holy hill?
theirs: <<A Psalm of David.>> LORD, who shall abide in thy tabernacle? who shall dwell in thy holy hill?

ours: He that backbiteth not with his tongue, nor doeth evil to his neighbour, nor taketh up a reproach against his neighbour.
theirs: [He that] backbiteth not with his tongue, nor doeth evil to his neighbour, nor taketh up a reproach against his neighbour.

ours: In whose eyes a vile person is contemned; but he honoureth them that fear the LORD. He that sweareth to his own hurt, and changeth not.
theirs: In whose eyes a vile person is contemned; but he honoureth them that fear the LORD. [He that] sweareth to [his own] hurt, and changeth not.

ours: He that putteth not out his money to usury, nor taketh reward against the innocent. He that doeth these things shall never be moved.
theirs: [He that] putteth not out his money to usury, nor taketh reward against the innocent. He that doeth these [things] shall never be moved.

ours: PRESERVE me, O God: for in thee do I put my trust.
theirs: <<Michtam of David.>> Preserve me, O God: for in thee do I put my trust.

ours: O my soul, thou hast said unto the LORD, Thou art my Lord: my goodness extendeth not to thee;
theirs: [O my soul], thou hast said unto the LORD, Thou [art] my Lord: my goodness [extendeth] not to thee;

ours: But to the saints that are in the earth, and to the excellent, in whom is all my delight.
theirs: [But] to the saints that [are] in the earth, and [to] the excellent, in whom [is] all my delight.

ours: Their sorrows shall be multiplied that hasten after another god: their drink offerings of blood will I not offer, nor take up their names into my lips.
theirs: Their sorrows shall be multiplied [that] hasten [after] another [god]: their drink offerings of blood will I not offer, nor take up their names into my lips.

ours: The LORD is the portion of mine inheritance and of my cup: thou maintainest my lot.
theirs: The LORD [is] the portion of mine inheritance and of my cup: thou maintainest my lot.

ours: The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places; yea, I have a goodly heritage.
theirs: The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant [places]; yea, I have a goodly heritage.

ours: I have set the LORD always before me: because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.
theirs: I have set the LORD always before me: because [he is] at my right hand, I shall not be moved.

ours: Thou wilt shew me the path of life: in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore.
theirs: Thou wilt shew me the path of life: in thy presence [is] fulness of joy; at thy right hand [there are] pleasures for evermore.

ours: HEAR the right, O LORD, attend unto my cry, give ear unto my prayer, that goeth not out of feigned lips.
theirs: <<A Prayer of David.>> Hear the right, O LORD, attend unto my cry, give ear unto my prayer, [that goeth] not out of feigned lips.

ours: Thou hast proved mine heart; thou hast visited me in the night; thou hast tried me, and shalt find nothing; I am purposed that my mouth shall not transgress.
theirs: Thou hast proved mine heart; thou hast visited [me] in the night; thou hast tried me, [and] shalt find nothing; I am purposed [that] my mouth shall not transgress.

ours: Concerning the works of men, by the word of thy lips I have kept me from the paths of the destroyer.
theirs: Concerning the works of men, by the word of thy lips I have kept [me from] the paths of the destroyer.

ours: Hold up my goings in thy paths, that my footsteps slip not.
theirs: Hold up my goings in thy paths, [that] my footsteps slip not.

ours: I have called upon thee, for thou wilt hear me, O God: incline thine ear unto me, and hear my speech.
theirs: I have called upon thee, for thou wilt hear me, O God: incline thine ear unto me, [and hear] my speech.

ours: Shew thy marvellous lovingkindness, O thou that savest by thy right hand them which put their trust in thee from those that rise up against them.
theirs: Shew thy marvellous lovingkindness, O thou that savest by thy right hand them which put their trust [in thee] from those that rise up [against them].

ours: From the wicked that oppress me, from my deadly enemies, who compass me about.
theirs: From the wicked that oppress me, [from] my deadly enemies, [who] compass me about.

ours: Like as a lion that is greedy of his prey, and as it were a young lion lurking in secret places.
theirs: Like as a lion [that] is greedy of his prey, and as it were a young lion lurking in secret places.

ours: Arise, O LORD, disappoint him, cast him down: deliver my soul from the wicked, which is thy sword:
theirs: Arise, O LORD, disappoint him, cast him down: deliver my soul from the wicked, [which is] thy sword:

ours: From men which are thy hand, O LORD, from men of the world, which have their portion in this life, and whose belly thou fillest with thy hid treasure: they are full of children, and leave the rest of their substance to their babes.
theirs: From men [which are] thy hand, O LORD, from men of the world, [which have] their portion in [this] life, and whose belly thou fillest with thy hid [treasure]: they are full of children, and leave the rest of their [substance] to their babes.

ours: I WILL love thee, O LORD, my strength.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, [A Psalm] of David, the servant of the LORD, who spake unto the LORD the words of this song in the day [that] the LORD delivered him from the hand of all his enemies, and from the hand of Saul: And he said,>> I will love thee, O LORD, my strength.

ours: The LORD is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my strength, in whom I will trust; my buckler, and the horn of my salvation, and my high tower.
theirs: The LORD [is] my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my strength, in whom I will trust; my buckler, and the horn of my salvation, [and] my high tower.

ours: I will call upon the LORD, who is worthy to be praised: so shall I be saved from mine enemies.
theirs: I will call upon the LORD, [who is worthy] to be praised: so shall I be saved from mine enemies.

ours: In my distress I called upon the LORD, and cried unto my God: he heard my voice out of his temple, and my cry came before him, even into his ears.
theirs: In my distress I called upon the LORD, and cried unto my God: he heard my voice out of his temple, and my cry came before him, [even] into his ears.

ours: He bowed the heavens also, and came down: and darkness was under his feet.
theirs: He bowed the heavens also, and came down: and darkness [was] under his feet.

ours: He made darkness his secret place; his pavilion round about him were dark waters and thick clouds of the skies.
theirs: He made darkness his secret place; his pavilion round about him [were] dark waters [and] thick clouds of the skies.

ours: At the brightness that was before him his thick clouds passed, hail stones and coals of fire.
theirs: At the brightness [that was] before him his thick clouds passed, hail [stones] and coals of fire.

ours: The LORD also thundered in the heavens, and the Highest gave his voice; hail stones and coals of fire.
theirs: The LORD also thundered in the heavens, and the Highest gave his voice; hail [stones] and coals of fire.

ours: For all his judgments were before me, and I did not put away his statutes from me.
theirs: For all his judgments [were] before me, and I did not put away his statutes from me.

ours: As for God, his way is perfect: the word of the LORD is tried: he is a buckler to all those that trust in him.
theirs: [As for] God, his way [is] perfect: the word of the LORD is tried: he [is] a buckler to all those that trust in him.

ours: For who is God save the LORD? or who is a rock save our God?
theirs: For who [is] God save the LORD? or who [is] a rock save our God?

ours: It is God that girdeth me with strength, and maketh my way perfect.
theirs: [It is] God that girdeth me with strength, and maketh my way perfect.

ours: He maketh my feet like hinds feet, and setteth me upon my high places.
theirs: He maketh my feet like hinds' [feet], and setteth me upon my high places.

ours: They cried, but there was none to save them: even unto the LORD, but he answered them not.
theirs: They cried, but [there was] none to save [them: even] unto the LORD, but he answered them not.

ours: Thou hast delivered me from the strivings of the people; and thou hast made me the head of the heathen: a people whom I have not known shall serve me.
theirs: Thou hast delivered me from the strivings of the people; [and] thou hast made me the head of the heathen: a people [whom] I have not known shall serve me.

ours: The LORD liveth; and blessed be my rock; and let the God of my salvation be exalted.
theirs: The LORD liveth; and blessed [be] my rock; and let the God of my salvation be exalted.

ours: It is God that avengeth me, and subdueth the people under me.
theirs: [It is] God that avengeth me, and subdueth the people under me.

ours: THE heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.

ours: There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard.
theirs: [There is] no speech nor language, [where] their voice is not heard.

ours: Which is as a bridegroom coming out of his chamber, and rejoiceth as a strong man to run a race.
theirs: Which [is] as a bridegroom coming out of his chamber, [and] rejoiceth as a strong man to run a race.

ours: His going forth is from the end of the heaven, and his circuit unto the ends of it: and there is nothing hid from the heat thereof.
theirs: His going forth [is] from the end of the heaven, and his circuit unto the ends of it: and there is nothing hid from the heat thereof.

ours: The law of the LORD is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple.
theirs: The law of the LORD [is] perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the LORD [is] sure, making wise the simple.

ours: The statutes of the LORD are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the LORD is pure, enlightening the eyes.
theirs: The statutes of the LORD [are] right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the LORD [is] pure, enlightening the eyes.

ours: The fear of the LORD is clean, enduring for ever: the judgments of the LORD are true and righteous altogether.
theirs: The fear of the LORD [is] clean, enduring for ever: the judgments of the LORD [are] true [and] righteous altogether.

ours: More to be desired are they than gold, yea, than much fine gold: sweeter also than honey and the honeycomb.
theirs: More to be desired [are they] than gold, yea, than much fine gold: sweeter also than honey and the honeycomb.

ours: Moreover by them is thy servant warned: and in keeping of them there is great reward.
theirs: Moreover by them is thy servant warned: [and] in keeping of them [there is] great reward.

ours: Who can understand his errors? cleanse thou me from secret faults.
theirs: Who can understand [his] errors? cleanse thou me from secret [faults].

ours: Keep back thy servant also from presumptuous sins; let them not have dominion over me: then shall I be upright, and I shall be innocent from the great transgression.
theirs: Keep back thy servant also from presumptuous [sins]; let them not have dominion over me: then shall I be upright, and I shall be innocent from the great transgression.

ours: THE LORD hear thee in the day of trouble; the name of the God of Jacob defend thee;
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> The LORD hear thee in the day of trouble; the name of the God of Jacob defend thee;

ours: We will rejoice in thy salvation, and in the name of our God we will set up our banners: the LORD fulfil all thy petitions.
theirs: We will rejoice in thy salvation, and in the name of our God we will set up [our] banners: the LORD fulfil all thy petitions.

ours: Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will remember the name of the LORD our God.
theirs: Some [trust] in chariots, and some in horses: but we will remember the name of the LORD our God.

ours: THE king shall joy in thy strength, O LORD; and in thy salvation how greatly shall he rejoice!
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> The king shall joy in thy strength, O LORD; and in thy salvation how greatly shall he rejoice!

ours: Thou hast given him his hearts desire, and hast not withholden the request of his lips. Selah.
theirs: Thou hast given him his heart's desire, and hast not withholden the request of his lips. Selah.

ours: He asked life of thee, and thou gavest it him, even length of days for ever and ever.
theirs: He asked life of thee, [and] thou gavest [it] him, [even] length of days for ever and ever.

ours: His glory is great in thy salvation: honour and majesty hast thou laid upon him.
theirs: His glory [is] great in thy salvation: honour and majesty hast thou laid upon him.

ours: For they intended evil against thee: they imagined a mischievous device, which they are not able to perform.
theirs: For they intended evil against thee: they imagined a mischievous device, [which] they are not able [to perform].

ours: Therefore shalt thou make them turn their back, when thou shalt make ready thine arrows upon thy strings against the face of them.
theirs: Therefore shalt thou make them turn their back, [when] thou shalt make ready [thine arrows] upon thy strings against the face of them.

ours: Be thou exalted, LORD, in thine own strength: so will we sing and praise thy power.
theirs: Be thou exalted, LORD, in thine own strength: [so] will we sing and praise thy power.

ours: MY God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? why art thou so far from helping me, and from the words of my roaring?
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Aijeleth Shahar, A Psalm of David.>> My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? [why art thou so] far from helping me, [and from] the words of my roaring?

ours: But thou art holy, O thou that inhabitest the praises of Israel.
theirs: But thou [art] holy, [O thou] that inhabitest the praises of Israel.

ours: But I am a worm, and no man; a reproach of men, and despised of the people.
theirs: But I [am] a worm, and no man; a reproach of men, and despised of the people.

ours: All they that see me laugh me to scorn: they shoot out the lip, they shake the head, saying,
theirs: All they that see me laugh me to scorn: they shoot out the lip, they shake the head, [saying],

ours: He trusted on the LORD that he would deliver him: let him deliver him, seeing he delighted in him.
theirs: He trusted on the LORD [that] he would deliver him: let him deliver him, seeing he delighted in him.

ours: But thou art he that took me out of the womb: thou didst make me hope when I was upon my mothers breasts.
theirs: But thou [art] he that took me out of the womb: thou didst make me hope [when I was] upon my mother's breasts.

ours: I was cast upon thee from the womb: thou art my God from my mothers belly.
theirs: I was cast upon thee from the womb: thou [art] my God from my mother's belly.

ours: Be not far from me; for trouble is near; for there is none to help.
theirs: Be not far from me; for trouble [is] near; for [there is] none to help.

ours: Many bulls have compassed me: strong bulls of Bashan have beset me round.
theirs: Many bulls have compassed me: strong [bulls] of Bashan have beset me round.

ours: They gaped upon me with their mouths, as a ravening and a roaring lion.
theirs: They gaped upon me [with] their mouths, [as] a ravening and a roaring lion.

ours: I may tell all my bones: they look and stare upon me.
theirs: I may tell all my bones: they look [and] stare upon me.

ours: Save me from the lions mouth: for thou hast heard me from the horns of the unicorns.
theirs: Save me from the lion's mouth: for thou hast heard me from the horns of the unicorns.

ours: My praise shall be of thee in the great congregation: I will pay my vows before them that fear him.
theirs: My praise [shall be] of thee in the great congregation: I will pay my vows before them that fear him.

ours: For the kingdom is the LORDs: and he is the governor among the nations.
theirs: For the kingdom [is] the LORD's: and he [is] the governor among the nations.

ours: All they that be fat upon earth shall eat and worship: all they that go down to the dust shall bow before him: and none can keep alive his own soul.
theirs: All [they that be] fat upon earth shall eat and worship: all they that go down to the dust shall bow before him: and none can keep alive his own soul.

ours: They shall come, and shall declare his righteousness unto a people that shall be born, that he hath done this.
theirs: They shall come, and shall declare his righteousness unto a people that shall be born, that he hath done [this].

ours: THE LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
theirs: <<A Psalm of David.>> The LORD [is] my shepherd; I shall not want.

ours: He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his names sake.
theirs: He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name's sake.

ours: Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.
theirs: Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou [art] with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.

ours: THE earth is the LORD's, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein.
theirs: <<A Psalm of David.>> The earth [is] the LORD's, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein.
