ours: This is the generation of them that seek him, that seek thy face, O Jacob. Selah.
theirs: This [is] the generation of them that seek him, that seek thy face, O Jacob. Selah.

ours: Who is this King of glory? The LORD strong and mighty, the LORD mighty in battle.
theirs: Who [is] this King of glory? The LORD strong and mighty, the LORD mighty in battle.

ours: Lift up your heads, O ye gates; even lift them up, ye everlasting doors; and the King of glory shall come in.
theirs: Lift up your heads, O ye gates; even lift [them] up, ye everlasting doors; and the King of glory shall come in.

ours: Who is this King of glory? The LORD of hosts, he is the King of glory. Selah.
theirs: Who is this King of glory? The LORD of hosts, he [is] the King of glory. Selah.

ours: UNTO thee, O LORD, do I lift up my soul.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David.>> Unto thee, O LORD, do I lift up my soul.

ours: Lead me in thy truth, and teach me: for thou art the God of my salvation; on thee do I wait all the day.
theirs: Lead me in thy truth, and teach me: for thou [art] the God of my salvation; on thee do I wait all the day.

ours: Remember, O LORD, thy tender mercies and thy lovingkindnesses; for they have been ever of old.
theirs: Remember, O LORD, thy tender mercies and thy lovingkindnesses; for they [have been] ever of old.

ours: Remember not the sins of my youth, nor my transgressions: according to thy mercy remember thou me for thy goodness sake, O LORD.
theirs: Remember not the sins of my youth, nor my transgressions: according to thy mercy remember thou me for thy goodness' sake, O LORD.

ours: Good and upright is the LORD: therefore will he teach sinners in the way.
theirs: Good and upright [is] the LORD: therefore will he teach sinners in the way.

ours: All the paths of the LORD are mercy and truth unto such as keep his covenant and his testimonies.
theirs: All the paths of the LORD [are] mercy and truth unto such as keep his covenant and his testimonies.

ours: For thy names sake, O LORD, pardon mine iniquity; for it is great.
theirs: For thy name's sake, O LORD, pardon mine iniquity; for it [is] great.

ours: What man is he that feareth the LORD? him shall he teach in the way that he shall choose.
theirs: What man [is] he that feareth the LORD? him shall he teach in the way [that] he shall choose.

ours: The secret of the LORD is with them that fear him; and he will shew them his covenant.
theirs: The secret of the LORD [is] with them that fear him; and he will shew them his covenant.

ours: Mine eyes are ever toward the LORD; for he shall pluck my feet out of the net.
theirs: Mine eyes [are] ever toward the LORD; for he shall pluck my feet out of the net.

ours: Turn thee unto me, and have mercy upon me; for I am desolate and afflicted.
theirs: Turn thee unto me, and have mercy upon me; for I [am] desolate and afflicted.

ours: The troubles of my heart are enlarged: O bring thou me out of my distresses.
theirs: The troubles of my heart are enlarged: [O] bring thou me out of my distresses.

ours: JUDGE me, O LORD; for I have walked in mine integrity: I have trusted also in the LORD; therefore I shall not slide.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David.>> Judge me, O LORD; for I have walked in mine integrity: I have trusted also in the LORD; [therefore] I shall not slide.

ours: For thy lovingkindness is before mine eyes: and I have walked in thy truth.
theirs: For thy lovingkindness [is] before mine eyes: and I have walked in thy truth.

ours: In whose hands is mischief, and their right hand is full of bribes.
theirs: In whose hands [is] mischief, and their right hand is full of bribes.

ours: THE LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David.>> The LORD [is] my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD [is] the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?

ours: When the wicked, even mine enemies and my foes, came upon me to eat up my flesh, they stumbled and fell.
theirs: When the wicked, [even] mine enemies and my foes, came upon me to eat up my flesh, they stumbled and fell.

ours: Though an host should encamp against me, my heart shall not fear: though war should rise against me, in this will I be confident.
theirs: Though an host should encamp against me, my heart shall not fear: though war should rise against me, in this [will] I [be] confident.

ours: One thing have I desired of the LORD, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to inquire in his temple.
theirs: One [thing] have I desired of the LORD, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to inquire in his temple.

ours: Hear, O LORD, when I cry with my voice: have mercy also upon me, and answer me.
theirs: Hear, O LORD, [when] I cry with my voice: have mercy also upon me, and answer me.

ours: When thou saidst, Seek ye my face; my heart said unto thee, Thy face, LORD, will I seek.
theirs: [When thou saidst], Seek ye my face; my heart said unto thee, Thy face, LORD, will I seek.

ours: Hide not thy face far from me; put not thy servant away in anger: thou hast been my help; leave me not, neither forsake me, O God of my salvation.
theirs: Hide not thy face [far] from me; put not thy servant away in anger: thou hast been my help; leave me not, neither forsake me, O God of my salvation.

ours: I had fainted, unless I had believed to see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living.
theirs: [I had fainted], unless I had believed to see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living.

ours: UNTO thee will I cry, O LORD my rock; be not silent to me: lest, if thou be silent to me, I become like them that go down into the pit.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David.>> Unto thee will I cry, O LORD my rock; be not silent to me: lest, [if] thou be silent to me, I become like them that go down into the pit.

ours: Draw me not away with the wicked, and with the workers of iniquity, which speak peace to their neighbours, but mischief is in their hearts.
theirs: Draw me not away with the wicked, and with the workers of iniquity, which speak peace to their neighbours, but mischief [is] in their hearts.

ours: Blessed be the LORD, because he hath heard the voice of my supplications.
theirs: Blessed [be] the LORD, because he hath heard the voice of my supplications.

ours: The LORD is my strength and my shield; my heart trusted in him, and I am helped: therefore my heart greatly rejoiceth; and with my song will I praise him.
theirs: The LORD [is] my strength and my shield; my heart trusted in him, and I am helped: therefore my heart greatly rejoiceth; and with my song will I praise him.

ours: The LORD is their strength, and he is the saving strength of his anointed.
theirs: The LORD [is] their strength, and he [is] the saving strength of his anointed.

ours: GIVE unto the LORD, O ye mighty, give unto the LORD glory and strength.
theirs: <<A Psalm of David.>> Give unto the LORD, O ye mighty, give unto the LORD glory and strength.

ours: The voice of the LORD is upon the waters: the God of glory thundereth: the LORD is upon many waters.
theirs: The voice of the LORD [is] upon the waters: the God of glory thundereth: the LORD [is] upon many waters.

ours: The voice of the LORD is powerful; the voice of the LORD is full of majesty.
theirs: The voice of the LORD [is] powerful; the voice of the LORD [is] full of majesty.

ours: The voice of the LORD maketh the hinds to calve, and discovereth the forests: and in his temple doth every one speak of his glory.
theirs: The voice of the LORD maketh the hinds to calve, and discovereth the forests: and in his temple doth every one speak of [his] glory.

ours: I WILL extol thee, O LORD; for thou hast lifted me up, and hast not made my foes to rejoice over me.
theirs: <<A Psalm [and] Song [at] the dedication of the house of David.>> I will extol thee, O LORD; for thou hast lifted me up, and hast not made my foes to rejoice over me.

ours: For his anger endureth but a moment; in his favour is life: weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.
theirs: For his anger [endureth but] a moment; in his favour [is] life: weeping may endure for a night, but joy [cometh] in the morning.

ours: LORD, by thy favour thou hast made my mountain to stand strong: thou didst hide thy face, and I was troubled.
theirs: LORD, by thy favour thou hast made my mountain to stand strong: thou didst hide thy face, [and] I was troubled.

ours: What profit is there in my blood, when I go down to the pit? Shall the dust praise thee? shall it declare thy truth?
theirs: What profit [is there] in my blood, when I go down to the pit? Shall the dust praise thee? shall it declare thy truth?

ours: To the end that my glory may sing praise to thee, and not be silent. O LORD my God, I will give thanks unto thee for ever.
theirs: To the end that [my] glory may sing praise to thee, and not be silent. O LORD my God, I will give thanks unto thee for ever.

ours: IN thee, O LORD, do I put my trust; let me never be ashamed: deliver me in thy righteousness.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> In thee, O LORD, do I put my trust; let me never be ashamed: deliver me in thy righteousness.

ours: For thou art my rock and my fortress; therefore for thy names sake lead me, and guide me.
theirs: For thou [art] my rock and my fortress; therefore for thy name's sake lead me, and guide me.

ours: Pull me out of the net that they have laid privily for me: for thou art my strength.
theirs: Pull me out of the net that they have laid privily for me: for thou [art] my strength.

ours: Have mercy upon me, O LORD, for I am in trouble: mine eye is consumed with grief, yea, my soul and my belly.
theirs: Have mercy upon me, O LORD, for I am in trouble: mine eye is consumed with grief, [yea], my soul and my belly.

ours: For I have heard the slander of many: fear was on every side: while they took counsel together against me, they devised to take away my life.
theirs: For I have heard the slander of many: fear [was] on every side: while they took counsel together against me, they devised to take away my life.

ours: But I trusted in thee, O LORD: I said, Thou art my God.
theirs: But I trusted in thee, O LORD: I said, Thou [art] my God.

ours: My times are in thy hand: deliver me from the hand of mine enemies, and from them that persecute me.
theirs: My times [are] in thy hand: deliver me from the hand of mine enemies, and from them that persecute me.

ours: Make thy face to shine upon thy servant: save me for thy mercies sake.
theirs: Make thy face to shine upon thy servant: save me for thy mercies' sake.

ours: Let me not be ashamed, O LORD; for I have called upon thee: let the wicked be ashamed, and let them be silent in the grave.
theirs: Let me not be ashamed, O LORD; for I have called upon thee: let the wicked be ashamed, [and] let them be silent in the grave.

ours: Oh how great is thy goodness, which thou hast laid up for them that fear thee; which thou hast wrought for them that trust in thee before the sons of men!
theirs: [Oh] how great [is] thy goodness, which thou hast laid up for them that fear thee; [which] thou hast wrought for them that trust in thee before the sons of men!

ours: Blessed be the LORD: for he hath shewed me his marvellous kindness in a strong city.
theirs: Blessed [be] the LORD: for he hath shewed me his marvellous kindness in a strong city.

ours: O love the LORD, all ye his saints: for the LORD preserveth the faithful, and plentifully rewardeth the proud doer.
theirs: O love the LORD, all ye his saints: [for] the LORD preserveth the faithful, and plentifully rewardeth the proud doer.

ours: BLESSED is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David, Maschil.>> Blessed [is he whose] transgression [is] forgiven, [whose] sin [is] covered.

ours: Blessed is the man unto whom the LORD imputeth not iniquity, and in whose spirit there is no guile.
theirs: Blessed [is] the man unto whom the LORD imputeth not iniquity, and in whose spirit [there is] no guile.

ours: Thou art my hiding place; thou shalt preserve me from trouble; thou shalt compass me about with songs of deliverance. Selah.
theirs: Thou [art] my hiding place; thou shalt preserve me from trouble; thou shalt compass me about with songs of deliverance. Selah.

ours: Be ye not as the horse, or as the mule, which have no understanding: whose mouth must be held in with bit and bridle, lest they come near unto thee.
theirs: Be ye not as the horse, [or] as the mule, [which] have no understanding: whose mouth must be held in with bit and bridle, lest they come near unto thee.

ours: Many sorrows shall be to the wicked: but he that trusteth in the LORD, mercy shall compass him about.
theirs: Many sorrows [shall be] to the wicked: but he that trusteth in the LORD, mercy shall compass him about.

ours: Be glad in the LORD, and rejoice, ye righteous: and shout for joy, all ye that are upright in heart.
theirs: Be glad in the LORD, and rejoice, ye righteous: and shout for joy, all [ye that are] upright in heart.

ours: REJOICE in the LORD, O ye righteous: for praise is comely for the upright.
theirs: Rejoice in the LORD, O ye righteous: [for] praise is comely for the upright.

ours: Praise the LORD with harp: sing unto him with the psaltery and an instrument of ten strings.
theirs: Praise the LORD with harp: sing unto him with the psaltery [and] an instrument of ten strings.

ours: For the word of the LORD is right; and all his works are done in truth.
theirs: For the word of the LORD [is] right; and all his works [are done] in truth.

ours: For he spake, and it was done; he commanded, and it stood fast.
theirs: For he spake, and it was [done]; he commanded, and it stood fast.

ours: Blessed is the nation whose God is the LORD; and the people whom he hath chosen for his own inheritance.
theirs: Blessed [is] the nation whose God [is] the LORD; [and] the people [whom] he hath chosen for his own inheritance.

ours: An horse is a vain thing for safety: neither shall he deliver any by his great strength.
theirs: An horse [is] a vain thing for safety: neither shall he deliver [any] by his great strength.

ours: Behold, the eye of the LORD is upon them that fear him, upon them that hope in his mercy;
theirs: Behold, the eye of the LORD [is] upon them that fear him, upon them that hope in his mercy;

ours: Our soul waiteth for the LORD: he is our help and our shield.
theirs: Our soul waiteth for the LORD: he [is] our help and our shield.

ours: I WILL bless the LORD at all times: his praise shall continually be in my mouth.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David, when he changed his behaviour before Abimelech; who drove him away, and he departed.>> I will bless the LORD at all times: his praise [shall] continually [be] in my mouth.

ours: My soul shall make her boast in the LORD: the humble shall hear thereof, and be glad.
theirs: My soul shall make her boast in the LORD: the humble shall hear [thereof], and be glad.

ours: This poor man cried, and the LORD heard him, and saved him out of all his troubles.
theirs: This poor man cried, and the LORD heard [him], and saved him out of all his troubles.

ours: O taste and see that the LORD is good: blessed is the man that trusteth in him.
theirs: O taste and see that the LORD [is] good: blessed [is] the man [that] trusteth in him.

ours: O fear the LORD, ye his saints: for there is no want to them that fear him.
theirs: O fear the LORD, ye his saints: for [there is] no want to them that fear him.

ours: The young lions do lack, and suffer hunger: but they that seek the LORD shall not want any good thing.
theirs: The young lions do lack, and suffer hunger: but they that seek the LORD shall not want any good [thing].

ours: What man is he that desireth life, and loveth many days, that he may see good?
theirs: What man [is he that] desireth life, [and] loveth [many] days, that he may see good?

ours: The eyes of the LORD are upon the righteous, and his ears are open unto their cry.
theirs: The eyes of the LORD [are] upon the righteous, and his ears [are open] unto their cry.

ours: The face of the LORD is against them that do evil, to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth.
theirs: The face of the LORD [is] against them that do evil, to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth.

ours: The righteous cry, and the LORD heareth, and delivereth them out of all their troubles.
theirs: [The righteous] cry, and the LORD heareth, and delivereth them out of all their troubles.

ours: The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.
theirs: The LORD [is] nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.

ours: Many are the afflictions of the righteous: but the LORD delivereth him out of them all.
theirs: Many [are] the afflictions of the righteous: but the LORD delivereth him out of them all.

ours: PLEAD my cause, O LORD, with them that strive with me: fight against them that fight against me.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David.>> Plead [my cause], O LORD, with them that strive with me: fight against them that fight against me.

ours: Draw out also the spear, and stop the way against them that persecute me: say unto my soul, I am thy salvation.
theirs: Draw out also the spear, and stop [the way] against them that persecute me: say unto my soul, I [am] thy salvation.

ours: Let them be as chaff before the wind: and let the angel of the LORD chase them.
theirs: Let them be as chaff before the wind: and let the angel of the LORD chase [them].

ours: For without cause have they hid for me their net in a pit, which without cause they have digged for my soul.
theirs: For without cause have they hid for me their net [in] a pit, [which] without cause they have digged for my soul.

ours: All my bones shall say, LORD, who is like unto thee, which deliverest the poor from him that is too strong for him, yea, the poor and the needy from him that spoileth him?
theirs: All my bones shall say, LORD, who [is] like unto thee, which deliverest the poor from him that is too strong for him, yea, the poor and the needy from him that spoileth him?

ours: False witnesses did rise up; they laid to my charge things that I knew not.
theirs: False witnesses did rise up; they laid to my charge [things] that I knew not.

ours: They rewarded me evil for good to the spoiling of my soul.
theirs: They rewarded me evil for good [to] the spoiling of my soul.

ours: But as for me, when they were sick, my clothing was sackcloth: I humbled my soul with fasting; and my prayer returned into mine own bosom.
theirs: But as for me, when they were sick, my clothing [was] sackcloth: I humbled my soul with fasting; and my prayer returned into mine own bosom.

ours: I behaved myself as though he had been my friend or brother: I bowed down heavily, as one that mourneth for his mother.
theirs: I behaved myself as though [he had been] my friend [or] brother: I bowed down heavily, as one that mourneth [for his] mother.

ours: But in mine adversity they rejoiced, and gathered themselves together: yea, the abjects gathered themselves together against me, and I knew it not; they did tear me, and ceased not:
theirs: But in mine adversity they rejoiced, and gathered themselves together: [yea], the abjects gathered themselves together against me, and I knew [it] not; they did tear [me], and ceased not:

ours: Let not them that are mine enemies wrongfully rejoice over me: neither let them wink with the eye that hate me without a cause.
theirs: Let not them that are mine enemies wrongfully rejoice over me: [neither] let them wink with the eye that hate me without a cause.

ours: For they speak not peace: but they devise deceitful matters against them that are quiet in the land.
theirs: For they speak not peace: but they devise deceitful matters against [them that are] quiet in the land.

ours: Yea, they opened their mouth wide against me, and said, Aha, aha, our eye hath seen it.
theirs: Yea, they opened their mouth wide against me, [and] said, Aha, aha, our eye hath seen [it].

ours: This thou hast seen, O LORD: keep not silence: O Lord, be not far from me.
theirs: [This] thou hast seen, O LORD: keep not silence: O Lord, be not far from me.

ours: Stir up thyself, and awake to my judgment, even unto my cause, my God and my Lord.
theirs: Stir up thyself, and awake to my judgment, [even] unto my cause, my God and my Lord.

ours: Let them be ashamed and brought to confusion together that rejoice at mine hurt: let them be clothed with shame and dishonour that magnify themselves against me.
theirs: Let them be ashamed and brought to confusion together that rejoice at mine hurt: let them be clothed with shame and dishonour that magnify [themselves] against me.

ours: And my tongue shall speak of thy righteousness and of thy praise all the day long.
theirs: And my tongue shall speak of thy righteousness [and] of thy praise all the day long.

ours: THE transgression of the wicked saith within my heart, that there is no fear of God before his eyes.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, [A Psalm] of David the servant of the LORD.>> The transgression of the wicked saith within my heart, [that there is] no fear of God before his eyes.

ours: The words of his mouth are iniquity and deceit: he hath left off to be wise, and to do good.
theirs: The words of his mouth [are] iniquity and deceit: he hath left off to be wise, [and] to do good.

ours: He deviseth mischief upon his bed; he setteth himself in a way that is not good; he abhorreth not evil.
theirs: He deviseth mischief upon his bed; he setteth himself in a way [that is] not good; he abhorreth not evil.

ours: Thy mercy, O LORD, is in the heavens; and thy faithfulness reacheth unto the clouds.
theirs: Thy mercy, O LORD, [is] in the heavens; [and] thy faithfulness [reacheth] unto the clouds.

ours: Thy righteousness is like the great mountains; thy judgments are a great deep: O LORD, thou preservest man and beast.
theirs: Thy righteousness [is] like the great mountains; thy judgments [are] a great deep: O LORD, thou preservest man and beast.

ours: How excellent is thy lovingkindness, O God! therefore the children of men put their trust under the shadow of thy wings.
theirs: How excellent [is] thy lovingkindness, O God! therefore the children of men put their trust under the shadow of thy wings.

ours: For with thee is the fountain of life: in thy light shall we see light.
theirs: For with thee [is] the fountain of life: in thy light shall we see light.

ours: FRET not thyself because of evildoers, neither be thou envious against the workers of iniquity.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David.>> Fret not thyself because of evildoers, neither be thou envious against the workers of iniquity.

ours: Trust in the LORD, and do good; so shalt thou dwell in the land, and verily thou shalt be fed.
theirs: Trust in the LORD, and do good; [so] shalt thou dwell in the land, and verily thou shalt be fed.

ours: Commit thy way unto the LORD; trust also in him; and he shall bring it to pass.
theirs: Commit thy way unto the LORD; trust also in him; and he shall bring [it] to pass.

ours: For yet a little while, and the wicked shall not be: yea, thou shalt diligently consider his place, and it shall not be.
theirs: For yet a little while, and the wicked [shall] not [be]: yea, thou shalt diligently consider his place, and it [shall] not [be].

ours: The wicked have drawn out the sword, and have bent their bow, to cast down the poor and needy, and to slay such as be of upright conversation.
theirs: The wicked have drawn out the sword, and have bent their bow, to cast down the poor and needy, [and] to slay such as be of upright conversation.

ours: A little that a righteous man hath is better than the riches of many wicked.
theirs: A little that a righteous man hath [is] better than the riches of many wicked.

ours: But the wicked shall perish, and the enemies of the LORD shall be as the fat of lambs: they shall consume; into smoke shall they consume away.
theirs: But the wicked shall perish, and the enemies of the LORD [shall be] as the fat of lambs: they shall consume; into smoke shall they consume away.

ours: For such as be blessed of him shall inherit the earth; and they that be cursed of him shall be cut off.
theirs: For [such as be] blessed of him shall inherit the earth; and [they that be] cursed of him shall be cut off.

ours: The steps of a good man are ordered by the LORD: and he delighteth in his way.
theirs: The steps of a [good] man are ordered by the LORD: and he delighteth in his way.

ours: Though he fall, he shall not be utterly cast down: for the LORD upholdeth him with his hand.
theirs: Though he fall, he shall not be utterly cast down: for the LORD upholdeth [him with] his hand.

ours: I have been young, and now am old; yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread.
theirs: I have been young, and [now] am old; yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread.

ours: He is ever merciful, and lendeth; and his seed is blessed.
theirs: [He is] ever merciful, and lendeth; and his seed [is] blessed.

ours: The law of his God is in his heart; none of his steps shall slide.
theirs: The law of his God [is] in his heart; none of his steps shall slide.

ours: Wait on the LORD, and keep his way, and he shall exalt thee to inherit the land: when the wicked are cut off, thou shalt see it.
theirs: Wait on the LORD, and keep his way, and he shall exalt thee to inherit the land: when the wicked are cut off, thou shalt see [it].

ours: Yet he passed away, and, lo, he was not: yea, I sought him, but he could not be found.
theirs: Yet he passed away, and, lo, he [was] not: yea, I sought him, but he could not be found.

ours: Mark the perfect man, and behold the upright: for the end of that man is peace.
theirs: Mark the perfect [man], and behold the upright: for the end of [that] man [is] peace.

ours: But the salvation of the righteous is of the LORD: he is their strength in the time of trouble.
theirs: But the salvation of the righteous [is] of the LORD: [he is] their strength in the time of trouble.

ours: O LORD, rebuke me not in thy wrath: neither chasten me in thy hot displeasure.
theirs: <<A Psalm of David, to bring to remembrance.>> O LORD, rebuke me not in thy wrath: neither chasten me in thy hot displeasure.

ours: There is no soundness in my flesh because of thine anger; neither is there any rest in my bones because of my sin.
theirs: [There is] no soundness in my flesh because of thine anger; neither [is there any] rest in my bones because of my sin.

ours: My wounds stink and are corrupt because of my foolishness.
theirs: My wounds stink [and] are corrupt because of my foolishness.

ours: For my loins are filled with a loathsome disease: and there is no soundness in my flesh.
theirs: For my loins are filled with a loathsome [disease]: and [there is] no soundness in my flesh.

ours: Lord, all my desire is before thee; and my groaning is not hid from thee.
theirs: Lord, all my desire [is] before thee; and my groaning is not hid from thee.

ours: They also that seek after my life lay snares for me: and they that seek my hurt speak mischievous things, and imagine deceits all the day long.
theirs: They also that seek after my life lay snares [for me]: and they that seek my hurt speak mischievous things, and imagine deceits all the day long.

ours: But I, as a deaf man, heard not; and I was as a dumb man that openeth not his mouth.
theirs: But I, as a deaf [man], heard not; and [I was] as a dumb man [that] openeth not his mouth.

ours: Thus I was as a man that heareth not, and in whose mouth are no reproofs.
theirs: Thus I was as a man that heareth not, and in whose mouth [are] no reproofs.

ours: For I said, Hear me, lest otherwise they should rejoice over me: when my foot slippeth, they magnify themselves against me.
theirs: For I said, [Hear me], lest [otherwise] they should rejoice over me: when my foot slippeth, they magnify [themselves] against me.

ours: For I am ready to halt, and my sorrow is continually before me.
theirs: For I [am] ready to halt, and my sorrow [is] continually before me.

ours: But mine enemies are lively, and they are strong: and they that hate me wrongfully are multiplied.
theirs: But mine enemies [are] lively, [and] they are strong: and they that hate me wrongfully are multiplied.

ours: They also that render evil for good are mine adversaries; because I follow the thing that good is.
theirs: They also that render evil for good are mine adversaries; because I follow [the thing that] good [is].

ours: I SAID, I will take heed to my ways, that I sin not with my tongue: I will keep my mouth with a bridle, while the wicked is before me.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, [even] to Jeduthun, A Psalm of David.>> I said, I will take heed to my ways, that I sin not with my tongue: I will keep my mouth with a bridle, while the wicked is before me.

ours: I was dumb with silence, I held my peace, even from good; and my sorrow was stirred.
theirs: I was dumb with silence, I held my peace, [even] from good; and my sorrow was stirred.

ours: My heart was hot within me, while I was musing the fire burned: then spake I with my tongue,
theirs: My heart was hot within me, while I was musing the fire burned: [then] spake I with my tongue,

ours: LORD, make me to know mine end, and the measure of my days, what it is; that I may know how frail I am.
theirs: LORD, make me to know mine end, and the measure of my days, what it [is; that] I may know how frail I [am].

ours: Behold, thou hast made my days as an handbreadth; and mine age is as nothing before thee: verily every man at his best state is altogether vanity. Selah.
theirs: Behold, thou hast made my days [as] an handbreadth; and mine age [is] as nothing before thee: verily every man at his best state [is] altogether vanity. Selah.

ours: Surely every man walketh in a vain shew: surely they are disquieted in vain: he heapeth up riches, and knoweth not who shall gather them.
theirs: Surely every man walketh in a vain shew: surely they are disquieted in vain: he heapeth up [riches], and knoweth not who shall gather them.

ours: And now, Lord, what wait I for? my hope is in thee.
theirs: And now, Lord, what wait I for? my hope [is] in thee.

ours: I was dumb, I opened not my mouth; because thou didst it.
theirs: I was dumb, I opened not my mouth; because thou didst [it].

ours: When thou with rebukes dost correct man for iniquity, thou makest his beauty to consume away like a moth: surely every man is vanity. Selah.
theirs: When thou with rebukes dost correct man for iniquity, thou makest his beauty to consume away like a moth: surely every man [is] vanity. Selah.

ours: Hear my prayer, O LORD, and give ear unto my cry; hold not thy peace at my tears: for I am a stranger with thee, and a sojourner, as all my fathers were.
theirs: Hear my prayer, O LORD, and give ear unto my cry; hold not thy peace at my tears: for I [am] a stranger with thee, [and] a sojourner, as all my fathers [were].

ours: I WAITED patiently for the LORD; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> I waited patiently for the LORD; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry.

ours: He brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock, and established my goings.
theirs: He brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock, [and] established my goings.

ours: And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God: many shall see it, and fear, and shall trust in the LORD.
theirs: And he hath put a new song in my mouth, [even] praise unto our God: many shall see [it], and fear, and shall trust in the LORD.

ours: Blessed is that man that maketh the LORD his trust, and respecteth not the proud, nor such as turn aside to lies.
theirs: Blessed [is] that man that maketh the LORD his trust, and respecteth not the proud, nor such as turn aside to lies.

ours: Many, O LORD my God, are thy wonderful works which thou hast done, and thy thoughts which are to us-ward: they cannot be reckoned up in order unto thee: if I would declare and speak of them, they are more than can be numbered.
theirs: Many, O LORD my God, [are] thy wonderful works [which] thou hast done, and thy thoughts [which are] to us-ward: they cannot be reckoned up in order unto thee: [if] I would declare and speak [of them], they are more than can be numbered.

ours: Then said I, Lo, I come: in the volume of the book it is written of me,
theirs: Then said I, Lo, I come: in the volume of the book [it is] written of me,

ours: I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.
theirs: I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law [is] within my heart.

ours: But I am poor and needy; yet the Lord thinketh upon me: thou art my help and my deliverer; make no tarrying, O my God.
theirs: But I [am] poor and needy; [yet] the Lord thinketh upon me: thou [art] my help and my deliverer; make no tarrying, O my God.

ours: BLESSED is he that considereth the poor: the LORD will deliver him in time of trouble.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> Blessed [is] he that considereth the poor: the LORD will deliver him in time of trouble.

ours: The LORD will preserve him, and keep him alive; and he shall be blessed upon the earth: and thou wilt not deliver him unto the will of his enemies.
theirs: The LORD will preserve him, and keep him alive; [and] he shall be blessed upon the earth: and thou wilt not deliver him unto the will of his enemies.

ours: And if he come to see me, he speaketh vanity: his heart gathereth iniquity to itself; when he goeth abroad, he telleth it.
theirs: And if he come to see [me], he speaketh vanity: his heart gathereth iniquity to itself; [when] he goeth abroad, he telleth [it].

ours: An evil disease, say they, cleaveth fast unto him: and now that he lieth he shall rise up no more.
theirs: An evil disease, [say they], cleaveth fast unto him: and [now] that he lieth he shall rise up no more.

ours: Yea, mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, which did eat of my bread, hath lifted up his heel against me.
theirs: Yea, mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, which did eat of my bread, hath lifted up [his] heel against me.

ours: Blessed be the LORD God of Israel from everlasting, and to everlasting. Amen, and Amen.
theirs: Blessed [be] the LORD God of Israel from everlasting, and to everlasting. Amen, and Amen.

ours: AS the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after thee, O God.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, Maschil, for the sons of Korah.>> As the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after thee, O God.

ours: My tears have been my meat day and night, while they continually say unto me, Where is thy God?
theirs: My tears have been my meat day and night, while they continually say unto me, Where [is] thy God?

ours: When I remember these things, I pour out my soul in me: for I had gone with the multitude, I went with them to the house of God, with the voice of joy and praise, with a multitude that kept holyday.
theirs: When I remember these [things], I pour out my soul in me: for I had gone with the multitude, I went with them to the house of God, with the voice of joy and praise, with a multitude that kept holyday.

ours: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted in me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him for the help of his countenance.
theirs: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and [why] art thou disquieted in me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him [for] the help of his countenance.

ours: Yet the LORD will command his lovingkindness in the daytime, and in the night his song shall be with me, and my prayer unto the God of my life.
theirs: [Yet] the LORD will command his lovingkindness in the daytime, and in the night his song [shall be] with me, [and] my prayer unto the God of my life.

ours: As with a sword in my bones, mine enemies reproach me; while they say daily unto me, Where is thy God?
theirs: [As] with a sword in my bones, mine enemies reproach me; while they say daily unto me, Where [is] thy God?

ours: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted within me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance, and my God.
theirs: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted within me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him, [who is] the health of my countenance, and my God.

ours: For thou art the God of my strength: why dost thou cast me off? why go I mourning because of the oppression of the enemy?
theirs: For thou [art] the God of my strength: why dost thou cast me off? why go I mourning because of the oppression of the enemy?

ours: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted within me? hope in God: for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance, and my God.
theirs: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted within me? hope in God: for I shall yet praise him, [who is] the health of my countenance, and my God.

ours: WE have heard with our ears, O God, our fathers have told us, what work thou didst in their days, in the times of old.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician for the sons of Korah, Maschil.>> We have heard with our ears, O God, our fathers have told us, [what] work thou didst in their days, in the times of old.

ours: How thou didst drive out the heathen with thy hand, and plantedst them; how thou didst afflict the people, and cast them out.
theirs: [How] thou didst drive out the heathen with thy hand, and plantedst them; [how] thou didst afflict the people, and cast them out.

ours: Thou hast given us like sheep appointed for meat; and hast scattered us among the heathen.
theirs: Thou hast given us like sheep [appointed] for meat; and hast scattered us among the heathen.

ours: Thou sellest thy people for nought, and dost not increase thy wealth by their price.
theirs: Thou sellest thy people for nought, and dost not increase [thy wealth] by their price.

ours: My confusion is continually before me, and the shame of my face hath covered me,
theirs: My confusion [is] continually before me, and the shame of my face hath covered me,

ours: Awake, why sleepest thou, O Lord? arise, cast us not off for ever.
theirs: Awake, why sleepest thou, O Lord? arise, cast [us] not off for ever.

ours: Wherefore hidest thou thy face, and forgettest our affliction and our oppression?
theirs: Wherefore hidest thou thy face, [and] forgettest our affliction and our oppression?

ours: Arise for our help, and redeem us for thy mercies sake.
theirs: Arise for our help, and redeem us for thy mercies' sake.

ours: MY heart is inditing a good matter: I speak of the things which I have made touching the king: my tongue is the pen of a ready writer.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Shoshannim, for the sons of Korah, Maschil, A Song of loves.>> My heart is inditing a good matter: I speak of the things which I have made touching the king: my tongue [is] the pen of a ready writer.

ours: Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, O most mighty, with thy glory and thy majesty.
theirs: Gird thy sword upon [thy] thigh, O [most] mighty, with thy glory and thy majesty.

ours: And in thy majesty ride prosperously because of truth and meekness and righteousness; and thy right hand shall teach thee terrible things.
theirs: And in thy majesty ride prosperously because of truth and meekness [and] righteousness; and thy right hand shall teach thee terrible things.

ours: Thine arrows are sharp in the heart of the kings enemies; whereby the people fall under thee.
theirs: Thine arrows [are] sharp in the heart of the king's enemies; [whereby] the people fall under thee.

ours: Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: the sceptre of thy kingdom is a right sceptre.
theirs: Thy throne, O God, [is] for ever and ever: the sceptre of thy kingdom [is] a right sceptre.

ours: All thy garments smell of myrrh, and aloes, and cassia, out of the ivory palaces, whereby they have made thee glad.
theirs: All thy garments [smell] of myrrh, and aloes, [and] cassia, out of the ivory palaces, whereby they have made thee glad.

ours: Kings daughters were among thy honourable women: upon thy right hand did stand the queen in gold of Ophir.
theirs: Kings' daughters [were] among thy honourable women: upon thy right hand did stand the queen in gold of Ophir.

ours: Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline thine ear; forget also thine own people, and thy fathers house;
theirs: Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline thine ear; forget also thine own people, and thy father's house;

ours: So shall the king greatly desire thy beauty: for he is thy Lord; and worship thou him.
theirs: So shall the king greatly desire thy beauty: for he [is] thy Lord; and worship thou him.

ours: And the daughter of Tyre shall be there with a gift; even the rich among the people shall intreat thy favour.
theirs: And the daughter of Tyre [shall be there] with a gift; [even] the rich among the people shall intreat thy favour.

ours: The kings daughter is all glorious within: her clothing is of wrought gold.
theirs: The king's daughter [is] all glorious within: her clothing [is] of wrought gold.

ours: With gladness and rejoicing shall they be brought: they shall enter into the kings palace.
theirs: With gladness and rejoicing shall they be brought: they shall enter into the king's palace.

ours: GOD is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician for the sons of Korah, A Song upon Alamoth.>> God [is] our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.

ours: Though the waters thereof roar and be troubled, though the mountains shake with the swelling thereof. Selah.
theirs: [Though] the waters thereof roar [and] be troubled, [though] the mountains shake with the swelling thereof. Selah.

ours: There is a river, the streams whereof shall make glad the city of God, the holy place of the tabernacles of the most High.
theirs: [There is] a river, the streams whereof shall make glad the city of God, the holy [place] of the tabernacles of the most High.

ours: God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved: God shall help her, and that right early.
theirs: God [is] in the midst of her; she shall not be moved: God shall help her, [and that] right early.

ours: The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah.
theirs: The LORD of hosts [is] with us; the God of Jacob [is] our refuge. Selah.

ours: Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth.
theirs: Be still, and know that I [am] God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth.

ours: The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah.
theirs: The LORD of hosts [is] with us; the God of Jacob [is] our refuge. Selah.

ours: O CLAP your hands, all ye people; shout unto God with the voice of triumph.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm for the sons of Korah.>> O clap your hands, all ye people; shout unto God with the voice of triumph.

ours: For the LORD most high is terrible; he is a great King over all the earth.
theirs: For the LORD most high [is] terrible; [he is] a great King over all the earth.

ours: For God is the King of all the earth: sing ye praises with understanding.
theirs: For God [is] the King of all the earth: sing ye praises with understanding.

ours: The princes of the people are gathered together, even the people of the God of Abraham: for the shields of the earth belong unto God: he is greatly exalted.
theirs: The princes of the people are gathered together, [even] the people of the God of Abraham: for the shields of the earth [belong] unto God: he is greatly exalted.

ours: GREAT is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of his holiness.
theirs: <<A Song [and] Psalm for the sons of Korah.>> Great [is] the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, [in] the mountain of his holiness.

ours: Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King.
theirs: Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, [is] mount Zion, [on] the sides of the north, the city of the great King.

ours: They saw it, and so they marvelled; they were troubled, and hasted away.
theirs: They saw [it, and] so they marvelled; they were troubled, [and] hasted away.

ours: Fear took hold upon them there, and pain, as of a woman in travail.
theirs: Fear took hold upon them there, [and] pain, as of a woman in travail.

ours: According to thy name, O God, so is thy praise unto the ends of the earth: thy right hand is full of righteousness.
theirs: According to thy name, O God, so [is] thy praise unto the ends of the earth: thy right hand is full of righteousness.

ours: Mark ye well her bulwarks, consider her palaces; that ye may tell it to the generation following.
theirs: Mark ye well her bulwarks, consider her palaces; that ye may tell [it] to the generation following.

ours: For this God is our God for ever and ever: he will be our guide even unto death.
theirs: For this God [is] our God for ever and ever: he will be our guide [even] unto death.

ours: HEAR this, all ye people; give ear, all ye inhabitants of the world:
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm for the sons of Korah.>> Hear this, all [ye] people; give ear, all [ye] inhabitants of the world:

ours: My mouth shall speak of wisdom; and the meditation of my heart shall be of understanding.
theirs: My mouth shall speak of wisdom; and the meditation of my heart [shall be] of understanding.

ours: Wherefore should I fear in the days of evil, when the iniquity of my heels shall compass me about?
theirs: Wherefore should I fear in the days of evil, [when] the iniquity of my heels shall compass me about?

ours: None of them can by any means redeem his brother, nor give to God a ransom for him:
theirs: None [of them] can by any means redeem his brother, nor give to God a ransom for him:

ours: (For the redemption of their soul is precious, and it ceaseth for ever:)
theirs: (For the redemption of their soul [is] precious, and it ceaseth for ever:)

ours: That he should still live for ever, and not see corruption.
theirs: That he should still live for ever, [and] not see corruption.

ours: For he seeth that wise men die, likewise the fool and the brutish person perish, and leave their wealth to others.
theirs: For he seeth [that] wise men die, likewise the fool and the brutish person perish, and leave their wealth to others.

ours: Their inward thought is, that their houses shall continue for ever, and their dwelling places to all generations; they call their lands after their own names.
theirs: Their inward thought [is, that] their houses [shall continue] for ever, [and] their dwelling places to all generations; they call [their] lands after their own names.

ours: Nevertheless man being in honour abideth not: he is like the beasts that perish.
theirs: Nevertheless man [being] in honour abideth not: he is like the beasts [that] perish.

ours: This their way is their folly: yet their posterity approve their sayings. Selah.
theirs: This their way [is] their folly: yet their posterity approve their sayings. Selah.

ours: Though while he lived he blessed his soul: and men will praise thee, when thou doest well to thyself.
theirs: Though while he lived he blessed his soul: and [men] will praise thee, when thou doest well to thyself.

ours: Man that is in honour, and understandeth not, is like the beasts that perish.
theirs: Man [that is] in honour, and understandeth not, is like the beasts [that] perish.

ours: THE mighty God, even the LORD, hath spoken, and called the earth from the rising of the sun unto the going down thereof.
theirs: <<A Psalm of Asaph.>> The mighty God, [even] the LORD, hath spoken, and called the earth from the rising of the sun unto the going down thereof.

ours: And the heavens shall declare his righteousness: for God is judge himself. Selah.
theirs: And the heavens shall declare his righteousness: for God [is] judge himself. Selah.

ours: Hear, O my people, and I will speak; O Israel, and I will testify against thee: I am God, even thy God.
theirs: Hear, O my people, and I will speak; O Israel, and I will testify against thee: I [am] God, [even] thy God.

ours: I will not reprove thee for thy sacrifices or thy burnt offerings, to have been continually before me.
theirs: I will not reprove thee for thy sacrifices or thy burnt offerings, [to have been] continually before me.

ours: I will take no bullock out of thy house, nor he goats out of thy folds.
theirs: I will take no bullock out of thy house, [nor] he goats out of thy folds.

ours: For every beast of the forest is mine, and the cattle upon a thousand hills.
theirs: For every beast of the forest [is] mine, [and] the cattle upon a thousand hills.

ours: I know all the fowls of the mountains: and the wild beasts of the field are mine.
theirs: I know all the fowls of the mountains: and the wild beasts of the field [are] mine.

ours: If I were hungry, I would not tell thee: for the world is mine, and the fulness thereof.
theirs: If I were hungry, I would not tell thee: for the world [is] mine, and the fulness thereof.

ours: But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?
theirs: But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or [that] thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?

ours: Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mothers son.
theirs: Thou sittest [and] speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother's son.

ours: These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself: but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.
theirs: These [things] hast thou done, and I kept silence; thou thoughtest that I was altogether [such an one] as thyself: [but] I will reprove thee, and set [them] in order before thine eyes.

ours: Now consider this, ye that forget God, lest I tear you in pieces, and there be none to deliver.
theirs: Now consider this, ye that forget God, lest I tear [you] in pieces, and [there be] none to deliver.

ours: Whoso offereth praise glorifieth me: and to him that ordereth his conversation aright will I shew the salvation of God.
theirs: Whoso offereth praise glorifieth me: and to him that ordereth [his] conversation [aright] will I shew the salvation of God.

ours: HAVE mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: according unto the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David, when Nathan the prophet came unto him, after he had gone in to Bathsheba.>> Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: according unto the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions.

ours: For I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me.
theirs: For I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin [is] ever before me.

ours: Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight: that thou mightest be justified when thou speakest, and be clear when thou judgest.
theirs: Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done [this] evil in thy sight: that thou mightest be justified when thou speakest, [and] be clear when thou judgest.

ours: Behold, thou desirest truth in the inward parts: and in the hidden part thou shalt make me to know wisdom.
theirs: Behold, thou desirest truth in the inward parts: and in the hidden [part] thou shalt make me to know wisdom.

ours: Make me to hear joy and gladness; that the bones which thou hast broken may rejoice.
theirs: Make me to hear joy and gladness; [that] the bones [which] thou hast broken may rejoice.

ours: Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit.
theirs: Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me [with thy] free spirit.

ours: Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee.
theirs: [Then] will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee.

ours: Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, thou God of my salvation: and my tongue shall sing aloud of thy righteousness.
theirs: Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, thou God of my salvation: [and] my tongue shall sing aloud of thy righteousness.

ours: For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it: thou delightest not in burnt offering.
theirs: For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give [it]: thou delightest not in burnt offering.

ours: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.
theirs: The sacrifices of God [are] a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.

ours: WHY boastest thou thyself in mischief, O mighty man? the goodness of God endureth continually.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, Maschil, [A Psalm] of David, when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul, and said unto him, David is come to the house of Ahimelech.>> Why boastest thou thyself in mischief, O mighty man? the goodness of God [endureth] continually.

ours: Thou lovest evil more than good; and lying rather than to speak righteousness. Selah.
theirs: Thou lovest evil more than good; [and] lying rather than to speak righteousness. Selah.

ours: Thou lovest all devouring words, O thou deceitful tongue.
theirs: Thou lovest all devouring words, O [thou] deceitful tongue.

ours: God shall likewise destroy thee for ever, he shall take thee away, and pluck thee out of thy dwelling place, and root thee out of the land of the living. Selah.
theirs: God shall likewise destroy thee for ever, he shall take thee away, and pluck thee out of [thy] dwelling place, and root thee out of the land of the living. Selah.

ours: Lo, this is the man that made not God his strength; but trusted in the abundance of his riches, and strengthened himself in his wickedness.
theirs: Lo, [this is] the man [that] made not God his strength; but trusted in the abundance of his riches, [and] strengthened himself in his wickedness.

ours: But I am like a green olive tree in the house of God: I trust in the mercy of God for ever and ever.
theirs: But I [am] like a green olive tree in the house of God: I trust in the mercy of God for ever and ever.

ours: I will praise thee for ever, because thou hast done it: and I will wait on thy name; for it is good before thy saints.
theirs: I will praise thee for ever, because thou hast done [it]: and I will wait on thy name; for [it is] good before thy saints.

ours: THE fool hath said in his heart, There is no God. Corrupt are they, and have done abominable iniquity: there is none that doeth good.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Mahalath, Maschil, [A Psalm] of David.>> The fool hath said in his heart, [There is] no God. Corrupt are they, and have done abominable iniquity: [there is] none that doeth good.

ours: God looked down from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there were any that did understand, that did seek God.
theirs: God looked down from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there were [any] that did understand, that did seek God.

ours: Every one of them is gone back: they are altogether become filthy; there is none that doeth good, no, not one.
theirs: Every one of them is gone back: they are altogether become filthy; [there is] none that doeth good, no, not one.

ours: Have the workers of iniquity no knowledge? who eat up my people as they eat bread: they have not called upon God.
theirs: Have the workers of iniquity no knowledge? who eat up my people [as] they eat bread: they have not called upon God.

ours: There were they in great fear, where no fear was: for God hath scattered the bones of him that encampeth against thee: thou hast put them to shame, because God hath despised them.
theirs: There were they in great fear, [where] no fear was: for God hath scattered the bones of him that encampeth [against] thee: thou hast put [them] to shame, because God hath despised them.

ours: Oh that the salvation of Israel were come out of Zion! When God bringeth back the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.
theirs: Oh that the salvation of Israel [were come] out of Zion! When God bringeth back the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice, [and] Israel shall be glad.

ours: SAVE me, O God, by thy name, and judge me by thy strength.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician on Neginoth, Maschil, [A Psalm] of David, when the Ziphims came and said to Saul, Doth not David hide himself with us?>> Save me, O God, by thy name, and judge me by thy strength.

ours: Behold, God is mine helper: the Lord is with them that uphold my soul.
theirs: Behold, God [is] mine helper: the Lord [is] with them that uphold my soul.

ours: I will freely sacrifice unto thee: I will praise thy name, O LORD; for it is good.
theirs: I will freely sacrifice unto thee: I will praise thy name, O LORD; for [it is] good.

ours: For he hath delivered me out of all trouble: and mine eye hath seen his desire upon mine enemies.
theirs: For he hath delivered me out of all trouble: and mine eye hath seen [his desire] upon mine enemies.

ours: GIVE ear to my prayer, O God; and hide not thyself from my supplication.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician on Neginoth, Maschil, [A Psalm] of David.>> Give ear to my prayer, O God; and hide not thyself from my supplication.

ours: And I said, Oh that I had wings like a dove! for then would I fly away, and be at rest.
theirs: And I said, Oh that I had wings like a dove! [for then] would I fly away, and be at rest.

ours: Lo, then would I wander far off, and remain in the wilderness. Selah.
theirs: Lo, [then] would I wander far off, [and] remain in the wilderness. Selah.

ours: I would hasten my escape from the windy storm and tempest.
theirs: I would hasten my escape from the windy storm [and] tempest.

ours: Destroy, O Lord, and divide their tongues: for I have seen violence and strife in the city.
theirs: Destroy, O Lord, [and] divide their tongues: for I have seen violence and strife in the city.

ours: Day and night they go about it upon the walls thereof: mischief also and sorrow are in the midst of it.
theirs: Day and night they go about it upon the walls thereof: mischief also and sorrow [are] in the midst of it.

ours: Wickedness is in the midst thereof: deceit and guile depart not from her streets.
theirs: Wickedness [is] in the midst thereof: deceit and guile depart not from her streets.

ours: For it was not an enemy that reproached me; then I could have borne it: neither was it he that hated me that did magnify himself against me; then I would have hid myself from him:
theirs: For [it was] not an enemy [that] reproached me; then I could have borne [it]: neither [was it] he that hated me [that] did magnify [himself] against me; then I would have hid myself from him:

ours: But it was thou, a man mine equal, my guide, and mine acquaintance.
theirs: But [it was] thou, a man mine equal, my guide, and mine acquaintance.

ours: We took sweet counsel together, and walked unto the house of God in company.
theirs: We took sweet counsel together, [and] walked unto the house of God in company.

ours: Let death seize upon them, and let them go down quick into hell: for wickedness is in their dwellings, and among them.
theirs: Let death seize upon them, [and] let them go down quick into hell: for wickedness [is] in their dwellings, [and] among them.

ours: He hath delivered my soul in peace from the battle that was against me: for there were many with me.
theirs: He hath delivered my soul in peace from the battle [that was] against me: for there were many with me.

ours: The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart: his words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords.
theirs: [The words] of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war [was] in his heart: his words were softer than oil, yet [were] they drawn swords.

ours: BE merciful unto me, O God: for man would swallow me up; he fighting daily oppresseth me.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Jonathelemrechokim, Michtam of David, when the Philistines took him in Gath.>> Be merciful unto me, O God: for man would swallow me up; he fighting daily oppresseth me.

ours: Mine enemies would daily swallow me up: for they be many that fight against me, O thou most High.
theirs: Mine enemies would daily swallow [me] up: for [they be] many that fight against me, O thou most High.

ours: Every day they wrest my words: all their thoughts are against me for evil.
theirs: Every day they wrest my words: all their thoughts [are] against me for evil.

ours: Shall they escape by iniquity? in thine anger cast down the people, O God.
theirs: Shall they escape by iniquity? in [thine] anger cast down the people, O God.

ours: Thou tellest my wanderings: put thou my tears into thy bottle: are they not in thy book?
theirs: Thou tellest my wanderings: put thou my tears into thy bottle: [are they] not in thy book?

ours: When I cry unto thee, then shall mine enemies turn back: this I know; for God is for me.
theirs: When I cry [unto thee], then shall mine enemies turn back: this I know; for God [is] for me.

ours: In God will I praise his word: in the LORD will I praise his word.
theirs: In God will I praise [his] word: in the LORD will I praise [his] word.

ours: Thy vows are upon me, O God: I will render praises unto thee.
theirs: Thy vows [are] upon me, O God: I will render praises unto thee.

ours: For thou hast delivered my soul from death: wilt not thou deliver my feet from falling, that I may walk before God in the light of the living?
theirs: For thou hast delivered my soul from death: [wilt] not [thou deliver] my feet from falling, that I may walk before God in the light of the living?

ours: BE merciful unto me, O God, be merciful unto me: for my soul trusteth in thee: yea, in the shadow of thy wings will I make my refuge, until these calamities be overpast.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, Altaschith, Michtam of David, when he fled from Saul in the cave.>> Be merciful unto me, O God, be merciful unto me: for my soul trusteth in thee: yea, in the shadow of thy wings will I make my refuge, until [these] calamities be overpast.

ours: I will cry unto God most high; unto God that performeth all things for me.
theirs: I will cry unto God most high; unto God that performeth [all things] for me.

ours: He shall send from heaven, and save me from the reproach of him that would swallow me up. Selah. God shall send forth his mercy and his truth.
theirs: He shall send from heaven, and save me [from] the reproach of him that would swallow me up. Selah. God shall send forth his mercy and his truth.

ours: My soul is among lions: and I lie even among them that are set on fire, even the sons of men, whose teeth are spears and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword.
theirs: My soul [is] among lions: [and] I lie [even among] them that are set on fire, [even] the sons of men, whose teeth [are] spears and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword.

ours: Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens; let thy glory be above all the earth.
theirs: Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens; [let] thy glory [be] above all the earth.

ours: They have prepared a net for my steps; my soul is bowed down: they have digged a pit before me, into the midst whereof they are fallen themselves. Selah.
theirs: They have prepared a net for my steps; my soul is bowed down: they have digged a pit before me, into the midst whereof they are fallen [themselves]. Selah.

ours: Awake up, my glory; awake, psaltery and harp: I myself will awake early.
theirs: Awake up, my glory; awake, psaltery and harp: I [myself] will awake early.

ours: For thy mercy is great unto the heavens, and thy truth unto the clouds.
theirs: For thy mercy [is] great unto the heavens, and thy truth unto the clouds.

ours: Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens: let thy glory be above all the earth.
theirs: Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens: [let] thy glory [be] above all the earth.

ours: DO ye indeed speak righteousness, O congregation? do ye judge uprightly, O ye sons of men?
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, Altaschith, Michtam of David.>> Do ye indeed speak righteousness, O congregation? do ye judge uprightly, O ye sons of men?

ours: Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: they are like the deaf adder that stoppeth her ear;
theirs: Their poison [is] like the poison of a serpent: [they are] like the deaf adder [that] stoppeth her ear;

ours: Let them melt away as waters which run continually: when he bendeth his bow to shoot his arrows, let them be as cut in pieces.
theirs: Let them melt away as waters [which] run continually: [when] he bendeth [his bow to shoot] his arrows, let them be as cut in pieces.

ours: As a snail which melteth, let every one of them pass away: like the untimely birth of a woman, that they may not see the sun.
theirs: As a snail [which] melteth, let [every one of them] pass away: [like] the untimely birth of a woman, [that] they may not see the sun.

ours: Before your pots can feel the thorns, he shall take them away as with a whirlwind, both living, and in his wrath.
theirs: Before your pots can feel the thorns, he shall take them away as with a whirlwind, both living, and in [his] wrath.

ours: So that a man shall say, Verily there is a reward for the righteous: verily he is a God that judgeth in the earth.
theirs: So that a man shall say, Verily [there is] a reward for the righteous: verily he is a God that judgeth in the earth.

ours: DELIVER me from mine enemies, O my God: defend me from them that rise up against me.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, Altaschith, Michtam of David; when Saul sent, and they watched the house to kill him.>> Deliver me from mine enemies, O my God: defend me from them that rise up against me.

ours: For, lo, they lie in wait for my soul: the mighty are gathered against me; not for my transgression, nor for my sin, O LORD.
theirs: For, lo, they lie in wait for my soul: the mighty are gathered against me; not [for] my transgression, nor [for] my sin, O LORD.

ours: They run and prepare themselves without my fault: awake to help me, and behold.
theirs: They run and prepare themselves without [my] fault: awake to help me, and behold.

ours: Behold, they belch out with their mouth: swords are in their lips: for who, say they, doth hear?
theirs: Behold, they belch out with their mouth: swords [are] in their lips: for who, [say they], doth hear?

ours: Because of his strength will I wait upon thee: for God is my defence.
theirs: [Because of] his strength will I wait upon thee: for God [is] my defence.

ours: The God of my mercy shall prevent me: God shall let me see my desire upon mine enemies.
theirs: The God of my mercy shall prevent me: God shall let me see [my desire] upon mine enemies.

ours: For the sin of their mouth and the words of their lips let them even be taken in their pride: and for cursing and lying which they speak.
theirs: [For] the sin of their mouth [and] the words of their lips let them even be taken in their pride: and for cursing and lying [which] they speak.

ours: Consume them in wrath, consume them, that they may not be: and let them know that God ruleth in Jacob unto the ends of the earth. Selah.
theirs: Consume [them] in wrath, consume [them], that they [may] not [be]: and let them know that God ruleth in Jacob unto the ends of the earth. Selah.

ours: And at evening let them return; and let them make a noise like a dog, and go round about the city.
theirs: And at evening let them return; [and] let them make a noise like a dog, and go round about the city.

ours: Unto thee, O my strength, will I sing: for God is my defence, and the God of my mercy.
theirs: Unto thee, O my strength, will I sing: for God [is] my defence, [and] the God of my mercy.

ours: O GOD, thou hast cast us off, thou hast scattered us, thou hast been displeased; O turn thyself to us again.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Shushaneduth, Michtam of David, to teach; when he strove with Aramnaharaim and with Aramzobah, when Joab returned, and smote of Edom in the valley of salt twelve thousand.>> O God, thou hast cast us off, thou hast scattered us, thou hast been displeased; O turn thyself to us again.

ours: That thy beloved may be delivered; save with thy right hand, and hear me.
theirs: That thy beloved may be delivered; save [with] thy right hand, and hear me.

ours: Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine; Ephraim also is the strength of mine head; Judah is my lawgiver;
theirs: Gilead [is] mine, and Manasseh [is] mine; Ephraim also [is] the strength of mine head; Judah [is] my lawgiver;

ours: Moab is my washpot; over Edom will I cast out my shoe: Philistia, triumph thou because of me.
theirs: Moab [is] my washpot; over Edom will I cast out my shoe: Philistia, triumph thou because of me.

ours: Who will bring me into the strong city? who will lead me into Edom?
theirs: Who will bring me [into] the strong city? who will lead me into Edom?

ours: Wilt not thou, O God, which hadst cast us off? and thou, O God, which didst not go out with our armies?
theirs: [Wilt] not thou, O God, [which] hadst cast us off? and [thou], O God, [which] didst not go out with our armies?

ours: Give us help from trouble: for vain is the help of man.
theirs: Give us help from trouble: for vain [is] the help of man.

ours: Through God we shall do valiantly: for he it is that shall tread down our enemies.
theirs: Through God we shall do valiantly: for he [it is that] shall tread down our enemies.

ours: HEAR my cry, O God; attend unto my prayer.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Neginah, [A Psalm] of David.>> Hear my cry, O God; attend unto my prayer.

ours: From the end of the earth will I cry unto thee, when my heart is overwhelmed: lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
theirs: From the end of the earth will I cry unto thee, when my heart is overwhelmed: lead me to the rock [that] is higher than I.

ours: For thou hast been a shelter for me, and a strong tower from the enemy.
theirs: For thou hast been a shelter for me, [and] a strong tower from the enemy.

ours: For thou, O God, hast heard my vows: thou hast given me the heritage of those that fear thy name.
theirs: For thou, O God, hast heard my vows: thou hast given [me] the heritage of those that fear thy name.

ours: Thou wilt prolong the kings life: and his years as many generations.
theirs: Thou wilt prolong the king's life: [and] his years as many generations.

ours: He shall abide before God for ever: O prepare mercy and truth, which may preserve him.
theirs: He shall abide before God for ever: O prepare mercy and truth, [which] may preserve him.

ours: TRULY my soul waiteth upon God: from him cometh my salvation.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, to Jeduthun, A Psalm of David.>> Truly my soul waiteth upon God: from him [cometh] my salvation.

ours: He only is my rock and my salvation; he is my defence; I shall not be greatly moved.
theirs: He only [is] my rock and my salvation; [he is] my defence; I shall not be greatly moved.

ours: How long will ye imagine mischief against a man? ye shall be slain all of you: as a bowing wall shall ye be, and as a tottering fence.
theirs: How long will ye imagine mischief against a man? ye shall be slain all of you: as a bowing wall [shall ye be, and as] a tottering fence.

ours: They only consult to cast him down from his excellency: they delight in lies: they bless with their mouth, but they curse inwardly. Selah.
theirs: They only consult to cast [him] down from his excellency: they delight in lies: they bless with their mouth, but they curse inwardly. Selah.

ours: My soul, wait thou only upon God; for my expectation is from him.
theirs: My soul, wait thou only upon God; for my expectation [is] from him.

ours: He only is my rock and my salvation: he is my defence; I shall not be moved.
theirs: He only [is] my rock and my salvation: [he is] my defence; I shall not be moved.

ours: In God is my salvation and my glory: the rock of my strength, and my refuge, is in God.
theirs: In God [is] my salvation and my glory: the rock of my strength, [and] my refuge, [is] in God.

ours: Trust in him at all times; ye people, pour out your heart before him: God is a refuge for us. Selah.
theirs: Trust in him at all times; ye people, pour out your heart before him: God [is] a refuge for us. Selah.

ours: Surely men of low degree are vanity, and men of high degree are a lie: to be laid in the balance, they are altogether lighter than vanity.
theirs: Surely men of low degree [are] vanity, [and] men of high degree [are] a lie: to be laid in the balance, they [are] altogether [lighter] than vanity.

ours: Trust not in oppression, and become not vain in robbery: if riches increase, set not your heart upon them.
theirs: Trust not in oppression, and become not vain in robbery: if riches increase, set not your heart [upon them].

ours: God hath spoken once; twice have I heard this; that power belongeth unto God.
theirs: God hath spoken once; twice have I heard this; that power [belongeth] unto God.

ours: Also unto thee, O Lord, belongeth mercy: for thou renderest to every man according to his work.
theirs: Also unto thee, O Lord, [belongeth] mercy: for thou renderest to every man according to his work.

ours: O GOD, thou art my God; early will I seek thee: my soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is;
theirs: <<A Psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah.>> O God, thou [art] my God; early will I seek thee: my soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is;

ours: To see thy power and thy glory, so as I have seen thee in the sanctuary.
theirs: To see thy power and thy glory, so [as] I have seen thee in the sanctuary.

ours: Because thy lovingkindness is better than life, my lips shall praise thee.
theirs: Because thy lovingkindness [is] better than life, my lips shall praise thee.

ours: My soul shall be satisfied as with marrow and fatness; and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips:
theirs: My soul shall be satisfied as [with] marrow and fatness; and my mouth shall praise [thee] with joyful lips:

ours: When I remember thee upon my bed, and meditate on thee in the night watches.
theirs: When I remember thee upon my bed, [and] meditate on thee in the [night] watches.

ours: But those that seek my soul, to destroy it, shall go into the lower parts of the earth.
theirs: But those [that] seek my soul, to destroy [it], shall go into the lower parts of the earth.

ours: HEAR my voice, O God, in my prayer: preserve my life from fear of the enemy.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> Hear my voice, O God, in my prayer: preserve my life from fear of the enemy.

ours: Who whet their tongue like a sword, and bend their bows to shoot their arrows, even bitter words:
theirs: Who whet their tongue like a sword, [and] bend [their bows to shoot] their arrows, [even] bitter words:

ours: They encourage themselves in an evil matter: they commune of laying snares privily; they say, Who shall see them?
theirs: They encourage themselves [in] an evil matter: they commune of laying snares privily; they say, Who shall see them?

ours: They search out iniquities; they accomplish a diligent search: both the inward thought of every one of them, and the heart, is deep.
theirs: They search out iniquities; they accomplish a diligent search: both the inward [thought] of every one [of them], and the heart, [is] deep.

ours: But God shall shoot at them with an arrow; suddenly shall they be wounded.
theirs: But God shall shoot at them [with] an arrow; suddenly shall they be wounded.

ours: PRAISE waiteth for thee, O God, in Sion: and unto thee shall the vow be performed.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm [and] Song of David.>> Praise waiteth for thee, O God, in Sion: and unto thee shall the vow be performed.

ours: Iniquities prevail against me: as for our transgressions, thou shalt purge them away.
theirs: Iniquities prevail against me: [as for] our transgressions, thou shalt purge them away.

ours: Blessed is the man whom thou choosest, and causest to approach unto thee, that he may dwell in thy courts: we shall be satisfied with the goodness of thy house, even of thy holy temple.
theirs: Blessed [is the man whom] thou choosest, and causest to approach [unto thee, that] he may dwell in thy courts: we shall be satisfied with the goodness of thy house, [even] of thy holy temple.

ours: By terrible things in righteousness wilt thou answer us, O God of our salvation; who art the confidence of all the ends of the earth, and of them that are afar off upon the sea:
theirs: [By] terrible things in righteousness wilt thou answer us, O God of our salvation; [who art] the confidence of all the ends of the earth, and of them that are afar off [upon] the sea:

ours: Which by his strength setteth fast the mountains; being girded with power:
theirs: Which by his strength setteth fast the mountains; [being] girded with power:

ours: Thou visitest the earth, and waterest it: thou greatly enrichest it with the river of God, which is full of water: thou preparest them corn, when thou hast so provided for it.
theirs: Thou visitest the earth, and waterest it: thou greatly enrichest it with the river of God, [which] is full of water: thou preparest them corn, when thou hast so provided for it.

ours: They drop upon the pastures of the wilderness: and the little hills rejoice on every side.
theirs: They drop [upon] the pastures of the wilderness: and the little hills rejoice on every side.

ours: MAKE a joyful noise unto God, all ye lands:
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Song [or] Psalm.>> Make a joyful noise unto God, all ye lands:

ours: Say unto God, How terrible art thou in thy works! through the greatness of thy power shall thine enemies submit themselves unto thee.
theirs: Say unto God, How terrible [art thou in] thy works! through the greatness of thy power shall thine enemies submit themselves unto thee.

ours: All the earth shall worship thee, and shall sing unto thee; they shall sing to thy name. Selah.
theirs: All the earth shall worship thee, and shall sing unto thee; they shall sing [to] thy name. Selah.

ours: Come and see the works of God: he is terrible in his doing toward the children of men.
theirs: Come and see the works of God: [he is] terrible [in his] doing toward the children of men.

ours: He turned the sea into dry land: they went through the flood on foot: there did we rejoice in him.
theirs: He turned the sea into dry [land]: they went through the flood on foot: there did we rejoice in him.

ours: Thou hast caused men to ride over our heads; we went through fire and through water: but thou broughtest us out into a wealthy place.
theirs: Thou hast caused men to ride over our heads; we went through fire and through water: but thou broughtest us out into a wealthy [place].
