ours: Come and hear, all ye that fear God, and I will declare what he hath done for my soul.
theirs: Come [and] hear, all ye that fear God, and I will declare what he hath done for my soul.

ours: If I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me:
theirs: If I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear [me]:

ours: But verily God hath heard me; he hath attended to the voice of my prayer.
theirs: [But] verily God hath heard [me]; he hath attended to the voice of my prayer.

ours: Blessed be God, which hath not turned away my prayer, nor his mercy from me.
theirs: Blessed [be] God, which hath not turned away my prayer, nor his mercy from me.

ours: GOD be merciful unto us, and bless us; and cause his face to shine upon us; Selah.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician on Neginoth, A Psalm [or] Song.>> God be merciful unto us, and bless us; [and] cause his face to shine upon us; Selah.

ours: Then shall the earth yield her increase; and God, even our own God, shall bless us.
theirs: [Then] shall the earth yield her increase; [and] God, [even] our own God, shall bless us.

ours: LET God arise, let his enemies be scattered: let them also that hate him flee before him.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm [or] Song of David.>> Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered: let them also that hate him flee before him.

ours: As smoke is driven away, so drive them away: as wax melteth before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God.
theirs: As smoke is driven away, [so] drive [them] away: as wax melteth before the fire, [so] let the wicked perish at the presence of God.

ours: A father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows, is God in his holy habitation.
theirs: A father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows, [is] God in his holy habitation.

ours: God setteth the solitary in families: he bringeth out those which are bound with chains: but the rebellious dwell in a dry land.
theirs: God setteth the solitary in families: he bringeth out those which are bound with chains: but the rebellious dwell in a dry [land].

ours: The earth shook, the heavens also dropped at the presence of God: even Sinai itself was moved at the presence of God, the God of Israel.
theirs: The earth shook, the heavens also dropped at the presence of God: [even] Sinai itself [was moved] at the presence of God, the God of Israel.

ours: The Lord gave the word: great was the company of those that published it.
theirs: The Lord gave the word: great [was] the company of those that published [it].

ours: Though ye have lien among the pots, yet shall ye be as the wings of a dove covered with silver, and her feathers with yellow gold.
theirs: Though ye have lien among the pots, [yet shall ye be as] the wings of a dove covered with silver, and her feathers with yellow gold.

ours: When the Almighty scattered kings in it, it was white as snow in Salmon.
theirs: When the Almighty scattered kings in it, it was [white] as snow in Salmon.

ours: The hill of God is as the hill of Bashan; an high hill as the hill of Bashan.
theirs: The hill of God [is as] the hill of Bashan; an high hill [as] the hill of Bashan.

ours: Why leap ye, ye high hills? this is the hill which God desireth to dwell in; yea, the LORD will dwell in it for ever.
theirs: Why leap ye, ye high hills? [this is] the hill [which] God desireth to dwell in; yea, the LORD will dwell [in it] for ever.

ours: The chariots of God are twenty thousand, even thousands of angels: the Lord is among them, as in Sinai, in the holy place.
theirs: The chariots of God [are] twenty thousand, [even] thousands of angels: the Lord [is] among them, [as in] Sinai, in the holy [place].

ours: Thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led captivity captive: thou hast received gifts for men; yea, for the rebellious also, that the LORD God might dwell among them.
theirs: Thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led captivity captive: thou hast received gifts for men; yea, [for] the rebellious also, that the LORD God might dwell [among them].

ours: Blessed be the Lord, who daily loadeth us with benefits, even the God of our salvation. Selah.
theirs: Blessed [be] the Lord, [who] daily loadeth us [with benefits, even] the God of our salvation. Selah.

ours: He that is our God is the God of salvation; and unto GOD the Lord belong the issues from death.
theirs: [He that is] our God [is] the God of salvation; and unto GOD the Lord [belong] the issues from death.

ours: But God shall wound the head of his enemies, and the hairy scalp of such an one as goeth on still in his trespasses.
theirs: But God shall wound the head of his enemies, [and] the hairy scalp of such an one as goeth on still in his trespasses.

ours: The Lord said, I will bring again from Bashan, I will bring my people again from the depths of the sea:
theirs: The Lord said, I will bring again from Bashan, I will bring [my people] again from the depths of the sea:

ours: That thy foot may be dipped in the blood of thine enemies, and the tongue of thy dogs in the same.
theirs: That thy foot may be dipped in the blood of [thine] enemies, [and] the tongue of thy dogs in the same.

ours: They have seen thy goings, O God; even the goings of my God, my King, in the sanctuary.
theirs: They have seen thy goings, O God; [even] the goings of my God, my King, in the sanctuary.

ours: The singers went before, the players on instruments followed after; among them were the damsels playing with timbrels.
theirs: The singers went before, the players on instruments [followed] after; among [them were] the damsels playing with timbrels.

ours: Bless ye God in the congregations, even the Lord, from the fountain of Israel.
theirs: Bless ye God in the congregations, [even] the Lord, from the fountain of Israel.

ours: There is little Benjamin with their ruler, the princes of Judah and their council, the princes of Zebulun, and the princes of Naphtali.
theirs: There [is] little Benjamin [with] their ruler, the princes of Judah [and] their council, the princes of Zebulun, [and] the princes of Naphtali.

ours: Rebuke the company of spearmen, the multitude of the bulls, with the calves of the people, till every one submit himself with pieces of silver: scatter thou the people that delight in war.
theirs: Rebuke the company of spearmen, the multitude of the bulls, with the calves of the people, [till every one] submit himself with pieces of silver: scatter thou the people [that] delight in war.

ours: To him that rideth upon the heavens of heavens, which were of old; lo, he doth send out his voice, and that a mighty voice.
theirs: To him that rideth upon the heavens of heavens, [which were] of old; lo, he doth send out his voice, [and that] a mighty voice.

ours: Ascribe ye strength unto God: his excellency is over Israel, and his strength is in the clouds.
theirs: Ascribe ye strength unto God: his excellency [is] over Israel, and his strength [is] in the clouds.

ours: O God, thou art terrible out of thy holy places: the God of Israel is he that giveth strength and power unto his people. Blessed be God.
theirs: O God, [thou art] terrible out of thy holy places: the God of Israel [is] he that giveth strength and power unto [his] people. Blessed [be] God.

ours: SAVE me, O God; for the waters are come in unto my soul.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Shoshannim, [A Psalm] of David.>> Save me, O God; for the waters are come in unto [my] soul.

ours: I sink in deep mire, where there is no standing: I am come into deep waters, where the floods overflow me.
theirs: I sink in deep mire, where [there is] no standing: I am come into deep waters, where the floods overflow me.

ours: They that hate me without a cause are more than the hairs of mine head: they that would destroy me, being mine enemies wrongfully, are mighty: then I restored that which I took not away.
theirs: They that hate me without a cause are more than the hairs of mine head: they that would destroy me, [being] mine enemies wrongfully, are mighty: then I restored [that] which I took not away.

ours: I am become a stranger unto my brethren, and an alien unto my mothers children.
theirs: I am become a stranger unto my brethren, and an alien unto my mother's children.

ours: When I wept, and chastened my soul with fasting, that was to my reproach.
theirs: When I wept, [and chastened] my soul with fasting, that was to my reproach.

ours: They that sit in the gate speak against me; and I was the song of the drunkards.
theirs: They that sit in the gate speak against me; and I [was] the song of the drunkards.

ours: But as for me, my prayer is unto thee, O LORD, in an acceptable time: O God, in the multitude of thy mercy hear me, in the truth of thy salvation.
theirs: But as for me, my prayer [is] unto thee, O LORD, [in] an acceptable time: O God, in the multitude of thy mercy hear me, in the truth of thy salvation.

ours: Hear me, O LORD; for thy lovingkindness is good: turn unto me according to the multitude of thy tender mercies.
theirs: Hear me, O LORD; for thy lovingkindness [is] good: turn unto me according to the multitude of thy tender mercies.

ours: Draw nigh unto my soul, and redeem it: deliver me because of mine enemies.
theirs: Draw nigh unto my soul, [and] redeem it: deliver me because of mine enemies.

ours: Thou hast known my reproach, and my shame, and my dishonour: mine adversaries are all before thee.
theirs: Thou hast known my reproach, and my shame, and my dishonour: mine adversaries [are] all before thee.

ours: Reproach hath broken my heart; and I am full of heaviness: and I looked for some to take pity, but there was none; and for comforters, but I found none.
theirs: Reproach hath broken my heart; and I am full of heaviness: and I looked [for some] to take pity, but [there was] none; and for comforters, but I found none.

ours: Let their table become a snare before them: and that which should have been for their welfare, let it become a trap.
theirs: Let their table become a snare before them: and [that which should have been] for [their] welfare, [let it become] a trap.

ours: Let their habitation be desolate; and let none dwell in their tents.
theirs: Let their habitation be desolate; [and] let none dwell in their tents.

ours: For they persecute him whom thou hast smitten; and they talk to the grief of those whom thou hast wounded.
theirs: For they persecute [him] whom thou hast smitten; and they talk to the grief of those whom thou hast wounded.

ours: But I am poor and sorrowful: let thy salvation, O God, set me up on high.
theirs: But I [am] poor and sorrowful: let thy salvation, O God, set me up on high.

ours: This also shall please the LORD better than an ox or bullock that hath horns and hoofs.
theirs: [This] also shall please the LORD better than an ox [or] bullock that hath horns and hoofs.

ours: The humble shall see this, and be glad: and your heart shall live that seek God.
theirs: The humble shall see [this, and] be glad: and your heart shall live that seek God.

ours: MAKE haste, O God, to deliver me; make haste to help me, O LORD.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, [A Psalm] of David, to bring to remembrance.>> [Make haste], O God, to deliver me; make haste to help me, O LORD.

ours: But I am poor and needy: make haste unto me, O God: thou art my help and my deliverer; O LORD, make no tarrying.
theirs: But I [am] poor and needy: make haste unto me, O God: thou [art] my help and my deliverer; O LORD, make no tarrying.

ours: Be thou my strong habitation, whereunto I may continually resort: thou hast given commandment to save me; for thou art my rock and my fortress.
theirs: Be thou my strong habitation, whereunto I may continually resort: thou hast given commandment to save me; for thou [art] my rock and my fortress.

ours: For thou art my hope, O Lord GOD: thou art my trust from my youth.
theirs: For thou [art] my hope, O Lord GOD: [thou art] my trust from my youth.

ours: By thee have I been holden up from the womb: thou art he that took me out of my mothers bowels: my praise shall be continually of thee.
theirs: By thee have I been holden up from the womb: thou art he that took me out of my mother's bowels: my praise [shall be] continually of thee.

ours: I am as a wonder unto many; but thou art my strong refuge.
theirs: I am as a wonder unto many; but thou [art] my strong refuge.

ours: Let my mouth be filled with thy praise and with thy honour all the day.
theirs: Let my mouth be filled [with] thy praise [and with] thy honour all the day.

ours: Saying, God hath forsaken him: persecute and take him; for there is none to deliver him.
theirs: Saying, God hath forsaken him: persecute and take him; for [there is] none to deliver [him].

ours: Let them be confounded and consumed that are adversaries to my soul; let them be covered with reproach and dishonour that seek my hurt.
theirs: Let them be confounded [and] consumed that are adversaries to my soul; let them be covered [with] reproach and dishonour that seek my hurt.

ours: My mouth shall shew forth thy righteousness and thy salvation all the day; for I know not the numbers thereof.
theirs: My mouth shall shew forth thy righteousness [and] thy salvation all the day; for I know not the numbers [thereof].

ours: I will go in the strength of the Lord GOD: I will make mention of thy righteousness, even of thine only.
theirs: I will go in the strength of the Lord GOD: I will make mention of thy righteousness, [even] of thine only.

ours: Now also when I am old and grayheaded, O God, forsake me not; until I have shewed thy strength unto this generation, and thy power to every one that is to come.
theirs: Now also when I am old and grayheaded, O God, forsake me not; until I have shewed thy strength unto [this] generation, [and] thy power to every one [that] is to come.

ours: Thy righteousness also, O God, is very high, who hast done great things: O God, who is like unto thee!
theirs: Thy righteousness also, O God, [is] very high, who hast done great things: O God, who [is] like unto thee!

ours: Thou, which hast shewed me great and sore troubles, shalt quicken me again, and shalt bring me up again from the depths of the earth.
theirs: [Thou], which hast shewed me great and sore troubles, shalt quicken me again, and shalt bring me up again from the depths of the earth.

ours: I will also praise thee with the psaltery, even thy truth, O my God: unto thee will I sing with the harp, O thou Holy One of Israel.
theirs: I will also praise thee with the psaltery, [even] thy truth, O my God: unto thee will I sing with the harp, O thou Holy One of Israel.

ours: GIVE the king thy judgments, O God, and thy righteousness unto the king's son.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] for Solomon.>> Give the king thy judgments, O God, and thy righteousness unto the king's son.

ours: He shall come down like rain upon the mown grass: as showers that water the earth.
theirs: He shall come down like rain upon the mown grass: as showers [that] water the earth.

ours: For he shall deliver the needy when he crieth; the poor also, and him that hath no helper.
theirs: For he shall deliver the needy when he crieth; the poor also, and [him] that hath no helper.

ours: And he shall live, and to him shall be given of the gold of Sheba: prayer also shall be made for him continually; and daily shall he be praised.
theirs: And he shall live, and to him shall be given of the gold of Sheba: prayer also shall be made for him continually; [and] daily shall he be praised.

ours: There shall be an handful of corn in the earth upon the top of the mountains; the fruit thereof shall shake like Lebanon: and they of the city shall flourish like grass of the earth.
theirs: There shall be an handful of corn in the earth upon the top of the mountains; the fruit thereof shall shake like Lebanon: and [they] of the city shall flourish like grass of the earth.

ours: His name shall endure for ever: his name shall be continued as long as the sun: and men shall be blessed in him: all nations shall call him blessed.
theirs: His name shall endure for ever: his name shall be continued as long as the sun: and [men] shall be blessed in him: all nations shall call him blessed.

ours: Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel, who only doeth wondrous things.
theirs: Blessed [be] the LORD God, the God of Israel, who only doeth wondrous things.

ours: And blessed be his glorious name for ever: and let the whole earth be filled with his glory; Amen, and Amen.
theirs: And blessed [be] his glorious name for ever: and let the whole earth be filled [with] his glory; Amen, and Amen.

ours: TRULY God is good to Israel, even to such as are of a clean heart.
theirs: <<A Psalm of Asaph.>> Truly God [is] good to Israel, [even] to such as are of a clean heart.

ours: For I was envious at the foolish, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.
theirs: For I was envious at the foolish, [when] I saw the prosperity of the wicked.

ours: For there are no bands in their death: but their strength is firm.
theirs: For [there are] no bands in their death: but their strength [is] firm.

ours: They are not in trouble as other men; neither are they plagued like other men.
theirs: They [are] not in trouble [as other] men; neither are they plagued like [other] men.

ours: Therefore pride compasseth them about as a chain; violence covereth them as a garment.
theirs: Therefore pride compasseth them about as a chain; violence covereth them [as] a garment.

ours: They are corrupt, and speak wickedly concerning oppression: they speak loftily.
theirs: They are corrupt, and speak wickedly [concerning] oppression: they speak loftily.

ours: Therefore his people return hither: and waters of a full cup are wrung out to them.
theirs: Therefore his people return hither: and waters of a full [cup] are wrung out to them.

ours: Behold, these are the ungodly, who prosper in the world; they increase in riches.
theirs: Behold, these [are] the ungodly, who prosper in the world; they increase [in] riches.

ours: Verily I have cleansed my heart in vain, and washed my hands in innocency.
theirs: Verily I have cleansed my heart [in] vain, and washed my hands in innocency.

ours: If I say, I will speak thus; behold, I should offend against the generation of thy children.
theirs: If I say, I will speak thus; behold, I should offend [against] the generation of thy children.

ours: When I thought to know this, it was too painful for me;
theirs: When I thought to know this, it [was] too painful for me;

ours: Until I went into the sanctuary of God; then understood I their end.
theirs: Until I went into the sanctuary of God; [then] understood I their end.

ours: How are they brought into desolation, as in a moment! they are utterly consumed with terrors.
theirs: How are they [brought] into desolation, as in a moment! they are utterly consumed with terrors.

ours: As a dream when one awaketh; so, O Lord, when thou awakest, thou shalt despise their image.
theirs: As a dream when [one] awaketh; [so], O Lord, when thou awakest, thou shalt despise their image.

ours: So foolish was I, and ignorant: I was as a beast before thee.
theirs: So foolish [was] I, and ignorant: I was [as] a beast before thee.

ours: Nevertheless I am continually with thee: thou hast holden me by my right hand.
theirs: Nevertheless I [am] continually with thee: thou hast holden [me] by my right hand.

ours: Thou shalt guide me with thy counsel, and afterward receive me to glory.
theirs: Thou shalt guide me with thy counsel, and afterward receive me [to] glory.

ours: Whom have I in heaven but thee? and there is none upon earth that I desire beside thee.
theirs: Whom have I in heaven [but thee]? and [there is] none upon earth [that] I desire beside thee.

ours: My flesh and my heart faileth: but God is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever.
theirs: My flesh and my heart faileth: [but] God [is] the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever.

ours: But it is good for me to draw near to God: I have put my trust in the Lord GOD, that I may declare all thy works.
theirs: But [it is] good for me to draw near to God: I have put my trust in the Lord GOD, that I may declare all thy works.

ours: O GOD, why hast thou cast us off for ever? why doth thine anger smoke against the sheep of thy pasture?
theirs: <<Maschil of Asaph.>> O God, why hast thou cast [us] off for ever? [why] doth thine anger smoke against the sheep of thy pasture?

ours: Remember thy congregation, which thou hast purchased of old; the rod of thine inheritance, which thou hast redeemed; this mount Zion, wherein thou hast dwelt.
theirs: Remember thy congregation, [which] thou hast purchased of old; the rod of thine inheritance, [which] thou hast redeemed; this mount Zion, wherein thou hast dwelt.

ours: Lift up thy feet unto the perpetual desolations; even all that the enemy hath done wickedly in the sanctuary.
theirs: Lift up thy feet unto the perpetual desolations; [even] all [that] the enemy hath done wickedly in the sanctuary.

ours: Thine enemies roar in the midst of thy congregations; they set up their ensigns for signs.
theirs: Thine enemies roar in the midst of thy congregations; they set up their ensigns [for] signs.

ours: A man was famous according as he had lifted up axes upon the thick trees.
theirs: [A man] was famous according as he had lifted up axes upon the thick trees.

ours: They have cast fire into thy sanctuary, they have defiled by casting down the dwelling place of thy name to the ground.
theirs: They have cast fire into thy sanctuary, they have defiled [by casting down] the dwelling place of thy name to the ground.

ours: We see not our signs: there is no more any prophet: neither is there among us any that knoweth how long.
theirs: We see not our signs: [there is] no more any prophet: neither [is there] among us any that knoweth how long.

ours: Why withdrawest thou thy hand, even thy right hand? pluck it out of thy bosom.
theirs: Why withdrawest thou thy hand, even thy right hand? pluck [it] out of thy bosom.

ours: For God is my King of old, working salvation in the midst of the earth.
theirs: For God [is] my King of old, working salvation in the midst of the earth.

ours: Thou brakest the heads of leviathan in pieces, and gavest him to be meat to the people inhabiting the wilderness.
theirs: Thou brakest the heads of leviathan in pieces, [and] gavest him [to be] meat to the people inhabiting the wilderness.

ours: The day is thine, the night also is thine: thou hast prepared the light and the sun.
theirs: The day [is] thine, the night also [is] thine: thou hast prepared the light and the sun.

ours: Remember this, that the enemy hath reproached, O LORD, and that the foolish people have blasphemed thy name.
theirs: Remember this, [that] the enemy hath reproached, O LORD, and [that] the foolish people have blasphemed thy name.

ours: O deliver not the soul of thy turtledove unto the multitude of the wicked: forget not the congregation of thy poor for ever.
theirs: O deliver not the soul of thy turtledove unto the multitude [of the wicked]: forget not the congregation of thy poor for ever.

ours: UNTO thee, O God, do we give thanks, unto thee do we give thanks: for that thy name is near thy wondrous works declare.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, Altaschith, A Psalm [or] Song of Asaph.>> Unto thee, O God, do we give thanks, [unto thee] do we give thanks: for [that] thy name is near thy wondrous works declare.

ours: Lift not up your horn on high: speak not with a stiff neck.
theirs: Lift not up your horn on high: speak [not with] a stiff neck.

ours: For promotion cometh neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the south.
theirs: For promotion [cometh] neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the south.

ours: But God is the judge: he putteth down one, and setteth up another.
theirs: But God [is] the judge: he putteth down one, and setteth up another.

ours: For in the hand of the LORD there is a cup, and the wine is red; it is full of mixture; and he poureth out of the same: but the dregs thereof, all the wicked of the earth shall wring them out, and drink them.
theirs: For in the hand of the LORD [there is] a cup, and the wine is red; it is full of mixture; and he poureth out of the same: but the dregs thereof, all the wicked of the earth shall wring [them] out, [and] drink [them].

ours: All the horns of the wicked also will I cut off; but the horns of the righteous shall be exalted.
theirs: All the horns of the wicked also will I cut off; [but] the horns of the righteous shall be exalted.

ours: IN Judah is God known: his name is great in Israel.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician on Neginoth, A Psalm [or] Song of Asaph.>> In Judah [is] God known: his name [is] great in Israel.

ours: Thou art more glorious and excellent than the mountains of prey.
theirs: Thou [art] more glorious [and] excellent than the mountains of prey.

ours: Thou, even thou, art to be feared: and who may stand in thy sight when once thou art angry?
theirs: Thou, [even] thou, [art] to be feared: and who may stand in thy sight when once thou art angry?

ours: He shall cut off the spirit of princes: he is terrible to the kings of the earth.
theirs: He shall cut off the spirit of princes: [he is] terrible to the kings of the earth.

ours: I CRIED unto God with my voice, even unto God with my voice; and he gave ear unto me.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, to Jeduthun, A Psalm of Asaph.>> I cried unto God with my voice, [even] unto God with my voice; and he gave ear unto me.

ours: Is his mercy clean gone for ever? doth his promise fail for evermore?
theirs: Is his mercy clean gone for ever? doth [his] promise fail for evermore?

ours: And I said, This is my infirmity: but I will remember the years of the right hand of the most High.
theirs: And I said, This [is] my infirmity: [but I will remember] the years of the right hand of the most High.

ours: Thy way, O God, is in the sanctuary: who is so great a God as our God?
theirs: Thy way, O God, [is] in the sanctuary: who [is so] great a God as [our] God?

ours: Thou art the God that doest wonders: thou hast declared thy strength among the people.
theirs: Thou [art] the God that doest wonders: thou hast declared thy strength among the people.

ours: Thou hast with thine arm redeemed thy people, the sons of Jacob and Joseph. Selah.
theirs: Thou hast with [thine] arm redeemed thy people, the sons of Jacob and Joseph. Selah.

ours: The voice of thy thunder was in the heaven: the lightnings lightened the world: the earth trembled and shook.
theirs: The voice of thy thunder [was] in the heaven: the lightnings lightened the world: the earth trembled and shook.

ours: Thy way is in the sea, and thy path in the great waters, and thy footsteps are not known.
theirs: Thy way [is] in the sea, and thy path in the great waters, and thy footsteps are not known.

ours: GIVE ear, O my people, to my law: incline your ears to the words of my mouth.
theirs: <<Maschil of Asaph.>> Give ear, O my people, [to] my law: incline your ears to the words of my mouth.

ours: We will not hide them from their children, shewing to the generation to come the praises of the LORD, and his strength, and his wonderful works that he hath done.
theirs: We will not hide [them] from their children, shewing to the generation to come the praises of the LORD, and his strength, and his wonderful works that he hath done.

ours: That the generation to come might know them, even the children which should be born; who should arise and declare them to their children:
theirs: That the generation to come might know [them, even] the children [which] should be born; [who] should arise and declare [them] to their children:

ours: And might not be as their fathers, a stubborn and rebellious generation; a generation that set not their heart aright, and whose spirit was not stedfast with God.
theirs: And might not be as their fathers, a stubborn and rebellious generation; a generation [that] set not their heart aright, and whose spirit was not stedfast with God.

ours: The children of Ephraim, being armed, and carrying bows, turned back in the day of battle.
theirs: The children of Ephraim, [being] armed, [and] carrying bows, turned back in the day of battle.

ours: Marvellous things did he in the sight of their fathers, in the land of Egypt, in the field of Zoan.
theirs: Marvellous things did he in the sight of their fathers, in the land of Egypt, [in] the field of Zoan.

ours: He clave the rocks in the wilderness, and gave them drink as out of the great depths.
theirs: He clave the rocks in the wilderness, and gave [them] drink as [out of] the great depths.

ours: Therefore the LORD heard this, and was wroth: so a fire was kindled against Jacob, and anger also came up against Israel;
theirs: Therefore the LORD heard [this], and was wroth: so a fire was kindled against Jacob, and anger also came up against Israel;

ours: Man did eat angels food: he sent them meat to the full.
theirs: Man did eat angels' food: he sent them meat to the full.

ours: And he let it fall in the midst of their camp, round about their habitations.
theirs: And he let [it] fall in the midst of their camp, round about their habitations.

ours: They were not estranged from their lust. But while their meat was yet in their mouths,
theirs: They were not estranged from their lust. But while their meat [was] yet in their mouths,

ours: The wrath of God came upon them, and slew the fattest of them, and smote down the chosen men of Israel.
theirs: The wrath of God came upon them, and slew the fattest of them, and smote down the chosen [men] of Israel.

ours: And they remembered that God was their rock, and the high God their redeemer.
theirs: And they remembered that God [was] their rock, and the high God their redeemer.

ours: But he, being full of compassion, forgave their iniquity, and destroyed them not: yea, many a time turned he his anger away, and did not stir up all his wrath.
theirs: But he, [being] full of compassion, forgave [their] iniquity, and destroyed [them] not: yea, many a time turned he his anger away, and did not stir up all his wrath.

ours: For he remembered that they were but flesh; a wind that passeth away, and cometh not again.
theirs: For he remembered that they [were but] flesh; a wind that passeth away, and cometh not again.

ours: How oft did they provoke him in the wilderness, and grieve him in the desert!
theirs: How oft did they provoke him in the wilderness, [and] grieve him in the desert!

ours: They remembered not his hand, nor the day when he delivered them from the enemy.
theirs: They remembered not his hand, [nor] the day when he delivered them from the enemy.

ours: He cast upon them the fierceness of his anger, wrath, and indignation, and trouble, by sending evil angels among them.
theirs: He cast upon them the fierceness of his anger, wrath, and indignation, and trouble, by sending evil angels [among them].

ours: And smote all the firstborn in Egypt; the chief of their strength in the tabernacles of Ham:
theirs: And smote all the firstborn in Egypt; the chief of [their] strength in the tabernacles of Ham:

ours: And he brought them to the border of his sanctuary, even to this mountain, which his right hand had purchased.
theirs: And he brought them to the border of his sanctuary, [even to] this mountain, [which] his right hand had purchased.

ours: When God heard this, he was wroth, and greatly abhorred Israel:
theirs: When God heard [this], he was wroth, and greatly abhorred Israel:

ours: So that he forsook the tabernacle of Shiloh, the tent which he placed among men;
theirs: So that he forsook the tabernacle of Shiloh, the tent [which] he placed among men;

ours: And delivered his strength into captivity, and his glory into the enemys hand.
theirs: And delivered his strength into captivity, and his glory into the enemy's hand.

ours: Then the Lord awaked as one out of sleep, and like a mighty man that shouteth by reason of wine.
theirs: Then the Lord awaked as one out of sleep, [and] like a mighty man that shouteth by reason of wine.

ours: And he built his sanctuary like high palaces, like the earth which he hath established for ever.
theirs: And he built his sanctuary like high [palaces], like the earth which he hath established for ever.

ours: O GOD, the heathen are come into thine inheritance; thy holy temple have they defiled; they have laid Jerusalem on heaps.
theirs: <<A Psalm of Asaph.>> O God, the heathen are come into thine inheritance; thy holy temple have they defiled; they have laid Jerusalem on heaps.

ours: The dead bodies of thy servants have they given to be meat unto the fowls of the heaven, the flesh of thy saints unto the beasts of the earth.
theirs: The dead bodies of thy servants have they given [to be] meat unto the fowls of the heaven, the flesh of thy saints unto the beasts of the earth.

ours: Their blood have they shed like water round about Jerusalem; and there was none to bury them.
theirs: Their blood have they shed like water round about Jerusalem; and [there was] none to bury [them].

ours: Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of thy name: and deliver us, and purge away our sins, for thy names sake.
theirs: Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of thy name: and deliver us, and purge away our sins, for thy name's sake.

ours: Wherefore should the heathen say, Where is their God? let him be known among the heathen in our sight by the revenging of the blood of thy servants which is shed.
theirs: Wherefore should the heathen say, Where [is] their God? let him be known among the heathen in our sight [by] the revenging of the blood of thy servants [which is] shed.

ours: GIVE ear, O Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a flock; thou that dwellest between the cherubims, shine forth.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon ShoshannimEduth, A Psalm of Asaph.>> Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a flock; thou that dwellest [between] the cherubims, shine forth.

ours: Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh stir up thy strength, and come and save us.
theirs: Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh stir up thy strength, and come [and] save us.

ours: Thou preparedst room before it, and didst cause it to take deep root, and it filled the land.
theirs: Thou preparedst [room] before it, and didst cause it to take deep root, and it filled the land.

ours: The hills were covered with the shadow of it, and the boughs thereof were like the goodly cedars.
theirs: The hills were covered with the shadow of it, and the boughs thereof [were like] the goodly cedars.

ours: Why hast thou then broken down her hedges, so that all they which pass by the way do pluck her?
theirs: Why hast thou [then] broken down her hedges, so that all they which pass by the way do pluck her?

ours: And the vineyard which thy right hand hath planted, and the branch that thou madest strong for thyself.
theirs: And the vineyard which thy right hand hath planted, and the branch [that] thou madest strong for thyself.

ours: It is burned with fire, it is cut down: they perish at the rebuke of thy countenance.
theirs: [It is] burned with fire, [it is] cut down: they perish at the rebuke of thy countenance.

ours: Let thy hand be upon the man of thy right hand, upon the son of man whom thou madest strong for thyself.
theirs: Let thy hand be upon the man of thy right hand, upon the son of man [whom] thou madest strong for thyself.

ours: SING aloud unto God our strength: make a joyful noise unto the God of Jacob.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Gittith, [A Psalm] of Asaph.>> Sing aloud unto God our strength: make a joyful noise unto the God of Jacob.

ours: For this was a statute for Israel, and a law of the God of Jacob.
theirs: For this [was] a statute for Israel, [and] a law of the God of Jacob.

ours: This he ordained in Joseph for a testimony, when he went out through the land of Egypt: where I heard a language that I understood not.
theirs: This he ordained in Joseph [for] a testimony, when he went out through the land of Egypt: [where] I heard a language [that] I understood not.

ours: I am the LORD thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt: open thy mouth wide, and I will fill it.
theirs: I [am] the LORD thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt: open thy mouth wide, and I will fill it.

ours: So I gave them up unto their own hearts lust: and they walked in their own counsels.
theirs: So I gave them up unto their own hearts' lust: [and] they walked in their own counsels.

ours: Oh that my people had hearkened unto me, and Israel had walked in my ways!
theirs: Oh that my people had hearkened unto me, [and] Israel had walked in my ways!

ours: GOD standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.
theirs: <<A Psalm of Asaph.>> God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.

ours: Deliver the poor and needy: rid them out of the hand of the wicked.
theirs: Deliver the poor and needy: rid [them] out of the hand of the wicked.

ours: I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.
theirs: I have said, Ye [are] gods; and all of you [are] children of the most High.

ours: KEEP not thou silence, O God: hold not thy peace, and be not still, O God.
theirs: <<A Song [or] Psalm of Asaph.>> Keep not thou silence, O God: hold not thy peace, and be not still, O God.

ours: They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.
theirs: They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from [being] a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.

ours: Do unto them as unto the Midianites; as to Sisera, as to Jabin, at the brook of Kison:
theirs: Do unto them as [unto] the Midianites; as [to] Sisera, as [to] Jabin, at the brook of Kison:

ours: Which perished at En-dor: they became as dung for the earth.
theirs: [Which] perished at Endor: they became [as] dung for the earth.

ours: That men may know that thou, whose name alone is JEHOVAH, art the most high over all the earth.
theirs: That [men] may know that thou, whose name alone [is] JEHOVAH, [art] the most high over all the earth.

ours: HOW amiable are thy tabernacles, O LORD of hosts!
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Gittith, A Psalm for the sons of Korah.>> How amiable [are] thy tabernacles, O LORD of hosts!

ours: Yea, the sparrow hath found an house, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she may lay her young, even thine altars, O LORD of hosts, my King, and my God.
theirs: Yea, the sparrow hath found an house, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she may lay her young, [even] thine altars, O LORD of hosts, my King, and my God.

ours: Blessed are they that dwell in thy house: they will be still praising thee. Selah.
theirs: Blessed [are] they that dwell in thy house: they will be still praising thee. Selah.

ours: Blessed is the man whose strength is in thee; in whose heart are the ways of them.
theirs: Blessed [is] the man whose strength [is] in thee; in whose heart [are] the ways [of them].

ours: Who passing through the valley of Baca make it a well; the rain also filleth the pools.
theirs: [Who] passing through the valley of Baca make it a well; the rain also filleth the pools.

ours: They go from strength to strength, every one of them in Zion appeareth before God.
theirs: They go from strength to strength, [every one of them] in Zion appeareth before God.

ours: For a day in thy courts is better than a thousand. I had rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God, than to dwell in the tents of wickedness.
theirs: For a day in thy courts [is] better than a thousand. I had rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God, than to dwell in the tents of wickedness.

ours: For the LORD God is a sun and shield: the LORD will give grace and glory: no good thing will he withhold from them that walk uprightly.
theirs: For the LORD God [is] a sun and shield: the LORD will give grace and glory: no good [thing] will he withhold from them that walk uprightly.

ours: O LORD of hosts, blessed is the man that trusteth in thee.
theirs: O LORD of hosts, blessed [is] the man that trusteth in thee.

ours: LORD, thou hast been favourable unto thy land: thou hast brought back the captivity of Jacob.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm for the sons of Korah.>> LORD, thou hast been favourable unto thy land: thou hast brought back the captivity of Jacob.

ours: Thou hast taken away all thy wrath: thou hast turned thyself from the fierceness of thine anger.
theirs: Thou hast taken away all thy wrath: thou hast turned [thyself] from the fierceness of thine anger.

ours: Surely his salvation is nigh them that fear him; that glory may dwell in our land.
theirs: Surely his salvation [is] nigh them that fear him; that glory may dwell in our land.

ours: Mercy and truth are met together; righteousness and peace have kissed each other.
theirs: Mercy and truth are met together; righteousness and peace have kissed [each other].

ours: Yea, the LORD shall give that which is good; and our land shall yield her increase.
theirs: Yea, the LORD shall give [that which is] good; and our land shall yield her increase.

ours: Righteousness shall go before him; and shall set us in the way of his steps.
theirs: Righteousness shall go before him; and shall set [us] in the way of his steps.

ours: BOW down thine ear, O LORD, hear me: for I am poor and needy.
theirs: <<A Prayer of David.>> Bow down thine ear, O LORD, hear me: for I [am] poor and needy.

ours: Preserve my soul; for I am holy: O thou my God, save thy servant that trusteth in thee.
theirs: Preserve my soul; for I [am] holy: O thou my God, save thy servant that trusteth in thee.

ours: For thou, Lord, art good, and ready to forgive; and plenteous in mercy unto all them that call upon thee.
theirs: For thou, Lord, [art] good, and ready to forgive; and plenteous in mercy unto all them that call upon thee.

ours: Among the gods there is none like unto thee, O Lord; neither are there any works like unto thy works.
theirs: Among the gods [there is] none like unto thee, O Lord; neither [are there any works] like unto thy works.

ours: For thou art great, and doest wondrous things: thou art God alone.
theirs: For thou [art] great, and doest wondrous things: thou [art] God alone.

ours: For great is thy mercy toward me: and thou hast delivered my soul from the lowest hell.
theirs: For great [is] thy mercy toward me: and thou hast delivered my soul from the lowest hell.

ours: O God, the proud are risen against me, and the assemblies of violent men have sought after my soul; and have not set thee before them.
theirs: O God, the proud are risen against me, and the assemblies of violent [men] have sought after my soul; and have not set thee before them.

ours: But thou, O Lord, art a God full of compassion, and gracious, longsuffering, and plenteous in mercy and truth.
theirs: But thou, O Lord, [art] a God full of compassion, and gracious, longsuffering, and plenteous in mercy and truth.

ours: Shew me a token for good; that they which hate me may see it, and be ashamed: because thou, LORD, hast holpen me, and comforted me.
theirs: Shew me a token for good; that they which hate me may see [it], and be ashamed: because thou, LORD, hast holpen me, and comforted me.

ours: HIS foundation is in the holy mountains.
theirs: <<A Psalm [or] Song for the sons of Korah.>> His foundation [is] in the holy mountains.

ours: I will make mention of Rahab and Babylon to them that know me: behold Philistia, and Tyre, with Ethiopia; this man was born there.
theirs: I will make mention of Rahab and Babylon to them that know me: behold Philistia, and Tyre, with Ethiopia; this [man] was born there.

ours: The LORD shall count, when he writeth up the people, that this man was born there. Selah.
theirs: The LORD shall count, when he writeth up the people, [that] this [man] was born there. Selah.

ours: As well the singers as the players on instruments shall be there: all my springs are in thee.
theirs: As well the singers as the players on instruments [shall be there]: all my springs [are] in thee.

ours: O LORD God of my salvation, I have cried day and night before thee:
theirs: <<A Song [or] Psalm for the sons of Korah, to the chief Musician upon Mahalath Leannoth, Maschil of Heman the Ezrahite.>> O LORD God of my salvation, I have cried day [and] night before thee:

ours: I am counted with them that go down into the pit: I am as a man that hath no strength:
theirs: I am counted with them that go down into the pit: I am as a man [that hath] no strength:

ours: Thy wrath lieth hard upon me, and thou hast afflicted me with all thy waves. Selah.
theirs: Thy wrath lieth hard upon me, and thou hast afflicted [me] with all thy waves. Selah.

ours: Thou hast put away mine acquaintance far from me; thou hast made me an abomination unto them: I am shut up, and I cannot come forth.
theirs: Thou hast put away mine acquaintance far from me; thou hast made me an abomination unto them: [I am] shut up, and I cannot come forth.

ours: Wilt thou shew wonders to the dead? shall the dead arise and praise thee? Selah.
theirs: Wilt thou shew wonders to the dead? shall the dead arise [and] praise thee? Selah.

ours: Shall thy lovingkindness be declared in the grave? or thy faithfulness in destruction?
theirs: Shall thy lovingkindness be declared in the grave? [or] thy faithfulness in destruction?

ours: LORD, why castest thou off my soul? why hidest thou thy face from me?
theirs: LORD, why castest thou off my soul? [why] hidest thou thy face from me?

ours: I am afflicted and ready to die from my youth up: while I suffer thy terrors I am distracted.
theirs: I [am] afflicted and ready to die from [my] youth up: [while] I suffer thy terrors I am distracted.

ours: Lover and friend hast thou put far from me, and mine acquaintance into darkness.
theirs: Lover and friend hast thou put far from me, [and] mine acquaintance into darkness.

ours: I WILL sing of the mercies of the LORD for ever: with my mouth will I make known thy faithfulness to all generations.
theirs: <<Maschil of Ethan the Ezrahite.>> I will sing of the mercies of the LORD for ever: with my mouth will I make known thy faithfulness to all generations.

ours: For who in the heaven can be compared unto the LORD? who among the sons of the mighty can be likened unto the LORD?
theirs: For who in the heaven can be compared unto the LORD? [who] among the sons of the mighty can be likened unto the LORD?

ours: God is greatly to be feared in the assembly of the saints, and to be had in reverence of all them that are about him.
theirs: God is greatly to be feared in the assembly of the saints, and to be had in reverence of all [them that are] about him.

ours: O LORD God of hosts, who is a strong LORD like unto thee? or to thy faithfulness round about thee?
theirs: O LORD God of hosts, who [is] a strong LORD like unto thee? or to thy faithfulness round about thee?

ours: The heavens are thine, the earth also is thine: as for the world and the fulness thereof, thou hast founded them.
theirs: The heavens [are] thine, the earth also [is] thine: [as for] the world and the fulness thereof, thou hast founded them.

ours: Thou hast a mighty arm: strong is thy hand, and high is thy right hand.
theirs: Thou hast a mighty arm: strong is thy hand, [and] high is thy right hand.

ours: Justice and judgment are the habitation of thy throne: mercy and truth shall go before thy face.
theirs: Justice and judgment [are] the habitation of thy throne: mercy and truth shall go before thy face.

ours: Blessed is the people that know the joyful sound: they shall walk, O LORD, in the light of thy countenance.
theirs: Blessed [is] the people that know the joyful sound: they shall walk, O LORD, in the light of thy countenance.

ours: For thou art the glory of their strength: and in thy favour our horn shall be exalted.
theirs: For thou [art] the glory of their strength: and in thy favour our horn shall be exalted.

ours: For the LORD is our defence; and the Holy One of Israel is our king.
theirs: For the LORD [is] our defence; and the Holy One of Israel [is] our king.

ours: Then thou spakest in vision to thy holy one, and saidst, I have laid help upon one that is mighty; I have exalted one chosen out of the people.
theirs: Then thou spakest in vision to thy holy one, and saidst, I have laid help upon [one that is] mighty; I have exalted [one] chosen out of the people.

ours: But my faithfulness and my mercy shall be with him: and in my name shall his horn be exalted.
theirs: But my faithfulness and my mercy [shall be] with him: and in my name shall his horn be exalted.

ours: He shall cry unto me, Thou art my father, my God, and the rock of my salvation.
theirs: He shall cry unto me, Thou [art] my father, my God, and the rock of my salvation.

ours: Also I will make him my firstborn, higher than the kings of the earth.
theirs: Also I will make him [my] firstborn, higher than the kings of the earth.

ours: His seed also will I make to endure for ever, and his throne as the days of heaven.
theirs: His seed also will I make [to endure] for ever, and his throne as the days of heaven.

ours: It shall be established for ever as the moon, and as a faithful witness in heaven. Selah.
theirs: It shall be established for ever as the moon, and [as] a faithful witness in heaven. Selah.

ours: Thou hast made void the covenant of thy servant: thou hast profaned his crown by casting it to the ground.
theirs: Thou hast made void the covenant of thy servant: thou hast profaned his crown [by casting it] to the ground.

ours: What man is he that liveth, and shall not see death? shall he deliver his soul from the hand of the grave? Selah.
theirs: What man [is he that] liveth, and shall not see death? shall he deliver his soul from the hand of the grave? Selah.

ours: Lord, where are thy former lovingkindnesses, which thou swarest unto David in thy truth?
theirs: Lord, where [are] thy former lovingkindnesses, [which] thou swarest unto David in thy truth?

ours: Remember, Lord, the reproach of thy servants; how I do bear in my bosom the reproach of all the mighty people;
theirs: Remember, Lord, the reproach of thy servants; [how] I do bear in my bosom [the reproach of] all the mighty people;

ours: Blessed be the LORD for evermore. Amen, and Amen.
theirs: Blessed [be] the LORD for evermore. Amen, and Amen.

ours: LORD, thou hast been our dwelling place in all generations.
theirs: <<A Prayer of Moses the man of God.>> Lord, thou hast been our dwelling place in all generations.

ours: Before the mountains were brought forth, or ever thou hadst formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, thou art God.
theirs: Before the mountains were brought forth, or ever thou hadst formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, thou [art] God.

ours: For a thousand years in thy sight are but as yesterday when it is past, and as a watch in the night.
theirs: For a thousand years in thy sight [are but] as yesterday when it is past, and [as] a watch in the night.

ours: Thou carriest them away as with a flood; they are as a sleep: in the morning they are like grass which groweth up.
theirs: Thou carriest them away as with a flood; they are [as] a sleep: in the morning [they are] like grass [which] groweth up.

ours: Thou hast set our iniquities before thee, our secret sins in the light of thy countenance.
theirs: Thou hast set our iniquities before thee, our secret [sins] in the light of thy countenance.

ours: For all our days are passed away in thy wrath: we spend our years as a tale that is told.
theirs: For all our days are passed away in thy wrath: we spend our years as a tale [that is told].

ours: The days of our years are threescore years and ten; and if by reason of strength they be fourscore years, yet is their strength labour and sorrow; for it is soon cut off, and we fly away.
theirs: The days of our years [are] threescore years and ten; and if by reason of strength [they be] fourscore years, yet [is] their strength labour and sorrow; for it is soon cut off, and we fly away.

ours: Who knoweth the power of thine anger? even according to thy fear, so is thy wrath.
theirs: Who knoweth the power of thine anger? even according to thy fear, [so is] thy wrath.

ours: So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.
theirs: So teach [us] to number our days, that we may apply [our] hearts unto wisdom.

ours: Make us glad according to the days wherein thou hast afflicted us, and the years wherein we have seen evil.
theirs: Make us glad according to the days [wherein] thou hast afflicted us, [and] the years [wherein] we have seen evil.

ours: I will say of the LORD, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust.
theirs: I will say of the LORD, [He is] my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust.

ours: Surely he shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler, and from the noisome pestilence.
theirs: Surely he shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler, [and] from the noisome pestilence.

ours: He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth shall be thy shield and buckler.
theirs: He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth [shall be thy] shield and buckler.

ours: Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night; nor for the arrow that flieth by day;
theirs: Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night; [nor] for the arrow [that] flieth by day;

ours: Nor for the pestilence that walketh in darkness; nor for the destruction that wasteth at noonday.
theirs: [Nor] for the pestilence [that] walketh in darkness; [nor] for the destruction [that] wasteth at noonday.

ours: A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand; but it shall not come nigh thee.
theirs: A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand; [but] it shall not come nigh thee.

ours: Because thou hast made the LORD, which is my refuge, even the most High, thy habitation;
theirs: Because thou hast made the LORD, [which is] my refuge, [even] the most High, thy habitation;

ours: They shall bear thee up in their hands, lest thou dash thy foot against a stone.
theirs: They shall bear thee up in [their] hands, lest thou dash thy foot against a stone.

ours: He shall call upon me, and I will answer him: I will be with him in trouble; I will deliver him, and honour him.
theirs: He shall call upon me, and I will answer him: I [will be] with him in trouble; I will deliver him, and honour him.

ours: IT is a good thing to give thanks unto the LORD, and to sing praises unto thy name, O most High:
theirs: <<A Psalm [or] Song for the sabbath day.>> [It is a] good [thing] to give thanks unto the LORD, and to sing praises unto thy name, O most High:

ours: O LORD, how great are thy works! and thy thoughts are very deep.
theirs: O LORD, how great are thy works! [and] thy thoughts are very deep.

ours: When the wicked spring as the grass, and when all the workers of iniquity do flourish; it is that they shall be destroyed for ever:
theirs: When the wicked spring as the grass, and when all the workers of iniquity do flourish; [it is] that they shall be destroyed for ever:

ours: But thou, LORD, art most high for evermore.
theirs: But thou, LORD, [art most] high for evermore.

ours: But my horn shalt thou exalt like the horn of an unicorn: I shall be anointed with fresh oil.
theirs: But my horn shalt thou exalt like [the horn of] an unicorn: I shall be anointed with fresh oil.

ours: Mine eye also shall see my desire on mine enemies, and mine ears shall hear my desire of the wicked that rise up against me.
theirs: Mine eye also shall see [my desire] on mine enemies, [and] mine ears shall hear [my desire] of the wicked that rise up against me.

ours: To shew that the LORD is upright: he is my rock, and there is no unrighteousness in him.
theirs: To shew that the LORD [is] upright: [he is] my rock, and [there is] no unrighteousness in him.

ours: THE LORD reigneth, he is clothed with majesty; the LORD is clothed with strength, wherewith he hath girded himself: the world also is stablished, that it cannot be moved.
theirs: The LORD reigneth, he is clothed with majesty; the LORD is clothed with strength, [wherewith] he hath girded himself: the world also is stablished, that it cannot be moved.

ours: Thy throne is established of old: thou art from everlasting.
theirs: Thy throne [is] established of old: thou [art] from everlasting.

ours: The LORD on high is mightier than the noise of many waters, yea, than the mighty waves of the sea.
theirs: The LORD on high [is] mightier than the noise of many waters, [yea, than] the mighty waves of the sea.

ours: How long shall they utter and speak hard things? and all the workers of iniquity boast themselves?
theirs: [How long] shall they utter [and] speak hard things? [and] all the workers of iniquity boast themselves?

ours: Yet they say, The LORD shall not see, neither shall the God of Jacob regard it.
theirs: Yet they say, The LORD shall not see, neither shall the God of Jacob regard [it].

ours: Understand, ye brutish among the people: and ye fools, when will ye be wise?
theirs: Understand, ye brutish among the people: and [ye] fools, when will ye be wise?

ours: He that chastiseth the heathen, shall not he correct? he that teacheth man knowledge, shall not he know?
theirs: He that chastiseth the heathen, shall not he correct? he that teacheth man knowledge, [shall not he know]?

ours: The LORD knoweth the thoughts of man, that they are vanity.
theirs: The LORD knoweth the thoughts of man, that they [are] vanity.

ours: Blessed is the man whom thou chastenest, O LORD, and teachest him out of thy law;
theirs: Blessed [is] the man whom thou chastenest, O LORD, and teachest him out of thy law;

ours: Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? or who will stand up for me against the workers of iniquity?
theirs: Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? [or] who will stand up for me against the workers of iniquity?

ours: Unless the LORD had been my help, my soul had almost dwelt in silence.
theirs: Unless the LORD [had been] my help, my soul had almost dwelt in silence.

ours: But the LORD is my defence; and my God is the rock of my refuge.
theirs: But the LORD is my defence; and my God [is] the rock of my refuge.

ours: And he shall bring upon them their own iniquity, and shall cut them off in their own wickedness; yea, the LORD our God shall cut them off.
theirs: And he shall bring upon them their own iniquity, and shall cut them off in their own wickedness; [yea], the LORD our God shall cut them off.

ours: For the LORD is a great God, and a great King above all gods.
theirs: For the LORD [is] a great God, and a great King above all gods.

ours: In his hand are the deep places of the earth: the strength of the hills is his also.
theirs: In his hand [are] the deep places of the earth: the strength of the hills [is] his also.

ours: The sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land.
theirs: The sea [is] his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry [land].

ours: For he is our God; and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand. To day if ye will hear his voice,
theirs: For he [is] our God; and we [are] the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand. To day if ye will hear his voice,

ours: Harden not your heart, as in the provocation, and as in the day of temptation in the wilderness:
theirs: Harden not your heart, as in the provocation, [and] as [in] the day of temptation in the wilderness:

ours: Forty years long was I grieved with this generation, and said, It is a people that do err in their heart, and they have not known my ways:
theirs: Forty years long was I grieved with [this] generation, and said, It [is] a people that do err in their heart, and they have not known my ways:

ours: For the LORD is great, and greatly to be praised: he is to be feared above all gods.
theirs: For the LORD [is] great, and greatly to be praised: he [is] to be feared above all gods.

ours: For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the LORD made the heavens.
theirs: For all the gods of the nations [are] idols: but the LORD made the heavens.

ours: Honour and majesty are before him: strength and beauty are in his sanctuary.
theirs: Honour and majesty [are] before him: strength and beauty [are] in his sanctuary.

ours: Give unto the LORD the glory due unto his name: bring an offering, and come into his courts.
theirs: Give unto the LORD the glory [due unto] his name: bring an offering, and come into his courts.

ours: Say among the heathen that the LORD reigneth: the world also shall be established that it shall not be moved: he shall judge the people righteously.
theirs: Say among the heathen [that] the LORD reigneth: the world also shall be established that it shall not be moved: he shall judge the people righteously.

ours: Let the field be joyful, and all that is therein: then shall all the trees of the wood rejoice
theirs: Let the field be joyful, and all that [is] therein: then shall all the trees of the wood rejoice

ours: THE LORD reigneth; let the earth rejoice; let the multitude of isles be glad thereof.
theirs: The LORD reigneth; let the earth rejoice; let the multitude of isles be glad [thereof].

ours: Clouds and darkness are round about him: righteousness and judgment are the habitation of his throne.
theirs: Clouds and darkness [are] round about him: righteousness and judgment [are] the habitation of his throne.

ours: Confounded be all they that serve graven images, that boast themselves of idols: worship him, all ye gods.
theirs: Confounded be all they that serve graven images, that boast themselves of idols: worship him, all [ye] gods.

ours: For thou, LORD, art high above all the earth: thou art exalted far above all gods.
theirs: For thou, LORD, [art] high above all the earth: thou art exalted far above all gods.

ours: O SING unto the LORD a new song; for he hath done marvellous things: his right hand, and his holy arm, hath gotten him the victory.
theirs: <<A Psalm.>> O sing unto the LORD a new song; for he hath done marvellous things: his right hand, and his holy arm, hath gotten him the victory.

ours: Let the floods clap their hands: let the hills be joyful together
theirs: Let the floods clap [their] hands: let the hills be joyful together

ours: THE LORD reigneth; let the people tremble: he sitteth between the cherubims; let the earth be moved.
theirs: The LORD reigneth; let the people tremble: he sitteth [between] the cherubims; let the earth be moved.

ours: The LORD is great in Zion; and he is high above all the people.
theirs: The LORD [is] great in Zion; and he [is] high above all the people.

ours: Let them praise thy great and terrible name; for it is holy.
theirs: Let them praise thy great and terrible name; [for] it [is] holy.

ours: The kings strength also loveth judgment; thou dost establish equity, thou executest judgment and righteousness in Jacob.
theirs: The king's strength also loveth judgment; thou dost establish equity, thou executest judgment and righteousness in Jacob.

ours: Exalt ye the LORD our God, and worship at his footstool; for he is holy.
theirs: Exalt ye the LORD our God, and worship at his footstool; [for] he [is] holy.

ours: He spake unto them in the cloudy pillar: they kept his testimonies, and the ordinance that he gave them.
theirs: He spake unto them in the cloudy pillar: they kept his testimonies, and the ordinance [that] he gave them.

ours: Exalt the LORD our God, and worship at his holy hill; for the LORD our God is holy.
theirs: Exalt the LORD our God, and worship at his holy hill; for the LORD our God [is] holy.

ours: MAKE a joyful noise unto the LORD, all ye lands.
theirs: <<A Psalm of praise.>> Make a joyful noise unto the LORD, all ye lands.

ours: Know ye that the LORD he is God: it is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves; we are his people, and the sheep of his pasture.
theirs: Know ye that the LORD he [is] God: [it is] he [that] hath made us, and not we ourselves; [we are] his people, and the sheep of his pasture.

ours: Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name.
theirs: Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, [and] into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, [and] bless his name.

ours: For the LORD is good; his mercy is everlasting; and his truth endureth to all generations.
theirs: For the LORD [is] good; his mercy [is] everlasting; and his truth [endureth] to all generations.

ours: I WILL sing of mercy and judgment: unto thee, O LORD, will I sing.
theirs: <<A Psalm of David.>> I will sing of mercy and judgment: unto thee, O LORD, will I sing.

ours: I will set no wicked thing before mine eyes: I hate the work of them that turn aside; it shall not cleave to me.
theirs: I will set no wicked thing before mine eyes: I hate the work of them that turn aside; [it] shall not cleave to me.

ours: A froward heart shall depart from me: I will not know a wicked person.
theirs: A froward heart shall depart from me: I will not know a wicked [person].

ours: Mine eyes shall be upon the faithful of the land, that they may dwell with me: he that walketh in a perfect way, he shall serve me.
theirs: Mine eyes [shall be] upon the faithful of the land, that they may dwell with me: he that walketh in a perfect way, he shall serve me.

ours: HEAR my prayer, O LORD, and let my cry come unto thee.
theirs: <<A Prayer of the afflicted, when he is overwhelmed, and poureth out his complaint before the LORD.>> Hear my prayer, O LORD, and let my cry come unto thee.

ours: Hide not thy face from me in the day when I am in trouble; incline thine ear unto me: in the day when I call answer me speedily.
theirs: Hide not thy face from me in the day [when] I am in trouble; incline thine ear unto me: in the day [when] I call answer me speedily.

ours: Mine enemies reproach me all the day; and they that are mad against me are sworn against me.
theirs: Mine enemies reproach me all the day; [and] they that are mad against me are sworn against me.

ours: My days are like a shadow that declineth; and I am withered like grass.
theirs: My days [are] like a shadow that declineth; and I am withered like grass.

ours: Thou shalt arise, and have mercy upon Zion: for the time to favour her, yea, the set time, is come.
theirs: Thou shalt arise, [and] have mercy upon Zion: for the time to favour her, yea, the set time, is come.

ours: I said, O my God, take me not away in the midst of my days: thy years are throughout all generations.
theirs: I said, O my God, take me not away in the midst of my days: thy years [are] throughout all generations.

ours: Of old hast thou laid the foundation of the earth: and the heavens are the work of thy hands.
theirs: Of old hast thou laid the foundation of the earth: and the heavens [are] the work of thy hands.

ours: But thou art the same, and thy years shall have no end.
theirs: But thou [art] the same, and thy years shall have no end.

ours: BLESS the LORD, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David.>> Bless the LORD, O my soul: and all that is within me, [bless] his holy name.

ours: Who satisfieth thy mouth with good things; so that thy youth is renewed like the eagles.
theirs: Who satisfieth thy mouth with good [things; so that] thy youth is renewed like the eagle's.

ours: The LORD is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy.
theirs: The LORD [is] merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy.

ours: He will not always chide: neither will he keep his anger for ever.
theirs: He will not always chide: neither will he keep [his anger] for ever.

ours: For as the heaven is high above the earth, so great is his mercy toward them that fear him.
theirs: For as the heaven is high above the earth, [so] great is his mercy toward them that fear him.

ours: As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us.
theirs: As far as the east is from the west, [so] far hath he removed our transgressions from us.

ours: Like as a father pitieth his children, so the LORD pitieth them that fear him.
theirs: Like as a father pitieth [his] children, [so] the LORD pitieth them that fear him.

ours: For he knoweth our frame; he remembereth that we are dust.
theirs: For he knoweth our frame; he remembereth that we [are] dust.

ours: As for man, his days are as grass: as a flower of the field, so he flourisheth.
theirs: [As for] man, his days [are] as grass: as a flower of the field, so he flourisheth.

ours: But the mercy of the LORD is from everlasting to everlasting upon them that fear him, and his righteousness unto childrens children;
theirs: But the mercy of the LORD [is] from everlasting to everlasting upon them that fear him, and his righteousness unto children's children;

ours: Bless ye the LORD, all ye his hosts; ye ministers of his, that do his pleasure.
theirs: Bless ye the LORD, all [ye] his hosts; [ye] ministers of his, that do his pleasure.

ours: Who coverest thyself with light as with a garment: who stretchest out the heavens like a curtain:
theirs: Who coverest [thyself] with light as [with] a garment: who stretchest out the heavens like a curtain:

ours: Who laid the foundations of the earth, that it should not be removed for ever.
theirs: [Who] laid the foundations of the earth, [that] it should not be removed for ever.

ours: Thou coveredst it with the deep as with a garment: the waters stood above the mountains.
theirs: Thou coveredst it with the deep as [with] a garment: the waters stood above the mountains.

ours: He sendeth the springs into the valleys, which run among the hills.
theirs: He sendeth the springs into the valleys, [which] run among the hills.

ours: By them shall the fowls of the heaven have their habitation, which sing among the branches.
theirs: By them shall the fowls of the heaven have their habitation, [which] sing among the branches.

ours: And wine that maketh glad the heart of man, and oil to make his face to shine, and bread which strengtheneth mans heart.
theirs: And wine [that] maketh glad the heart of man, [and] oil to make [his] face to shine, and bread [which] strengtheneth man's heart.

ours: The trees of the LORD are full of sap; the cedars of Lebanon, which he hath planted;
theirs: The trees of the LORD are full [of sap]; the cedars of Lebanon, which he hath planted;

ours: Where the birds make their nests: as for the stork, the fir trees are her house.
theirs: Where the birds make their nests: [as for] the stork, the fir trees [are] her house.

ours: The high hills are a refuge for the wild goats; and the rocks for the conies.
theirs: The high hills [are] a refuge for the wild goats; [and] the rocks for the conies.

ours: Thou makest darkness, and it is night: wherein all the beasts of the forest do creep forth.
theirs: Thou makest darkness, and it is night: wherein all the beasts of the forest do creep [forth].

ours: So is this great and wide sea, wherein are things creeping innumerable, both small and great beasts.
theirs: [So is] this great and wide sea, wherein [are] things creeping innumerable, both small and great beasts.

ours: There go the ships: there is that leviathan, whom thou hast made to play therein.
theirs: There go the ships: [there is] that leviathan, [whom] thou hast made to play therein.

ours: These wait all upon thee; that thou mayest give them their meat in due season.
theirs: These wait all upon thee; that thou mayest give [them] their meat in due season.

ours: That thou givest them they gather: thou openest thine hand, they are filled with good.
theirs: [That] thou givest them they gather: thou openest thine hand, they are filled with good.

ours: He is the LORD our God: his judgments are in all the earth.
theirs: He [is] the LORD our God: his judgments [are] in all the earth.

ours: He hath remembered his covenant for ever, the word which he commanded to a thousand generations.
theirs: He hath remembered his covenant for ever, the word [which] he commanded to a thousand generations.

ours: Which covenant he made with Abraham, and his oath unto Isaac;
theirs: Which [covenant] he made with Abraham, and his oath unto Isaac;

ours: And confirmed the same unto Jacob for a law, and to Israel for an everlasting covenant:
theirs: And confirmed the same unto Jacob for a law, [and] to Israel [for] an everlasting covenant:

ours: When they were but a few men in number; yea, very few, and strangers in it.
theirs: When they were [but] a few men in number; yea, very few, and strangers in it.

ours: When they went from one nation to another, from one kingdom to another people;
theirs: When they went from one nation to another, from [one] kingdom to another people;

ours: Saying, Touch not mine anointed, and do my prophets no harm.
theirs: [Saying], Touch not mine anointed, and do my prophets no harm.

ours: He sent a man before them, even Joseph, who was sold for a servant:
theirs: He sent a man before them, [even] Joseph, [who] was sold for a servant:

ours: The king sent and loosed him; even the ruler of the people, and let him go free.
theirs: The king sent and loosed him; [even] the ruler of the people, and let him go free.

ours: He sent Moses his servant; and Aaron whom he had chosen.
theirs: He sent Moses his servant; [and] Aaron whom he had chosen.

ours: He spake, and there came divers sorts of flies, and lice in all their coasts.
theirs: He spake, and there came divers sorts of flies, [and] lice in all their coasts.

ours: He gave them hail for rain, and flaming fire in their land.
theirs: He gave them hail for rain, [and] flaming fire in their land.

ours: He brought them forth also with silver and gold: and there was not one feeble person among their tribes.
theirs: He brought them forth also with silver and gold: and [there was] not one feeble [person] among their tribes.

ours: The people asked, and he brought quails, and satisfied them with the bread of heaven.
theirs: [The people] asked, and he brought quails, and satisfied them with the bread of heaven.

ours: He opened the rock, and the waters gushed out; they ran in the dry places like a river.
theirs: He opened the rock, and the waters gushed out; they ran in the dry places [like] a river.

ours: For he remembered his holy promise, and Abraham his servant.
theirs: For he remembered his holy promise, [and] Abraham his servant.

ours: And he brought forth his people with joy, and his chosen with gladness:
theirs: And he brought forth his people with joy, [and] his chosen with gladness:

ours: PRAISE ye the LORD. O give thanks unto the LORD; for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.
theirs: Praise ye the LORD. O give thanks unto the LORD; for [he is] good: for his mercy [endureth] for ever.

ours: Who can utter the mighty acts of the LORD? who can shew forth all his praise?
theirs: Who can utter the mighty acts of the LORD? [who] can shew forth all his praise?

ours: Blessed are they that keep judgment, and he that doeth righteousness at all times.
theirs: Blessed [are] they that keep judgment, [and] he that doeth righteousness at all times.

ours: Remember me, O LORD, with the favour that thou bearest unto thy people: O visit me with thy salvation;
theirs: Remember me, O LORD, with the favour [that thou bearest unto] thy people: O visit me with thy salvation;

ours: Our fathers understood not thy wonders in Egypt; they remembered not the multitude of thy mercies; but provoked him at the sea, even at the Red sea.
theirs: Our fathers understood not thy wonders in Egypt; they remembered not the multitude of thy mercies; but provoked [him] at the sea, [even] at the Red sea.

ours: Nevertheless he saved them for his names sake, that he might make his mighty power to be known.
theirs: Nevertheless he saved them for his name's sake, that he might make his mighty power to be known.

ours: And he saved them from the hand of him that hated them, and redeemed them from the hand of the enemy.
theirs: And he saved them from the hand of him that hated [them], and redeemed them from the hand of the enemy.

ours: They envied Moses also in the camp, and Aaron the saint of the LORD.
theirs: They envied Moses also in the camp, [and] Aaron the saint of the LORD.

ours: Wondrous works in the land of Ham, and terrible things by the Red sea.
theirs: Wondrous works in the land of Ham, [and] terrible things by the Red sea.

ours: Therefore he said that he would destroy them, had not Moses his chosen stood before him in the breach, to turn away his wrath, lest he should destroy them.
theirs: Therefore he said that he would destroy them, had not Moses his chosen stood before him in the breach, to turn away his wrath, lest he should destroy [them].

ours: But murmured in their tents, and hearkened not unto the voice of the LORD.
theirs: But murmured in their tents, [and] hearkened not unto the voice of the LORD.

ours: They joined themselves also unto Baal-peor, and ate the sacrifices of the dead.
theirs: They joined themselves also unto Baalpeor, and ate the sacrifices of the dead.

ours: Thus they provoked him to anger with their inventions: and the plague brake in upon them.
theirs: Thus they provoked [him] to anger with their inventions: and the plague brake in upon them.

ours: Then stood up Phinehas, and executed judgment: and so the plague was stayed.
theirs: Then stood up Phinehas, and executed judgment: and [so] the plague was stayed.

ours: They angered him also at the waters of strife, so that it went ill with Moses for their sakes:
theirs: They angered [him] also at the waters of strife, so that it went ill with Moses for their sakes:

ours: And shed innocent blood, even the blood of their sons and of their daughters, whom they sacrificed unto the idols of Canaan: and the land was polluted with blood.
theirs: And shed innocent blood, [even] the blood of their sons and of their daughters, whom they sacrificed unto the idols of Canaan: and the land was polluted with blood.

ours: Many times did he deliver them; but they provoked him with their counsel, and were brought low for their iniquity.
theirs: Many times did he deliver them; but they provoked [him] with their counsel, and were brought low for their iniquity.

ours: Save us, O LORD our God, and gather us from among the heathen, to give thanks unto thy holy name, and to triumph in thy praise.
theirs: Save us, O LORD our God, and gather us from among the heathen, to give thanks unto thy holy name, [and] to triumph in thy praise.

ours: Blessed be the LORD God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting: and let all the people say, Amen. Praise ye the LORD.
theirs: Blessed [be] the LORD God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting: and let all the people say, Amen. Praise ye the LORD.

ours: O GIVE thanks unto the LORD, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.
theirs: O give thanks unto the LORD, for [he is] good: for his mercy [endureth] for ever.

ours: Let the redeemed of the LORD say so, whom he hath redeemed from the hand of the enemy;
theirs: Let the redeemed of the LORD say [so], whom he hath redeemed from the hand of the enemy;

ours: Then they cried unto the LORD in their trouble, and he delivered them out of their distresses.
theirs: Then they cried unto the LORD in their trouble, [and] he delivered them out of their distresses.
