ours: For the ways of man are before the eyes of the LORD, and he pondereth all his goings.
theirs: For the ways of man [are] before the eyes of the LORD, and he pondereth all his goings.

ours: MY son, if thou be surety for thy friend, if thou hast stricken thy hand with a stranger,
theirs: My son, if thou be surety for thy friend, [if] thou hast stricken thy hand with a stranger,

ours: Deliver thyself as a roe from the hand of the hunter, and as a bird from the hand of the fowler.
theirs: Deliver thyself as a roe from the hand [of the hunter], and as a bird from the hand of the fowler.

ours: Provideth her meat in the summer, and gathereth her food in the harvest.
theirs: Provideth her meat in the summer, [and] gathereth her food in the harvest.

ours: Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep:
theirs: [Yet] a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep:

ours: Frowardness is in his heart, he deviseth mischief continually; he soweth discord.
theirs: Frowardness [is] in his heart, he deviseth mischief continually; he soweth discord.

ours: These six things doth the LORD hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him:
theirs: These six [things] doth the LORD hate: yea, seven [are] an abomination unto him:

ours: A false witness that speaketh lies, and he that soweth discord among brethren.
theirs: A false witness [that] speaketh lies, and he that soweth discord among brethren.

ours: My son, keep thy fathers commandment, and forsake not the law of thy mother:
theirs: My son, keep thy father's commandment, and forsake not the law of thy mother:

ours: Bind them continually upon thine heart, and tie them about thy neck.
theirs: Bind them continually upon thine heart, [and] tie them about thy neck.

ours: When thou goest, it shall lead thee; when thou sleepest, it shall keep thee; and when thou awakest, it shall talk with thee.
theirs: When thou goest, it shall lead thee; when thou sleepest, it shall keep thee; and [when] thou awakest, it shall talk with thee.

ours: For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life:
theirs: For the commandment [is] a lamp; and the law [is] light; and reproofs of instruction [are] the way of life:

ours: For by means of a whorish woman a man is brought to a piece of bread: and the adulteress will hunt for the precious life.
theirs: For by means of a whorish woman [a man is brought] to a piece of bread: and the adulteress will hunt for the precious life.

ours: So he that goeth in to his neighbours wife; whosoever toucheth her shall not be innocent.
theirs: So he that goeth in to his neighbour's wife; whosoever toucheth her shall not be innocent.

ours: Men do not despise a thief, if he steal to satisfy his soul when he is hungry;
theirs: [Men] do not despise a thief, if he steal to satisfy his soul when he is hungry;

ours: But if he be found, he shall restore sevenfold; he shall give all the substance of his house.
theirs: But [if] he be found, he shall restore sevenfold; he shall give all the substance of his house.

ours: But whoso committeth adultery with a woman lacketh understanding: he that doeth it destroyeth his own soul.
theirs: [But] whoso committeth adultery with a woman lacketh understanding: he [that] doeth it destroyeth his own soul.

ours: For jealousy is the rage of a man: therefore he will not spare in the day of vengeance.
theirs: For jealousy [is] the rage of a man: therefore he will not spare in the day of vengeance.

ours: Say unto wisdom, Thou art my sister; and call understanding thy kinswoman:
theirs: Say unto wisdom, Thou [art] my sister; and call understanding [thy] kinswoman:

ours: That they may keep thee from the strange woman, from the stranger which flattereth with her words.
theirs: That they may keep thee from the strange woman, from the stranger [which] flattereth with her words.

ours: And, behold, there met him a woman with the attire of an harlot, and subtil of heart.
theirs: And, behold, there met him a woman [with] the attire of an harlot, and subtil of heart.

ours: (She is loud and stubborn; her feet abide not in her house:
theirs: (She [is] loud and stubborn; her feet abide not in her house:

ours: Now is she without, now in the streets, and lieth in wait at every corner.)
theirs: Now [is she] without, now in the streets, and lieth in wait at every corner.)

ours: So she caught him, and kissed him, and with an impudent face said unto him,
theirs: So she caught him, and kissed him, [and] with an impudent face said unto him,

ours: I have peace offerings with me; this day have I payed my vows.
theirs: [I have] peace offerings with me; this day have I payed my vows.

ours: I have decked my bed with coverings of tapestry, with carved works, with fine linen of Egypt.
theirs: I have decked my bed with coverings of tapestry, with carved [works], with fine linen of Egypt.

ours: For the goodman is not at home, he is gone a long journey:
theirs: For the goodman [is] not at home, he is gone a long journey:

ours: He hath taken a bag of money with him, and will come home at the day appointed.
theirs: He hath taken a bag of money with him, [and] will come home at the day appointed.

ours: Till a dart strike through his liver; as a bird hasteth to the snare, and knoweth not that it is for his life.
theirs: Till a dart strike through his liver; as a bird hasteth to the snare, and knoweth not that it [is] for his life.

ours: For she hath cast down many wounded: yea, many strong men have been slain by her.
theirs: For she hath cast down many wounded: yea, many strong [men] have been slain by her.

ours: Her house is the way to hell, going down to the chambers of death.
theirs: Her house [is] the way to hell, going down to the chambers of death.

ours: Unto you, O men, I call; and my voice is to the sons of man.
theirs: Unto you, O men, I call; and my voice [is] to the sons of man.

ours: Hear; for I will speak of excellent things; and the opening of my lips shall be right things.
theirs: Hear; for I will speak of excellent things; and the opening of my lips [shall be] right things.

ours: For my mouth shall speak truth; and wickedness is an abomination to my lips.
theirs: For my mouth shall speak truth; and wickedness [is] an abomination to my lips.

ours: All the words of my mouth are in righteousness; there is nothing froward or perverse in them.
theirs: All the words of my mouth [are] in righteousness; [there is] nothing froward or perverse in them.

ours: They are all plain to him that understandeth, and right to them that find knowledge.
theirs: They [are] all plain to him that understandeth, and right to them that find knowledge.

ours: For wisdom is better than rubies; and all the things that may be desired are not to be compared to it.
theirs: For wisdom [is] better than rubies; and all the things that may be desired are not to be compared to it.

ours: The fear of the LORD is to hate evil: pride, and arrogancy, and the evil way, and the froward mouth, do I hate.
theirs: The fear of the LORD [is] to hate evil: pride, and arrogancy, and the evil way, and the froward mouth, do I hate.

ours: Counsel is mine, and sound wisdom: I am understanding; I have strength.
theirs: Counsel [is] mine, and sound wisdom: I [am] understanding; I have strength.

ours: By me princes rule, and nobles, even all the judges of the earth.
theirs: By me princes rule, and nobles, [even] all the judges of the earth.

ours: Riches and honour are with me; yea, durable riches and righteousness.
theirs: Riches and honour [are] with me; [yea], durable riches and righteousness.

ours: My fruit is better than gold, yea, than fine gold; and my revenue than choice silver.
theirs: My fruit [is] better than gold, yea, than fine gold; and my revenue than choice silver.

ours: When there were no depths, I was brought forth; when there were no fountains abounding with water.
theirs: When [there were] no depths, I was brought forth; when [there were] no fountains abounding with water.

ours: When he prepared the heavens, I was there: when he set a compass upon the face of the depth:
theirs: When he prepared the heavens, I [was] there: when he set a compass upon the face of the depth:

ours: Then I was by him, as one brought up with him: and I was daily his delight, rejoicing always before him;
theirs: Then I was by him, [as] one brought up [with him]: and I was daily [his] delight, rejoicing always before him;

ours: Rejoicing in the habitable part of his earth; and my delights were with the sons of men.
theirs: Rejoicing in the habitable part of his earth; and my delights [were] with the sons of men.

ours: Now therefore hearken unto me, O ye children: for blessed are they that keep my ways.
theirs: Now therefore hearken unto me, O ye children: for blessed [are they that] keep my ways.

ours: Blessed is the man that heareth me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at the posts of my doors.
theirs: Blessed [is] the man that heareth me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at the posts of my doors.

ours: Whoso is simple, let him turn in hither: as for him that wanteth understanding, she saith to him,
theirs: Whoso [is] simple, let him turn in hither: [as for] him that wanteth understanding, she saith to him,

ours: Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine which I have mingled.
theirs: Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine [which] I have mingled.

ours: He that reproveth a scorner getteth to himself shame: and he that rebuketh a wicked man getteth himself a blot.
theirs: He that reproveth a scorner getteth to himself shame: and he that rebuketh a wicked [man getteth] himself a blot.

ours: Give instruction to a wise man, and he will be yet wiser: teach a just man, and he will increase in learning.
theirs: Give [instruction] to a wise [man], and he will be yet wiser: teach a just [man], and he will increase in learning.

ours: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.
theirs: The fear of the LORD [is] the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy [is] understanding.

ours: If thou be wise, thou shalt be wise for thyself: but if thou scornest, thou alone shalt bear it.
theirs: If thou be wise, thou shalt be wise for thyself: but [if] thou scornest, thou alone shalt bear [it].

ours: A foolish woman is clamorous: she is simple, and knoweth nothing.
theirs: A foolish woman [is] clamorous: [she is] simple, and knoweth nothing.

ours: Whoso is simple, let him turn in hither: and as for him that wanteth understanding, she saith to him,
theirs: Whoso [is] simple, let him turn in hither: and [as for] him that wanteth understanding, she saith to him,

ours: Stolen waters are sweet, and bread eaten in secret is pleasant.
theirs: Stolen waters are sweet, and bread [eaten] in secret is pleasant.

ours: But he knoweth not that the dead are there; and that her guests are in the depths of hell.
theirs: But he knoweth not that the dead [are] there; [and that] her guests [are] in the depths of hell.

ours: THE proverbs of Solomon. A wise son maketh a glad father: but a foolish son is the heaviness of his mother.
theirs: The proverbs of Solomon. A wise son maketh a glad father: but a foolish son [is] the heaviness of his mother.

ours: He becometh poor that dealeth with a slack hand: but the hand of the diligent maketh rich.
theirs: He becometh poor that dealeth [with] a slack hand: but the hand of the diligent maketh rich.

ours: He that gathereth in summer is a wise son: but he that sleepeth in harvest is a son that causeth shame.
theirs: He that gathereth in summer [is] a wise son: [but] he that sleepeth in harvest [is] a son that causeth shame.

ours: Blessings are upon the head of the just: but violence covereth the mouth of the wicked.
theirs: Blessings [are] upon the head of the just: but violence covereth the mouth of the wicked.

ours: The memory of the just is blessed: but the name of the wicked shall rot.
theirs: The memory of the just [is] blessed: but the name of the wicked shall rot.

ours: The mouth of a righteous man is a well of life: but violence covereth the mouth of the wicked.
theirs: The mouth of a righteous [man is] a well of life: but violence covereth the mouth of the wicked.

ours: In the lips of him that hath understanding wisdom is found: but a rod is for the back of him that is void of understanding.
theirs: In the lips of him that hath understanding wisdom is found: but a rod [is] for the back of him that is void of understanding.

ours: Wise men lay up knowledge: but the mouth of the foolish is near destruction.
theirs: Wise [men] lay up knowledge: but the mouth of the foolish [is] near destruction.

ours: The rich mans wealth is his strong city: the destruction of the poor is their poverty.
theirs: The rich man's wealth [is] his strong city: the destruction of the poor [is] their poverty.

ours: The labour of the righteous tendeth to life: the fruit of the wicked to sin.
theirs: The labour of the righteous [tendeth] to life: the fruit of the wicked to sin.

ours: He is in the way of life that keepeth instruction: but he that refuseth reproof erreth.
theirs: He [is in] the way of life that keepeth instruction: but he that refuseth reproof erreth.

ours: He that hideth hatred with lying lips, and he that uttereth a slander, is a fool.
theirs: He that hideth hatred [with] lying lips, and he that uttereth a slander, [is] a fool.

ours: In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips is wise.
theirs: In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips [is] wise.

ours: The tongue of the just is as choice silver: the heart of the wicked is little worth.
theirs: The tongue of the just [is as] choice silver: the heart of the wicked [is] little worth.

ours: It is as sport to a fool to do mischief: but a man of understanding hath wisdom.
theirs: [It is] as sport to a fool to do mischief: but a man of understanding hath wisdom.

ours: As the whirlwind passeth, so is the wicked no more: but the righteous is an everlasting foundation.
theirs: As the whirlwind passeth, so [is] the wicked no [more]: but the righteous [is] an everlasting foundation.

ours: As vinegar to the teeth, and as smoke to the eyes, so is the sluggard to them that send him.
theirs: As vinegar to the teeth, and as smoke to the eyes, so [is] the sluggard to them that send him.

ours: The hope of the righteous shall be gladness: but the expectation of the wicked shall perish.
theirs: The hope of the righteous [shall be] gladness: but the expectation of the wicked shall perish.

ours: The way of the LORD is strength to the upright: but destruction shall be to the workers of iniquity.
theirs: The way of the LORD [is] strength to the upright: but destruction [shall be] to the workers of iniquity.

ours: The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable: but the mouth of the wicked speaketh frowardness.
theirs: The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable: but the mouth of the wicked [speaketh] frowardness.

ours: A FALSE balance is abomination to the LORD: but a just weight is his delight.
theirs: A false balance [is] abomination to the LORD: but a just weight [is] his delight.

ours: When pride cometh, then cometh shame: but with the lowly is wisdom.
theirs: [When] pride cometh, then cometh shame: but with the lowly [is] wisdom.

ours: The righteousness of the upright shall deliver them: but transgressors shall be taken in their own naughtiness.
theirs: The righteousness of the upright shall deliver them: but transgressors shall be taken in [their own] naughtiness.

ours: When a wicked man dieth, his expectation shall perish: and the hope of unjust men perisheth.
theirs: When a wicked man dieth, [his] expectation shall perish: and the hope of unjust [men] perisheth.

ours: An hypocrite with his mouth destroyeth his neighbour: but through knowledge shall the just be delivered.
theirs: An hypocrite with [his] mouth destroyeth his neighbour: but through knowledge shall the just be delivered.

ours: When it goeth well with the righteous, the city rejoiceth: and when the wicked perish, there is shouting.
theirs: When it goeth well with the righteous, the city rejoiceth: and when the wicked perish, [there is] shouting.

ours: Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellers there is safety.
theirs: Where no counsel [is], the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellers [there is] safety.

ours: He that is surety for a stranger shall smart for it: and he that hateth suretiship is sure.
theirs: He that is surety for a stranger shall smart [for it]: and he that hateth suretiship is sure.

ours: A gracious woman retaineth honour: and strong men retain riches.
theirs: A gracious woman retaineth honour: and strong [men] retain riches.

ours: The merciful man doeth good to his own soul: but he that is cruel troubleth his own flesh.
theirs: The merciful man doeth good to his own soul: but [he that is] cruel troubleth his own flesh.

ours: The wicked worketh a deceitful work: but to him that soweth righteousness shall be a sure reward.
theirs: The wicked worketh a deceitful work: but to him that soweth righteousness [shall be] a sure reward.

ours: As righteousness tendeth to life: so he that pursueth evil pursueth it to his own death.
theirs: As righteousness [tendeth] to life: so he that pursueth evil [pursueth it] to his own death.

ours: They that are of a froward heart are abomination to the LORD: but such as are upright in their way are his delight.
theirs: They that are of a froward heart [are] abomination to the LORD: but [such as are] upright in [their] way [are] his delight.

ours: Though hand join in hand, the wicked shall not be unpunished: but the seed of the righteous shall be delivered.
theirs: [Though] hand [join] in hand, the wicked shall not be unpunished: but the seed of the righteous shall be delivered.

ours: As a jewel of gold in a swines snout, so is a fair woman which is without discretion.
theirs: [As] a jewel of gold in a swine's snout, [so is] a fair woman which is without discretion.

ours: The desire of the righteous is only good: but the expectation of the wicked is wrath.
theirs: The desire of the righteous [is] only good: [but] the expectation of the wicked [is] wrath.

ours: There is that scattereth, and yet increaseth; and there is that withholdeth more than is meet, but it tendeth to poverty.
theirs: There is that scattereth, and yet increaseth; and [there is] that withholdeth more than is meet, but [it tendeth] to poverty.

ours: He that withholdeth corn, the people shall curse him: but blessing shall be upon the head of him that selleth it.
theirs: He that withholdeth corn, the people shall curse him: but blessing [shall be] upon the head of him that selleth [it].

ours: He that troubleth his own house shall inherit the wind: and the fool shall be servant to the wise of heart.
theirs: He that troubleth his own house shall inherit the wind: and the fool [shall be] servant to the wise of heart.

ours: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life; and he that winneth souls is wise.
theirs: The fruit of the righteous [is] a tree of life; and he that winneth souls [is] wise.

ours: WHOSO loveth instruction loveth knowledge: but he that hateth reproof is brutish.
theirs: Whoso loveth instruction loveth knowledge: but he that hateth reproof [is] brutish.

ours: A good man obtaineth favour of the LORD: but a man of wicked devices will he condemn.
theirs: A good [man] obtaineth favour of the LORD: but a man of wicked devices will he condemn.

ours: A virtuous woman is a crown to her husband: but she that maketh ashamed is as rottenness in his bones.
theirs: A virtuous woman [is] a crown to her husband: but she that maketh ashamed [is] as rottenness in his bones.

ours: The thoughts of the righteous are right: but the counsels of the wicked are deceit.
theirs: The thoughts of the righteous [are] right: [but] the counsels of the wicked [are] deceit.

ours: The words of the wicked are to lie in wait for blood: but the mouth of the upright shall deliver them.
theirs: The words of the wicked [are] to lie in wait for blood: but the mouth of the upright shall deliver them.

ours: The wicked are overthrown, and are not: but the house of the righteous shall stand.
theirs: The wicked are overthrown, and [are] not: but the house of the righteous shall stand.

ours: He that is despised, and hath a servant, is better than he that honoureth himself, and lacketh bread.
theirs: [He that is] despised, and hath a servant, [is] better than he that honoureth himself, and lacketh bread.

ours: A righteous man regardeth the life of his beast: but the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel.
theirs: A righteous [man] regardeth the life of his beast: but the tender mercies of the wicked [are] cruel.

ours: He that tilleth his land shall be satisfied with bread: but he that followeth vain persons is void of understanding.
theirs: He that tilleth his land shall be satisfied with bread: but he that followeth vain [persons is] void of understanding.

ours: The wicked desireth the net of evil men: but the root of the righteous yieldeth fruit.
theirs: The wicked desireth the net of evil [men]: but the root of the righteous yieldeth [fruit].

ours: The wicked is snared by the transgression of his lips: but the just shall come out of trouble.
theirs: The wicked is snared by the transgression of [his] lips: but the just shall come out of trouble.

ours: A man shall be satisfied with good by the fruit of his mouth: and the recompence of a mans hands shall be rendered unto him.
theirs: A man shall be satisfied with good by the fruit of [his] mouth: and the recompence of a man's hands shall be rendered unto him.

ours: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes: but he that hearkeneth unto counsel is wise.
theirs: The way of a fool [is] right in his own eyes: but he that hearkeneth unto counsel [is] wise.

ours: A fools wrath is presently known: but a prudent man covereth shame.
theirs: A fool's wrath is presently known: but a prudent [man] covereth shame.

ours: He that speaketh truth sheweth forth righteousness: but a false witness deceit.
theirs: [He that] speaketh truth sheweth forth righteousness: but a false witness deceit.

ours: There is that speaketh like the piercings of a sword: but the tongue of the wise is health.
theirs: There is that speaketh like the piercings of a sword: but the tongue of the wise [is] health.

ours: The lip of truth shall be established for ever: but a lying tongue is but for a moment.
theirs: The lip of truth shall be established for ever: but a lying tongue [is] but for a moment.

ours: Deceit is in the heart of them that imagine evil: but to the counsellers of peace is joy.
theirs: Deceit [is] in the heart of them that imagine evil: but to the counsellers of peace [is] joy.

ours: Lying lips are abomination to the LORD: but they that deal truly are his delight.
theirs: Lying lips [are] abomination to the LORD: but they that deal truly [are] his delight.

ours: The righteous is more excellent than his neighbour: but the way of the wicked seduceth them.
theirs: The righteous [is] more excellent than his neighbour: but the way of the wicked seduceth them.

ours: The slothful man roasteth not that which he took in hunting: but the substance of a diligent man is precious.
theirs: The slothful [man] roasteth not that which he took in hunting: but the substance of a diligent man [is] precious.

ours: In the way of righteousness is life; and in the pathway thereof there is no death.
theirs: In the way of righteousness [is] life; and [in] the pathway [thereof there is] no death.

ours: A WISE son heareth his fathers instruction: but a scorner heareth not rebuke.
theirs: A wise son [heareth] his father's instruction: but a scorner heareth not rebuke.

ours: A man shall eat good by the fruit of his mouth: but the soul of the transgressors shall eat violence.
theirs: A man shall eat good by the fruit of [his] mouth: but the soul of the transgressors [shall eat] violence.

ours: He that keepeth his mouth keepeth his life: but he that openeth wide his lips shall have destruction.
theirs: He that keepeth his mouth keepeth his life: [but] he that openeth wide his lips shall have destruction.

ours: The soul of the sluggard desireth, and hath nothing: but the soul of the diligent shall be made fat.
theirs: The soul of the sluggard desireth, and [hath] nothing: but the soul of the diligent shall be made fat.

ours: A righteous man hateth lying: but a wicked man is loathsome, and cometh to shame.
theirs: A righteous [man] hateth lying: but a wicked [man] is loathsome, and cometh to shame.

ours: Righteousness keepeth him that is upright in the way: but wickedness overthroweth the sinner.
theirs: Righteousness keepeth [him that is] upright in the way: but wickedness overthroweth the sinner.

ours: There is that maketh himself rich, yet hath nothing: there is that maketh himself poor, yet hath great riches.
theirs: There is that maketh himself rich, yet [hath] nothing: [there is] that maketh himself poor, yet [hath] great riches.

ours: The ransom of a mans life are his riches: but the poor heareth not rebuke.
theirs: The ransom of a man's life [are] his riches: but the poor heareth not rebuke.

ours: Only by pride cometh contention: but with the well advised is wisdom.
theirs: Only by pride cometh contention: but with the well advised [is] wisdom.

ours: Wealth gotten by vanity shall be diminished: but he that gathereth by labour shall increase.
theirs: Wealth [gotten] by vanity shall be diminished: but he that gathereth by labour shall increase.

ours: Hope deferred maketh the heart sick: but when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life.
theirs: Hope deferred maketh the heart sick: but [when] the desire cometh, [it is] a tree of life.

ours: The law of the wise is a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death.
theirs: The law of the wise [is] a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death.

ours: Good understanding giveth favour: but the way of transgressors is hard.
theirs: Good understanding giveth favour: but the way of transgressors [is] hard.

ours: Every prudent man dealeth with knowledge: but a fool layeth open his folly.
theirs: Every prudent [man] dealeth with knowledge: but a fool layeth open [his] folly.

ours: A wicked messenger falleth into mischief: but a faithful ambassador is health.
theirs: A wicked messenger falleth into mischief: but a faithful ambassador [is] health.

ours: Poverty and shame shall be to him that refuseth instruction: but he that regardeth reproof shall be honoured.
theirs: Poverty and shame [shall be to] him that refuseth instruction: but he that regardeth reproof shall be honoured.

ours: The desire accomplished is sweet to the soul: but it is abomination to fools to depart from evil.
theirs: The desire accomplished is sweet to the soul: but [it is] abomination to fools to depart from evil.

ours: He that walketh with wise men shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed.
theirs: He that walketh with wise [men] shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed.

ours: A good man leaveth an inheritance to his childrens children: and the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the just.
theirs: A good [man] leaveth an inheritance to his children's children: and the wealth of the sinner [is] laid up for the just.

ours: Much food is in the tillage of the poor: but there is that is destroyed for want of judgment.
theirs: Much food [is in] the tillage of the poor: but there is [that is] destroyed for want of judgment.

ours: He that walketh in his uprightness feareth the LORD: but he that is perverse in his ways despiseth him.
theirs: He that walketh in his uprightness feareth the LORD: but [he that is] perverse in his ways despiseth him.

ours: In the mouth of the foolish is a rod of pride: but the lips of the wise shall preserve them.
theirs: In the mouth of the foolish [is] a rod of pride: but the lips of the wise shall preserve them.

ours: Where no oxen are, the crib is clean: but much increase is by the strength of the ox.
theirs: Where no oxen [are], the crib [is] clean: but much increase [is] by the strength of the ox.

ours: A scorner seeketh wisdom, and findeth it not: but knowledge is easy unto him that understandeth.
theirs: A scorner seeketh wisdom, and [findeth it] not: but knowledge [is] easy unto him that understandeth.

ours: Go from the presence of a foolish man, when thou perceivest not in him the lips of knowledge.
theirs: Go from the presence of a foolish man, when thou perceivest not [in him] the lips of knowledge.

ours: The wisdom of the prudent is to understand his way: but the folly of fools is deceit.
theirs: The wisdom of the prudent [is] to understand his way: but the folly of fools [is] deceit.

ours: Fools make a mock at sin: but among the righteous there is favour.
theirs: Fools make a mock at sin: but among the righteous [there is] favour.

ours: There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death.
theirs: There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof [are] the ways of death.

ours: Even in laughter the heart is sorrowful; and the end of that mirth is heaviness.
theirs: Even in laughter the heart is sorrowful; and the end of that mirth [is] heaviness.

ours: The backslider in heart shall be filled with his own ways: and a good man shall be satisfied from himself.
theirs: The backslider in heart shall be filled with his own ways: and a good man [shall be satisfied] from himself.

ours: The simple believeth every word: but the prudent man looketh well to his going.
theirs: The simple believeth every word: but the prudent [man] looketh well to his going.

ours: A wise man feareth, and departeth from evil: but the fool rageth, and is confident.
theirs: A wise [man] feareth, and departeth from evil: but the fool rageth, and is confident.

ours: He that is soon angry dealeth foolishly: and a man of wicked devices is hated.
theirs: [He that is] soon angry dealeth foolishly: and a man of wicked devices is hated.

ours: The poor is hated even of his own neighbour: but the rich hath many friends.
theirs: The poor is hated even of his own neighbour: but the rich [hath] many friends.

ours: He that despiseth his neighbour sinneth: but he that hath mercy on the poor, happy is he.
theirs: He that despiseth his neighbour sinneth: but he that hath mercy on the poor, happy [is] he.

ours: Do they not err that devise evil? but mercy and truth shall be to them that devise good.
theirs: Do they not err that devise evil? but mercy and truth [shall be] to them that devise good.

ours: In all labour there is profit: but the talk of the lips tendeth only to penury.
theirs: In all labour there is profit: but the talk of the lips [tendeth] only to penury.

ours: The crown of the wise is their riches: but the foolishness of fools is folly.
theirs: The crown of the wise [is] their riches: [but] the foolishness of fools [is] folly.

ours: A true witness delivereth souls: but a deceitful witness speaketh lies.
theirs: A true witness delivereth souls: but a deceitful [witness] speaketh lies.

ours: In the fear of the LORD is strong confidence: and his children shall have a place of refuge.
theirs: In the fear of the LORD [is] strong confidence: and his children shall have a place of refuge.

ours: The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death.
theirs: The fear of the LORD [is] a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death.

ours: In the multitude of people is the kings honour: but in the want of people is the destruction of the prince.
theirs: In the multitude of people [is] the king's honour: but in the want of people [is] the destruction of the prince.

ours: He that is slow to wrath is of great understanding: but he that is hasty of spirit exalteth folly.
theirs: [He that is] slow to wrath [is] of great understanding: but [he that is] hasty of spirit exalteth folly.

ours: A sound heart is the life of the flesh: but envy the rottenness of the bones.
theirs: A sound heart [is] the life of the flesh: but envy the rottenness of the bones.

ours: Wisdom resteth in the heart of him that hath understanding: but that which is in the midst of fools is made known.
theirs: Wisdom resteth in the heart of him that hath understanding: but [that which is] in the midst of fools is made known.

ours: Righteousness exalteth a nation: but sin is a reproach to any people.
theirs: Righteousness exalteth a nation: but sin [is] a reproach to any people.

ours: The kings favour is toward a wise servant: but his wrath is against him that causeth shame.
theirs: The king's favour [is] toward a wise servant: but his wrath is [against] him that causeth shame.

ours: The eyes of the LORD are in every place, beholding the evil and the good.
theirs: The eyes of the LORD [are] in every place, beholding the evil and the good.

ours: A wholesome tongue is a tree of life: but perverseness therein is a breach in the spirit.
theirs: A wholesome tongue [is] a tree of life: but perverseness therein [is] a breach in the spirit.

ours: A fool despiseth his fathers instruction: but he that regardeth reproof is prudent.
theirs: A fool despiseth his father's instruction: but he that regardeth reproof is prudent.

ours: In the house of the righteous is much treasure: but in the revenues of the wicked is trouble.
theirs: In the house of the righteous [is] much treasure: but in the revenues of the wicked is trouble.

ours: The lips of the wise disperse knowledge: but the heart of the foolish doeth not so.
theirs: The lips of the wise disperse knowledge: but the heart of the foolish [doeth] not so.

ours: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to the LORD: but the prayer of the upright is his delight.
theirs: The sacrifice of the wicked [is] an abomination to the LORD: but the prayer of the upright [is] his delight.

ours: The way of the wicked is an abomination unto the LORD: but he loveth him that followeth after righteousness.
theirs: The way of the wicked [is] an abomination unto the LORD: but he loveth him that followeth after righteousness.

ours: Correction is grievous unto him that forsaketh the way: and he that hateth reproof shall die.
theirs: Correction [is] grievous unto him that forsaketh the way: [and] he that hateth reproof shall die.

ours: Hell and destruction are before the LORD: how much more then the hearts of the children of men?
theirs: Hell and destruction [are] before the LORD: how much more then the hearts of the children of men?

ours: All the days of the afflicted are evil: but he that is of a merry heart hath a continual feast.
theirs: All the days of the afflicted [are] evil: but he that is of a merry heart [hath] a continual feast.

ours: Better is little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure and trouble therewith.
theirs: Better [is] little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure and trouble therewith.

ours: Better is a dinner of herbs where love is, than a stalled ox and hatred therewith.
theirs: Better [is] a dinner of herbs where love is, than a stalled ox and hatred therewith.

ours: A wrathful man stirreth up strife: but he that is slow to anger appeaseth strife.
theirs: A wrathful man stirreth up strife: but [he that is] slow to anger appeaseth strife.

ours: The way of the slothful man is as an hedge of thorns: but the way of the righteous is made plain.
theirs: The way of the slothful [man is] as an hedge of thorns: but the way of the righteous [is] made plain.

ours: Folly is joy to him that is destitute of wisdom: but a man of understanding walketh uprightly.
theirs: Folly [is] joy to [him that is] destitute of wisdom: but a man of understanding walketh uprightly.

ours: A man hath joy by the answer of his mouth: and a word spoken in due season, how good is it!
theirs: A man hath joy by the answer of his mouth: and a word [spoken] in due season, how good [is it]!

ours: The way of life is above to the wise, that he may depart from hell beneath.
theirs: The way of life [is] above to the wise, that he may depart from hell beneath.

ours: The thoughts of the wicked are an abomination to the LORD: but the words of the pure are pleasant words.
theirs: The thoughts of the wicked [are] an abomination to the LORD: but [the words] of the pure [are] pleasant words.

ours: The LORD is far from the wicked: but he heareth the prayer of the righteous.
theirs: The LORD [is] far from the wicked: but he heareth the prayer of the righteous.

ours: The light of the eyes rejoiceth the heart: and a good report maketh the bones fat.
theirs: The light of the eyes rejoiceth the heart: [and] a good report maketh the bones fat.

ours: The fear of the LORD is the instruction of wisdom; and before honour is humility.
theirs: The fear of the LORD [is] the instruction of wisdom; and before honour [is] humility.

ours: THE preparations of the heart in man, and the answer of the tongue, is from the LORD.
theirs: The preparations of the heart in man, and the answer of the tongue, [is] from the LORD.

ours: All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes; but the LORD weigheth the spirits.
theirs: All the ways of a man [are] clean in his own eyes; but the LORD weigheth the spirits.

ours: The LORD hath made all things for himself: yea, even the wicked for the day of evil.
theirs: The LORD hath made all [things] for himself: yea, even the wicked for the day of evil.

ours: Every one that is proud in heart is an abomination to the LORD: though hand join in hand, he shall not be unpunished.
theirs: Every one [that is] proud in heart [is] an abomination to the LORD: [though] hand [join] in hand, he shall not be unpunished.

ours: By mercy and truth iniquity is purged: and by the fear of the LORD men depart from evil.
theirs: By mercy and truth iniquity is purged: and by the fear of the LORD [men] depart from evil.

ours: When a mans ways please the LORD, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.
theirs: When a man's ways please the LORD, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.

ours: Better is a little with righteousness than great revenues without right.
theirs: Better [is] a little with righteousness than great revenues without right.

ours: A mans heart deviseth his way: but the LORD directeth his steps.
theirs: A man's heart deviseth his way: but the LORD directeth his steps.

ours: A divine sentence is in the lips of the king: his mouth transgresseth not in judgment.
theirs: A divine sentence [is] in the lips of the king: his mouth transgresseth not in judgment.

ours: A just weight and balance are the LORDs: all the weights of the bag are his work.
theirs: A just weight and balance [are] the LORD's: all the weights of the bag [are] his work.

ours: It is an abomination to kings to commit wickedness: for the throne is established by righteousness.
theirs: [It is] an abomination to kings to commit wickedness: for the throne is established by righteousness.

ours: Righteous lips are the delight of kings; and they love him that speaketh right.
theirs: Righteous lips [are] the delight of kings; and they love him that speaketh right.

ours: The wrath of a king is as messengers of death: but a wise man will pacify it.
theirs: The wrath of a king [is as] messengers of death: but a wise man will pacify it.

ours: In the light of the kings countenance is life; and his favour is as a cloud of the latter rain.
theirs: In the light of the king's countenance [is] life; and his favour [is] as a cloud of the latter rain.

ours: How much better is it to get wisdom than gold! and to get understanding rather to be chosen than silver!
theirs: How much better [is it] to get wisdom than gold! and to get understanding rather to be chosen than silver!

ours: The highway of the upright is to depart from evil: he that keepeth his way preserveth his soul.
theirs: The highway of the upright [is] to depart from evil: he that keepeth his way preserveth his soul.

ours: Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.
theirs: Pride [goeth] before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.

ours: Better it is to be of an humble spirit with the lowly, than to divide the spoil with the proud.
theirs: Better [it is to be] of an humble spirit with the lowly, than to divide the spoil with the proud.

ours: He that handleth a matter wisely shall find good: and whoso trusteth in the LORD, happy is he.
theirs: He that handleth a matter wisely shall find good: and whoso trusteth in the LORD, happy [is] he.

ours: Understanding is a wellspring of life unto him that hath it: but the instruction of fools is folly.
theirs: Understanding [is] a wellspring of life unto him that hath it: but the instruction of fools [is] folly.

ours: Pleasant words are as an honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.
theirs: Pleasant words [are as] an honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.

ours: There is a way that seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death.
theirs: There is a way that seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof [are] the ways of death.

ours: An ungodly man diggeth up evil: and in his lips there is as a burning fire.
theirs: An ungodly man diggeth up evil: and in his lips [there is] as a burning fire.

ours: A violent man enticeth his neighbour, and leadeth him into the way that is not good.
theirs: A violent man enticeth his neighbour, and leadeth him into the way [that is] not good.

ours: The hoary head is a crown of glory, if it be found in the way of righteousness.
theirs: The hoary head [is] a crown of glory, [if] it be found in the way of righteousness.

ours: He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city.
theirs: [He that is] slow to anger [is] better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city.

ours: The lot is cast into the lap; but the whole disposing thereof is of the LORD.
theirs: The lot is cast into the lap; but the whole disposing thereof [is] of the LORD.

ours: BETTER is a dry morsel, and quietness therewith, than an house full of sacrifices with strife.
theirs: Better [is] a dry morsel, and quietness therewith, than an house full of sacrifices [with] strife.

ours: The fining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold: but the LORD trieth the hearts.
theirs: The fining pot [is] for silver, and the furnace for gold: but the LORD trieth the hearts.

ours: A wicked doer giveth heed to false lips; and a liar giveth ear to a naughty tongue.
theirs: A wicked doer giveth heed to false lips; [and] a liar giveth ear to a naughty tongue.

ours: Whoso mocketh the poor reproacheth his Maker: and he that is glad at calamities shall not be unpunished.
theirs: Whoso mocketh the poor reproacheth his Maker: [and] he that is glad at calamities shall not be unpunished.

ours: Childrens children are the crown of old men; and the glory of children are their fathers.
theirs: Children's children [are] the crown of old men; and the glory of children [are] their fathers.

ours: A gift is as a precious stone in the eyes of him that hath it: whithersoever it turneth, it prospereth.
theirs: A gift [is as] a precious stone in the eyes of him that hath it: whithersoever it turneth, it prospereth.

ours: He that covereth a transgression seeketh love; but he that repeateth a matter separateth very friends.
theirs: He that covereth a transgression seeketh love; but he that repeateth a matter separateth [very] friends.

ours: An evil man seeketh only rebellion: therefore a cruel messenger shall be sent against him.
theirs: An evil [man] seeketh only rebellion: therefore a cruel messenger shall be sent against him.

ours: The beginning of strife is as when one letteth out water: therefore leave off contention, before it be meddled with.
theirs: The beginning of strife [is as] when one letteth out water: therefore leave off contention, before it be meddled with.

ours: He that justifieth the wicked, and he that condemneth the just, even they both are abomination to the LORD.
theirs: He that justifieth the wicked, and he that condemneth the just, even they both [are] abomination to the LORD.

ours: Wherefore is there a price in the hand of a fool to get wisdom, seeing he hath no heart to it?
theirs: Wherefore [is there] a price in the hand of a fool to get wisdom, seeing [he hath] no heart [to it]?

ours: A man void of understanding striketh hands, and becometh surety in the presence of his friend.
theirs: A man void of understanding striketh hands, [and] becometh surety in the presence of his friend.

ours: He loveth transgression that loveth strife: and he that exalteth his gate seeketh destruction.
theirs: He loveth transgression that loveth strife: [and] he that exalteth his gate seeketh destruction.

ours: He that begetteth a fool doeth it to his sorrow: and the father of a fool hath no joy.
theirs: He that begetteth a fool [doeth it] to his sorrow: and the father of a fool hath no joy.

ours: A merry heart doeth good like a medicine: but a broken spirit drieth the bones.
theirs: A merry heart doeth good [like] a medicine: but a broken spirit drieth the bones.

ours: A wicked man taketh a gift out of the bosom to pervert the ways of judgment.
theirs: A wicked [man] taketh a gift out of the bosom to pervert the ways of judgment.

ours: Wisdom is before him that hath understanding; but the eyes of a fool are in the ends of the earth.
theirs: Wisdom [is] before him that hath understanding; but the eyes of a fool [are] in the ends of the earth.

ours: A foolish son is a grief to his father, and bitterness to her that bare him.
theirs: A foolish son [is] a grief to his father, and bitterness to her that bare him.

ours: Also to punish the just is not good, nor to strike princes for equity.
theirs: Also to punish the just [is] not good, [nor] to strike princes for equity.

ours: He that hath knowledge spareth his words: and a man of understanding is of an excellent spirit.
theirs: He that hath knowledge spareth his words: [and] a man of understanding is of an excellent spirit.

ours: Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise: and he that shutteth his lips is esteemed a man of understanding.
theirs: Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise: [and] he that shutteth his lips [is esteemed] a man of understanding.

ours: THROUGH desire a man, having separated himself, seeketh and intermeddleth with all wisdom.
theirs: Through desire a man, having separated himself, seeketh [and] intermeddleth with all wisdom.

ours: When the wicked cometh, then cometh also contempt, and with ignominy reproach.
theirs: When the wicked cometh, [then] cometh also contempt, and with ignominy reproach.

ours: The words of a mans mouth are as deep waters, and the wellspring of wisdom as a flowing brook.
theirs: The words of a man's mouth [are as] deep waters, [and] the wellspring of wisdom [as] a flowing brook.

ours: It is not good to accept the person of the wicked, to overthrow the righteous in judgment.
theirs: [It is] not good to accept the person of the wicked, to overthrow the righteous in judgment.

ours: A fools lips enter into contention, and his mouth calleth for strokes.
theirs: A fool's lips enter into contention, and his mouth calleth for strokes.

ours: A fools mouth is his destruction, and his lips are the snare of his soul.
theirs: A fool's mouth [is] his destruction, and his lips [are] the snare of his soul.

ours: The words of a talebearer are as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.
theirs: The words of a talebearer [are] as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.

ours: The name of the LORD is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe.
theirs: The name of the LORD [is] a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe.

ours: The rich mans wealth is his strong city, and as an high wall in his own conceit.
theirs: The rich man's wealth [is] his strong city, and as an high wall in his own conceit.

ours: Before destruction the heart of man is haughty, and before honour is humility.
theirs: Before destruction the heart of man is haughty, and before honour [is] humility.

ours: He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him.
theirs: He that answereth a matter before he heareth [it], it [is] folly and shame unto him.

ours: A mans gift maketh room for him, and bringeth him before great men.
theirs: A man's gift maketh room for him, and bringeth him before great men.

ours: He that is first in his own cause seemeth just; but his neighbour cometh and searcheth him.
theirs: [He that is] first in his own cause [seemeth] just; but his neighbour cometh and searcheth him.

ours: A brother offended is harder to be won than a strong city: and their contentions are like the bars of a castle.
theirs: A brother offended [is harder to be won] than a strong city: and [their] contentions [are] like the bars of a castle.

ours: A mans belly shall be satisfied with the fruit of his mouth; and with the increase of his lips shall he be filled.
theirs: A man's belly shall be satisfied with the fruit of his mouth; [and] with the increase of his lips shall he be filled.

ours: Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.
theirs: Death and life [are] in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.

ours: Whoso findeth a wife findeth a good thing, and obtaineth favour of the LORD.
theirs: [Whoso] findeth a wife findeth a good [thing], and obtaineth favour of the LORD.

ours: A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.
theirs: A man [that hath] friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend [that] sticketh closer than a brother.

ours: BETTER is the poor that walketh in his integrity, than he that is perverse in his lips, and is a fool.
theirs: Better [is] the poor that walketh in his integrity, than [he that is] perverse in his lips, and is a fool.

ours: Also, that the soul be without knowledge, it is not good; and he that hasteth with his feet sinneth.
theirs: Also, [that] the soul [be] without knowledge, [it is] not good; and he that hasteth with [his] feet sinneth.

ours: A false witness shall not be unpunished, and he that speaketh lies shall not escape.
theirs: A false witness shall not be unpunished, and [he that] speaketh lies shall not escape.

ours: Many will intreat the favour of the prince: and every man is a friend to him that giveth gifts.
theirs: Many will intreat the favour of the prince: and every man [is] a friend to him that giveth gifts.

ours: All the brethren of the poor do hate him: how much more do his friends go far from him? he pursueth them with words, yet they are wanting to him.
theirs: All the brethren of the poor do hate him: how much more do his friends go far from him? he pursueth [them with] words, [yet] they [are] wanting [to him].

ours: A false witness shall not be unpunished, and he that speaketh lies shall perish.
theirs: A false witness shall not be unpunished, and [he that] speaketh lies shall perish.

ours: The discretion of a man deferreth his anger; and it is his glory to pass over a transgression.
theirs: The discretion of a man deferreth his anger; and [it is] his glory to pass over a transgression.

ours: The kings wrath is as the roaring of a lion; but his favour is as dew upon the grass.
theirs: The king's wrath [is] as the roaring of a lion; but his favour [is] as dew upon the grass.

ours: A foolish son is the calamity of his father: and the contentions of a wife are a continual dropping.
theirs: A foolish son [is] the calamity of his father: and the contentions of a wife [are] a continual dropping.

ours: House and riches are the inheritance of fathers: and a prudent wife is from the LORD.
theirs: House and riches [are] the inheritance of fathers: and a prudent wife [is] from the LORD.

ours: He that keepeth the commandment keepeth his own soul; but he that despiseth his ways shall die.
theirs: He that keepeth the commandment keepeth his own soul; [but] he that despiseth his ways shall die.

ours: A man of great wrath shall suffer punishment: for if thou deliver him, yet thou must do it again.
theirs: A man of great wrath shall suffer punishment: for if thou deliver [him], yet thou must do it again.

ours: There are many devices in a mans heart; nevertheless the counsel of the LORD, that shall stand.
theirs: [There are] many devices in a man's heart; nevertheless the counsel of the LORD, that shall stand.

ours: The desire of a man is his kindness: and a poor man is better than a liar.
theirs: The desire of a man [is] his kindness: and a poor man [is] better than a liar.

ours: The fear of the LORD tendeth to life: and he that hath it shall abide satisfied; he shall not be visited with evil.
theirs: The fear of the LORD [tendeth] to life: and [he that hath it] shall abide satisfied; he shall not be visited with evil.

ours: A slothful man hideth his hand in his bosom, and will not so much as bring it to his mouth again.
theirs: A slothful [man] hideth his hand in [his] bosom, and will not so much as bring it to his mouth again.

ours: Smite a scorner, and the simple will beware: and reprove one that hath understanding, and he will understand knowledge.
theirs: Smite a scorner, and the simple will beware: and reprove one that hath understanding, [and] he will understand knowledge.

ours: He that wasteth his father, and chaseth away his mother, is a son that causeth shame, and bringeth reproach.
theirs: He that wasteth [his] father, [and] chaseth away [his] mother, [is] a son that causeth shame, and bringeth reproach.

ours: Cease, my son, to hear the instruction that causeth to err from the words of knowledge.
theirs: Cease, my son, to hear the instruction [that causeth] to err from the words of knowledge.

ours: WINE is a mocker, strong drink is raging: and whosoever is deceived thereby is not wise.
theirs: Wine [is] a mocker, strong drink [is] raging: and whosoever is deceived thereby is not wise.

ours: The fear of a king is as the roaring of a lion: whoso provoketh him to anger sinneth against his own soul.
theirs: The fear of a king [is] as the roaring of a lion: [whoso] provoketh him to anger sinneth [against] his own soul.

ours: It is an honour for a man to cease from strife: but every fool will be meddling.
theirs: [It is] an honour for a man to cease from strife: but every fool will be meddling.

ours: The sluggard will not plow by reason of the cold; therefore shall he beg in harvest, and have nothing.
theirs: The sluggard will not plow by reason of the cold; [therefore] shall he beg in harvest, and [have] nothing.

ours: Counsel in the heart of man is like deep water; but a man of understanding will draw it out.
theirs: Counsel in the heart of man [is like] deep water; but a man of understanding will draw it out.

ours: The just man walketh in his integrity: his children are blessed after him.
theirs: The just [man] walketh in his integrity: his children [are] blessed after him.

ours: Divers weights, and divers measures, both of them are alike abomination to the LORD.
theirs: Divers weights, [and] divers measures, both of them [are] alike abomination to the LORD.

ours: Even a child is known by his doings, whether his work be pure, and whether it be right.
theirs: Even a child is known by his doings, whether his work [be] pure, and whether [it be] right.

ours: Love not sleep, lest thou come to poverty; open thine eyes, and thou shalt be satisfied with bread.
theirs: Love not sleep, lest thou come to poverty; open thine eyes, [and] thou shalt be satisfied with bread.

ours: It is naught, it is naught, saith the buyer: but when he is gone his way, then he boasteth.
theirs: [It is] naught, [it is] naught, saith the buyer: but when he is gone his way, then he boasteth.

ours: There is gold, and a multitude of rubies: but the lips of knowledge are a precious jewel.
theirs: There is gold, and a multitude of rubies: but the lips of knowledge [are] a precious jewel.

ours: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger: and take a pledge of him for a strange woman.
theirs: Take his garment that is surety [for] a stranger: and take a pledge of him for a strange woman.

ours: Bread of deceit is sweet to a man; but afterwards his mouth shall be filled with gravel.
theirs: Bread of deceit [is] sweet to a man; but afterwards his mouth shall be filled with gravel.

ours: Every purpose is established by counsel: and with good advice make war.
theirs: [Every] purpose is established by counsel: and with good advice make war.

ours: He that goeth about as a talebearer revealeth secrets: therefore meddle not with him that flattereth with his lips.
theirs: He that goeth about [as] a talebearer revealeth secrets: therefore meddle not with him that flattereth with his lips.

ours: An inheritance may be gotten hastily at the beginning; but the end thereof shall not be blessed.
theirs: An inheritance [may be] gotten hastily at the beginning; but the end thereof shall not be blessed.

ours: Say not thou, I will recompense evil; but wait on the LORD, and he shall save thee.
theirs: Say not thou, I will recompense evil; [but] wait on the LORD, and he shall save thee.

ours: Divers weights are an abomination unto the LORD; and a false balance is not good.
theirs: Divers weights [are] an abomination unto the LORD; and a false balance [is] not good.

ours: Mans goings are of the LORD; how can a man then understand his own way?
theirs: Man's goings [are] of the LORD; how can a man then understand his own way?

ours: It is a snare to the man who devoureth that which is holy, and after vows to make inquiry.
theirs: [It is] a snare to the man [who] devoureth [that which is] holy, and after vows to make inquiry.

ours: The spirit of man is the candle of the LORD, searching all the inward parts of the belly.
theirs: The spirit of man [is] the candle of the LORD, searching all the inward parts of the belly.

ours: The glory of young men is their strength: and the beauty of old men is the gray head.
theirs: The glory of young men [is] their strength: and the beauty of old men [is] the gray head.

ours: The blueness of a wound cleanseth away evil: so do stripes the inward parts of the belly.
theirs: The blueness of a wound cleanseth away evil: so [do] stripes the inward parts of the belly.

ours: THE kings heart is in the hand of the LORD, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.
theirs: The king's heart [is] in the hand of the LORD, [as] the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.

ours: Every way of a man is right in his own eyes: but the LORD pondereth the hearts.
theirs: Every way of a man [is] right in his own eyes: but the LORD pondereth the hearts.

ours: To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice.
theirs: To do justice and judgment [is] more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice.

ours: An high look, and a proud heart, and the plowing of the wicked, is sin.
theirs: An high look, and a proud heart, [and] the plowing of the wicked, [is] sin.

ours: The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness; but of every one that is hasty only to want.
theirs: The thoughts of the diligent [tend] only to plenteousness; but of every one [that is] hasty only to want.

ours: The getting of treasures by a lying tongue is a vanity tossed to and fro of them that seek death.
theirs: The getting of treasures by a lying tongue [is] a vanity tossed to and fro of them that seek death.

ours: The way of man is froward and strange: but as for the pure, his work is right.
theirs: The way of man [is] froward and strange: but [as for] the pure, his work [is] right.

ours: It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman in a wide house.
theirs: [It is] better to dwell in a corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman in a wide house.

ours: The righteous man wisely considereth the house of the wicked: but God overthroweth the wicked for their wickedness.
theirs: The righteous [man] wisely considereth the house of the wicked: [but God] overthroweth the wicked for [their] wickedness.

ours: It is joy to the just to do judgment: but destruction shall be to the workers of iniquity.
theirs: [It is] joy to the just to do judgment: but destruction [shall be] to the workers of iniquity.

ours: He that loveth pleasure shall be a poor man: he that loveth wine and oil shall not be rich.
theirs: He that loveth pleasure [shall be] a poor man: he that loveth wine and oil shall not be rich.

ours: The wicked shall be a ransom for the righteous, and the transgressor for the upright.
theirs: The wicked [shall be] a ransom for the righteous, and the transgressor for the upright.

ours: It is better to dwell in the wilderness, than with a contentious and an angry woman.
theirs: [It is] better to dwell in the wilderness, than with a contentious and an angry woman.

ours: There is treasure to be desired and oil in the dwelling of the wise; but a foolish man spendeth it up.
theirs: [There is] treasure to be desired and oil in the dwelling of the wise; but a foolish man spendeth it up.

ours: A wise man scaleth the city of the mighty, and casteth down the strength of the confidence thereof.
theirs: A wise [man] scaleth the city of the mighty, and casteth down the strength of the confidence thereof.

ours: Proud and haughty scorner is his name, who dealeth in proud wrath.
theirs: Proud [and] haughty scorner [is] his name, who dealeth in proud wrath.

ours: The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination: how much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind?
theirs: The sacrifice of the wicked [is] abomination: how much more, [when] he bringeth it with a wicked mind?

ours: A wicked man hardeneth his face: but as for the upright, he directeth his way.
theirs: A wicked man hardeneth his face: but [as for] the upright, he directeth his way.

ours: There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against the LORD.
theirs: [There is] no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against the LORD.

ours: The horse is prepared against the day of battle: but safety is of the LORD.
theirs: The horse [is] prepared against the day of battle: but safety [is] of the LORD.

ours: A GOOD name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold.
theirs: A [good] name [is] rather to be chosen than great riches, [and] loving favour rather than silver and gold.

ours: The rich and poor meet together: the LORD is the maker of them all.
theirs: The rich and poor meet together: the LORD [is] the maker of them all.

ours: A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.
theirs: A prudent [man] foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.

ours: By humility and the fear of the LORD are riches, and honour, and life.
theirs: By humility [and] the fear of the LORD [are] riches, and honour, and life.

ours: Thorns and snares are in the way of the froward: he that doth keep his soul shall be far from them.
theirs: Thorns [and] snares [are] in the way of the froward: he that doth keep his soul shall be far from them.

ours: The rich ruleth over the poor, and the borrower is servant to the lender.
theirs: The rich ruleth over the poor, and the borrower [is] servant to the lender.

ours: He that loveth pureness of heart, for the grace of his lips the king shall be his friend.
theirs: He that loveth pureness of heart, [for] the grace of his lips the king [shall be] his friend.

ours: The slothful man saith, There is a lion without, I shall be slain in the streets.
theirs: The slothful [man] saith, [There is] a lion without, I shall be slain in the streets.

ours: The mouth of strange women is a deep pit: he that is abhorred of the LORD shall fall therein.
theirs: The mouth of strange women [is] a deep pit: he that is abhorred of the LORD shall fall therein.

ours: Foolishness is bound in the heart of a child; but the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.
theirs: Foolishness [is] bound in the heart of a child; [but] the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.

ours: He that oppresseth the poor to increase his riches, and he that giveth to the rich, shall surely come to want.
theirs: He that oppresseth the poor to increase his [riches, and] he that giveth to the rich, [shall] surely [come] to want.

ours: For it is a pleasant thing if thou keep them within thee; they shall withal be fitted in thy lips.
theirs: For [it is] a pleasant thing if thou keep them within thee; they shall withal be fitted in thy lips.

ours: Rob not the poor, because he is poor: neither oppress the afflicted in the gate:
theirs: Rob not the poor, because he [is] poor: neither oppress the afflicted in the gate:

ours: Be not thou one of them that strike hands, or of them that are sureties for debts.
theirs: Be not thou [one] of them that strike hands, [or] of them that are sureties for debts.

ours: Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.
theirs: Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean [men].

ours: WHEN thou sittest to eat with a ruler, consider diligently what is before thee:
theirs: When thou sittest to eat with a ruler, consider diligently what [is] before thee:

ours: And put a knife to thy throat, if thou be a man given to appetite.
theirs: And put a knife to thy throat, if thou [be] a man given to appetite.

ours: Be not desirous of his dainties: for they are deceitful meat.
theirs: Be not desirous of his dainties: for they [are] deceitful meat.

ours: Wilt thou set thine eyes upon that which is not? for riches certainly make themselves wings; they fly away as an eagle toward heaven.
theirs: Wilt thou set thine eyes upon that which is not? for [riches] certainly make themselves wings; they fly away as an eagle toward heaven.

ours: Eat thou not the bread of him that hath an evil eye, neither desire thou his dainty meats:
theirs: Eat thou not the bread of [him that hath] an evil eye, neither desire thou his dainty meats:

ours: For as he thinketh in his heart, so is he: Eat and drink, saith he to thee; but his heart is not with thee.
theirs: For as he thinketh in his heart, so [is] he: Eat and drink, saith he to thee; but his heart [is] not with thee.

ours: The morsel which thou hast eaten shalt thou vomit up, and lose thy sweet words.
theirs: The morsel [which] thou hast eaten shalt thou vomit up, and lose thy sweet words.

ours: For their redeemer is mighty; he shall plead their cause with thee.
theirs: For their redeemer [is] mighty; he shall plead their cause with thee.

ours: Withhold not correction from the child: for if thou beatest him with the rod, he shall not die.
theirs: Withhold not correction from the child: for [if] thou beatest him with the rod, he shall not die.

ours: Let not thine heart envy sinners: but be thou in the fear of the LORD all the day long.
theirs: Let not thine heart envy sinners: but [be thou] in the fear of the LORD all the day long.

ours: For the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty: and drowsiness shall clothe a man with rags.
theirs: For the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty: and drowsiness shall clothe [a man] with rags.

ours: Buy the truth, and sell it not; also wisdom, and instruction, and understanding.
theirs: Buy the truth, and sell [it] not; [also] wisdom, and instruction, and understanding.

ours: The father of the righteous shall greatly rejoice: and he that begetteth a wise child shall have joy of him.
theirs: The father of the righteous shall greatly rejoice: and he that begetteth a wise [child] shall have joy of him.

ours: For a whore is a deep ditch; and a strange woman is a narrow pit.
theirs: For a whore [is] a deep ditch; and a strange woman [is] a narrow pit.

ours: She also lieth in wait as for a prey, and increaseth the transgressors among men.
theirs: She also lieth in wait as [for] a prey, and increaseth the transgressors among men.

ours: Look not thou upon the wine when it is red, when it giveth his colour in the cup, when it moveth itself aright.
theirs: Look not thou upon the wine when it is red, when it giveth his colour in the cup, [when] it moveth itself aright.

ours: They have stricken me, shalt thou say, and I was not sick; they have beaten me, and I felt it not: when shall I awake? I will seek it yet again.
theirs: They have stricken me, [shalt thou say, and] I was not sick; they have beaten me, [and] I felt [it] not: when shall I awake? I will seek it yet again.

ours: A wise man is strong; yea, a man of knowledge increaseth strength.
theirs: A wise man [is] strong; yea, a man of knowledge increaseth strength.

ours: For by wise counsel thou shalt make thy war: and in multitude of counsellers there is safety.
theirs: For by wise counsel thou shalt make thy war: and in multitude of counsellers [there is] safety.

ours: Wisdom is too high for a fool: he openeth not his mouth in the gate.
theirs: Wisdom [is] too high for a fool: he openeth not his mouth in the gate.

ours: The thought of foolishness is sin: and the scorner is an abomination to men.
theirs: The thought of foolishness [is] sin: and the scorner [is] an abomination to men.

ours: If thou faint in the day of adversity, thy strength is small.
theirs: [If] thou faint in the day of adversity, thy strength [is] small.

ours: If thou forbear to deliver them that are drawn unto death, and those that are ready to be slain;
theirs: If thou forbear to deliver [them that are] drawn unto death, and [those that are] ready to be slain;

ours: If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? and shall not he render to every man according to his works?
theirs: If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider [it]? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth [not] he know [it]? and shall [not] he render to [every] man according to his works?

ours: My son, eat thou honey, because it is good; and the honeycomb, which is sweet to thy taste:
theirs: My son, eat thou honey, because [it is] good; and the honeycomb, [which is] sweet to thy taste:

ours: So shall the knowledge of wisdom be unto thy soul: when thou hast found it, then there shall be a reward, and thy expectation shall not be cut off.
theirs: So [shall] the knowledge of wisdom [be] unto thy soul: when thou hast found [it], then there shall be a reward, and thy expectation shall not be cut off.

ours: Lay not wait, O wicked man, against the dwelling of the righteous; spoil not his resting place:
theirs: Lay not wait, O wicked [man], against the dwelling of the righteous; spoil not his resting place:

ours: For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.
theirs: For a just [man] falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.

ours: Lest the LORD see it, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him.
theirs: Lest the LORD see [it], and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him.

ours: Fret not thyself because of evil men, neither be thou envious at the wicked;
theirs: Fret not thyself because of evil [men], neither be thou envious at the wicked;

ours: For there shall be no reward to the evil man; the candle of the wicked shall be put out.
theirs: For there shall be no reward to the evil [man]; the candle of the wicked shall be put out.

ours: My son, fear thou the LORD and the king: and meddle not with them that are given to change:
theirs: My son, fear thou the LORD and the king: [and] meddle not with them that are given to change:

ours: These things also belong to the wise. It is not good to have respect of persons in judgment.
theirs: These [things] also [belong] to the wise. [It is] not good to have respect of persons in judgment.

ours: He that saith unto the wicked, Thou art righteous; him shall the people curse, nations shall abhor him:
theirs: He that saith unto the wicked, Thou [art] righteous; him shall the people curse, nations shall abhor him:

ours: But to them that rebuke him shall be delight, and a good blessing shall come upon them.
theirs: But to them that rebuke [him] shall be delight, and a good blessing shall come upon them.

ours: Every man shall kiss his lips that giveth a right answer.
theirs: [Every man] shall kiss [his] lips that giveth a right answer.

ours: Be not a witness against thy neighbour without cause; and deceive not with thy lips.
theirs: Be not a witness against thy neighbour without cause; and deceive [not] with thy lips.

ours: And, lo, it was all grown over with thorns, and nettles had covered the face thereof, and the stone wall thereof was broken down.
theirs: And, lo, it was all grown over with thorns, [and] nettles had covered the face thereof, and the stone wall thereof was broken down.

ours: Then I saw, and considered it well: I looked upon it, and received instruction.
theirs: Then I saw, [and] considered [it] well: I looked upon [it, and] received instruction.

ours: Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep:
theirs: [Yet] a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep:

ours: So shall thy poverty come as one that travelleth; and thy want as an armed man.
theirs: So shall thy poverty come [as] one that travelleth; and thy want as an armed man.

ours: THESE are also proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.
theirs: These [are] also proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.

ours: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings is to search out a matter.
theirs: [It is] the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings [is] to search out a matter.

ours: The heaven for height, and the earth for depth, and the heart of kings is unsearchable.
theirs: The heaven for height, and the earth for depth, and the heart of kings [is] unsearchable.

ours: Take away the wicked from before the king, and his throne shall be established in righteousness.
theirs: Take away the wicked [from] before the king, and his throne shall be established in righteousness.

ours: Put not forth thyself in the presence of the king, and stand not in the place of great men:
theirs: Put not forth thyself in the presence of the king, and stand not in the place of great [men]:

ours: For better it is that it be said unto thee, Come up hither; than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince whom thine eyes have seen.
theirs: For better [it is] that it be said unto thee, Come up hither; than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince whom thine eyes have seen.

ours: Go not forth hastily to strive, lest thou know not what to do in the end thereof, when thy neighbour hath put thee to shame.
theirs: Go not forth hastily to strive, lest [thou know not] what to do in the end thereof, when thy neighbour hath put thee to shame.

ours: Debate thy cause with thy neighbour himself; and discover not a secret to another:
theirs: Debate thy cause with thy neighbour [himself]; and discover not a secret to another:

ours: Lest he that heareth it put thee to shame, and thine infamy turn not away.
theirs: Lest he that heareth [it] put thee to shame, and thine infamy turn not away.

ours: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver.
theirs: A word fitly spoken [is like] apples of gold in pictures of silver.

ours: As an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, so is a wise reprover upon an obedient ear.
theirs: [As] an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, [so is] a wise reprover upon an obedient ear.

ours: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to them that send him: for he refresheth the soul of his masters.
theirs: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, [so is] a faithful messenger to them that send him: for he refresheth the soul of his masters.

ours: Whoso boasteth himself of a false gift is like clouds and wind without rain.
theirs: Whoso boasteth himself of a false gift [is like] clouds and wind without rain.

ours: Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbours house; lest he be weary of thee, and so hate thee.
theirs: Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbour's house; lest he be weary of thee, and [so] hate thee.

ours: A man that beareth false witness against his neighbour is a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.
theirs: A man that beareth false witness against his neighbour [is] a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.

ours: Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble is like a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.
theirs: Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble [is like] a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.

ours: As he that taketh away a garment in cold weather, and as vinegar upon nitre, so is he that singeth songs to an heavy heart.
theirs: [As] he that taketh away a garment in cold weather, [and as] vinegar upon nitre, so [is] he that singeth songs to an heavy heart.

ours: The north wind driveth away rain: so doth an angry countenance a backbiting tongue.
theirs: The north wind driveth away rain: so [doth] an angry countenance a backbiting tongue.

ours: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman and in a wide house.
theirs: [It is] better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman and in a wide house.

ours: As cold waters to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country.
theirs: [As] cold waters to a thirsty soul, so [is] good news from a far country.

ours: A righteous man falling down before the wicked is as a troubled fountain, and a corrupt spring.
theirs: A righteous man falling down before the wicked [is as] a troubled fountain, and a corrupt spring.

ours: It is not good to eat much honey: so for men to search their own glory is not glory.
theirs: [It is] not good to eat much honey: so [for men] to search their own glory [is not] glory.

ours: He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls.
theirs: He that [hath] no rule over his own spirit [is like] a city [that is] broken down, [and] without walls.

ours: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fools back.
theirs: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fool's back.

ours: He that sendeth a message by the hand of a fool cutteth off the feet, and drinketh damage.
theirs: He that sendeth a message by the hand of a fool cutteth off the feet, [and] drinketh damage.

ours: The legs of the lame are not equal: so is a parable in the mouth of fools.
theirs: The legs of the lame are not equal: so [is] a parable in the mouth of fools.

ours: As he that bindeth a stone in a sling, so is he that giveth honour to a fool.
theirs: As he that bindeth a stone in a sling, so [is] he that giveth honour to a fool.

ours: As a thorn goeth up into the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouth of fools.
theirs: [As] a thorn goeth up into the hand of a drunkard, so [is] a parable in the mouth of fools.

ours: The great God that formed all things both rewardeth the fool, and rewardeth transgressors.
