theirs: The great [God] that formed all [things] both rewardeth the fool, and rewardeth transgressors.

ours: As a dog returneth to his vomit, so a fool returneth to his folly.
theirs: As a dog returneth to his vomit, [so] a fool returneth to his folly.

ours: Seest thou a man wise in his own conceit? there is more hope of a fool than of him.
theirs: Seest thou a man wise in his own conceit? [there is] more hope of a fool than of him.

ours: The slothful man saith, There is a lion in the way; a lion is in the streets.
theirs: The slothful [man] saith, [There is] a lion in the way; a lion [is] in the streets.

ours: As the door turneth upon his hinges, so doth the slothful upon his bed.
theirs: [As] the door turneth upon his hinges, so [doth] the slothful upon his bed.

ours: The slothful hideth his hand in his bosom; it grieveth him to bring it again to his mouth.
theirs: The slothful hideth his hand in [his] bosom; it grieveth him to bring it again to his mouth.

ours: The sluggard is wiser in his own conceit than seven men that can render a reason.
theirs: The sluggard [is] wiser in his own conceit than seven men that can render a reason.

ours: He that passeth by, and meddleth with strife belonging not to him, is like one that taketh a dog by the ears.
theirs: He that passeth by, [and] meddleth with strife [belonging] not to him, [is like] one that taketh a dog by the ears.

ours: As a mad man who casteth firebrands, arrows, and death,
theirs: As a mad [man] who casteth firebrands, arrows, and death,

ours: So is the man that deceiveth his neighbour, and saith, Am not I in sport?
theirs: So [is] the man [that] deceiveth his neighbour, and saith, Am not I in sport?

ours: Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: so where there is no talebearer, the strife ceaseth.
theirs: Where no wood is, [there] the fire goeth out: so where [there is] no talebearer, the strife ceaseth.

ours: As coals are to burning coals, and wood to fire; so is a contentious man to kindle strife.
theirs: [As] coals [are] to burning coals, and wood to fire; so [is] a contentious man to kindle strife.

ours: The words of a talebearer are as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.
theirs: The words of a talebearer [are] as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.

ours: Burning lips and a wicked heart are like a potsherd covered with silver dross.
theirs: Burning lips and a wicked heart [are like] a potsherd covered with silver dross.

ours: When he speaketh fair, believe him not: for there are seven abominations in his heart.
theirs: When he speaketh fair, believe him not: for [there are] seven abominations in his heart.

ours: Whose hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shewed before the whole congregation.
theirs: [Whose] hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shewed before the [whole] congregation.

ours: A lying tongue hateth those that are afflicted by it; and a flattering mouth worketh ruin.
theirs: A lying tongue hateth [those that are] afflicted by it; and a flattering mouth worketh ruin.

ours: A stone is heavy, and the sand weighty; but a fools wrath is heavier than them both.
theirs: A stone [is] heavy, and the sand weighty; but a fool's wrath [is] heavier than them both.

ours: Wrath is cruel, and anger is outrageous; but who is able to stand before envy?
theirs: Wrath [is] cruel, and anger [is] outrageous; but who [is] able to stand before envy?

ours: Open rebuke is better than secret love.
theirs: Open rebuke [is] better than secret love.

ours: Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.
theirs: Faithful [are] the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy [are] deceitful.

ours: As a bird that wandereth from her nest, so is a man that wandereth from his place.
theirs: As a bird that wandereth from her nest, so [is] a man that wandereth from his place.

ours: Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart: so doth the sweetness of a mans friend by hearty counsel.
theirs: Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart: so [doth] the sweetness of a man's friend by hearty counsel.

ours: Thine own friend, and thy fathers friend, forsake not; neither go into thy brothers house in the day of thy calamity: for better is a neighbour that is near than a brother far off.
theirs: Thine own friend, and thy father's friend, forsake not; neither go into thy brother's house in the day of thy calamity: [for] better [is] a neighbour [that is] near than a brother far off.

ours: A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself; but the simple pass on, and are punished.
theirs: A prudent [man] foreseeth the evil, [and] hideth himself; [but] the simple pass on, [and] are punished.

ours: Whosoever hideth her hideth the wind, and the ointment of his right hand, which bewrayeth itself.
theirs: Whosoever hideth her hideth the wind, and the ointment of his right hand, [which] bewrayeth [itself].

ours: As in water face answereth to face, so the heart of man to man.
theirs: As in water face [answereth] to face, so the heart of man to man.

ours: As the fining pot for silver, and the furnace for gold; so is a man to his praise.
theirs: [As] the fining pot for silver, and the furnace for gold; so [is] a man to his praise.

ours: Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar among wheat with a pestle, yet will not his foolishness depart from him.
theirs: Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar among wheat with a pestle, [yet] will not his foolishness depart from him.

ours: Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds.
theirs: Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, [and] look well to thy herds.

ours: For riches are not for ever: and doth the crown endure to every generation?
theirs: For riches [are] not for ever: and doth the crown [endure] to every generation?

ours: The lambs are for thy clothing, and the goats are the price of the field.
theirs: The lambs [are] for thy clothing, and the goats [are] the price of the field.

ours: And thou shalt have goats milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, and for the maintenance for thy maidens.
theirs: And [thou shalt have] goats' milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, and [for] the maintenance for thy maidens.

ours: For the transgression of a land many are the princes thereof: but by a man of understanding and knowledge the state thereof shall be prolonged.
theirs: For the transgression of a land many [are] the princes thereof: but by a man of understanding [and] knowledge the state [thereof] shall be prolonged.

ours: A poor man that oppresseth the poor is like a sweeping rain which leaveth no food.
theirs: A poor man that oppresseth the poor [is like] a sweeping rain which leaveth no food.

ours: Evil men understand not judgment: but they that seek the LORD understand all things.
theirs: Evil men understand not judgment: but they that seek the LORD understand all [things].

ours: Better is the poor that walketh in his uprightness, than he that is perverse in his ways, though he be rich.
theirs: Better [is] the poor that walketh in his uprightness, than [he that is] perverse [in his] ways, though he [be] rich.

ours: Whoso keepeth the law is a wise son: but he that is a companion of riotous men shameth his father.
theirs: Whoso keepeth the law [is] a wise son: but he that is a companion of riotous [men] shameth his father.

ours: He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be abomination.
theirs: He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer [shall be] abomination.

ours: Whoso causeth the righteous to go astray in an evil way, he shall fall himself into his own pit: but the upright shall have good things in possession.
theirs: Whoso causeth the righteous to go astray in an evil way, he shall fall himself into his own pit: but the upright shall have good [things] in possession.

ours: The rich man is wise in his own conceit; but the poor that hath understanding searcheth him out.
theirs: The rich man [is] wise in his own conceit; but the poor that hath understanding searcheth him out.

ours: When righteous men do rejoice, there is great glory: but when the wicked rise, a man is hidden.
theirs: When righteous [men] do rejoice, [there is] great glory: but when the wicked rise, a man is hidden.

ours: He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.
theirs: He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh [them] shall have mercy.

ours: Happy is the man that feareth alway: but he that hardeneth his heart shall fall into mischief.
theirs: Happy [is] the man that feareth alway: but he that hardeneth his heart shall fall into mischief.

ours: As a roaring lion, and a ranging bear; so is a wicked ruler over the poor people.
theirs: [As] a roaring lion, and a ranging bear; [so is] a wicked ruler over the poor people.

ours: The prince that wanteth understanding is also a great oppressor: but he that hateth covetousness shall prolong his days.
theirs: The prince that wanteth understanding [is] also a great oppressor: [but] he that hateth covetousness shall prolong [his] days.

ours: A man that doeth violence to the blood of any person shall flee to the pit; let no man stay him.
theirs: A man that doeth violence to the blood of [any] person shall flee to the pit; let no man stay him.

ours: Whoso walketh uprightly shall be saved: but he that is perverse in his ways shall fall at once.
theirs: Whoso walketh uprightly shall be saved: but [he that is] perverse [in his] ways shall fall at once.

ours: He that tilleth his land shall have plenty of bread: but he that followeth after vain persons shall have poverty enough.
theirs: He that tilleth his land shall have plenty of bread: but he that followeth after vain [persons] shall have poverty enough.

ours: To have respect of persons is not good: for for a piece of bread that man will transgress.
theirs: To have respect of persons [is] not good: for for a piece of bread [that] man will transgress.

ours: He that hasteth to be rich hath an evil eye, and considereth not that poverty shall come upon him.
theirs: He that hasteth to be rich [hath] an evil eye, and considereth not that poverty shall come upon him.

ours: Whoso robbeth his father or his mother, and saith, It is no transgression; the same is the companion of a destroyer.
theirs: Whoso robbeth his father or his mother, and saith, [It is] no transgression; the same [is] the companion of a destroyer.

ours: HE, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.
theirs: He, that being often reproved hardeneth [his] neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.

ours: Whoso loveth wisdom rejoiceth his father: but he that keepeth company with harlots spendeth his substance.
theirs: Whoso loveth wisdom rejoiceth his father: but he that keepeth company with harlots spendeth [his] substance.

ours: In the transgression of an evil man there is a snare: but the righteous doth sing and rejoice.
theirs: In the transgression of an evil man [there is] a snare: but the righteous doth sing and rejoice.

ours: The righteous considereth the cause of the poor: but the wicked regardeth not to know it.
theirs: The righteous considereth the cause of the poor: [but] the wicked regardeth not to know [it].

ours: Scornful men bring a city into a snare: but wise men turn away wrath.
theirs: Scornful men bring a city into a snare: but wise [men] turn away wrath.

ours: If a wise man contendeth with a foolish man, whether he rage or laugh, there is no rest.
theirs: [If] a wise man contendeth with a foolish man, whether he rage or laugh, [there is] no rest.

ours: A fool uttereth all his mind: but a wise man keepeth it in till afterwards.
theirs: A fool uttereth all his mind: but a wise [man] keepeth it in till afterwards.

ours: If a ruler hearken to lies, all his servants are wicked.
theirs: If a ruler hearken to lies, all his servants [are] wicked.

ours: The rod and reproof give wisdom: but a child left to himself bringeth his mother to shame.
theirs: The rod and reproof give wisdom: but a child left [to himself] bringeth his mother to shame.

ours: Where there is no vision, the people perish: but he that keepeth the law, happy is he.
theirs: Where [there is] no vision, the people perish: but he that keepeth the law, happy [is] he.

ours: Seest thou a man that is hasty in his words? there is more hope of a fool than of him.
theirs: Seest thou a man [that is] hasty in his words? [there is] more hope of a fool than of him.

ours: He that delicately bringeth up his servant from a child shall have him become his son at the length.
theirs: He that delicately bringeth up his servant from a child shall have him become [his] son at the length.

ours: A mans pride shall bring him low: but honour shall uphold the humble in spirit.
theirs: A man's pride shall bring him low: but honour shall uphold the humble in spirit.

ours: Whoso is partner with a thief hateth his own soul: he heareth cursing, and bewrayeth it not.
theirs: Whoso is partner with a thief hateth his own soul: he heareth cursing, and bewrayeth [it] not.

ours: Many seek the rulers favour; but every mans judgment cometh from the LORD.
theirs: Many seek the ruler's favour; but [every] man's judgment [cometh] from the LORD.

ours: An unjust man is an abomination to the just: and he that is upright in the way is abomination to the wicked.
theirs: An unjust man [is] an abomination to the just: and [he that is] upright in the way [is] abomination to the wicked.

ours: THE words of Agur the son of Jakeh, even the prophecy: the man spake unto Ithiel, even unto Ithiel and Ucal,
theirs: The words of Agur the son of Jakeh, [even] the prophecy: the man spake unto Ithiel, even unto Ithiel and Ucal,

ours: Surely I am more brutish than any man, and have not the understanding of a man.
theirs: Surely I [am] more brutish than [any] man, and have not the understanding of a man.

ours: Who hath ascended up into heaven, or descended? who hath gathered the wind in his fists? who hath bound the waters in a garment? who hath established all the ends of the earth? what is his name, and what is his sons name, if thou canst tell?
theirs: Who hath ascended up into heaven, or descended? who hath gathered the wind in his fists? who hath bound the waters in a garment? who hath established all the ends of the earth? what [is] his name, and what [is] his son's name, if thou canst tell?

ours: Every word of God is pure: he is a shield unto them that put their trust in him.
theirs: Every word of God [is] pure: he [is] a shield unto them that put their trust in him.

ours: Two things have I required of thee; deny me them not before I die:
theirs: Two [things] have I required of thee; deny me [them] not before I die:

ours: Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the LORD? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.
theirs: Lest I be full, and deny [thee], and say, Who [is] the LORD? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God [in vain].

ours: There is a generation that curseth their father, and doth not bless their mother.
theirs: [There is] a generation [that] curseth their father, and doth not bless their mother.

ours: There is a generation that are pure in their own eyes, and yet is not washed from their filthiness.
theirs: [There is] a generation [that are] pure in their own eyes, and [yet] is not washed from their filthiness.

ours: There is a generation, O how lofty are their eyes! and their eyelids are lifted up.
theirs: [There is] a generation, O how lofty are their eyes! and their eyelids are lifted up.

ours: There is a generation, whose teeth are as swords, and their jaw teeth as knives, to devour the poor from off the earth, and the needy from among men.
theirs: [There is] a generation, whose teeth [are as] swords, and their jaw teeth [as] knives, to devour the poor from off the earth, and the needy from [among] men.

ours: The horseleach hath two daughters, crying, Give, give. There are three things that are never satisfied, yea, four things say not, It is enough:
theirs: The horseleach hath two daughters, [crying], Give, give. There are three [things that] are never satisfied, [yea], four [things] say not, [It is] enough:

ours: The grave; and the barren womb; the earth that is not filled with water; and the fire that saith not, It is enough.
theirs: The grave; and the barren womb; the earth [that] is not filled with water; and the fire [that] saith not, [It is] enough.

ours: The eye that mocketh at his father, and despiseth to obey his mother, the ravens of the valley shall pick it out, and the young eagles shall eat it.
theirs: The eye [that] mocketh at [his] father, and despiseth to obey [his] mother, the ravens of the valley shall pick it out, and the young eagles shall eat it.

ours: There be three things which are too wonderful for me, yea, four which I know not:
theirs: There be three [things which] are too wonderful for me, yea, four which I know not:

ours: Such is the way of an adulterous woman; she eateth, and wipeth her mouth, and saith, I have done no wickedness.
theirs: Such [is] the way of an adulterous woman; she eateth, and wipeth her mouth, and saith, I have done no wickedness.

ours: For three things the earth is disquieted, and for four which it cannot bear:
theirs: For three [things] the earth is disquieted, and for four [which] it cannot bear:

ours: For an odious woman when she is married; and an handmaid that is heir to her mistress.
theirs: For an odious [woman] when she is married; and an handmaid that is heir to her mistress.

ours: There be four things which are little upon the earth, but they are exceeding wise:
theirs: There be four [things which are] little upon the earth, but they [are] exceeding wise:

ours: The ants are a people not strong, yet they prepare their meat in the summer;
theirs: The ants [are] a people not strong, yet they prepare their meat in the summer;

ours: The conies are but a feeble folk, yet make they their houses in the rocks;
theirs: The conies [are but] a feeble folk, yet make they their houses in the rocks;

ours: The spider taketh hold with her hands, and is in kings palaces.
theirs: The spider taketh hold with her hands, and is in kings' palaces.

ours: There be three things which go well, yea, four are comely in going:
theirs: There be three [things] which go well, yea, four are comely in going:

ours: A lion which is strongest among beasts, and turneth not away for any;
theirs: A lion [which is] strongest among beasts, and turneth not away for any;

ours: A greyhound; an he goat also; and a king, against whom there is no rising up.
theirs: A greyhound; an he goat also; and a king, against whom [there is] no rising up.

ours: If thou hast done foolishly in lifting up thyself, or if thou hast thought evil, lay thine hand upon thy mouth.
theirs: If thou hast done foolishly in lifting up thyself, or if thou hast thought evil, [lay] thine hand upon thy mouth.

ours: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine; nor for princes strong drink:
theirs: [It is] not for kings, O Lemuel, [it is] not for kings to drink wine; nor for princes strong drink:

ours: Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies.
theirs: Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price [is] far above rubies.

ours: She is like the merchants ships; she bringeth her food from afar.
theirs: She is like the merchants' ships; she bringeth her food from afar.

ours: She perceiveth that her merchandise is good: her candle goeth not out by night.
theirs: She perceiveth that her merchandise [is] good: her candle goeth not out by night.

ours: She is not afraid of the snow for her household: for all her household are clothed with scarlet.
theirs: She is not afraid of the snow for her household: for all her household [are] clothed with scarlet.

ours: She maketh herself coverings of tapestry; her clothing is silk and purple.
theirs: She maketh herself coverings of tapestry; her clothing [is] silk and purple.

ours: She maketh fine linen, and selleth it; and delivereth girdles unto the merchant.
theirs: She maketh fine linen, and selleth [it]; and delivereth girdles unto the merchant.

ours: Strength and honour are her clothing; and she shall rejoice in time to come.
theirs: Strength and honour [are] her clothing; and she shall rejoice in time to come.

ours: She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue is the law of kindness.
theirs: She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue [is] the law of kindness.

ours: Her children arise up, and call her blessed; her husband also, and he praiseth her.
theirs: Her children arise up, and call her blessed; her husband [also], and he praiseth her.

ours: Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised.
theirs: Favour [is] deceitful, and beauty [is] vain: [but] a woman [that] feareth the LORD, she shall be praised.

ours: Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher, vanity of vanities; all is vanity.
theirs: Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher, vanity of vanities; all [is] vanity.

ours: One generation passeth away, and another generation cometh: but the earth abideth for ever.
theirs: [One] generation passeth away, and [another] generation cometh: but the earth abideth for ever.

ours: All the rivers run into the sea; yet the sea is not full; unto the place from whence the rivers come, thither they return again.
theirs: All the rivers run into the sea; yet the sea [is] not full; unto the place from whence the rivers come, thither they return again.

ours: All things are full of labour; man cannot utter it: the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.
theirs: All things [are] full of labour; man cannot utter [it]: the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.

ours: The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.
theirs: The thing that hath been, it [is that] which shall be; and that which is done [is] that which shall be done: and [there is] no new [thing] under the sun.

ours: Is there any thing whereof it may be said, See, this is new? it hath been already of old time, which was before us.
theirs: Is there [any] thing whereof it may be said, See, this [is] new? it hath been already of old time, which was before us.

ours: There is no remembrance of former things; neither shall there be any remembrance of things that are to come with those that shall come after.
theirs: [There is] no remembrance of former [things]; neither shall there be [any] remembrance of [things] that are to come with [those] that shall come after.

ours: And I gave my heart to seek and search out by wisdom concerning all things that are done under heaven: this sore travail hath God given to the sons of man to be exercised therewith.
theirs: And I gave my heart to seek and search out by wisdom concerning all [things] that are done under heaven: this sore travail hath God given to the sons of man to be exercised therewith.

ours: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and, behold, all is vanity and vexation of spirit.
theirs: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and, behold, all [is] vanity and vexation of spirit.

ours: That which is crooked cannot be made straight: and that which is wanting cannot be numbered.
theirs: [That which is] crooked cannot be made straight: and that which is wanting cannot be numbered.

ours: I communed with mine own heart, saying, Lo, I am come to great estate, and have gotten more wisdom than all they that have been before me in Jerusalem: yea, my heart had great experience of wisdom and knowledge.
theirs: I communed with mine own heart, saying, Lo, I am come to great estate, and have gotten more wisdom than all [they] that have been before me in Jerusalem: yea, my heart had great experience of wisdom and knowledge.

ours: For in much wisdom is much grief: and he that increaseth knowledge increaseth sorrow.
theirs: For in much wisdom [is] much grief: and he that increaseth knowledge increaseth sorrow.

ours: I SAID in mine heart, Go to now, I will prove thee with mirth, therefore enjoy pleasure: and, behold, this also is vanity.
theirs: I said in mine heart, Go to now, I will prove thee with mirth, therefore enjoy pleasure: and, behold, this also [is] vanity.

ours: I said of laughter, It is mad: and of mirth, What doeth it?
theirs: I said of laughter, [It is] mad: and of mirth, What doeth it?

ours: I sought in mine heart to give myself unto wine, yet acquainting mine heart with wisdom; and to lay hold on folly, till I might see what was that good for the sons of men, which they should do under the heaven all the days of their life.
theirs: I sought in mine heart to give myself unto wine, yet acquainting mine heart with wisdom; and to lay hold on folly, till I might see what [was] that good for the sons of men, which they should do under the heaven all the days of their life.

ours: I made me gardens and orchards, and I planted trees in them of all kind of fruits:
theirs: I made me gardens and orchards, and I planted trees in them of all [kind of] fruits:

ours: I got me servants and maidens, and had servants born in my house; also I had great possessions of great and small cattle above all that were in Jerusalem before me:
theirs: I got [me] servants and maidens, and had servants born in my house; also I had great possessions of great and small cattle above all that were in Jerusalem before me:

ours: I gathered me also silver and gold, and the peculiar treasure of kings and of the provinces: I gat me men singers and women singers, and the delights of the sons of men, as musical instruments, and that of all sorts.
theirs: I gathered me also silver and gold, and the peculiar treasure of kings and of the provinces: I gat me men singers and women singers, and the delights of the sons of men, [as] musical instruments, and that of all sorts.

ours: Then I looked on all the works that my hands had wrought, and on the labour that I had laboured to do: and, behold, all was vanity and vexation of spirit, and there was no profit under the sun.
theirs: Then I looked on all the works that my hands had wrought, and on the labour that I had laboured to do: and, behold, all [was] vanity and vexation of spirit, and [there was] no profit under the sun.

ours: And I turned myself to behold wisdom, and madness, and folly: for what can the man do that cometh after the king? even that which hath been already done.
theirs: And I turned myself to behold wisdom, and madness, and folly: for what [can] the man [do] that cometh after the king? [even] that which hath been already done.

ours: The wise mans eyes are in his head; but the fool walketh in darkness: and I myself perceived also that one event happeneth to them all.
theirs: The wise man's eyes [are] in his head; but the fool walketh in darkness: and I myself perceived also that one event happeneth to them all.

ours: Then said I in my heart, As it happeneth to the fool, so it happeneth even to me; and why was I then more wise? Then I said in my heart, that this also is vanity.
theirs: Then said I in my heart, As it happeneth to the fool, so it happeneth even to me; and why was I then more wise? Then I said in my heart, that this also [is] vanity.

ours: For there is no remembrance of the wise more than of the fool for ever; seeing that which now is in the days to come shall all be forgotten. And how dieth the wise man? as the fool.
theirs: For [there is] no remembrance of the wise more than of the fool for ever; seeing that which now [is] in the days to come shall all be forgotten. And how dieth the wise [man]? as the fool.

ours: Therefore I hated life; because the work that is wrought under the sun is grievous unto me: for all is vanity and vexation of spirit.
theirs: Therefore I hated life; because the work that is wrought under the sun [is] grievous unto me: for all [is] vanity and vexation of spirit.

ours: And who knoweth whether he shall be a wise man or a fool? yet shall he have rule over all my labour wherein I have laboured, and wherein I have shewed myself wise under the sun. This is also vanity.
theirs: And who knoweth whether he shall be a wise [man] or a fool? yet shall he have rule over all my labour wherein I have laboured, and wherein I have shewed myself wise under the sun. This [is] also vanity.

ours: For there is a man whose labour is in wisdom, and in knowledge, and in equity; yet to a man that hath not laboured therein shall he leave it for his portion. This also is vanity and a great evil.
theirs: For there is a man whose labour [is] in wisdom, and in knowledge, and in equity; yet to a man that hath not laboured therein shall he leave it [for] his portion. This also [is] vanity and a great evil.

ours: For all his days are sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.
theirs: For all his days [are] sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.

ours: There is nothing better for a man, than that he should eat and drink, and that he should make his soul enjoy good in his labour. This also I saw, that it was from the hand of God.
theirs: [There is] nothing better for a man, [than] that he should eat and drink, and [that] he should make his soul enjoy good in his labour. This also I saw, that it [was] from the hand of God.

ours: For who can eat, or who else can hasten hereunto, more than I?
theirs: For who can eat, or who else can hasten [hereunto], more than I?

ours: For God giveth to a man that is good in his sight wisdom, and knowledge, and joy: but to the sinner he giveth travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to him that is good before God. This also is vanity and vexation of spirit.
theirs: For [God] giveth to a man that [is] good in his sight wisdom, and knowledge, and joy: but to the sinner he giveth travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to [him that is] good before God. This also [is] vanity and vexation of spirit.

ours: TO every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:
theirs: To every [thing there is] a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:

ours: A time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted;
theirs: A time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up [that which is] planted;

ours: He hath made every thing beautiful in his time: also he hath set the world in their heart, so that no man can find out the work that God maketh from the beginning to the end.
theirs: He hath made every [thing] beautiful in his time: also he hath set the world in their heart, so that no man can find out the work that God maketh from the beginning to the end.

ours: I know that there is no good in them, but for a man to rejoice, and to do good in his life.
theirs: I know that [there is] no good in them, but for [a man] to rejoice, and to do good in his life.

ours: And also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy the good of all his labour, it is the gift of God.
theirs: And also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy the good of all his labour, it [is] the gift of God.

ours: I know that, whatsoever God doeth, it shall be for ever: nothing can be put to it, nor any thing taken from it: and God doeth it, that men should fear before him.
theirs: I know that, whatsoever God doeth, it shall be for ever: nothing can be put to it, nor any thing taken from it: and God doeth [it], that [men] should fear before him.

ours: And moreover I saw under the sun the place of judgment, that wickedness was there; and the place of righteousness, that iniquity was there.
theirs: And moreover I saw under the sun the place of judgment, [that] wickedness [was] there; and the place of righteousness, [that] iniquity [was] there.

ours: I said in mine heart, God shall judge the righteous and the wicked: for there is a time there for every purpose and for every work.
theirs: I said in mine heart, God shall judge the righteous and the wicked: for [there is] a time there for every purpose and for every work.

ours: For that which befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dieth, so dieth the other; yea, they have all one breath; so that a man hath no preeminence above a beast: for all is vanity.
theirs: For that which befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dieth, so dieth the other; yea, they have all one breath; so that a man hath no preeminence above a beast: for all [is] vanity.

ours: Wherefore I perceive that there is nothing better, than that a man should rejoice in his own works; for that is his portion: for who shall bring him to see what shall be after him?
theirs: Wherefore I perceive that [there is] nothing better, than that a man should rejoice in his own works; for that [is] his portion: for who shall bring him to see what shall be after him?

ours: SO I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power; but they had no comforter.
theirs: So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold the tears of [such as were] oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors [there was] power; but they had no comforter.

ours: Yea, better is he than both they, which hath not yet been, who hath not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.
theirs: Yea, better [is he] than both they, which hath not yet been, who hath not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.

ours: Again, I considered all travail, and every right work, that for this a man is envied of his neighbour. This is also vanity and vexation of spirit.
theirs: Again, I considered all travail, and every right work, that for this a man is envied of his neighbour. This [is] also vanity and vexation of spirit.

ours: Better is an handful with quietness, than both the hands full with travail and vexation of spirit.
theirs: Better [is] an handful [with] quietness, than both the hands full [with] travail and vexation of spirit.

ours: There is one alone, and there is not a second; yea, he hath neither child nor brother: yet is there no end of all his labour; neither is his eye satisfied with riches; neither saith he, For whom do I labour, and bereave my soul of good? This is also vanity, yea, it is a sore travail.
theirs: There is one [alone], and [there is] not a second; yea, he hath neither child nor brother: yet [is there] no end of all his labour; neither is his eye satisfied with riches; neither [saith he], For whom do I labour, and bereave my soul of good? This [is] also vanity, yea, it [is] a sore travail.

ours: Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.
theirs: Two [are] better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.

ours: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up.
theirs: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him [that is] alone when he falleth; for [he hath] not another to help him up.

ours: Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm alone?
theirs: Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm [alone]?

ours: Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished.
theirs: Better [is] a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished.

ours: For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becometh poor.
theirs: For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also [he that is] born in his kingdom becometh poor.

ours: There is no end of all the people, even of all that have been before them: they also that come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also is vanity and vexation of spirit.
theirs: [There is] no end of all the people, [even] of all that have been before them: they also that come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also [is] vanity and vexation of spirit.

ours: Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter any thing before God: for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.
theirs: Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter [any] thing before God: for God [is] in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.

ours: For a dream cometh through the multitude of business; and a fools voice is known by multitude of words.
theirs: For a dream cometh through the multitude of business; and a fool's voice [is known] by multitude of words.

ours: When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.
theirs: When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for [he hath] no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.

ours: Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.
theirs: Better [is it] that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.

ours: Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?
theirs: Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it [was] an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?

ours: For in the multitude of dreams and many words there are also divers vanities: but fear thou God.
theirs: For in the multitude of dreams and many words [there are] also [divers] vanities: but fear thou God.

ours: If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province, marvel not at the matter: for he that is higher than the highest regardeth; and there be higher than they.
theirs: If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province, marvel not at the matter: for [he that is] higher than the highest regardeth; and [there be] higher than they.

ours: Moreover the profit of the earth is for all: the king himself is served by the field.
theirs: Moreover the profit of the earth is for all: the king [himself] is served by the field.

ours: He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loveth abundance with increase: this is also vanity.
theirs: He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loveth abundance with increase: this [is] also vanity.

ours: When goods increase, they are increased that eat them: and what good is there to the owners thereof, saving the beholding of them with their eyes?
theirs: When goods increase, they are increased that eat them: and what good [is there] to the owners thereof, saving the beholding [of them] with their eyes?

ours: The sleep of a labouring man is sweet, whether he eat little or much: but the abundance of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.
theirs: The sleep of a labouring man [is] sweet, whether he eat little or much: but the abundance of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.

ours: There is a sore evil which I have seen under the sun, namely, riches kept for the owners thereof to their hurt.
theirs: There is a sore evil [which] I have seen under the sun, [namely], riches kept for the owners thereof to their hurt.

ours: But those riches perish by evil travail: and he begetteth a son, and there is nothing in his hand.
theirs: But those riches perish by evil travail: and he begetteth a son, and [there is] nothing in his hand.

ours: As he came forth of his mothers womb, naked shall he return to go as he came, and shall take nothing of his labour, which he may carry away in his hand.
theirs: As he came forth of his mother's womb, naked shall he return to go as he came, and shall take nothing of his labour, which he may carry away in his hand.

ours: And this also is a sore evil, that in all points as he came, so shall he go: and what profit hath he that hath laboured for the wind?
theirs: And this also [is] a sore evil, [that] in all points as he came, so shall he go: and what profit hath he that hath laboured for the wind?

ours: All his days also he eateth in darkness, and he hath much sorrow and wrath with his sickness.
theirs: All his days also he eateth in darkness, and [he hath] much sorrow and wrath with his sickness.

ours: Behold that which I have seen: it is good and comely for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy the good of all his labour that he taketh under the sun all the days of his life, which God giveth him: for it is his portion.
theirs: Behold [that] which I have seen: [it is] good and comely [for one] to eat and to drink, and to enjoy the good of all his labour that he taketh under the sun all the days of his life, which God giveth him: for it [is] his portion.

ours: Every man also to whom God hath given riches and wealth, and hath given him power to eat thereof, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labour; this is the gift of God.
theirs: Every man also to whom God hath given riches and wealth, and hath given him power to eat thereof, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labour; this [is] the gift of God.

ours: For he shall not much remember the days of his life; because God answereth him in the joy of his heart.
theirs: For he shall not much remember the days of his life; because God answereth [him] in the joy of his heart.

ours: THERE is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is common among men:
theirs: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it [is] common among men:

ours: A man to whom God hath given riches, wealth, and honour, so that he wanteth nothing for his soul of all that he desireth, yet God giveth him not power to eat thereof, but a stranger eateth it: this is vanity, and it is an evil disease.
theirs: A man to whom God hath given riches, wealth, and honour, so that he wanteth nothing for his soul of all that he desireth, yet God giveth him not power to eat thereof, but a stranger eateth it: this [is] vanity, and it [is] an evil disease.

ours: If a man beget an hundred children, and live many years, so that the days of his years be many, and his soul be not filled with good, and also that he have no burial; I say, that an untimely birth is better than he.
theirs: If a man beget an hundred [children], and live many years, so that the days of his years be many, and his soul be not filled with good, and also [that] he have no burial; I say, [that] an untimely birth [is] better than he.

ours: Moreover he hath not seen the sun, nor known any thing: this hath more rest than the other.
theirs: Moreover he hath not seen the sun, nor known [any thing]: this hath more rest than the other.

ours: Yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?
theirs: Yea, though he live a thousand years twice [told], yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?

ours: All the labour of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.
theirs: All the labour of man [is] for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.

ours: Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire: this is also vanity and vexation of spirit.
theirs: Better [is] the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire: this [is] also vanity and vexation of spirit.

ours: That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man: neither may he contend with him that is mightier than he.
theirs: That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it [is] man: neither may he contend with him that is mightier than he.

ours: Seeing there be many things that increase vanity, what is man the better?
theirs: Seeing there be many things that increase vanity, what [is] man the better?

ours: For who knoweth what is good for man in this life, all the days of his vain life which he spendeth as a shadow? for who can tell a man what shall be after him under the sun?
theirs: For who knoweth what [is] good for man in [this] life, all the days of his vain life which he spendeth as a shadow? for who can tell a man what shall be after him under the sun?

ours: A GOOD name is better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of ones birth.
theirs: A good name [is] better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one's birth.

ours: It is better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men; and the living will lay it to his heart.
theirs: [It is] better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the house of feasting: for that [is] the end of all men; and the living will lay [it] to his heart.

ours: Sorrow is better than laughter: for by the sadness of the countenance the heart is made better.
theirs: Sorrow [is] better than laughter: for by the sadness of the countenance the heart is made better.

ours: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
theirs: The heart of the wise [is] in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools [is] in the house of mirth.

ours: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.
theirs: [It is] better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.

ours: For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool: this also is vanity.
theirs: For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so [is] the laughter of the fool: this also [is] vanity.

ours: Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof: and the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
theirs: Better [is] the end of a thing than the beginning thereof: [and] the patient in spirit [is] better than the proud in spirit.

ours: Say not thou, What is the cause that the former days were better than these? for thou dost not inquire wisely concerning this.
theirs: Say not thou, What is [the cause] that the former days were better than these? for thou dost not inquire wisely concerning this.

ours: Wisdom is good with an inheritance: and by it there is profit to them that see the sun.
theirs: Wisdom [is] good with an inheritance: and [by it there is] profit to them that see the sun.

ours: For wisdom is a defence, and money is a defence: but the excellency of knowledge is, that wisdom giveth life to them that have it.
theirs: For wisdom [is] a defence, [and] money [is] a defence: but the excellency of knowledge [is, that] wisdom giveth life to them that have it.

ours: Consider the work of God: for who can make that straight, which he hath made crooked?
theirs: Consider the work of God: for who can make [that] straight, which he hath made crooked?

ours: All things have I seen in the days of my vanity: there is a just man that perisheth in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man that prolongeth his life in his wickedness.
theirs: All [things] have I seen in the days of my vanity: there is a just [man] that perisheth in his righteousness, and there is a wicked [man] that prolongeth [his life] in his wickedness.

ours: It is good that thou shouldest take hold of this; yea, also from this withdraw not thine hand: for he that feareth God shall come forth of them all.
theirs: [It is] good that thou shouldest take hold of this; yea, also from this withdraw not thine hand: for he that feareth God shall come forth of them all.

ours: Wisdom strengtheneth the wise more than ten mighty men which are in the city.
theirs: Wisdom strengtheneth the wise more than ten mighty [men] which are in the city.

ours: For there is not a just man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not.
theirs: For [there is] not a just man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not.

ours: All this have I proved by wisdom: I said, I will be wise; but it was far from me.
theirs: All this have I proved by wisdom: I said, I will be wise; but it [was] far from me.

ours: I applied mine heart to know, and to search, and to seek out wisdom, and the reason of things, and to know the wickedness of folly, even of foolishness and madness:
theirs: I applied mine heart to know, and to search, and to seek out wisdom, and the reason [of things], and to know the wickedness of folly, even of foolishness [and] madness:

ours: And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.
theirs: And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart [is] snares and nets, [and] her hands [as] bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.

ours: Behold, this have I found, saith the preacher, counting one by one, to find out the account:
theirs: Behold, this have I found, saith the preacher, [counting] one by one, to find out the account:

ours: WHO is as the wise man? and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing? a mans wisdom maketh his face to shine, and the boldness of his face shall be changed.
theirs: Who [is] as the wise [man]? and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing? a man's wisdom maketh his face to shine, and the boldness of his face shall be changed.

ours: I counsel thee to keep the kings commandment, and that in regard of the oath of God.
theirs: I [counsel thee] to keep the king's commandment, and [that] in regard of the oath of God.

ours: Where the word of a king is, there is power: and who may say unto him, What doest thou?
theirs: Where the word of a king [is, there is] power: and who may say unto him, What doest thou?

ours: Whoso keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing: and a wise mans heart discerneth both time and judgment.
theirs: Whoso keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing: and a wise man's heart discerneth both time and judgment.

ours: Because to every purpose there is time and judgment, therefore the misery of man is great upon him.
theirs: Because to every purpose there is time and judgment, therefore the misery of man [is] great upon him.

ours: There is no man that hath power over the spirit to retain the spirit; neither hath he power in the day of death: and there is no discharge in that war; neither shall wickedness deliver those that are given to it.
theirs: [There is] no man that hath power over the spirit to retain the spirit; neither [hath he] power in the day of death: and [there is] no discharge in [that] war; neither shall wickedness deliver those that are given to it.

ours: All this have I seen, and applied my heart unto every work that is done under the sun: there is a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt.
theirs: All this have I seen, and applied my heart unto every work that is done under the sun: [there is] a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt.

ours: And so I saw the wicked buried, who had come and gone from the place of the holy, and they were forgotten in the city where they had so done: this is also vanity.
theirs: And so I saw the wicked buried, who had come and gone from the place of the holy, and they were forgotten in the city where they had so done: this [is] also vanity.

ours: Though a sinner do evil an hundred times, and his days be prolonged, yet surely I know that it shall be well with them that fear God, which fear before him:
theirs: Though a sinner do evil an hundred times, and his [days] be prolonged, yet surely I know that it shall be well with them that fear God, which fear before him:

ours: But it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he prolong his days, which are as a shadow; because he feareth not before God.
theirs: But it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he prolong [his] days, [which are] as a shadow; because he feareth not before God.

ours: There is a vanity which is done upon the earth; that there be just men, unto whom it happeneth according to the work of the wicked; again, there be wicked men, to whom it happeneth according to the work of the righteous: I said that this also is vanity.
theirs: There is a vanity which is done upon the earth; that there be just [men], unto whom it happeneth according to the work of the wicked; again, there be wicked [men], to whom it happeneth according to the work of the righteous: I said that this also [is] vanity.

ours: When I applied mine heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done upon the earth: (for also there is that neither day nor night seeth sleep with his eyes:)
theirs: When I applied mine heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done upon the earth: (for also [there is that] neither day nor night seeth sleep with his eyes:)

ours: Then I beheld all the work of God, that a man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun: because though a man labour to seek it out, yet he shall not find it; yea further; though a wise man think to know it, yet shall he not be able to find it.
theirs: Then I beheld all the work of God, that a man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun: because though a man labour to seek [it] out, yet he shall not find [it]; yea further; though a wise [man] think to know [it], yet shall he not be able to find [it].

ours: FOR all this I considered in my heart even to declare all this, that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of God: no man knoweth either love or hatred by all that is before them.
theirs: For all this I considered in my heart even to declare all this, that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, [are] in the hand of God: no man knoweth either love or hatred [by] all [that is] before them.

ours: All things come alike to all: there is one event to the righteous, and to the wicked; to the good and to the clean, and to the unclean; to him that sacrificeth, and to him that sacrificeth not: as is the good, so is the sinner; and he that sweareth, as he that feareth an oath.
theirs: All [things come] alike to all: [there is] one event to the righteous, and to the wicked; to the good and to the clean, and to the unclean; to him that sacrificeth, and to him that sacrificeth not: as [is] the good, so [is] the sinner; [and] he that sweareth, as [he] that feareth an oath.

ours: This is an evil among all things that are done under the sun, that there is one event unto all: yea, also the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live, and after that they go to the dead.
theirs: This [is] an evil among all [things] that are done under the sun, that [there is] one event unto all: yea, also the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness [is] in their heart while they live, and after that [they go] to the dead.

ours: Also their love, and their hatred, and their envy, is now perished; neither have they any more a portion for ever in any thing that is done under the sun.
theirs: Also their love, and their hatred, and their envy, is now perished; neither have they any more a portion for ever in any [thing] that is done under the sun.

ours: Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun, all the days of thy vanity: for that is thy portion in this life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun.
theirs: Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun, all the days of thy vanity: for that [is] thy portion in [this] life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun.

ours: Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest.
theirs: Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do [it] with thy might; for [there is] no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest.

ours: I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all.
theirs: I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race [is] not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all.

ours: For man also knoweth not his time: as the fishes that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare; so are the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falleth suddenly upon them.
theirs: For man also knoweth not his time: as the fishes that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare; so [are] the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falleth suddenly upon them.

ours: This wisdom have I seen also under the sun, and it seemed great unto me:
theirs: This wisdom have I seen also under the sun, and it [seemed] great unto me:

ours: There was a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it:
theirs: [There was] a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it:

ours: Then said I, Wisdom is better than strength: nevertheless the poor mans wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.
theirs: Then said I, Wisdom [is] better than strength: nevertheless the poor man's wisdom [is] despised, and his words are not heard.

ours: The words of wise men are heard in quiet more than the cry of him that ruleth among fools.
theirs: The words of wise [men are] heard in quiet more than the cry of him that ruleth among fools.

ours: Wisdom is better than weapons of war: but one sinner destroyeth much good.
theirs: Wisdom [is] better than weapons of war: but one sinner destroyeth much good.

ours: DEAD flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth a stinking savour: so doth a little folly him that is in reputation for wisdom and honour.
theirs: Dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth a stinking savour: [so doth] a little folly him that is in reputation for wisdom [and] honour.

ours: A wise mans heart is at his right hand; but a fools heart at his left.
theirs: A wise man's heart [is] at his right hand; but a fool's heart at his left.

ours: Yea also, when he that is a fool walketh by the way, his wisdom faileth him, and he saith to every one that he is a fool.
theirs: Yea also, when he that is a fool walketh by the way, his wisdom faileth [him], and he saith to every one [that] he [is] a fool.

ours: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, as an error which proceedeth from the ruler:
theirs: There is an evil [which] I have seen under the sun, as an error [which] proceedeth from the ruler:

ours: Whoso removeth stones shall be hurt therewith; and he that cleaveth wood shall be endangered thereby.
theirs: Whoso removeth stones shall be hurt therewith; [and] he that cleaveth wood shall be endangered thereby.

ours: If the iron be blunt, and he do not whet the edge, then must he put to more strength: but wisdom is profitable to direct.
theirs: If the iron be blunt, and he do not whet the edge, then must he put to more strength: but wisdom [is] profitable to direct.

ours: The words of a wise mans mouth are gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.
theirs: The words of a wise man's mouth [are] gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.

ours: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness: and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.
theirs: The beginning of the words of his mouth [is] foolishness: and the end of his talk [is] mischievous madness.

ours: Woe to thee, O land, when thy king is a child, and thy princes eat in the morning!
theirs: Woe to thee, O land, when thy king [is] a child, and thy princes eat in the morning!

ours: Blessed art thou, O land, when thy king is the son of nobles, and thy princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!
theirs: Blessed [art] thou, O land, when thy king [is] the son of nobles, and thy princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!

ours: A feast is made for laughter, and wine maketh merry: but money answereth all things.
theirs: A feast is made for laughter, and wine maketh merry: but money answereth all [things].

ours: If the clouds be full of rain, they empty themselves upon the earth: and if the tree fall toward the south, or toward the north, in the place where the tree falleth, there it shall be.
theirs: If the clouds be full of rain, they empty [themselves] upon the earth: and if the tree fall toward the south, or toward the north, in the place where the tree falleth, there it shall be.

ours: As thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit, nor how the bones do grow in the womb of her that is with child: even so thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all.
theirs: As thou knowest not what [is] the way of the spirit, [nor] how the bones [do grow] in the womb of her that is with child: even so thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all.

ours: In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening withhold not thine hand: for thou knowest not whether shall prosper, either this or that, or whether they both shall be alike good.
theirs: In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening withhold not thine hand: for thou knowest not whether shall prosper, either this or that, or whether they both [shall be] alike good.

ours: Truly the light is sweet, and a pleasant thing it is for the eyes to behold the sun:
theirs: Truly the light [is] sweet, and a pleasant [thing it is] for the eyes to behold the sun:

ours: But if a man live many years, and rejoice in them all; yet let him remember the days of darkness; for they shall be many. All that cometh is vanity.
theirs: But if a man live many years, [and] rejoice in them all; yet let him remember the days of darkness; for they shall be many. All that cometh [is] vanity.

ours: Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth; and let thy heart cheer thee in the days of thy youth, and walk in the ways of thine heart, and in the sight of thine eyes: but know thou, that for all these things God will bring thee into judgment.
theirs: Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth; and let thy heart cheer thee in the days of thy youth, and walk in the ways of thine heart, and in the sight of thine eyes: but know thou, that for all these [things] God will bring thee into judgment.

ours: Therefore remove sorrow from thy heart, and put away evil from thy flesh: for childhood and youth are vanity.
theirs: Therefore remove sorrow from thy heart, and put away evil from thy flesh: for childhood and youth [are] vanity.

ours: Also when they shall be afraid of that which is high, and fears shall be in the way, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goeth to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets:
theirs: Also [when] they shall be afraid of [that which is] high, and fears [shall be] in the way, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goeth to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets:

ours: Vanity of vanities, saith the preacher; all is vanity.
theirs: Vanity of vanities, saith the preacher; all [is] vanity.

ours: And moreover, because the preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yea, he gave good heed, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs.
theirs: And moreover, because the preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yea, he gave good heed, and sought out, [and] set in order many proverbs.

ours: The preacher sought to find out acceptable words: and that which was written was upright, even words of truth.
theirs: The preacher sought to find out acceptable words: and [that which was] written [was] upright, [even] words of truth.

ours: The words of the wise are as goads, and as nails fastened by the masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd.
theirs: The words of the wise [are] as goads, and as nails fastened [by] the masters of assemblies, [which] are given from one shepherd.

ours: And further, by these, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.
theirs: And further, by these, my son, be admonished: of making many books [there is] no end; and much study [is] a weariness of the flesh.

ours: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.
theirs: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this [is] the whole [duty] of man.

ours: For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.
theirs: For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether [it be] good, or whether [it be] evil.

ours: THE song of songs, which is Solomons.
theirs: The song of songs, which [is] Solomon's.

ours: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth: for thy love is better than wine.
theirs: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth: for thy love [is] better than wine.

ours: Because of the savour of thy good ointments thy name is as ointment poured forth, therefore do the virgins love thee.
theirs: Because of the savour of thy good ointments thy name [is as] ointment poured forth, therefore do the virgins love thee.

ours: I am black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Kedar, as the curtains of Solomon.
theirs: I [am] black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Kedar, as the curtains of Solomon.

ours: Look not upon me, because I am black, because the sun hath looked upon me: my mothers children were angry with me; they made me the keeper of the vineyards; but mine own vineyard have I not kept.
theirs: Look not upon me, because I [am] black, because the sun hath looked upon me: my mother's children were angry with me; they made me the keeper of the vineyards; [but] mine own vineyard have I not kept.

ours: Tell me, O thou whom my soul loveth, where thou feedest, where thou makest thy flock to rest at noon: for why should I be as one that turneth aside by the flocks of thy companions?
theirs: Tell me, O thou whom my soul loveth, where thou feedest, where thou makest [thy flock] to rest at noon: for why should I be as one that turneth aside by the flocks of thy companions?

ours: If thou know not, O thou fairest among women, go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock, and feed thy kids beside the shepherds tents.
theirs: If thou know not, O thou fairest among women, go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock, and feed thy kids beside the shepherds' tents.

ours: I have compared thee, O my love, to a company of horses in Pharaohs chariots.
theirs: I have compared thee, O my love, to a company of horses in Pharaoh's chariots.

ours: Thy cheeks are comely with rows of jewels, thy neck with chains of gold.
theirs: Thy cheeks are comely with rows [of jewels], thy neck with chains [of gold].

ours: While the king sitteth at his table, my spikenard sendeth forth the smell thereof.
theirs: While the king [sitteth] at his table, my spikenard sendeth forth the smell thereof.

ours: A bundle of myrrh is my wellbeloved unto me; he shall lie all night betwixt my breasts.
theirs: A bundle of myrrh [is] my wellbeloved unto me; he shall lie all night betwixt my breasts.

ours: My beloved is unto me as a cluster of camphire in the vineyards of En-gedi.
theirs: My beloved [is] unto me [as] a cluster of camphire in the vineyards of Engedi.

ours: Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; thou hast doves eyes.
theirs: Behold, thou [art] fair, my love; behold, thou [art] fair; thou [hast] doves' eyes.

ours: Behold, thou art fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant: also our bed is green.
theirs: Behold, thou [art] fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant: also our bed [is] green.

ours: The beams of our house are cedar, and our rafters of fir.
theirs: The beams of our house [are] cedar, [and] our rafters of fir.

ours: I AM the rose of Sharon, and the lily of the valleys.
theirs: I [am] the rose of Sharon, [and] the lily of the valleys.

ours: As the lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.
theirs: As the lily among thorns, so [is] my love among the daughters.

ours: As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, and his fruit was sweet to my taste.
theirs: As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so [is] my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, and his fruit [was] sweet to my taste.

ours: He brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me was love.
theirs: He brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me [was] love.

ours: Stay me with flagons, comfort me with apples: for I am sick of love.
theirs: Stay me with flagons, comfort me with apples: for I [am] sick of love.

ours: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand doth embrace me.
theirs: His left hand [is] under my head, and his right hand doth embrace me.

ours: I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.
theirs: I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake [my] love, till he please.

ours: For, lo, the winter is past, the rain is over and gone;
theirs: For, lo, the winter is past, the rain is over [and] gone;

ours: The flowers appear on the earth; the time of the singing of birds is come, and the voice of the turtle is heard in our land;
theirs: The flowers appear on the earth; the time of the singing [of birds] is come, and the voice of the turtle is heard in our land;

ours: The fig tree putteth forth her green figs, and the vines with the tender grape give a good smell. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away.
theirs: The fig tree putteth forth her green figs, and the vines [with] the tender grape give a [good] smell. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away.

ours: O my dove, that art in the clefts of the rock, in the secret places of the stairs, let me see thy countenance, let me hear thy voice; for sweet is thy voice, and thy countenance is comely.
theirs: O my dove, [that art] in the clefts of the rock, in the secret [places] of the stairs, let me see thy countenance, let me hear thy voice; for sweet [is] thy voice, and thy countenance [is] comely.

ours: Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines: for our vines have tender grapes.
theirs: Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines: for our vines [have] tender grapes.

ours: My beloved is mine, and I am his: he feedeth among the lilies.
theirs: My beloved [is] mine, and I [am] his: he feedeth among the lilies.

ours: The watchmen that go about the city found me: to whom I said, Saw ye him whom my soul loveth?
theirs: The watchmen that go about the city found me: [to whom I said], Saw ye him whom my soul loveth?

ours: It was but a little that I passed from them, but I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mothers house, and into the chamber of her that conceived me.
theirs: [It was] but a little that I passed from them, but I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother's house, and into the chamber of her that conceived me.

ours: I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.
theirs: I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake [my] love, till he please.

ours: Who is this that cometh out of the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all powders of the merchant?
theirs: Who [is] this that cometh out of the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all powders of the merchant?

ours: Behold his bed, which is Solomons; threescore valiant men are about it, of the valiant of Israel.
theirs: Behold his bed, which [is] Solomon's; threescore valiant men [are] about it, of the valiant of Israel.

ours: They all hold swords, being expert in war: every man hath his sword upon his thigh because of fear in the night.
theirs: They all hold swords, [being] expert in war: every man [hath] his sword upon his thigh because of fear in the night.

ours: He made the pillars thereof of silver, the bottom thereof of gold, the covering of it of purple, the midst thereof being paved with love, for the daughters of Jerusalem.
theirs: He made the pillars thereof [of] silver, the bottom thereof [of] gold, the covering of it [of] purple, the midst thereof being paved [with] love, for the daughters of Jerusalem.

ours: BEHOLD, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; thou hast doves eyes within thy locks: thy hair is as a flock of goats, that appear from mount Gilead.
theirs: Behold, thou [art] fair, my love; behold, thou [art] fair; thou [hast] doves' eyes within thy locks: thy hair [is] as a flock of goats, that appear from mount Gilead.

ours: Thy teeth are like a flock of sheep that are even shorn, which came up from the washing; whereof every one bear twins, and none is barren among them.
theirs: Thy teeth [are] like a flock [of sheep that are even] shorn, which came up from the washing; whereof every one bear twins, and none [is] barren among them.

ours: Thy lips are like a thread of scarlet, and thy speech is comely: thy temples are like a piece of a pomegranate within thy locks.
theirs: Thy lips [are] like a thread of scarlet, and thy speech [is] comely: thy temples [are] like a piece of a pomegranate within thy locks.

ours: Thy neck is like the tower of David builded for an armoury, whereon there hang a thousand bucklers, all shields of mighty men.
theirs: Thy neck [is] like the tower of David builded for an armoury, whereon there hang a thousand bucklers, all shields of mighty men.

ours: Thy two breasts are like two young roes that are twins, which feed among the lilies.
theirs: Thy two breasts [are] like two young roes that are twins, which feed among the lilies.

ours: Thou art all fair, my love; there is no spot in thee.
theirs: Thou [art] all fair, my love; [there is] no spot in thee.

ours: Come with me from Lebanon, my spouse, with me from Lebanon: look from the top of Amana, from the top of Shenir and Hermon, from the lions dens, from the mountains of the leopards.
theirs: Come with me from Lebanon, [my] spouse, with me from Lebanon: look from the top of Amana, from the top of Shenir and Hermon, from the lions' dens, from the mountains of the leopards.

ours: Thou hast ravished my heart, my sister, my spouse; thou hast ravished my heart with one of thine eyes, with one chain of thy neck.
theirs: Thou hast ravished my heart, my sister, [my] spouse; thou hast ravished my heart with one of thine eyes, with one chain of thy neck.

ours: How fair is thy love, my sister, my spouse! how much better is thy love than wine! and the smell of thine ointments than all spices!
theirs: How fair is thy love, my sister, [my] spouse! how much better is thy love than wine! and the smell of thine ointments than all spices!

ours: Thy lips, O my spouse, drop as the honeycomb: honey and milk are under thy tongue; and the smell of thy garments is like the smell of Lebanon.
theirs: Thy lips, O [my] spouse, drop [as] the honeycomb: honey and milk [are] under thy tongue; and the smell of thy garments [is] like the smell of Lebanon.

ours: A garden inclosed is my sister, my spouse; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed.
theirs: A garden inclosed [is] my sister, [my] spouse; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed.

ours: Thy plants are an orchard of pomegranates, with pleasant fruits; camphire, with spikenard,
theirs: Thy plants [are] an orchard of pomegranates, with pleasant fruits; camphire, with spikenard,

ours: Awake, O north wind; and come, thou south; blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits.
theirs: Awake, O north wind; and come, thou south; blow upon my garden, [that] the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits.

ours: I AM come into my garden, my sister, my spouse: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk: eat, O friends; drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved.
theirs: I am come into my garden, my sister, [my] spouse: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk: eat, O friends; drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved.

ours: I sleep, but my heart waketh: it is the voice of my beloved that knocketh, saying, Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is filled with dew, and my locks with the drops of the night.
theirs: I sleep, but my heart waketh: [it is] the voice of my beloved that knocketh, [saying], Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is filled with dew, [and] my locks with the drops of the night.

ours: My beloved put in his hand by the hole of the door, and my bowels were moved for him.
theirs: My beloved put in his hand by the hole [of the door], and my bowels were moved for him.

ours: I rose up to open to my beloved; and my hands dropped with myrrh, and my fingers with sweet smelling myrrh, upon the handles of the lock.
theirs: I rose up to open to my beloved; and my hands dropped [with] myrrh, and my fingers [with] sweet smelling myrrh, upon the handles of the lock.

ours: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved had withdrawn himself, and was gone: my soul failed when he spake: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.
theirs: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved had withdrawn himself, [and] was gone: my soul failed when he spake: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.

ours: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if ye find my beloved, that ye tell him, that I am sick of love.
theirs: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if ye find my beloved, that ye tell him, that I [am] sick of love.

ours: What is thy beloved more than another beloved, O thou fairest among women? what is thy beloved more than another beloved, that thou dost so charge us?
theirs: What [is] thy beloved more than [another] beloved, O thou fairest among women? what [is] thy beloved more than [another] beloved, that thou dost so charge us?

ours: My beloved is white and ruddy, the chiefest among ten thousand.
theirs: My beloved [is] white and ruddy, the chiefest among ten thousand.
