ours: For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body, whether we be Jews or Gentiles, whether we be bond or free; and have been all made to drink into one Spirit.
theirs: For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body, whether [we be] Jews or Gentiles, whether [we be] bond or free; and have been all made to drink into one Spirit.

ours: If the whole body were an eye, where were the hearing? If the whole were hearing, where were the smelling?
theirs: If the whole body [were] an eye, where [were] the hearing? If the whole [were] hearing, where [were] the smelling?

ours: And if they were all one member, where were the body?
theirs: And if they were all one member, where [were] the body?

ours: But now are they many members, yet but one body.
theirs: But now [are they] many members, yet but one body.

ours: And those members of the body, which we think to be less honourable, upon these we bestow more abundant honour; and our uncomely parts have more abundant comeliness.
theirs: And those [members] of the body, which we think to be less honourable, upon these we bestow more abundant honour; and our uncomely [parts] have more abundant comeliness.

ours: For our comely parts have no need: but God hath tempered the body together, having given more abundant honour to that part which lacked:
theirs: For our comely [parts] have no need: but God hath tempered the body together, having given more abundant honour to that [part] which lacked:

ours: That there should be no schism in the body; but that the members should have the same care one for another.
theirs: That there should be no schism in the body; but [that] the members should have the same care one for another.

ours: Are all apostles? are all prophets? are all teachers? are all workers of miracles?
theirs: [Are] all apostles? [are] all prophets? [are] all teachers? [are] all workers of miracles?

ours: THOUGH I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.
theirs: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become [as] sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.

ours: And though I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries, and all knowledge; and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, and have not charity, I am nothing.
theirs: And though I have [the gift of] prophecy, and understand all mysteries, and all knowledge; and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, and have not charity, I am nothing.

ours: And though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, and have not charity, it profiteth me nothing.
theirs: And though I bestow all my goods to feed [the poor], and though I give my body to be burned, and have not charity, it profiteth me nothing.

ours: Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up,
theirs: Charity suffereth long, [and] is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up,

ours: Charity never faileth: but whether there be prophecies, they shall fail; whether there be tongues, they shall cease; whether there be knowledge, it shall vanish away.
theirs: Charity never faileth: but whether [there be] prophecies, they shall fail; whether [there be] tongues, they shall cease; whether [there be] knowledge, it shall vanish away.

ours: And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.
theirs: And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these [is] charity.

ours: FOLLOW after charity, and desire spiritual gifts, but rather that ye may prophesy.
theirs: Follow after charity, and desire spiritual [gifts], but rather that ye may prophesy.

ours: For he that speaketh in an unknown tongue speaketh not unto men, but unto God: for no man understandeth him; howbeit in the spirit he speaketh mysteries.
theirs: For he that speaketh in an [unknown] tongue speaketh not unto men, but unto God: for no man understandeth [him]; howbeit in the spirit he speaketh mysteries.

ours: But he that prophesieth speaketh unto men to edification, and exhortation, and comfort.
theirs: But he that prophesieth speaketh unto men [to] edification, and exhortation, and comfort.

ours: He that speaketh in an unknown tongue edifieth himself; but he that prophesieth edifieth the church.
theirs: He that speaketh in an [unknown] tongue edifieth himself; but he that prophesieth edifieth the church.

ours: I would that ye all spake with tongues, but rather that ye prophesied: for greater is he that prophesieth than he that speaketh with tongues, except he interpret, that the church may receive edifying.
theirs: I would that ye all spake with tongues, but rather that ye prophesied: for greater [is] he that prophesieth than he that speaketh with tongues, except he interpret, that the church may receive edifying.

ours: There are, it may be, so many kinds of voices in the world, and none of them is without signification.
theirs: There are, it may be, so many kinds of voices in the world, and none of them [is] without signification.

ours: Therefore if I know not the meaning of the voice, I shall be unto him that speaketh a barbarian, and he that speaketh shall be a barbarian unto me.
theirs: Therefore if I know not the meaning of the voice, I shall be unto him that speaketh a barbarian, and he that speaketh [shall be] a barbarian unto me.

ours: Even so ye, forasmuch as ye are zealous of spiritual gifts, seek that ye may excel to the edifying of the church.
theirs: Even so ye, forasmuch as ye are zealous of spiritual [gifts], seek that ye may excel to the edifying of the church.

ours: Wherefore let him that speaketh in an unknown tongue pray that he may interpret.
theirs: Wherefore let him that speaketh in an [unknown] tongue pray that he may interpret.

ours: For if I pray in an unknown tongue, my spirit prayeth, but my understanding is unfruitful.
theirs: For if I pray in an [unknown] tongue, my spirit prayeth, but my understanding is unfruitful.

ours: Yet in the church I had rather speak five words with my understanding, that by my voice I might teach others also, than ten thousand words in an unknown tongue.
theirs: Yet in the church I had rather speak five words with my understanding, that [by my voice] I might teach others also, than ten thousand words in an [unknown] tongue.

ours: In the law it is written, With men of other tongues and other lips will I speak unto this people; and yet for all that will they not hear me, saith the Lord.
theirs: In the law it is written, With [men of] other tongues and other lips will I speak unto this people; and yet for all that will they not hear me, saith the Lord.

ours: Wherefore tongues are for a sign, not to them that believe, but to them that believe not: but prophesying serveth not for them that believe not, but for them which believe.
theirs: Wherefore tongues are for a sign, not to them that believe, but to them that believe not: but prophesying [serveth] not for them that believe not, but for them which believe.

ours: If therefore the whole church be come together into one place, and all speak with tongues, and there come in those that are unlearned, or unbelievers, will they not say that ye are mad?
theirs: If therefore the whole church be come together into one place, and all speak with tongues, and there come in [those that are] unlearned, or unbelievers, will they not say that ye are mad?

ours: But if all prophesy, and there come in one that believeth not, or one unlearned, he is convinced of all, he is judged of all:
theirs: But if all prophesy, and there come in one that believeth not, or [one] unlearned, he is convinced of all, he is judged of all:

ours: And thus are the secrets of his heart made manifest; and so falling down on his face he will worship God, and report that God is in you of a truth.
theirs: And thus are the secrets of his heart made manifest; and so falling down on [his] face he will worship God, and report that God is in you of a truth.

ours: If any man speak in an unknown tongue, let it be by two, or at the most by three, and that by course; and let one interpret.
theirs: If any man speak in an [unknown] tongue, [let it be] by two, or at the most [by] three, and [that] by course; and let one interpret.

ours: If any thing be revealed to another that sitteth by, let the first hold his peace.
theirs: If [any thing] be revealed to another that sitteth by, let the first hold his peace.

ours: For God is not the author of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints.
theirs: For God is not [the author] of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints.

ours: Let your women keep silence in the churches: for it is not permitted unto them to speak; but they are commanded to be under obedience, as also saith the law.
theirs: Let your women keep silence in the churches: for it is not permitted unto them to speak; but [they are commanded] to be under obedience, as also saith the law.

ours: But by the grace of God I am what I am: and his grace which was bestowed upon me was not in vain; but I laboured more abundantly than they all: yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.
theirs: But by the grace of God I am what I am: and his grace which [was bestowed] upon me was not in vain; but I laboured more abundantly than they all: yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.

ours: Therefore whether it were I or they, so we preach, and so ye believed.
theirs: Therefore whether [it were] I or they, so we preach, and so ye believed.

ours: And if Christ be not risen, then is our preaching vain, and your faith is also vain.
theirs: And if Christ be not risen, then [is] our preaching vain, and your faith [is] also vain.

ours: And if Christ be not raised, your faith is vain; ye are yet in your sins.
theirs: And if Christ be not raised, your faith [is] vain; ye are yet in your sins.

ours: But now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept.
theirs: But now is Christ risen from the dead, [and] become the firstfruits of them that slept.

ours: For since by man came death, by man came also the resurrection of the dead.
theirs: For since by man [came] death, by man [came] also the resurrection of the dead.

ours: But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christs at his coming.
theirs: But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ's at his coming.

ours: Then cometh the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father; when he shall have put down all rule and all authority and power.
theirs: Then [cometh] the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father; when he shall have put down all rule and all authority and power.

ours: The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death.
theirs: The last enemy [that] shall be destroyed [is] death.

ours: For he hath put all things under his feet. But when he saith, all things are put under him, it is manifest that he is excepted, which did put all things under him.
theirs: For he hath put all things under his feet. But when he saith, all things are put under [him, it is] manifest that he is excepted, which did put all things under him.

ours: Awake to righteousness, and sin not; for some have not the knowledge of God: I speak this to your shame.
theirs: Awake to righteousness, and sin not; for some have not the knowledge of God: I speak [this] to your shame.

ours: But some man will say, How are the dead raised up? and with what body do they come?
theirs: But some [man] will say, How are the dead raised up? and with what body do they come?

ours: Thou fool, that which thou sowest is not quickened, except it die:
theirs: [Thou] fool, that which thou sowest is not quickened, except it die:

ours: And that which thou sowest, thou sowest not that body that shall be, but bare grain, it may chance of wheat, or of some other grain:
theirs: And that which thou sowest, thou sowest not that body that shall be, but bare grain, it may chance of wheat, or of some other [grain]:

ours: All flesh is not the same flesh: but there is one kind of flesh of men, another flesh of beasts, another of fishes, and another of birds.
theirs: All flesh [is] not the same flesh: but [there is] one [kind of] flesh of men, another flesh of beasts, another of fishes, [and] another of birds.

ours: There are also celestial bodies, and bodies terrestrial: but the glory of the celestial is one, and the glory of the terrestrial is another.
theirs: [There are] also celestial bodies, and bodies terrestrial: but the glory of the celestial [is] one, and the [glory] of the terrestrial [is] another.

ours: There is one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars: for one star differeth from another star in glory.
theirs: [There is] one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars: for [one] star differeth from [another] star in glory.

ours: So also is the resurrection of the dead. It is sown in corruption; it is raised in incorruption:
theirs: So also [is] the resurrection of the dead. It is sown in corruption; it is raised in incorruption:

ours: And so it is written, The first man Adam was made a living soul; the last Adam was made a quickening spirit.
theirs: And so it is written, The first man Adam was made a living soul; the last Adam [was made] a quickening spirit.

ours: Howbeit that was not first which is spiritual, but that which is natural; and afterward that which is spiritual.
theirs: Howbeit that [was] not first which is spiritual, but that which is natural; and afterward that which is spiritual.

ours: The first man is of the earth, earthy: the second man is the Lord from heaven.
theirs: The first man [is] of the earth, earthy: the second man [is] the Lord from heaven.

ours: As is the earthy, such are they also that are earthy: and as is the heavenly, such are they also that are heavenly.
theirs: As [is] the earthy, such [are] they also that are earthy: and as [is] the heavenly, such [are] they also that are heavenly.

ours: For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality.
theirs: For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal [must] put on immortality.

ours: O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory?
theirs: O death, where [is] thy sting? O grave, where [is] thy victory?

ours: The sting of death is sin; and the strength of sin is the law.
theirs: The sting of death [is] sin; and the strength of sin [is] the law.

ours: But thanks be to God, which giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
theirs: But thanks [be] to God, which giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.

ours: Upon the first day of the week let every one of you lay by him in store, as God hath prospered him, that there be no gatherings when I come.
theirs: Upon the first [day] of the week let every one of you lay by him in store, as [God] hath prospered him, that there be no gatherings when I come.

ours: And when I come, whomsoever ye shall approve by your letters, them will I send to bring your liberality unto Jerusalem.
theirs: And when I come, whomsoever ye shall approve by [your] letters, them will I send to bring your liberality unto Jerusalem.

ours: For a great door and effectual is opened unto me, and there are many adversaries.
theirs: For a great door and effectual is opened unto me, and [there are] many adversaries.

ours: Now if Timotheus come, see that he may be with you without fear: for he worketh the work of the Lord, as I also do.
theirs: Now if Timotheus come, see that he may be with you without fear: for he worketh the work of the Lord, as I also [do].

ours: As touching our brother Apollos, I greatly desired him to come unto you with the brethren: but his will was not at all to come at this time; but he will come when he shall have convenient time.
theirs: As touching [our] brother Apollos, I greatly desired him to come unto you with the brethren: but his will was not at all to come at this time; but he will come when he shall have convenient time.

ours: I beseech you, brethren, (ye know the house of Stephanas, that it is the firstfruits of Achaia, and that they have addicted themselves to the ministry of the saints,)
theirs: I beseech you, brethren, (ye know the house of Stephanas, that it is the firstfruits of Achaia, and [that] they have addicted themselves to the ministry of the saints,)

ours: That ye submit yourselves unto such, and to every one that helpeth with us, and laboureth.
theirs: That ye submit yourselves unto such, and to every one that helpeth with [us], and laboureth.

ours: The salutation of me Paul with mine own hand.
theirs: The salutation of [me] Paul with mine own hand.

ours: If any man love not the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be Anathema Maran-atha.
theirs: If any man love not the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be Anathema Maranatha.

ours: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
theirs: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] with you.

ours: My love be with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen.
theirs: My love [be] with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen. <<[The first [epistle] to the Corinthians was written from Philippi by Stephanas, and Fortunatus, and Achaicus, and Timotheus.]>>

ours: PAUL, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy our brother, unto the church of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints which are in all Achaia:
theirs: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy [our] brother, unto the church of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints which are in all Achaia:

ours: Grace be to you and peace from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
theirs: Grace [be] to you and peace from God our Father, and [from] the Lord Jesus Christ.

ours: Blessed be God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort;
theirs: Blessed [be] God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort;

ours: And whether we be afflicted, it is for your consolation and salvation, which is effectual in the enduring of the same sufferings which we also suffer: or whether we be comforted, it is for your consolation and salvation.
theirs: And whether we be afflicted, [it is] for your consolation and salvation, which is effectual in the enduring of the same sufferings which we also suffer: or whether we be comforted, [it is] for your consolation and salvation.

ours: And our hope of you is stedfast, knowing, that as ye are partakers of the sufferings, so shall ye be also of the consolation.
theirs: And our hope of you [is] stedfast, knowing, that as ye are partakers of the sufferings, so [shall ye be] also of the consolation.

ours: Who delivered us from so great a death, and doth deliver: in whom we trust that he will yet deliver us;
theirs: Who delivered us from so great a death, and doth deliver: in whom we trust that he will yet deliver [us];

ours: Ye also helping together by prayer for us, that for the gift bestowed upon us by the means of many persons thanks may be given by many on our behalf.
theirs: Ye also helping together by prayer for us, that for the gift [bestowed] upon us by the means of many persons thanks may be given by many on our behalf.

ours: As also ye have acknowledged us in part, that we are your rejoicing, even as ye also are ours in the day of the Lord Jesus.
theirs: As also ye have acknowledged us in part, that we are your rejoicing, even as ye also [are] ours in the day of the Lord Jesus.

ours: And to pass by you into Macedonia, and to come again out of Macedonia unto you, and of you to be brought on my way toward Judæa.
theirs: And to pass by you into Macedonia, and to come again out of Macedonia unto you, and of you to be brought on my way toward Judaea.

ours: But as God is true, our word toward you was not yea and nay.
theirs: But [as] God [is] true, our word toward you was not yea and nay.

ours: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us, even by me and Silvanus and Timotheus, was not yea and nay, but in him was yea.
theirs: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us, [even] by me and Silvanus and Timotheus, was not yea and nay, but in him was yea.

ours: For all the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen, unto the glory of God by us.
theirs: For all the promises of God in him [are] yea, and in him Amen, unto the glory of God by us.

ours: Now he which stablisheth us with you in Christ, and hath anointed us, is God;
theirs: Now he which stablisheth us with you in Christ, and hath anointed us, [is] God;

ours: And I wrote this same unto you, lest, when I came, I should have sorrow from them of whom I ought to rejoice; having confidence in you all, that my joy is the joy of you all.
theirs: And I wrote this same unto you, lest, when I came, I should have sorrow from them of whom I ought to rejoice; having confidence in you all, that my joy is [the joy] of you all.

ours: Sufficient to such a man is this punishment, which was inflicted of many.
theirs: Sufficient to such a man [is] this punishment, which [was inflicted] of many.

ours: So that contrariwise ye ought rather to forgive him, and comfort him, lest perhaps such a one should be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow.
theirs: So that contrariwise ye [ought] rather to forgive [him], and comfort [him], lest perhaps such a one should be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow.

ours: Wherefore I beseech you that ye would confirm your love toward him.
theirs: Wherefore I beseech you that ye would confirm [your] love toward him.

ours: To whom ye forgive any thing, I forgive also: for if I forgave any thing, to whom I forgave it, for your sakes forgave I it in the person of Christ;
theirs: To whom ye forgive any thing, I [forgive] also: for if I forgave any thing, to whom I forgave [it], for your sakes [forgave I it] in the person of Christ;

ours: Furthermore, when I came to Troas to preach Christs gospel, and a door was opened unto me of the Lord,
theirs: Furthermore, when I came to Troas to [preach] Christ's gospel, and a door was opened unto me of the Lord,

ours: Now thanks be unto God, which always causeth us to triumph in Christ, and maketh manifest the savour of his knowledge by us in every place.
theirs: Now thanks [be] unto God, which always causeth us to triumph in Christ, and maketh manifest the savour of his knowledge by us in every place.

ours: To the one we are the savour of death unto death; and to the other the savour of life unto life. And who is sufficient for these things?
theirs: To the one [we are] the savour of death unto death; and to the other the savour of life unto life. And who [is] sufficient for these things?

ours: DO we begin again to commend ourselves? or need we, as some others, epistles of commendation to you, or letters of commendation from you?
theirs: Do we begin again to commend ourselves? or need we, as some [others], epistles of commendation to you, or [letters] of commendation from you?

ours: Forasmuch as ye are manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ ministered by us, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not in tables of stone, but in fleshy tables of the heart.
theirs: [Forasmuch as ye are] manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ ministered by us, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not in tables of stone, but in fleshy tables of the heart.

ours: Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think any thing as of ourselves; but our sufficiency is of God;
theirs: Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think any thing as of ourselves; but our sufficiency [is] of God;

ours: But if the ministration of death, written and engraven in stones, was glorious, so that the children of Israel could not stedfastly behold the face of Moses for the glory of his countenance; which glory was to be done away:
theirs: But if the ministration of death, written [and] engraven in stones, was glorious, so that the children of Israel could not stedfastly behold the face of Moses for the glory of his countenance; which [glory] was to be done away:

ours: For if the ministration of condemnation be glory, much more doth the ministration of righteousness exceed in glory.
theirs: For if the ministration of condemnation [be] glory, much more doth the ministration of righteousness exceed in glory.

ours: For if that which is done away was glorious, much more that which remaineth is glorious.
theirs: For if that which is done away [was] glorious, much more that which remaineth [is] glorious.

ours: And not as Moses, which put a vail over his face, that the children of Israel could not stedfastly look to the end of that which is abolished:
theirs: And not as Moses, [which] put a vail over his face, that the children of Israel could not stedfastly look to the end of that which is abolished:

ours: But their minds were blinded: for until this day remaineth the same vail untaken away in the reading of the old testament; which vail is done away in Christ.
theirs: But their minds were blinded: for until this day remaineth the same vail untaken away in the reading of the old testament; which [vail] is done away in Christ.

ours: Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.
theirs: Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord [is], there [is] liberty.

ours: But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord.
theirs: But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, [even] as by the Spirit of the Lord.

ours: But have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully; but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every mans conscience in the sight of God.
theirs: But have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully; but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man's conscience in the sight of God.

ours: For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus sake.
theirs: For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake.

ours: For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
theirs: For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to [give] the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.

ours: We are troubled on every side, yet not distressed; we are perplexed, but not in despair;
theirs: [We are] troubled on every side, yet not distressed; [we are] perplexed, but not in despair;

ours: For we which live are alway delivered unto death for Jesus sake, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our mortal flesh.
theirs: For we which live are alway delivered unto death for Jesus' sake, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our mortal flesh.

ours: Knowing that he which raised up the Lord Jesus shall raise up us also by Jesus, and shall present us with you.
theirs: Knowing that he which raised up the Lord Jesus shall raise up us also by Jesus, and shall present [us] with you.

ours: For all things are for your sakes, that the abundant grace might through the thanksgiving of many redound to the glory of God.
theirs: For all things [are] for your sakes, that the abundant grace might through the thanksgiving of many redound to the glory of God.

ours: For which cause we faint not; but though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day.
theirs: For which cause we faint not; but though our outward man perish, yet the inward [man] is renewed day by day.

ours: For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory;
theirs: For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding [and] eternal weight of glory;

ours: While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal.
theirs: While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen [are] temporal; but the things which are not seen [are] eternal.

ours: FOR we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.
theirs: For we know that if our earthly house of [this] tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.

ours: For we that are in this tabernacle do groan, being burdened: not for that we would be unclothed, but clothed upon, that mortality might be swallowed up of life.
theirs: For we that are in [this] tabernacle do groan, being burdened: not for that we would be unclothed, but clothed upon, that mortality might be swallowed up of life.

ours: Now he that hath wrought us for the selfsame thing is God, who also hath given unto us the earnest of the Spirit.
theirs: Now he that hath wrought us for the selfsame thing [is] God, who also hath given unto us the earnest of the Spirit.

ours: Therefore we are always confident, knowing that, whilst we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord:
theirs: Therefore [we are] always confident, knowing that, whilst we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord:

ours: We are confident, I say, and willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be present with the Lord.
theirs: We are confident, [I say], and willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be present with the Lord.

ours: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad.
theirs: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things [done] in [his] body, according to that he hath done, whether [it be] good or bad.

ours: For we commend not ourselves again unto you, but give you occasion to glory on our behalf, that ye may have somewhat to answer them which glory in appearance, and not in heart.
theirs: For we commend not ourselves again unto you, but give you occasion to glory on our behalf, that ye may have somewhat to [answer] them which glory in appearance, and not in heart.

ours: For whether we be beside ourselves, it is to God: or whether we be sober, it is for your cause.
theirs: For whether we be beside ourselves, [it is] to God: or whether we be sober, [it is] for your cause.

ours: And that he died for all, that they which live should not henceforth live unto themselves, but unto him which died for them, and rose again.
theirs: And [that] he died for all, that they which live should not henceforth live unto themselves, but unto him which died for them, and rose again.

ours: Wherefore henceforth know we no man after the flesh: yea, though we have known Christ after the flesh, yet now henceforth know we him no more.
theirs: Wherefore henceforth know we no man after the flesh: yea, though we have known Christ after the flesh, yet now henceforth know we [him] no more.

ours: Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.
theirs: Therefore if any man [be] in Christ, [he is] a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.

ours: And all things are of God, who hath reconciled us to himself by Jesus Christ, and hath given to us the ministry of reconciliation;
theirs: And all things [are] of God, who hath reconciled us to himself by Jesus Christ, and hath given to us the ministry of reconciliation;

ours: Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us: we pray you in Christs stead, be ye reconciled to God.
theirs: Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech [you] by us: we pray [you] in Christ's stead, be ye reconciled to God.

ours: For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.
theirs: For he hath made him [to be] sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.

ours: WE then, as workers together with him, beseech you also that ye receive not the grace of God in vain.
theirs: We then, [as] workers together [with him], beseech [you] also that ye receive not the grace of God in vain.

ours: (For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.)
theirs: (For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now [is] the accepted time; behold, now [is] the day of salvation.)

ours: But in all things approving ourselves as the ministers of God, in much patience, in afflictions, in necessities, in distresses,
theirs: But in all [things] approving ourselves as the ministers of God, in much patience, in afflictions, in necessities, in distresses,

ours: By honour and dishonour, by evil report and good report: as deceivers, and yet true;
theirs: By honour and dishonour, by evil report and good report: as deceivers, and [yet] true;

ours: As unknown, and yet well known; as dying, and, behold, we live; as chastened, and not killed;
theirs: As unknown, and [yet] well known; as dying, and, behold, we live; as chastened, and not killed;

ours: As sorrowful, yet alway rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing all things.
theirs: As sorrowful, yet alway rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and [yet] possessing all things.

ours: O ye Corinthians, our mouth is open unto you, our heart is enlarged.
theirs: O [ye] Corinthians, our mouth is open unto you, our heart is enlarged.

ours: Now for a recompence in the same, (I speak as unto my children,) be ye also enlarged.
theirs: Now for a recompence in the same, (I speak as unto [my] children,) be ye also enlarged.

ours: And what agreement hath the temple of God with idols? for ye are the temple of the living God; as God hath said, I will dwell in them, and walk in them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
theirs: And what agreement hath the temple of God with idols? for ye are the temple of the living God; as God hath said, I will dwell in them, and walk in [them]; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

ours: Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you,
theirs: Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean [thing]; and I will receive you,

ours: I speak not this to condemn you: for I have said before, that ye are in our hearts to die and live with you.
theirs: I speak not [this] to condemn [you]: for I have said before, that ye are in our hearts to die and live with [you].

ours: Great is my boldness of speech toward you, great is my glorying of you: I am filled with comfort, I am exceeding joyful in all our tribulation.
theirs: Great [is] my boldness of speech toward you, great [is] my glorying of you: I am filled with comfort, I am exceeding joyful in all our tribulation.

ours: For, when we were come into Macedonia, our flesh had no rest, but we were troubled on every side; without were fightings, within were fears.
theirs: For, when we were come into Macedonia, our flesh had no rest, but we were troubled on every side; without [were] fightings, within [were] fears.

ours: For though I made you sorry with a letter, I do not repent, though I did repent: for I perceive that the same epistle hath made you sorry, though it were but for a season.
theirs: For though I made you sorry with a letter, I do not repent, though I did repent: for I perceive that the same epistle hath made you sorry, though [it were] but for a season.

ours: For behold this selfsame thing, that ye sorrowed after a godly sort, what carefulness it wrought in you, yea, what clearing of yourselves, yea, what indignation, yea, what fear, yea, what vehement desire, yea, what zeal, yea, what revenge! In all things ye have approved yourselves to be clear in this matter.
theirs: For behold this selfsame thing, that ye sorrowed after a godly sort, what carefulness it wrought in you, yea, [what] clearing of yourselves, yea, [what] indignation, yea, [what] fear, yea, [what] vehement desire, yea, [what] zeal, yea, [what] revenge! In all [things] ye have approved yourselves to be clear in this matter.

ours: Wherefore, though I wrote unto you, I did it not for his cause that had done the wrong, nor for his cause that suffered wrong, but that our care for you in the sight of God might appear unto you.
theirs: Wherefore, though I wrote unto you, [I did it] not for his cause that had done the wrong, nor for his cause that suffered wrong, but that our care for you in the sight of God might appear unto you.

ours: For if I have boasted any thing to him of you, I am not ashamed; but as we spake all things to you in truth, even so our boasting, which I made before Titus, is found a truth.
theirs: For if I have boasted any thing to him of you, I am not ashamed; but as we spake all things to you in truth, even so our boasting, which [I made] before Titus, is found a truth.

ours: I rejoice therefore that I have confidence in you in all things.
theirs: I rejoice therefore that I have confidence in you in all [things].

ours: For to their power, I bear record, yea, and beyond their power they were willing of themselves;
theirs: For to [their] power, I bear record, yea, and beyond [their] power [they were] willing of themselves;

ours: Praying us with much intreaty that we would receive the gift, and take upon us the fellowship of the ministering to the saints.
theirs: Praying us with much intreaty that we would receive the gift, and [take upon us] the fellowship of the ministering to the saints.

ours: And this they did, not as we hoped, but first gave their own selves to the Lord, and unto us by the will of God.
theirs: And [this they did], not as we hoped, but first gave their own selves to the Lord, and unto us by the will of God.

ours: Therefore, as ye abound in every thing, in faith, and utterance, and knowledge, and in all diligence, and in your love to us, see that ye abound in this grace also.
theirs: Therefore, as ye abound in every [thing, in] faith, and utterance, and knowledge, and [in] all diligence, and [in] your love to us, [see] that ye abound in this grace also.

ours: And herein I give my advice: for this is expedient for you, who have begun before, not only to do, but also to be forward a year ago.
theirs: And herein I give [my] advice: for this is expedient for you, who have begun before, not only to do, but also to be forward a year ago.

ours: Now therefore perform the doing of it; that as there was a readiness to will, so there may be a performance also out of that which ye have.
theirs: Now therefore perform the doing [of it]; that as [there was] a readiness to will, so [there may be] a performance also out of that which ye have.

ours: For if there be first a willing mind, it is accepted according to that a man hath, and not according to that he hath not.
theirs: For if there be first a willing mind, [it is] accepted according to that a man hath, [and] not according to that he hath not.

ours: For I mean not that other men be eased, and ye burdened:
theirs: For [I mean] not that other men be eased, and ye burdened:

ours: But by an equality, that now at this time your abundance may be a supply for their want, that their abundance also may be a supply for your want: that there may be equality:
theirs: But by an equality, [that] now at this time your abundance [may be a supply] for their want, that their abundance also may be [a supply] for your want: that there may be equality:

ours: As it is written, He that had gathered much had nothing over; and he that had gathered little had no lack.
theirs: As it is written, He that [had gathered] much had nothing over; and he that [had gathered] little had no lack.

ours: But thanks be to God, which put the same earnest care into the heart of Titus for you.
theirs: But thanks [be] to God, which put the same earnest care into the heart of Titus for you.

ours: And we have sent with him the brother, whose praise is in the gospel throughout all the churches;
theirs: And we have sent with him the brother, whose praise [is] in the gospel throughout all the churches;

ours: And not that only, but who was also chosen of the churches to travel with us with this grace, which is administered by us to the glory of the same Lord, and declaration of your ready mind:
theirs: And not [that] only, but who was also chosen of the churches to travel with us with this grace, which is administered by us to the glory of the same Lord, and [declaration of] your ready mind:

ours: And we have sent with them our brother, whom we have oftentimes proved diligent in many things, but now much more diligent, upon the great confidence which I have in you.
theirs: And we have sent with them our brother, whom we have oftentimes proved diligent in many things, but now much more diligent, upon the great confidence which [I have] in you.

ours: Whether any do inquire of Titus, he is my partner and fellowhelper concerning you: or our brethren be inquired of, they are the messengers of the churches, and the glory of Christ.
theirs: Whether [any do inquire] of Titus, [he is] my partner and fellowhelper concerning you: or our brethren [be inquired of, they are] the messengers of the churches, [and] the glory of Christ.

ours: Therefore I thought it necessary to exhort the brethren, that they would go before unto you, and make up beforehand your bounty, whereof ye had notice before, that the same might be ready, as a matter of bounty, and not as of covetousness.
theirs: Therefore I thought it necessary to exhort the brethren, that they would go before unto you, and make up beforehand your bounty, whereof ye had notice before, that the same might be ready, as [a matter of] bounty, and not as [of] covetousness.

ours: But this I say, He which soweth sparingly shall reap also sparingly; and he which soweth bountifully shall reap also bountifully.
theirs: But this [I say], He which soweth sparingly shall reap also sparingly; and he which soweth bountifully shall reap also bountifully.

ours: Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver.
theirs: Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, [so let him give]; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver.

ours: And God is able to make all grace abound toward you; that ye, always having all sufficiency in all things, may abound to every good work:
theirs: And God [is] able to make all grace abound toward you; that ye, always having all sufficiency in all [things], may abound to every good work:

ours: Now he that ministereth seed to the sower both minister bread for your food, and multiply your seed sown, and increase the fruits of your righteousness;)
theirs: Now he that ministereth seed to the sower both minister bread for [your] food, and multiply your seed sown, and increase the fruits of your righteousness;)

ours: Whiles by the experiment of this ministration they glorify God for your professed subjection unto the gospel of Christ, and for your liberal distribution unto them, and unto all men;
theirs: Whiles by the experiment of this ministration they glorify God for your professed subjection unto the gospel of Christ, and for [your] liberal distribution unto them, and unto all [men];

ours: Thanks be unto God for his unspeakable gift.
theirs: Thanks [be] unto God for his unspeakable gift.

ours: NOW I Paul myself beseech you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ, who in presence am base among you, but being absent am bold toward you:
theirs: Now I Paul myself beseech you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ, who in presence [am] base among you, but being absent am bold toward you:

ours: But I beseech you, that I may not be bold when I am present with that confidence, wherewith I think to be bold against some, which think of us as if we walked according to the flesh.
theirs: But I beseech [you], that I may not be bold when I am present with that confidence, wherewith I think to be bold against some, which think of us as if we walked according to the flesh.

ours: (For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds;)
theirs: (For the weapons of our warfare [are] not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds;)

ours: Do ye look on things after the outward appearance? If any man trust to himself that he is Christs, let him of himself think this again, that, as he is Christs, even so are we Christs.
theirs: Do ye look on things after the outward appearance? If any man trust to himself that he is Christ's, let him of himself think this again, that, as he [is] Christ's, even so [are] we Christ's.

ours: For his letters, say they, are weighty and powerful; but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech contemptible.
theirs: For [his] letters, say they, [are] weighty and powerful; but [his] bodily presence [is] weak, and [his] speech contemptible.

ours: Let such an one think this, that, such as we are in word by letters when we are absent, such will we be also in deed when we are present.
theirs: Let such an one think this, that, such as we are in word by letters when we are absent, such [will we be] also in deed when we are present.

ours: But we will not boast of things without our measure, but according to the measure of the rule which God hath distributed to us, a measure to reach even unto you.
theirs: But we will not boast of things without [our] measure, but according to the measure of the rule which God hath distributed to us, a measure to reach even unto you.

ours: For we stretch not ourselves beyond our measure, as though we reached not unto you: for we are come as far as to you also in preaching the gospel of Christ:
theirs: For we stretch not ourselves beyond [our measure], as though we reached not unto you: for we are come as far as to you also in [preaching] the gospel of Christ:

ours: Not boasting of things without our measure, that is, of other mens labours; but having hope, when your faith is increased, that we shall be enlarged by you according to our rule abundantly,
theirs: Not boasting of things without [our] measure, [that is], of other men's labours; but having hope, when your faith is increased, that we shall be enlarged by you according to our rule abundantly,

ours: To preach the gospel in the regions beyond you, and not to boast in another mans line of things made ready to our hand.
theirs: To preach the gospel in the [regions] beyond you, [and] not to boast in another man's line of things made ready to our hand.

ours: WOULD to God ye could bear with me a little in my folly: and indeed bear with me.
theirs: Would to God ye could bear with me a little in [my] folly: and indeed bear with me.

ours: For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.
theirs: For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present [you as] a chaste virgin to Christ.

ours: For if he that cometh preacheth another Jesus, whom we have not preached, or if ye receive another spirit, which ye have not received, or another gospel, which ye have not accepted, ye might well bear with him.
theirs: For if he that cometh preacheth another Jesus, whom we have not preached, or [if] ye receive another spirit, which ye have not received, or another gospel, which ye have not accepted, ye might well bear with [him].

ours: But though I be rude in speech, yet not in knowledge; but we have been throughly made manifest among you in all things.
theirs: But though [I be] rude in speech, yet not in knowledge; but we have been throughly made manifest among you in all things.

ours: I robbed other churches, taking wages of them, to do you service.
theirs: I robbed other churches, taking wages [of them], to do you service.

ours: And when I was present with you, and wanted, I was chargeable to no man: for that which was lacking to me the brethren which came from Macedonia supplied: and in all things I have kept myself from being burdensome unto you, and so will I keep myself.
theirs: And when I was present with you, and wanted, I was chargeable to no man: for that which was lacking to me the brethren which came from Macedonia supplied: and in all [things] I have kept myself from being burdensome unto you, and [so] will I keep [myself].

ours: For such are false apostles, deceitful workers, transforming themselves into the apostles of Christ.
theirs: For such [are] false apostles, deceitful workers, transforming themselves into the apostles of Christ.

ours: Therefore it is no great thing if his ministers also be transformed as the ministers of righteousness; whose end shall be according to their works.
theirs: Therefore [it is] no great thing if his ministers also be transformed as the ministers of righteousness; whose end shall be according to their works.

ours: That which I speak, I speak it not after the Lord, but as it were foolishly, in this confidence of boasting.
theirs: That which I speak, I speak [it] not after the Lord, but as it were foolishly, in this confidence of boasting.

ours: For ye suffer fools gladly, seeing ye yourselves are wise.
theirs: For ye suffer fools gladly, seeing ye [yourselves] are wise.

ours: For ye suffer, if a man bring you into bondage, if a man devour you, if a man take of you, if a man exalt himself, if a man smite you on the face.
theirs: For ye suffer, if a man bring you into bondage, if a man devour [you], if a man take [of you], if a man exalt himself, if a man smite you on the face.

ours: Are they Hebrews? so am I. Are they Israelites? so am I. Are they the seed of Abraham? so am I.
theirs: Are they Hebrews? so [am] I. Are they Israelites? so [am] I. Are they the seed of Abraham? so [am] I.

ours: Are they ministers of Christ? (I speak as a fool) I am more; in labours more abundant, in stripes above measure, in prisons more frequent, in deaths oft.
theirs: Are they ministers of Christ? (I speak as a fool) I [am] more; in labours more abundant, in stripes above measure, in prisons more frequent, in deaths oft.

ours: Of the Jews five times received I forty stripes save one.
theirs: Of the Jews five times received I forty [stripes] save one.

ours: In journeyings often, in perils of waters, in perils of robbers, in perils by mine own countrymen, in perils by the heathen, in perils in the city, in perils in the wilderness, in perils in the sea, in perils among false brethren;
theirs: [In] journeyings often, [in] perils of waters, [in] perils of robbers, [in] perils by [mine own] countrymen, [in] perils by the heathen, [in] perils in the city, [in] perils in the wilderness, [in] perils in the sea, [in] perils among false brethren;

ours: For though I would desire to glory, I shall not be a fool; for I will say the truth: but now I forbear, lest any man should think of me above that which he seeth me to be, or that he heareth of me.
theirs: For though I would desire to glory, I shall not be a fool; for I will say the truth: but [now] I forbear, lest any man should think of me above that which he seeth me [to be], or [that] he heareth of me.

ours: Therefore I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christs sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong.
theirs: Therefore I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ's sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong.

ours: For what is it wherein ye were inferior to other churches, except it be that I myself was not burdensome to you? forgive me this wrong.
theirs: For what is it wherein ye were inferior to other churches, except [it be] that I myself was not burdensome to you? forgive me this wrong.

ours: I desired Titus, and with him I sent a brother. Did Titus make a gain of you? walked we not in the same spirit? walked we not in the same steps?
theirs: I desired Titus, and with [him] I sent a brother. Did Titus make a gain of you? walked we not in the same spirit? [walked we] not in the same steps?

ours: Again, think ye that we excuse ourselves unto you? we speak before God in Christ: but we do all things, dearly beloved, for your edifying.
theirs: Again, think ye that we excuse ourselves unto you? we speak before God in Christ: but [we do] all things, dearly beloved, for your edifying.

ours: For I fear, lest, when I come, I shall not find you such as I would, and that I shall be found unto you such as ye would not: lest there be debates, envyings, wraths, strifes, backbitings, whisperings, swellings, tumults:
theirs: For I fear, lest, when I come, I shall not find you such as I would, and [that] I shall be found unto you such as ye would not: lest [there be] debates, envyings, wraths, strifes, backbitings, whisperings, swellings, tumults:

ours: And lest, when I come again, my God will humble me among you, and that I shall bewail many which have sinned already, and have not repented of the uncleanness and fornication and lasciviousness which they have committed.
theirs: [And] lest, when I come again, my God will humble me among you, and [that] I shall bewail many which have sinned already, and have not repented of the uncleanness and fornication and lasciviousness which they have committed.

ours: THIS is the third time I am coming to you. In the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established.
theirs: This [is] the third [time] I am coming to you. In the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established.

ours: For we are glad, when we are weak, and ye are strong: and this also we wish, even your perfection.
theirs: For we are glad, when we are weak, and ye are strong: and this also we wish, [even] your perfection.

ours: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Ghost, be with you all. Amen.
theirs: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Ghost, [be] with you all. Amen. <<[The second [epistle] to the Corinthians was written from Philippi, [a city] of Macedonia, by Titus and Lucas.]>>

ours: Grace be to you and peace from God the Father, and from our Lord Jesus Christ,
theirs: Grace [be] to you and peace from God the Father, and [from] our Lord Jesus Christ,

ours: To whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen.
theirs: To whom [be] glory for ever and ever. Amen.

ours: As we said before, so say I now again, If any man preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.
theirs: As we said before, so say I now again, If any [man] preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.

ours: For I neither received it of man, neither was I taught it, but by the revelation of Jesus Christ.
theirs: For I neither received it of man, neither was I taught [it], but by the revelation of Jesus Christ.

ours: For ye have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it:
theirs: For ye have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews' religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it:

ours: And profited in the Jews religion above many my equals in mine own nation, being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers.
theirs: And profited in the Jews' religion above many my equals in mine own nation, being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers.

ours: But when it pleased God, who separated me from my mothers womb, and called me by his grace,
theirs: But when it pleased God, who separated me from my mother's womb, and called [me] by his grace,

ours: But other of the apostles saw I none, save James the Lords brother.
theirs: But other of the apostles saw I none, save James the Lord's brother.

ours: And was unknown by face unto the churches of Judæa which were in Christ:
theirs: And was unknown by face unto the churches of Judaea which were in Christ:

ours: THEN fourteen years after I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, and took Titus with me also.
theirs: Then fourteen years after I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, and took Titus with [me] also.

ours: But of these who seemed to be somewhat, (whatsoever they were, it maketh no matter to me: God accepteth no mans person:) for they who seemed to be somewhat in conference added nothing to me:
theirs: But of these who seemed to be somewhat, (whatsoever they were, it maketh no matter to me: God accepteth no man's person:) for they who seemed [to be somewhat] in conference added nothing to me:

ours: But contrariwise, when they saw that the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter;
theirs: But contrariwise, when they saw that the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as [the gospel] of the circumcision [was] unto Peter;

ours: And when James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived the grace that was given unto me, they gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship; that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision.
theirs: And when James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived the grace that was given unto me, they gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship; that we [should go] unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision.

ours: Only they would that we should remember the poor; the same which I also was forward to do.
theirs: Only [they would] that we should remember the poor; the same which I also was forward to do.

ours: But when I saw that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, I said unto Peter before them all, If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews?
theirs: But when I saw that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, I said unto Peter before [them] all, If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews?

ours: We who are Jews by nature, and not sinners of the Gentiles,
theirs: We [who are] Jews by nature, and not sinners of the Gentiles,

ours: But if, while we seek to be justified by Christ, we ourselves also are found sinners, is therefore Christ the minister of sin? God forbid.
theirs: But if, while we seek to be justified by Christ, we ourselves also are found sinners, [is] therefore Christ the minister of sin? God forbid.

ours: I do not frustrate the grace of God: for if righteousness come by the law, then Christ is dead in vain.
theirs: I do not frustrate the grace of God: for if righteousness [come] by the law, then Christ is dead in vain.

ours: Have ye suffered so many things in vain? if it be yet in vain.
theirs: Have ye suffered so many things in vain? if [it be] yet in vain.

ours: He therefore that ministereth to you the Spirit, and worketh miracles among you, doeth he it by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?
theirs: He therefore that ministereth to you the Spirit, and worketh miracles among you, [doeth he it] by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?

ours: And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, saying, In thee shall all nations be blessed.
theirs: And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, [saying], In thee shall all nations be blessed.

ours: For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse: for it is written, Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them.
theirs: For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse: for it is written, Cursed [is] every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them.

ours: But that no man is justified by the law in the sight of God, it is evident: for, The just shall live by faith.
theirs: But that no man is justified by the law in the sight of God, [it is] evident: for, The just shall live by faith.

ours: Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree:
theirs: Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed [is] every one that hangeth on a tree:

ours: Brethren, I speak after the manner of men; Though it be but a mans covenant, yet if it be confirmed, no man disannulleth, or addeth thereto.
theirs: Brethren, I speak after the manner of men; Though [it be] but a man's covenant, yet [if it be] confirmed, no man disannulleth, or addeth thereto.

ours: And this I say, that the covenant, that was confirmed before of God in Christ, the law, which was four hundred and thirty years after, cannot disannul, that it should make the promise of none effect.
theirs: And this I say, [that] the covenant, that was confirmed before of God in Christ, the law, which was four hundred and thirty years after, cannot disannul, that it should make the promise of none effect.

ours: For if the inheritance be of the law, it is no more of promise: but God gave it to Abraham by promise.
theirs: For if the inheritance [be] of the law, [it is] no more of promise: but God gave [it] to Abraham by promise.

ours: Wherefore then serveth the law? It was added because of transgressions, till the seed should come to whom the promise was made; and it was ordained by angels in the hand of a mediator.
theirs: Wherefore then [serveth] the law? It was added because of transgressions, till the seed should come to whom the promise was made; [and it was] ordained by angels in the hand of a mediator.

ours: Now a mediator is not a mediator of one, but God is one.
theirs: Now a mediator is not [a mediator] of one, but God is one.

ours: Is the law then against the promises of God? God forbid: for if there had been a law given which could have given life, verily righteousness should have been by the law.
theirs: [Is] the law then against the promises of God? God forbid: for if there had been a law given which could have given life, verily righteousness should have been by the law.

ours: Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith.
theirs: Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster [to bring us] unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith.

ours: And if ye be Christs, then are ye Abrahams seed, and heirs according to the promise.
theirs: And if ye [be] Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise.

ours: NOW I say, That the heir, as long as he is a child, differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all;
theirs: Now I say, [That] the heir, as long as he is a child, differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all;

ours: Brethren, I beseech you, be as I am; for I am as ye are: ye have not injured me at all.
theirs: Brethren, I beseech you, be as I [am]; for I [am] as ye [are]: ye have not injured me at all.

ours: And my temptation which was in my flesh ye despised not, nor rejected; but received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus.
theirs: And my temptation which was in my flesh ye despised not, nor rejected; but received me as an angel of God, [even] as Christ Jesus.

ours: Where is then the blessedness ye spake of? for I bear you record, that, if it had been possible, ye would have plucked out your own eyes, and have given them to me.
theirs: Where is then the blessedness ye spake of? for I bear you record, that, if [it had been] possible, ye would have plucked out your own eyes, and have given them to me.

ours: They zealously affect you, but not well; yea, they would exclude you, that ye might affect them.
theirs: They zealously affect you, [but] not well; yea, they would exclude you, that ye might affect them.

ours: But it is good to be zealously affected always in a good thing, and not only when I am present with you.
theirs: But [it is] good to be zealously affected always in [a] good [thing], and not only when I am present with you.

ours: But he who was of the bondwoman was born after the flesh; but he of the freewoman was by promise.
theirs: But he [who was] of the bondwoman was born after the flesh; but he of the freewoman [was] by promise.

ours: For it is written, Rejoice, thou barren that bearest not; break forth and cry, thou that travailest not: for the desolate hath many more children than she which hath an husband.
theirs: For it is written, Rejoice, [thou] barren that bearest not; break forth and cry, thou that travailest not: for the desolate hath many more children than she which hath an husband.

ours: But as then he that was born after the flesh persecuted him that was born after the Spirit, even so it is now.
theirs: But as then he that was born after the flesh persecuted him [that was born] after the Spirit, even so [it is] now.

ours: This persuasion cometh not of him that calleth you.
theirs: This persuasion [cometh] not of him that calleth you.

ours: For, brethren, ye have been called unto liberty; only use not liberty for an occasion to the flesh, but by love serve one another.
theirs: For, brethren, ye have been called unto liberty; only [use] not liberty for an occasion to the flesh, but by love serve one another.

ours: For all the law is fulfilled in one word, even in this; Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.
theirs: For all the law is fulfilled in one word, [even] in this; Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.

ours: This I say then, Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.
theirs: [This] I say then, Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.

ours: Now the works of the flesh are manifest, which are these; Adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lasciviousness,
theirs: Now the works of the flesh are manifest, which are [these]; Adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lasciviousness,

ours: Envyings, murders, drunkenness, revellings, and such like: of the which I tell you before, as I have also told you in time past, that they which do such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God.
theirs: Envyings, murders, drunkenness, revellings, and such like: of the which I tell you before, as I have also told [you] in time past, that they which do such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God.

ours: And they that are Christs have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts.
theirs: And they that are Christ's have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts.

ours: Bear ye one anothers burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.
theirs: Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.

ours: As we have therefore opportunity, let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith.
theirs: As we have therefore opportunity, let us do good unto all [men], especially unto them who are of the household of faith.

ours: And as many as walk according to this rule, peace be on them, and mercy, and upon the Israel of God.
theirs: And as many as walk according to this rule, peace [be] on them, and mercy, and upon the Israel of God.

ours: Brethren, the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
theirs: Brethren, the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] with your spirit. Amen. <<[Unto the Galatians written from Rome.]>>

ours: Grace be to you, and peace, from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
theirs: Grace [be] to you, and peace, from God our Father, and [from] the Lord Jesus Christ.

ours: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ:
theirs: Blessed [be] the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly [places] in Christ:

ours: That in the dispensation of the fulness of times he might gather together in one all things in Christ, both which are in heaven, and which are on earth; even in him:
theirs: That in the dispensation of the fulness of times he might gather together in one all things in Christ, both which are in heaven, and which are on earth; [even] in him:

ours: In whom ye also trusted, after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise,
theirs: In whom ye also [trusted], after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise,

ours: And what is the exceeding greatness of his power to us-ward who believe, according to the working of his mighty power,
theirs: And what [is] the exceeding greatness of his power to us-ward who believe, according to the working of his mighty power,

ours: Which he wrought in Christ, when he raised him from the dead, and set him at his own right hand in the heavenly places,
theirs: Which he wrought in Christ, when he raised him from the dead, and set [him] at his own right hand in the heavenly [places],

ours: And hath put all things under his feet, and gave him to be the head over all things to the church,
theirs: And hath put all [things] under his feet, and gave him [to be] the head over all [things] to the church,

ours: AND you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins;
theirs: And you [hath he quickened], who were dead in trespasses and sins;

ours: And hath raised us up together, and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus:
theirs: And hath raised [us] up together, and made [us] sit together in heavenly [places] in Christ Jesus:

ours: That in the ages to come he might shew the exceeding riches of his grace in his kindness toward us through Christ Jesus.
theirs: That in the ages to come he might shew the exceeding riches of his grace in [his] kindness toward us through Christ Jesus.

ours: For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God:
theirs: For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: [it is] the gift of God:

ours: Wherefore remember, that ye being in time past Gentiles in the flesh, who are called Uncircumcision by that which is called the Circumcision in the flesh made by hands;
theirs: Wherefore remember, that ye [being] in time past Gentiles in the flesh, who are called Uncircumcision by that which is called the Circumcision in the flesh made by hands;

ours: For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us;
theirs: For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition [between us];

ours: Having abolished in his flesh the enmity, even the law of commandments contained in ordinances; for to make in himself of twain one new man, so making peace;
theirs: Having abolished in his flesh the enmity, [even] the law of commandments [contained] in ordinances; for to make in himself of twain one new man, [so] making peace;

ours: And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone;
theirs: And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner [stone];

ours: And to make all men see what is the fellowship of the mystery, which from the beginning of the world hath been hid in God, who created all things by Jesus Christ:
theirs: And to make all [men] see what [is] the fellowship of the mystery, which from the beginning of the world hath been hid in God, who created all things by Jesus Christ:

ours: To the intent that now unto the principalities and powers in heavenly places might be known by the church the manifold wisdom of God,
theirs: To the intent that now unto the principalities and powers in heavenly [places] might be known by the church the manifold wisdom of God,

ours: May be able to comprehend with all saints what is the breadth, and length, and depth, and height;
theirs: May be able to comprehend with all saints what [is] the breadth, and length, and depth, and height;

ours: Unto him be glory in the church by Christ Jesus throughout all ages, world without end. Amen.
theirs: Unto him [be] glory in the church by Christ Jesus throughout all ages, world without end. Amen.

ours: There is one body, and one Spirit, even as ye are called in one hope of your calling;
theirs: [There is] one body, and one Spirit, even as ye are called in one hope of your calling;

ours: One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all.
theirs: One God and Father of all, who [is] above all, and through all, and in you all.

ours: That we henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men, and cunning craftiness, whereby they lie in wait to deceive;
theirs: That we [henceforth] be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men, [and] cunning craftiness, whereby they lie in wait to deceive;

ours: But speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ:
theirs: But speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things, which is the head, [even] Christ:

ours: Let him that stole steal no more: but rather let him labour, working with his hands the thing which is good, that he may have to give to him that needeth.
theirs: Let him that stole steal no more: but rather let him labour, working with [his] hands the thing which is good, that he may have to give to him that needeth.

ours: And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christs sake hath forgiven you.
theirs: And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you.

ours: For ye were sometimes darkness, but now are ye light in the Lord: walk as children of light:
theirs: For ye were sometimes darkness, but now [are ye] light in the Lord: walk as children of light:

ours: (For the fruit of the Spirit is in all goodness and righteousness and truth;)
theirs: (For the fruit of the Spirit [is] in all goodness and righteousness and truth;)

ours: And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove them.
theirs: And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove [them].

ours: Wherefore be ye not unwise, but understanding what the will of the Lord is.
theirs: Wherefore be ye not unwise, but understanding what the will of the Lord [is].

ours: Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing.
theirs: Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so [let] the wives [be] to their own husbands in every thing.

ours: Nevertheless let every one of you in particular so love his wife even as himself; and the wife see that she reverence her husband.
theirs: Nevertheless let every one of you in particular so love his wife even as himself; and the wife [see] that she reverence [her] husband.

ours: Servants, be obedient to them that are your masters according to the flesh, with fear and trembling, in singleness of your heart, as unto Christ;
theirs: Servants, be obedient to them that are [your] masters according to the flesh, with fear and trembling, in singleness of your heart, as unto Christ;

ours: Knowing that whatsoever good thing any man doeth, the same shall he receive of the Lord, whether he be bond or free.
theirs: Knowing that whatsoever good thing any man doeth, the same shall he receive of the Lord, whether [he be] bond or free.

ours: For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.
theirs: For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high [places].

ours: But that ye also may know my affairs, and how I do, Tychicus, a beloved brother and faithful minister in the Lord, shall make known to you all things:
theirs: But that ye also may know my affairs, [and] how I do, Tychicus, a beloved brother and faithful minister in the Lord, shall make known to you all things:

ours: Whom I have sent unto you for the same purpose, that ye might know our affairs, and that he might comfort your hearts.
theirs: Whom I have sent unto you for the same purpose, that ye might know our affairs, and [that] he might comfort your hearts.

ours: Peace be to the brethren, and love with faith, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
theirs: Peace [be] to the brethren, and love with faith, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

ours: Grace be with all them that love our Lord Jesus Christ in sincerity. Amen.
theirs: Grace [be] with all them that love our Lord Jesus Christ in sincerity. Amen. <<[Written from Rome unto the Ephesians by Tychicus.]>>

ours: Grace be unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
theirs: Grace [be] unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and [from] the Lord Jesus Christ.

ours: Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ:
theirs: Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform [it] until the day of Jesus Christ:

ours: And this I pray, that your love may abound yet more and more in knowledge and in all judgment;
theirs: And this I pray, that your love may abound yet more and more in knowledge and [in] all judgment;

ours: But I would ye should understand, brethren, that the things which happened unto me have fallen out rather unto the furtherance of the gospel;
theirs: But I would ye should understand, brethren, that the things [which happened] unto me have fallen out rather unto the furtherance of the gospel;

ours: So that my bonds in Christ are manifest in all the palace, and in all other places;
theirs: So that my bonds in Christ are manifest in all the palace, and in all other [places];
