ours: According to my earnest expectation and my hope, that in nothing I shall be ashamed, but that with all boldness, as always, so now also Christ shall be magnified in my body, whether it be by life, or by death.
theirs: According to my earnest expectation and [my] hope, that in nothing I shall be ashamed, but [that] with all boldness, as always, [so] now also Christ shall be magnified in my body, whether [it be] by life, or by death.

ours: For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
theirs: For to me to live [is] Christ, and to die [is] gain.

ours: But if I live in the flesh, this is the fruit of my labour: yet what I shall choose I wot not.
theirs: But if I live in the flesh, this [is] the fruit of my labour: yet what I shall choose I wot not.

ours: Nevertheless to abide in the flesh is more needful for you.
theirs: Nevertheless to abide in the flesh [is] more needful for you.

ours: Having the same conflict which ye saw in me, and now hear to be in me.
theirs: Having the same conflict which ye saw in me, and now hear [to be] in me.

ours: IF there be therefore any consolation in Christ, if any comfort of love, if any fellowship of the Spirit, if any bowels and mercies,
theirs: If [there be] therefore any consolation in Christ, if any comfort of love, if any fellowship of the Spirit, if any bowels and mercies,

ours: Fulfil ye my joy, that ye be likeminded, having the same love, being of one accord, of one mind.
theirs: Fulfil ye my joy, that ye be likeminded, having the same love, [being] of one accord, of one mind.

ours: Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.
theirs: [Let] nothing [be done] through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.

ours: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth;
theirs: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of [things] in heaven, and [things] in earth, and [things] under the earth;

ours: And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
theirs: And [that] every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ [is] Lord, to the glory of God the Father.

ours: For it is God which worketh in you both to will and to do of his good pleasure.
theirs: For it is God which worketh in you both to will and to do of [his] good pleasure.

ours: For all seek their own, not the things which are Jesus Christs.
theirs: For all seek their own, not the things which are Jesus Christ's.

ours: FINALLY, my brethren, rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things to you, to me indeed is not grievous, but for you it is safe.
theirs: Finally, my brethren, rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things to you, to me indeed [is] not grievous, but for you [it is] safe.

ours: Circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, an Hebrew of the Hebrews; as touching the law, a Pharisee;
theirs: Circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, [of] the tribe of Benjamin, an Hebrew of the Hebrews; as touching the law, a Pharisee;

ours: Yea doubtless, and I count all things but loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord: for whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and do count them but dung, that I may win Christ,
theirs: Yea doubtless, and I count all things [but] loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord: for whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and do count them [but] dung, that I may win Christ,

ours: Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before,
theirs: Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but [this] one thing [I do], forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before,

ours: (For many walk, of whom I have told you often, and now tell you even weeping, that they are the enemies of the cross of Christ:
theirs: (For many walk, of whom I have told you often, and now tell you even weeping, [that they are] the enemies of the cross of Christ:

ours: Whose end is destruction, whose God is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things.)
theirs: Whose end [is] destruction, whose God [is their] belly, and [whose] glory [is] in their shame, who mind earthly things.)

ours: THEREFORE, my brethren dearly beloved and longed for, my joy and crown, so stand fast in the Lord, my dearly beloved.
theirs: Therefore, my brethren dearly beloved and longed for, my joy and crown, so stand fast in the Lord, [my] dearly beloved.

ours: And I intreat thee also, true yokefellow, help those women which laboured with me in the gospel, with Clement also, and with other my fellowlabourers, whose names are in the book of life.
theirs: And I intreat thee also, true yokefellow, help those women which laboured with me in the gospel, with Clement also, and [with] other my fellowlabourers, whose names [are] in the book of life.

ours: Rejoice in the Lord alway: and again I say, Rejoice.
theirs: Rejoice in the Lord alway: [and] again I say, Rejoice.

ours: Let your moderation be known unto all men. The Lord is at hand.
theirs: Let your moderation be known unto all men. The Lord [is] at hand.

ours: Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things.
theirs: Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things [are] honest, whatsoever things [are] just, whatsoever things [are] pure, whatsoever things [are] lovely, whatsoever things [are] of good report; if [there be] any virtue, and if [there be] any praise, think on these things.

ours: Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.
theirs: Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, [therewith] to be content.

ours: But I have all, and abound: I am full, having received of Epaphroditus the things which were sent from you, an odour of a sweet smell, a sacrifice acceptable, wellpleasing to God.
theirs: But I have all, and abound: I am full, having received of Epaphroditus the things [which were sent] from you, an odour of a sweet smell, a sacrifice acceptable, wellpleasing to God.

ours: Now unto God and our Father be glory for ever and ever. Amen.
theirs: Now unto God and our Father [be] glory for ever and ever. Amen.

ours: All the saints salute you, chiefly they that are of Cæsars household.
theirs: All the saints salute you, chiefly they that are of Caesar's household.

ours: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
theirs: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] with you all. Amen. <<[It was written to the Philippians from Rome by Epaphroditus.]>>

ours: PAUL, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timotheus our brother,
theirs: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timotheus [our] brother,

ours: To the saints and faithful brethren in Christ which are at Colosse: Grace be unto you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
theirs: To the saints and faithful brethren in Christ which are at Colosse: Grace [be] unto you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

ours: Since we heard of your faith in Christ Jesus, and of the love which ye have to all the saints,
theirs: Since we heard of your faith in Christ Jesus, and of the love [which ye have] to all the saints,

ours: Which is come unto you, as it is in all the world; and bringeth forth fruit, as it doth also in you, since the day ye heard of it, and knew the grace of God in truth:
theirs: Which is come unto you, as [it is] in all the world; and bringeth forth fruit, as [it doth] also in you, since the day ye heard [of it], and knew the grace of God in truth:

ours: For this cause we also, since the day we heard it, do not cease to pray for you, and to desire that ye might be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding;
theirs: For this cause we also, since the day we heard [it], do not cease to pray for you, and to desire that ye might be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding;

ours: Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of his dear Son:
theirs: Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated [us] into the kingdom of his dear Son:

ours: In whom we have redemption through his blood, even the forgiveness of sins:
theirs: In whom we have redemption through his blood, [even] the forgiveness of sins:

ours: For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him:
theirs: For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether [they be] thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him:

ours: And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence.
theirs: And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all [things] he might have the preeminence.

ours: For it pleased the Father that in him should all fulness dwell;
theirs: For it pleased [the Father] that in him should all fulness dwell;

ours: And, having made peace through the blood of his cross, by him to reconcile all things unto himself; by him, I say, whether they be things in earth, or things in heaven.
theirs: And, having made peace through the blood of his cross, by him to reconcile all things unto himself; by him, [I say], whether [they be] things in earth, or things in heaven.

ours: And you, that were sometime alienated and enemies in your mind by wicked works, yet now hath he reconciled
theirs: And you, that were sometime alienated and enemies in [your] mind by wicked works, yet now hath he reconciled

ours: If ye continue in the faith grounded and settled, and be not moved away from the hope of the gospel, which ye have heard, and which was preached to every creature which is under heaven; whereof I Paul am made a minister;
theirs: If ye continue in the faith grounded and settled, and [be] not moved away from the hope of the gospel, which ye have heard, [and] which was preached to every creature which is under heaven; whereof I Paul am made a minister;

ours: Who now rejoice in my sufferings for you, and fill up that which is behind of the afflictions of Christ in my flesh for his bodys sake, which is the church:
theirs: Who now rejoice in my sufferings for you, and fill up that which is behind of the afflictions of Christ in my flesh for his body's sake, which is the church:

ours: Even the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints:
theirs: [Even] the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints:

ours: To whom God would make known what is the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles; which is Christ in you, the hope of glory:
theirs: To whom God would make known what [is] the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles; which is Christ in you, the hope of glory:

ours: FOR I would that ye knew what great conflict I have for you, and for them at Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh;
theirs: For I would that ye knew what great conflict I have for you, and [for] them at Laodicea, and [for] as many as have not seen my face in the flesh;

ours: As ye have therefore received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk ye in him:
theirs: As ye have therefore received Christ Jesus the Lord, [so] walk ye in him:

ours: Buried with him in baptism, wherein also ye are risen with him through the faith of the operation of God, who hath raised him from the dead.
theirs: Buried with him in baptism, wherein also ye are risen with [him] through the faith of the operation of God, who hath raised him from the dead.

ours: And having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it.
theirs: [And] having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it.

ours: Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days:
theirs: Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath [days]:

ours: Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.
theirs: Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body [is] of Christ.

ours: When Christ, who is our life, shall appear, then shall ye also appear with him in glory.
theirs: When Christ, [who is] our life, shall appear, then shall ye also appear with him in glory.

ours: For which things sake the wrath of God cometh on the children of disobedience:
theirs: For which things' sake the wrath of God cometh on the children of disobedience:

ours: And have put on the new man, which is renewed in knowledge after the image of him that created him:
theirs: And have put on the new [man], which is renewed in knowledge after the image of him that created him:

ours: Where there is neither Greek nor Jew, circumcision nor uncircumcision, Barbarian, Scythian, bond nor free: but Christ is all, and in all.
theirs: Where there is neither Greek nor Jew, circumcision nor uncircumcision, Barbarian, Scythian, bond [nor] free: but Christ [is] all, and in all.

ours: Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.
theirs: Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also [do] ye.

ours: And above all these things put on charity, which is the bond of perfectness.
theirs: And above all these things [put on] charity, which is the bond of perfectness.

ours: And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.
theirs: And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, [do] all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.

ours: Husbands, love your wives, and be not bitter against them.
theirs: Husbands, love [your] wives, and be not bitter against them.

ours: Children, obey your parents in all things: for this is well pleasing unto the Lord.
theirs: Children, obey [your] parents in all things: for this is well pleasing unto the Lord.

ours: Fathers, provoke not your children to anger, lest they be discouraged.
theirs: Fathers, provoke not your children [to anger], lest they be discouraged.

ours: Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh; not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but in singleness of heart, fearing God:
theirs: Servants, obey in all things [your] masters according to the flesh; not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but in singleness of heart, fearing God:

ours: And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men;
theirs: And whatsoever ye do, do [it] heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men;

ours: MASTERS, give unto your servants that which is just and equal; knowing that ye also have a Master in heaven.
theirs: Masters, give unto [your] servants that which is just and equal; knowing that ye also have a Master in heaven.

ours: Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man.
theirs: Let your speech [be] alway with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man.

ours: All my state shall Tychicus declare unto you, who is a beloved brother, and a faithful minister and fellowservant in the Lord:
theirs: All my state shall Tychicus declare unto you, [who is] a beloved brother, and a faithful minister and fellowservant in the Lord:

ours: With Onesimus, a faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They shall make known unto you all things which are done here.
theirs: With Onesimus, a faithful and beloved brother, who is [one] of you. They shall make known unto you all things which [are done] here.

ours: Aristarchus my fellowprisoner saluteth you, and Marcus, sisters son to Barnabas, (touching whom ye received commandments: if he come unto you, receive him;)
theirs: Aristarchus my fellowprisoner saluteth you, and Marcus, sister's son to Barnabas, (touching whom ye received commandments: if he come unto you, receive him;)

ours: And Jesus, which is called Justus, who are of the circumcision. These only are my fellowworkers unto the kingdom of God, which have been a comfort unto me.
theirs: And Jesus, which is called Justus, who are of the circumcision. These only [are my] fellowworkers unto the kingdom of God, which have been a comfort unto me.

ours: Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ, saluteth you, always labouring fervently for you in prayers, that ye may stand perfect and complete in all the will of God.
theirs: Epaphras, who is [one] of you, a servant of Christ, saluteth you, always labouring fervently for you in prayers, that ye may stand perfect and complete in all the will of God.

ours: For I bear him record, that he hath a great zeal for you, and them that are in Laodicea, and them in Hierapolis.
theirs: For I bear him record, that he hath a great zeal for you, and them [that are] in Laodicea, and them in Hierapolis.

ours: And when this epistle is read among you, cause that it be read also in the church of the Laodiceans; and that ye likewise read the epistle from Laodicea.
theirs: And when this epistle is read among you, cause that it be read also in the church of the Laodiceans; and that ye likewise read the [epistle] from Laodicea.

ours: The salutation by the hand of me Paul. Remember my bonds. Grace be with you. Amen.
theirs: The salutation by the hand of me Paul. Remember my bonds. Grace [be] with you. Amen. <<[Written from Rome to the Colossians by Tychicus and Onesimus.]>>

ours: PAUL, and Silvanus, and Timotheus, unto the church of the Thessalonians which is in God the Father and in the Lord Jesus Christ: Grace be unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
theirs: Paul, and Silvanus, and Timotheus, unto the church of the Thessalonians [which is] in God the Father and [in] the Lord Jesus Christ: Grace [be] unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.

ours: And to wait for his Son from heaven, whom he raised from the dead, even Jesus, which delivered us from the wrath to come.
theirs: And to wait for his Son from heaven, whom he raised from the dead, [even] Jesus, which delivered us from the wrath to come.

ours: For our exhortation was not of deceit, nor of uncleanness, nor in guile:
theirs: For our exhortation [was] not of deceit, nor of uncleanness, nor in guile:

ours: For neither at any time used we flattering words, as ye know, nor a cloke of covetousness; God is witness:
theirs: For neither at any time used we flattering words, as ye know, nor a cloke of covetousness; God [is] witness:

ours: Nor of men sought we glory, neither of you, nor yet of others, when we might have been burdensome, as the apostles of Christ.
theirs: Nor of men sought we glory, neither of you, nor [yet] of others, when we might have been burdensome, as the apostles of Christ.

ours: Ye are witnesses, and God also, how holily and justly and unblameably we behaved ourselves among you that believe:
theirs: Ye [are] witnesses, and God [also], how holily and justly and unblameably we behaved ourselves among you that believe:

ours: As ye know how we exhorted and comforted and charged every one of you, as a father doth his children,
theirs: As ye know how we exhorted and comforted and charged every one of you, as a father [doth] his children,

ours: For this cause also thank we God without ceasing, because, when ye received the word of God which ye heard of us, ye received it not as the word of men, but as it is in truth, the word of God, which effectually worketh also in you that believe.
theirs: For this cause also thank we God without ceasing, because, when ye received the word of God which ye heard of us, ye received [it] not [as] the word of men, but as it is in truth, the word of God, which effectually worketh also in you that believe.

ours: For ye, brethren, became followers of the churches of God which in Judæa are in Christ Jesus: for ye also have suffered like things of your own countrymen, even as they have of the Jews:
theirs: For ye, brethren, became followers of the churches of God which in Judaea are in Christ Jesus: for ye also have suffered like things of your own countrymen, even as they [have] of the Jews:

ours: For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of rejoicing? Are not even ye in the presence of our Lord Jesus Christ at his coming?
theirs: For what [is] our hope, or joy, or crown of rejoicing? [Are] not even ye in the presence of our Lord Jesus Christ at his coming?

ours: But now when Timotheus came from you unto us, and brought us good tidings of your faith and charity, and that ye have good remembrance of us always, desiring greatly to see us, as we also to see you:
theirs: But now when Timotheus came from you unto us, and brought us good tidings of your faith and charity, and that ye have good remembrance of us always, desiring greatly to see us, as we also [to see] you:

ours: And the Lord make you to increase and abound in love one toward another, and toward all men, even as we do toward you:
theirs: And the Lord make you to increase and abound in love one toward another, and toward all [men], even as we [do] toward you:

ours: FURTHERMORE then we beseech you, brethren, and exhort you by the Lord Jesus, that as ye have received of us how ye ought to walk and to please God, so ye would abound more and more.
theirs: Furthermore then we beseech you, brethren, and exhort [you] by the Lord Jesus, that as ye have received of us how ye ought to walk and to please God, [so] ye would abound more and more.

ours: For this is the will of God, even your sanctification, that ye should abstain from fornication:
theirs: For this is the will of God, [even] your sanctification, that ye should abstain from fornication:

ours: That no man go beyond and defraud his brother in any matter: because that the Lord is the avenger of all such, as we also have forewarned you and testified.
theirs: That no [man] go beyond and defraud his brother in [any] matter: because that the Lord [is] the avenger of all such, as we also have forewarned you and testified.

ours: That ye may walk honestly toward them that are without, and that ye may have lack of nothing.
theirs: That ye may walk honestly toward them that are without, and [that] ye may have lack of nothing.

ours: For this we say unto you by the word of the Lord, that we which are alive and remain unto the coming of the Lord shall not prevent them which are asleep.
theirs: For this we say unto you by the word of the Lord, that we which are alive [and] remain unto the coming of the Lord shall not prevent them which are asleep.

ours: Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.
theirs: Then we which are alive [and] remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.

ours: Therefore let us not sleep, as do others; but let us watch and be sober.
theirs: Therefore let us not sleep, as [do] others; but let us watch and be sober.

ours: And to esteem them very highly in love for their works sake. And be at peace among yourselves.
theirs: And to esteem them very highly in love for their work's sake. [And] be at peace among yourselves.

ours: Now we exhort you, brethren, warn them that are unruly, comfort the feebleminded, support the weak, be patient toward all men.
theirs: Now we exhort you, brethren, warn them that are unruly, comfort the feebleminded, support the weak, be patient toward all [men].

ours: See that none render evil for evil unto any man; but ever follow that which is good, both among yourselves, and to all men.
theirs: See that none render evil for evil unto any [man]; but ever follow that which is good, both among yourselves, and to all [men].

ours: And the very God of peace sanctify you wholly; and I pray God your whole spirit and soul and body be preserved blameless unto the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
theirs: And the very God of peace sanctify you wholly; and [I pray God] your whole spirit and soul and body be preserved blameless unto the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.

ours: Faithful is he that calleth you, who also will do it.
theirs: Faithful [is] he that calleth you, who also will do [it].

ours: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.
theirs: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] with you. Amen. <<[The first [epistle] unto the Thessalonians was written from Athens.]>>

ours: Which is a manifest token of the righteous judgment of God, that ye may be counted worthy of the kingdom of God, for which ye also suffer:
theirs: [Which is] a manifest token of the righteous judgment of God, that ye may be counted worthy of the kingdom of God, for which ye also suffer:

ours: Seeing it is a righteous thing with God to recompense tribulation to them that trouble you;
theirs: Seeing [it is] a righteous thing with God to recompense tribulation to them that trouble you;

ours: Wherefore also we pray always for you, that our God would count you worthy of this calling, and fulfil all the good pleasure of his goodness, and the work of faith with power:
theirs: Wherefore also we pray always for you, that our God would count you worthy of [this] calling, and fulfil all the good pleasure of [his] goodness, and the work of faith with power:

ours: NOW we beseech you, brethren, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and by our gathering together unto him,
theirs: Now we beseech you, brethren, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and [by] our gathering together unto him,

ours: Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition;
theirs: Let no man deceive you by any means: for [that day shall not come], except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition;

ours: For the mystery of iniquity doth already work: only he who now letteth will let, until he be taken out of the way.
theirs: For the mystery of iniquity doth already work: only he who now letteth [will let], until he be taken out of the way.

ours: Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders,
theirs: [Even him], whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders,

ours: Now our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God, even our Father, which hath loved us, and hath given us everlasting consolation and good hope through grace,
theirs: Now our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God, even our Father, which hath loved us, and hath given [us] everlasting consolation and good hope through grace,

ours: FINALLY, brethren, pray for us, that the word of the Lord may have free course, and be glorified, even as it is with you:
theirs: Finally, brethren, pray for us, that the word of the Lord may have [free] course, and be glorified, even as [it is] with you:

ours: And that we may be delivered from unreasonable and wicked men: for all men have not faith.
theirs: And that we may be delivered from unreasonable and wicked men: for all [men] have not faith.

ours: But the Lord is faithful, who shall stablish you, and keep you from evil.
theirs: But the Lord is faithful, who shall stablish you, and keep [you] from evil.

ours: Neither did we eat any mans bread for nought; but wrought with labour and travail night and day, that we might not be chargeable to any of you:
theirs: Neither did we eat any man's bread for nought; but wrought with labour and travail night and day, that we might not be chargeable to any of you:

ours: Yet count him not as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother.
theirs: Yet count [him] not as an enemy, but admonish [him] as a brother.

ours: Now the Lord of peace himself give you peace always by all means. The Lord be with you all.
theirs: Now the Lord of peace himself give you peace always by all means. The Lord [be] with you all.

ours: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
theirs: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] with you all. Amen. <<[The second [epistle] to the Thessalonians was written from Athens.]>>

ours: PAUL, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the commandment of God our Saviour, and Lord Jesus Christ, which is our hope;
theirs: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the commandment of God our Saviour, and Lord Jesus Christ, [which is] our hope;

ours: Unto Timothy, my own son in the faith: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God our Father and Jesus Christ our Lord.
theirs: Unto Timothy, [my] own son in the faith: Grace, mercy, [and] peace, from God our Father and Jesus Christ our Lord.

ours: Neither give heed to fables and endless genealogies, which minister questions, rather than godly edifying which is in faith: so do.
theirs: Neither give heed to fables and endless genealogies, which minister questions, rather than godly edifying which is in faith: [so do].

ours: Now the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned:
theirs: Now the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart, and [of] a good conscience, and [of] faith unfeigned:

ours: But we know that the law is good, if a man use it lawfully;
theirs: But we know that the law [is] good, if a man use it lawfully;

ours: Who was before a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious: but I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief.
theirs: Who was before a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious: but I obtained mercy, because I did [it] ignorantly in unbelief.

ours: This is a faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief.
theirs: This [is] a faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief.

ours: Now unto the King eternal, immortal, invisible, the only wise God, be honour and glory for ever and ever. Amen.
theirs: Now unto the King eternal, immortal, invisible, the only wise God, [be] honour and glory for ever and ever. Amen.

ours: Of whom is Hymenæus and Alexander; whom I have delivered unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme.
theirs: Of whom is Hymenaeus and Alexander; whom I have delivered unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme.

ours: I EXHORT therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men;
theirs: I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, [and] giving of thanks, be made for all men;

ours: For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty.
theirs: For kings, and [for] all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty.

ours: For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour;
theirs: For this [is] good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour;

ours: For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus;
theirs: For [there is] one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus;

ours: Whereunto I am ordained a preacher, and an apostle, (I speak the truth in Christ, and lie not;) a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and verity.
theirs: Whereunto I am ordained a preacher, and an apostle, (I speak the truth in Christ, [and] lie not;) a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and verity.

ours: THIS is a true saying, If a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work.
theirs: This [is] a true saying, If a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work.

ours: Likewise must the deacons be grave, not doubletongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre;
theirs: Likewise [must] the deacons [be] grave, not doubletongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre;

ours: And let these also first be proved; then let them use the office of a deacon, being found blameless.
theirs: And let these also first be proved; then let them use the office of a deacon, being [found] blameless.

ours: Even so must their wives be grave, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things.
theirs: Even so [must their] wives [be] grave, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things.

ours: Forbidding to marry, and commanding to abstain from meats, which God hath created to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth.
theirs: Forbidding to marry, [and commanding] to abstain from meats, which God hath created to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth.

ours: For every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving:
theirs: For every creature of God [is] good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving:

ours: But refuse profane and old wives fables, and exercise thyself rather unto godliness.
theirs: But refuse profane and old wives' fables, and exercise thyself [rather] unto godliness.

ours: This is a faithful saying and worthy of all acceptation.
theirs: This [is] a faithful saying and worthy of all acceptation.

ours: REBUKE not an elder, but intreat him as a father; and the younger men as brethren;
theirs: Rebuke not an elder, but intreat [him] as a father; [and] the younger men as brethren;

ours: Well reported of for good works; if she have brought up children, if she have lodged strangers, if she have washed the saints feet, if she have relieved the afflicted, if she have diligently followed every good work.
theirs: Well reported of for good works; if she have brought up children, if she have lodged strangers, if she have washed the saints' feet, if she have relieved the afflicted, if she have diligently followed every good work.

ours: And withal they learn to be idle, wandering about from house to house; and not only idle, but tattlers also and busybodies, speaking things which they ought not.
theirs: And withal they learn [to be] idle, wandering about from house to house; and not only idle, but tattlers also and busybodies, speaking things which they ought not.

ours: For the scripture saith, Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn. And, The labourer is worthy of his reward.
theirs: For the scripture saith, Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn. And, The labourer [is] worthy of his reward.

ours: I charge thee before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, and the elect angels, that thou observe these things without preferring one before another, doing nothing by partiality.
theirs: I charge [thee] before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, and the elect angels, that thou observe these things without preferring one before another, doing nothing by partiality.

ours: Lay hands suddenly on no man, neither be partaker of other mens sins: keep thyself pure.
theirs: Lay hands suddenly on no man, neither be partaker of other men's sins: keep thyself pure.

ours: Drink no longer water, but use a little wine for thy stomachs sake and thine often infirmities.
theirs: Drink no longer water, but use a little wine for thy stomach's sake and thine often infirmities.

ours: Some mens sins are open beforehand, going before to judgment; and some men they follow after.
theirs: Some men's sins are open beforehand, going before to judgment; and some [men] they follow after.

ours: Likewise also the good works of some are manifest beforehand; and they that are otherwise cannot be hid.
theirs: Likewise also the good works [of some] are manifest beforehand; and they that are otherwise cannot be hid.

ours: LET as many servants as are under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honour, that the name of God and his doctrine be not blasphemed.
theirs: Let as many servants as are under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honour, that the name of God and [his] doctrine be not blasphemed.

ours: And they that have believing masters, let them not despise them, because they are brethren; but rather do them service, because they are faithful and beloved, partakers of the benefit. These things teach and exhort.
theirs: And they that have believing masters, let them not despise [them], because they are brethren; but rather do [them] service, because they are faithful and beloved, partakers of the benefit. These things teach and exhort.

ours: If any man teach otherwise, and consent not to wholesome words, even the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and to the doctrine which is according to godliness;
theirs: If any man teach otherwise, and consent not to wholesome words, [even] the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and to the doctrine which is according to godliness;

ours: For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out.
theirs: For we brought nothing into [this] world, [and it is] certain we can carry nothing out.

ours: But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.
theirs: But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and [into] many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.

ours: I give thee charge in the sight of God, who quickeneth all things, and before Christ Jesus, who before Pontius Pilate witnessed a good confession;
theirs: I give thee charge in the sight of God, who quickeneth all things, and [before] Christ Jesus, who before Pontius Pilate witnessed a good confession;

ours: That thou keep this commandment without spot, unrebukeable, until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ:
theirs: That thou keep [this] commandment without spot, unrebukeable, until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ:

ours: Which in his times he shall shew, who is the blessed and only Potentate, the King of kings, and Lord of lords;
theirs: Which in his times he shall shew, [who is] the blessed and only Potentate, the King of kings, and Lord of lords;

ours: Who only hath immortality, dwelling in the light which no man can approach unto; whom no man hath seen, nor can see: to whom be honour and power everlasting. Amen.
theirs: Who only hath immortality, dwelling in the light which no man can approach unto; whom no man hath seen, nor can see: to whom [be] honour and power everlasting. Amen.

ours: O Timothy, keep that which is committed to thy trust, avoiding profane and vain babblings, and oppositions of science falsely so called:
theirs: O Timothy, keep that which is committed to thy trust, avoiding profane [and] vain babblings, and oppositions of science falsely so called:

ours: Which some professing have erred concerning the faith. Grace be with thee. Amen.
theirs: Which some professing have erred concerning the faith. Grace [be] with thee. Amen. <<[The first to Timothy was written from Laodicea, which is the chiefest city of Phrygia Pacatiana.]>>

ours: To Timothy, my dearly beloved son: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
theirs: To Timothy, [my] dearly beloved son: Grace, mercy, [and] peace, from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.

ours: I thank God, whom I serve from my forefathers with pure conscience, that without ceasing I have remembrance of thee in my prayers night and day;
theirs: I thank God, whom I serve from [my] forefathers with pure conscience, that without ceasing I have remembrance of thee in my prayers night and day;

ours: Who hath saved us, and called us with an holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given us in Christ Jesus before the world began,
theirs: Who hath saved us, and called [us] with an holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given us in Christ Jesus before the world began,

ours: But, when he was in Rome, he sought me out very diligently, and found me.
theirs: But, when he was in Rome, he sought me out very diligently, and found [me].

ours: No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.
theirs: No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of [this] life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.

ours: And if a man also strive for masteries, yet is he not crowned, except he strive lawfully.
theirs: And if a man also strive for masteries, [yet] is he not crowned, except he strive lawfully.

ours: Wherein I suffer trouble, as an evil doer, even unto bonds; but the word of God is not bound.
theirs: Wherein I suffer trouble, as an evil doer, [even] unto bonds; but the word of God is not bound.

ours: Therefore I endure all things for the elects sakes, that they may also obtain the salvation which is in Christ Jesus with eternal glory.
theirs: Therefore I endure all things for the elect's sakes, that they may also obtain the salvation which is in Christ Jesus with eternal glory.

ours: It is a faithful saying: For if we be dead with him, we shall also live with him:
theirs: [It is] a faithful saying: For if we be dead with [him], we shall also live with [him]:

ours: If we suffer, we shall also reign with him: if we deny him, he also will deny us:
theirs: If we suffer, we shall also reign with [him]: if we deny [him], he also will deny us:

ours: If we believe not, yet he abideth faithful: he cannot deny himself.
theirs: If we believe not, [yet] he abideth faithful: he cannot deny himself.

ours: Of these things put them in remembrance, charging them before the Lord that they strive not about words to no profit, but to the subverting of the hearers.
theirs: Of these things put [them] in remembrance, charging [them] before the Lord that they strive not about words to no profit, [but] to the subverting of the hearers.

ours: But shun profane and vain babblings: for they will increase unto more ungodliness.
theirs: But shun profane [and] vain babblings: for they will increase unto more ungodliness.

ours: And their word will eat as doth a canker: of whom is Hymenæus and Philetus;
theirs: And their word will eat as doth a canker: of whom is Hymenaeus and Philetus;

ours: If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the masters use, and prepared unto every good work.
theirs: If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master's use, [and] prepared unto every good work.

ours: And the servant of the Lord must not strive; but be gentle unto all men, apt to teach, patient,
theirs: And the servant of the Lord must not strive; but be gentle unto all [men], apt to teach, patient,

ours: And that they may recover themselves out of the snare of the devil, who are taken captive by him at his will.
theirs: And [that] they may recover themselves out of the snare of the devil, who are taken captive by him at his will.

ours: But they shall proceed no further: for their folly shall be manifest unto all men, as theirs also was.
theirs: But they shall proceed no further: for their folly shall be manifest unto all [men], as theirs also was.

ours: Persecutions, afflictions, which came unto me at Antioch, at Iconium, at Lystra; what persecutions I endured: but out of them all the Lord delivered me.
theirs: Persecutions, afflictions, which came unto me at Antioch, at Iconium, at Lystra; what persecutions I endured: but out of [them] all the Lord delivered me.

ours: But continue thou in the things which thou hast learned and hast been assured of, knowing of whom thou hast learned them;
theirs: But continue thou in the things which thou hast learned and hast been assured of, knowing of whom thou hast learned [them];

ours: All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness:
theirs: All scripture [is] given by inspiration of God, and [is] profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness:

ours: I CHARGE thee therefore before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, who shall judge the quick and the dead at his appearing and his kingdom;
theirs: I charge [thee] therefore before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, who shall judge the quick and the dead at his appearing and his kingdom;

ours: And they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables.
theirs: And they shall turn away [their] ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables.

ours: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith:
theirs: I have fought a good fight, I have finished [my] course, I have kept the faith:

ours: The cloke that I left at Troas with Carpus, when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books, but especially the parchments.
theirs: The cloke that I left at Troas with Carpus, when thou comest, bring [with thee], and the books, [but] especially the parchments.

ours: At my first answer no man stood with me, but all men forsook me: I pray God that it may not be laid to their charge.
theirs: At my first answer no man stood with me, but all [men] forsook me: [I pray God] that it may not be laid to their charge.

ours: Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me; that by me the preaching might be fully known, and that all the Gentiles might hear: and I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion.
theirs: Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me; that by me the preaching might be fully known, and [that] all the Gentiles might hear: and I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion.

ours: And the Lord shall deliver me from every evil work, and will preserve me unto his heavenly kingdom: to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen.
theirs: And the Lord shall deliver me from every evil work, and will preserve [me] unto his heavenly kingdom: to whom [be] glory for ever and ever. Amen.

ours: The Lord Jesus Christ be with thy spirit. Grace be with you. Amen.
theirs: The Lord Jesus Christ [be] with thy spirit. Grace [be] with you. Amen. <<[The second [epistle] unto Timotheus, ordained the first bishop of the church of the Ephesians, was written from Rome, when Paul was brought before Nero the second time.]>>

ours: PAUL, a servant of God, and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of Gods elect, and the acknowledging of the truth which is after godliness;
theirs: Paul, a servant of God, and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of God's elect, and the acknowledging of the truth which is after godliness;

ours: To Titus, mine own son after the common faith: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ our Saviour.
theirs: To Titus, [mine] own son after the common faith: Grace, mercy, [and] peace, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ our Saviour.

ours: Whose mouths must be stopped, who subvert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucres sake.
theirs: Whose mouths must be stopped, who subvert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucre's sake.

ours: One of themselves, even a prophet of their own, said, The Cretians are alway liars, evil beasts, slow bellies.
theirs: One of themselves, [even] a prophet of their own, said, The Cretians [are] alway liars, evil beasts, slow bellies.

ours: Unto the pure all things are pure: but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure; but even their mind and conscience is defiled.
theirs: Unto the pure all things [are] pure: but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving [is] nothing pure; but even their mind and conscience is defiled.

ours: They profess that they know God; but in works they deny him, being abominable, and disobedient, and unto every good work reprobate.
theirs: They profess that they know God; but in works they deny [him], being abominable, and disobedient, and unto every good work reprobate.

ours: The aged women likewise, that they be in behaviour as becometh holiness, not false accusers, not given to much wine, teachers of good things;
theirs: The aged women likewise, that [they be] in behaviour as becometh holiness, not false accusers, not given to much wine, teachers of good things;

ours: To be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed.
theirs: [To be] discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed.

ours: In all things shewing thyself a pattern of good works: in doctrine shewing uncorruptness, gravity, sincerity,
theirs: In all things shewing thyself a pattern of good works: in doctrine [shewing] uncorruptness, gravity, sincerity,

ours: Exhort servants to be obedient unto their own masters, and to please them well in all things; not answering again;
theirs: [Exhort] servants to be obedient unto their own masters, [and] to please [them] well in all [things]; not answering again;

ours: To speak evil of no man, to be no brawlers, but gentle, shewing all meekness unto all men.
theirs: To speak evil of no man, to be no brawlers, [but] gentle, shewing all meekness unto all men.

ours: For we ourselves also were sometimes foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving divers lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another.
theirs: For we ourselves also were sometimes foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving divers lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, [and] hating one another.

ours: This is a faithful saying, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly, that they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable unto men.
theirs: [This is] a faithful saying, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly, that they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable unto men.

ours: All that are with me salute thee. Greet them that love us in the faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.
theirs: All that are with me salute thee. Greet them that love us in the faith. Grace [be] with you all. Amen. <<[It was written to Titus, ordained the first bishop of the church of the Cretians, from Nicopolis of Macedonia.]>>

ours: PAUL, a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy our brother, unto Philemon our dearly beloved, and fellowlabourer,
theirs: Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy [our] brother, unto Philemon our dearly beloved, and fellowlabourer,

ours: And to our beloved Apphia, and Archippus our fellowsoldier, and to the church in thy house:
theirs: And to [our] beloved Apphia, and Archippus our fellowsoldier, and to the church in thy house:

ours: Yet for loves sake I rather beseech thee, being such an one as Paul the aged, and now also a prisoner of Jesus Christ.
theirs: Yet for love's sake I rather beseech [thee], being such an one as Paul the aged, and now also a prisoner of Jesus Christ.

ours: If he hath wronged thee, or oweth thee ought, put that on mine account;
theirs: If he hath wronged thee, or oweth [thee] ought, put that on mine account;

ours: I Paul have written it with mine own hand, I will repay it: albeit I do not say to thee how thou owest unto me even thine own self besides.
theirs: I Paul have written [it] with mine own hand, I will repay [it]: albeit I do not say to thee how thou owest unto me even thine own self besides.

ours: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
theirs: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] with your spirit. Amen. <<[Written from Rome to Philemon, by Onesimus a servant.]>>

ours: Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds;
theirs: Hath in these last days spoken unto us by [his] Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds;

ours: Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high;
theirs: Who being the brightness of [his] glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high;

ours: But unto the Son he saith, Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: a sceptre of righteousness is the sceptre of thy kingdom.
theirs: But unto the Son [he saith], Thy throne, O God, [is] for ever and ever: a sceptre of righteousness [is] the sceptre of thy kingdom.

ours: Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God, even thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.
theirs: Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God, [even] thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.

ours: THEREFORE we ought to give the more earnest heed to the things which we have heard, lest at any time we should let them slip.
theirs: Therefore we ought to give the more earnest heed to the things which we have heard, lest at any time we should let [them] slip.

ours: How shall we escape, if we neglect so great salvation; which at the first began to be spoken by the Lord, and was confirmed unto us by them that heard him;
theirs: How shall we escape, if we neglect so great salvation; which at the first began to be spoken by the Lord, and was confirmed unto us by them that heard [him];

ours: God also bearing them witness, both with signs and wonders, and with divers miracles, and gifts of the Holy Ghost, according to his own will?
theirs: God also bearing [them] witness, both with signs and wonders, and with divers miracles, and gifts of the Holy Ghost, according to his own will?

ours: Thou hast put all things in subjection under his feet. For in that he put all in subjection under him, he left nothing that is not put under him. But now we see not yet all things put under him.
theirs: Thou hast put all things in subjection under his feet. For in that he put all in subjection under him, he left nothing [that is] not put under him. But now we see not yet all things put under him.

ours: For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings.
theirs: For it became him, for whom [are] all things, and by whom [are] all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings.

ours: For both he that sanctifieth and they who are sanctified are all of one: for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brethren,
theirs: For both he that sanctifieth and they who are sanctified [are] all of one: for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brethren,

ours: For verily he took not on him the nature of angels; but he took on him the seed of Abraham.
theirs: For verily he took not on [him the nature of] angels; but he took on [him] the seed of Abraham.

ours: Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren, that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.
theirs: Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto [his] brethren, that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things [pertaining] to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.

ours: Who was faithful to him that appointed him, as also Moses was faithful in all his house.
theirs: Who was faithful to him that appointed him, as also Moses [was faithful] in all his house.

ours: For this man was counted worthy of more glory than Moses, inasmuch as he who hath builded the house hath more honour than the house.
theirs: For this [man] was counted worthy of more glory than Moses, inasmuch as he who hath builded the house hath more honour than the house.

ours: For every house is builded by some man; but he that built all things is God.
theirs: For every house is builded by some [man]; but he that built all things [is] God.

ours: And Moses verily was faithful in all his house, as a servant, for a testimony of those things which were to be spoken after;
theirs: And Moses verily [was] faithful in all his house, as a servant, for a testimony of those things which were to be spoken after;

ours: Wherefore I was grieved with that generation, and said, They do alway err in their heart; and they have not known my ways.
theirs: Wherefore I was grieved with that generation, and said, They do alway err in [their] heart; and they have not known my ways.

ours: But with whom was he grieved forty years? was it not with them that had sinned, whose carcases fell in the wilderness?
theirs: But with whom was he grieved forty years? [was it] not with them that had sinned, whose carcases fell in the wilderness?

ours: LET us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it.
theirs: Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left [us] of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it.

ours: For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them: but the word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it.
theirs: For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them: but the word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard [it].

ours: For he spake in a certain place of the seventh day on this wise, And God did rest the seventh day from all his works.
theirs: For he spake in a certain place of the seventh [day] on this wise, And God did rest the seventh day from all his works.

ours: And in this place again, If they shall enter into my rest.
theirs: And in this [place] again, If they shall enter into my rest.

ours: For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his.
theirs: For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God [did] from his.

ours: For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.
theirs: For the word of God [is] quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and [is] a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.

ours: Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do.
theirs: Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things [are] naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do.

ours: Seeing then that we have a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profession.
theirs: Seeing then that we have a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast [our] profession.

ours: For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin.
theirs: For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as [we are, yet] without sin.

ours: FOR every high priest taken from among men is ordained for men in things pertaining to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins:
theirs: For every high priest taken from among men is ordained for men in things [pertaining] to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins:

ours: And no man taketh this honour unto himself, but he that is called of God, as was Aaron.
theirs: And no man taketh this honour unto himself, but he that is called of God, as [was] Aaron.

ours: As he saith also in another place, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.
theirs: As he saith also in another [place], Thou [art] a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.

ours: For when for the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have need that one teach you again which be the first principles of the oracles of God; and are become such as have need of milk, and not of strong meat.
theirs: For when for the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have need that one teach you again which [be] the first principles of the oracles of God; and are become such as have need of milk, and not of strong meat.

ours: For every one that useth milk is unskilful in the word of righteousness: for he is a babe.
theirs: For every one that useth milk [is] unskilful in the word of righteousness: for he is a babe.

ours: But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.
theirs: But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, [even] those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.

ours: For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost,
theirs: For [it is] impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost,

ours: If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame.
theirs: If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put [him] to an open shame.

ours: But that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned.
theirs: But that which beareth thorns and briers [is] rejected, and [is] nigh unto cursing; whose end [is] to be burned.

ours: For God is not unrighteous to forget your work and labour of love, which ye have shewed toward his name, in that ye have ministered to the saints, and do minister.
theirs: For God [is] not unrighteous to forget your work and labour of love, which ye have shewed toward his name, in that ye have ministered to the saints, and do minister.

ours: For men verily swear by the greater: and an oath for confirmation is to them an end of all strife.
theirs: For men verily swear by the greater: and an oath for confirmation [is] to them an end of all strife.

ours: Wherein God, willing more abundantly to shew unto the heirs of promise the immutability of his counsel, confirmed it by an oath:
theirs: Wherein God, willing more abundantly to shew unto the heirs of promise the immutability of his counsel, confirmed [it] by an oath:

ours: That by two immutable things, in which it was impossible for God to lie, we might have a strong consolation, who have fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us:
theirs: That by two immutable things, in which [it was] impossible for God to lie, we might have a strong consolation, who have fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us:

ours: Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast, and which entereth into that within the veil;
theirs: Which [hope] we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast, and which entereth into that within the veil;

ours: Whither the forerunner is for us entered, even Jesus, made an high priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.
theirs: Whither the forerunner is for us entered, [even] Jesus, made an high priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.

ours: Now consider how great this man was, unto whom even the patriarch Abraham gave the tenth of the spoils.
theirs: Now consider how great this man [was], unto whom even the patriarch Abraham gave the tenth of the spoils.

ours: And here men that die receive tithes; but there he receiveth them, of whom it is witnessed that he liveth.
theirs: And here men that die receive tithes; but there he [receiveth them], of whom it is witnessed that he liveth.

ours: If therefore perfection were by the Levitical priesthood, (for under it the people received the law,) what further need was there that another priest should rise after the order of Melchisedec, and not be called after the order of Aaron?
theirs: If therefore perfection were by the Levitical priesthood, (for under it the people received the law,) what further need [was there] that another priest should rise after the order of Melchisedec, and not be called after the order of Aaron?

ours: For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.
theirs: For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.

ours: For he testifieth, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.
theirs: For he testifieth, Thou [art] a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.

ours: For the law made nothing perfect, but the bringing in of a better hope did; by the which we draw nigh unto God.
theirs: For the law made nothing perfect, but the bringing in of a better hope [did]; by the which we draw nigh unto God.

ours: And inasmuch as not without an oath he was made priest:
theirs: And inasmuch as not without an oath [he was made priest]:

ours: (For those priests were made without an oath; but this with an oath by him that said unto him, The Lord sware and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec:)
theirs: (For those priests were made without an oath; but this with an oath by him that said unto him, The Lord sware and will not repent, Thou [art] a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec:)

ours: But this man, because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood.
theirs: But this [man], because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood.

ours: For such an high priest became us, who is holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens;
theirs: For such an high priest became us, [who is] holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens;

ours: Who needeth not daily, as those high priests, to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the peoples: for this he did once, when he offered up himself.
theirs: Who needeth not daily, as those high priests, to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the people's: for this he did once, when he offered up himself.

ours: For the law maketh men high priests which have infirmity; but the word of the oath, which was since the law, maketh the Son, who is consecrated for evermore.
theirs: For the law maketh men high priests which have infirmity; but the word of the oath, which was since the law, [maketh] the Son, who is consecrated for evermore.

ours: NOW of the things which we have spoken this is the sum: We have such an high priest, who is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens;
theirs: Now of the things which we have spoken [this is] the sum: We have such an high priest, who is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens;

ours: For every high priest is ordained to offer gifts and sacrifices: wherefore it is of necessity that this man have somewhat also to offer.
theirs: For every high priest is ordained to offer gifts and sacrifices: wherefore [it is] of necessity that this man have somewhat also to offer.

ours: Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount.
theirs: Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, [that] thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount.

ours: For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second.
theirs: For if that first [covenant] had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second.

ours: For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people:
theirs: For this [is] the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people:

ours: In that he saith, A new covenant, he hath made the first old. Now that which decayeth and waxeth old is ready to vanish away.
theirs: In that he saith, A new [covenant], he hath made the first old. Now that which decayeth and waxeth old [is] ready to vanish away.

ours: THEN verily the first covenant had also ordinances of divine service, and a worldly sanctuary.
theirs: Then verily the first [covenant] had also ordinances of divine service, and a worldly sanctuary.

ours: For there was a tabernacle made; the first, wherein was the candlestick, and the table, and the shewbread; which is called the sanctuary.
theirs: For there was a tabernacle made; the first, wherein [was] the candlestick, and the table, and the shewbread; which is called the sanctuary.

ours: Which had the golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold, wherein was the golden pot that had manna, and Aarons rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant;
theirs: Which had the golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold, wherein [was] the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron's rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant;

ours: Now when these things were thus ordained, the priests went always into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the service of God.
theirs: Now when these things were thus ordained, the priests went always into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the service [of God].

ours: But into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people:
theirs: But into the second [went] the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and [for] the errors of the people:

ours: Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience;
theirs: Which [was] a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience;

ours: Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.
theirs: [Which stood] only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed [on them] until the time of reformation.

ours: Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us.
theirs: Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption [for us].

ours: And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance.
theirs: And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions [that were] under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance.

ours: For where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator.
theirs: For where a testament [is], there must also of necessity be the death of the testator.

ours: For a testament is of force after men are dead: otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator liveth.
theirs: For a testament [is] of force after men are dead: otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator liveth.

ours: Whereupon neither the first testament was dedicated without blood.
theirs: Whereupon neither the first [testament] was dedicated without blood.

ours: Saying, This is the blood of the testament which God hath enjoined unto you.
theirs: Saying, This [is] the blood of the testament which God hath enjoined unto you.

ours: It was therefore necessary that the patterns of things in the heavens should be purified with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
theirs: [It was] therefore necessary that the patterns of things in the heavens should be purified with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.

ours: For Christ is not entered into the holy places made with hands, which are the figures of the true; but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us:
theirs: For Christ is not entered into the holy places made with hands, [which are] the figures of the true; but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us:

ours: FOR the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.
theirs: For the law having a shadow of good things to come, [and] not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.

ours: But in those sacrifices there is a remembrance again made of sins every year.
theirs: But in those [sacrifices there is] a remembrance again [made] of sins every year.

ours: For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins.
theirs: For [it is] not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins.

ours: In burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin thou hast had no pleasure.
theirs: In burnt offerings and [sacrifices] for sin thou hast had no pleasure.

ours: Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law;
theirs: Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and [offering] for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure [therein]; which are offered by the law;

ours: By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
theirs: By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once [for all].

ours: Whereof the Holy Ghost also is a witness to us: for after that he had said before,
theirs: [Whereof] the Holy Ghost also is a witness to us: for after that he had said before,

ours: This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord, I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them;
theirs: This [is] the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord, I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them;

ours: Now where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin.
theirs: Now where remission of these [is, there is] no more offering for sin.

ours: And having an high priest over the house of God;
theirs: And [having] an high priest over the house of God;

ours: Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering; (for he is faithful that promised;)
theirs: Let us hold fast the profession of [our] faith without wavering; (for he [is] faithful that promised;)

ours: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.
theirs: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some [is]; but exhorting [one another]: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.

ours: He that despised Moses law died without mercy under two or three witnesses:
theirs: He that despised Moses' law died without mercy under two or three witnesses:

ours: For we know him that hath said, Vengeance belongeth unto me, I will recompense, saith the Lord. And again, The Lord shall judge his people.
theirs: For we know him that hath said, Vengeance [belongeth] unto me, I will recompense, saith the Lord. And again, The Lord shall judge his people.

ours: It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
theirs: [It is] a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.

ours: Now the just shall live by faith: but if any man draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him.
theirs: Now the just shall live by faith: but if [any man] draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him.

ours: But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.
theirs: But without faith [it is] impossible to please [him]: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and [that] he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.

ours: By faith he sojourned in the land of promise, as in a strange country, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise:
theirs: By faith he sojourned in the land of promise, as [in] a strange country, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise:

ours: For he looked for a city which hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God.
theirs: For he looked for a city which hath foundations, whose builder and maker [is] God.

ours: Therefore sprang there even of one, and him as good as dead, so many as the stars of the sky in multitude, and as the sand which is by the sea shore innumerable.
theirs: Therefore sprang there even of one, and him as good as dead, [so many] as the stars of the sky in multitude, and as the sand which is by the sea shore innumerable.

ours: These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them afar off, and were persuaded of them, and embraced them, and confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.
theirs: These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them afar off, and were persuaded of [them], and embraced [them], and confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.
